episodeTitle.en: The rise of taste, human authenticity and judgment in an AI world | Adam Mosseri (Head of IG)
episodeTitle.zh: 在AI世界中品味、人类真实性与判断力的崛起 | 亚当·莫塞里（Instagram负责人）

bio.en: Adam Mosseri is the Head of Instagram, leading a platform used by over three billion people monthly, and previously designed and led the early Facebook News Feed and its ranking algorithm.
bio.zh: Adam Mosseri 是 Instagram 负责人，领导着月活超过 30 亿人的平台，此前曾设计并主导 Facebook 早期动态消息（News Feed）及其排序算法。

guestBioOfficial.en: Adam Mosseri is the Head of Instagram, where he oversees an app used by over 3 billion people. He also leads the team building Threads. Adam has run Instagram for longer than its founders did, after taking over from Kevin Systrom and Mike Krieger in 2018. A designer by training, he spent over 15 years at Meta, starting as a designer on Facebook’s mobile app, rising to lead Facebook’s News Feed, and eventually chosen to lead Instagram. During his tenure, Instagram’s user base has more than tripled. *In our in-depth conversation, we discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 亚当·莫塞里是Instagram的负责人，管理着一个拥有30亿以上用户的应用程序。他还领导着Threads团队的建设。亚当接手Instagram的时间比创始人更长，自2018年接替凯文·西斯特罗姆和迈克·克里格尔后掌管Instagram。作为训练有素的设计师，他在Meta工作了15余年，最初在Facebook移动应用担任设计师，随后负责Facebook新闻推送，最终被选中领导Instagram。在他的任期内，Instagram的用户基础增长了两倍多。在我们的深度对话中，我们讨论了：

summary.en: Adam argues that taste matters more than ever in an AI world where building is cheap, and that the most valuable people will be clear-eyed about what AI is and isn't good at. He explains that the Instagram algorithm understands users far less semantically than people assume, and predicts AI-generated content will ultimately be a tailwind as people seek out authenticity. He also discusses why human judgment remains essential in the product development lifecycle even as AI eats more of it.
summary.zh: Adam 认为，在 AI 让“造东西”变得廉价的时代，品味比以往任何时候都更重要，而最有价值的人是对 AI 擅长与不擅长之处有清醒认知的人。他解释道，Instagram 算法对用户兴趣的理解远比人们想象的更“非语义化”，并预测 AI 生成内容最终会是顺风，因为人们会更渴望真实。他还讨论了为何即便 AI 吞噬更多产品开发环节，人类判断依然不可或缺。

episodeTitle.en: Why OpenAI is merging Codex and ChatGPT and the future of knowledge work | Andrew Ambrosino
episodeTitle.zh: 为什么 OpenAI 正在合并 Codex 和 ChatGPT？未来知识工作的走向 | 安德鲁·安布罗西诺

bio.en: Andrew Ambrosino is the product and engineering lead for the Codex app at OpenAI, which is quickly becoming a go-to tool for building products with AI.
bio.zh: Andrew Ambrosino 是 OpenAI Codex 应用的产品与工程负责人，该应用正迅速成为用 AI 构建产品的首选工具。

guestBioOfficial.en: Andrew Ambrosino leads development of the Codex desktop app at OpenAI. Nearly 100% of OpenAI employees—not just engineers—now use Codex weekly. A lifelong builder with a background spanning engineering, design, product management, and founding companies, he is now responsible for turning the Codex desktop experience into what he calls “the best desktop app that has ever existed, full stop.” *In our in-depth conversation, we discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 安德鲁·安布罗西诺是 OpenAI 的 Codex 桌面应用开发负责人。目前，OpenAI 几乎 100%的员工（不仅仅是工程师）每周都会使用 Codex。他是一位终身创业者，拥有工程、设计、产品管理和创办公司的背景，现在负责将 Codex 桌面体验打造成他口中“有史以来最好的桌面应用，没有之一”。*在我们的深度对话中，我们将探讨：*

summary.en: Andrew notes that 90% of OpenAI's entire company uses Codex and aims to make it the best desktop app ever, with quality high enough that it becomes people's natural default. He argues design remains hard for frontier models to grade because taste is inherently human, and that implementation is no longer the expensive part—taste is. The conversation covers how product teams are shifting toward everyone being agentic builders and the risks of prematurely eliminating the PM role.
summary.zh: Andrew 提到 OpenAI 全公司 90% 的人都在使用 Codex，并致力于把它打造成史上最好的桌面应用，质量之高让它成为人们的自然默认选择。他认为设计对前沿模型而言仍难评判，因为品味本质上是人类的，且实现已不再是昂贵环节——品味才是。对话涵盖产品团队正向“人人都是能动型构建者”转变，以及过早取消 PM 角色的风险。

episodeTitle.en: What happens after coding is solved? | Fiona Fung (Claude Code & Cowork)
episodeTitle.zh: 编码问题解决后会发生什么？ | 冯丽芬（Claude Code & Cowork）

bio.en: Fiona Fung leads the teams behind Claude Code and Cowork at Anthropic, and is a 25-year engineering veteran who previously built TypeScript and Visual Studio at Microsoft and founded Facebook Marketplace, which now drives over $100 billion in GMV a year.
bio.zh: Fiona Fung 在 Anthropic 领导 Claude Code 和 Cowork 背后的团队，是一位拥有 25 年经验的工程老将，此前在微软打造了 TypeScript 和 Visual Studio，并在 Facebook 创立了如今年 GMV 超 1000 亿美元的 Facebook Marketplace。

guestBioOfficial.en: Fiona Fung leads the teams behind Claude Code and Cowork at Anthropic (overseeing Boris Cherny and the entire engineering and PM team). Before Anthropic, she spent 11 years at Microsoft building Visual Studio and TypeScript and then moved to Meta, where she started Facebook Marketplace (now generating over $100 billion in GMV annually), worked on Meta’s first smart glasses and AR glasses, and led infrastructure, growth, integrity, and safety teams at Instagram. She’s been an engineer for over 25 years and has a unique perspective on how the role of building software is changing. *In our in-depth conversation, we discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 冯丽芬在Anthropic领导Claude Code和Cowork团队（监督鲍里斯·切尔尼及整个工程和产品管理团队）。加入Anthropic之前，她在微软工作11年，参与Visual Studio和TypeScript的开发，随后转至Meta，在那里她创立了Facebook Marketplace（目前年交易额超过1000亿美元），参与了Meta首款智能眼镜和AR眼镜的研发，并在Instagram领导基础设施、增长、诚信和安全团队。她拥有超过25年的工程师经验，对软件开发角色的变化有着独特的见解。在我们的深度对话中，我们将讨论：

summary.en: Fiona describes how AI has removed coding as the bottleneck—Anthropic engineers now ship roughly 8x the code per quarter versus 2025—so the constraint is ambition, not ability. She explains that the people thriving are those with the most agency and initiative, paired with accountability, and argues teams should 'lean in' to fear rather than resist it. We also hear about the emerging gap between AI-native and AI-resistant engineers, the loneliness risk of agent-only work (and their 'pair-wise programming lunch'), and what long-time engineering leaders should be thinking about right now.
summary.zh: Fiona 描述了 AI 如何消除了编码这一瓶颈——Anthropic 工程师如今每季度提交的代码量约为 2025 年的 8 倍——所以限制因素变成了“野心”而非“能力”。她解释道，表现最好的人是那些最具主动性、最有能动性、同时又能承担责任的人，并主张团队应“迎难而上”面对恐惧而非抗拒。我们还听到 AI 原生工程师与抗拒 AI 的工程师之间正在拉开的差距、纯靠智能体工作的孤独风险（以及他们的“结对编程午餐”），以及资深工程领导者当下应当思考什么。

episodeTitle.en: The hidden pattern behind successful products | Mark Pincus (FarmVille, Words with Friends, & more)
episodeTitle.zh: 成功产品的隐藏模式 | 马克·平卡斯（《开心农场》《好友消消乐》等）

bio.en: Mark Pincus is the founder of Zynga, the social-gaming pioneer behind FarmVille, and a serial consumer-internet entrepreneur and investor.
bio.zh: 马克·平卡斯（Mark Pincus）是 Zynga 的创始人，即《FarmVille》背后的社交游戏先驱，也是一位连续消费互联网创业者与投资人。

guestBioOfficial.en: Mark Pincus founded Zynga—the company behind Words With Friends, FarmVille, and Zynga Poker—and has arguably created more hit consumer products than anyone in history. At Zynga, eight of 10 major game launches became massive hits, reaching over a billion players. Over the past five years, Mark has been synthesizing everything he’s learned about building successful consumer products and turning it into a book, Life at the Speed of Play, which comes out on June 23. This is the first interview he’s done about the book. *In our in-depth conversation, we discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 马克·平卡斯创立了Zynga——《开心农场》《好友消消乐》和《Zynga扑克》的母公司——可以说，他比历史上任何人都创造了更多的热门消费产品。在Zynga，10款主要游戏中有8款成为大热门，玩家数量超过10亿。过去五年，马克一直在总结他在打造成功消费产品方面的经验，并将其写成一本书《游戏速度下的生活》，该书将于6月23日出版。这是他首次就这本书接受采访。在我们的深入对话中，我们讨论了：

summary.en: Mark offers contrarian advice like "burn your resume" if you're truly ambitious, trusting your instincts (right ~95% of the time) over ideas (wrong ~75%). He warns against founders who stoically cling to losing ideas instead of reading market signals. The episode is a blunt, experienced take on spotting real product-market fit and avoiding self-deception.
summary.zh: 马克给出了反共识的建议：如果你真的有野心，就"烧掉你的简历"，并相信直觉（约 95% 正确）而非想法（约 75% 错误）。他警告那些固执地抱着失败想法、不去读取市场信号的创始人。本期以坦诚而老练的口吻，讲述了如何识别真正的产品-市场契合、避免自欺。

episodeTitle.en: Tony Fadell: How to build real taste (and why AI makes it matter more)
episodeTitle.zh: 托尼·法德尔（Tony Fadell）：如何打造真正的品味（以及AI为何让它变得更重要）

bio.en: Tony Fadell is a legendary product creator who co-created the iPod, iPhone, and Nest Thermostat, was part of the legendary team at General Magic, holds 300+ patents, and authored Build.
bio.zh: Tony Fadell 是一位传奇产品创造者，他共同打造了 iPod、iPhone 与 Nest 恒温器，曾是 General Magic 传奇团队的一员，拥有 300 多项专利，并著有《Build》一书。

guestBioOfficial.en: Tony Fadell created the iPod, co-created the iPhone, and founded Nest (which he sold to Google for $3.2 billion). He’s co-authored over 300 patents, was part of the legendary team at General Magic, and wrote one of the most important and inspiring books for builders, called Build. *In our in-depth conversation, we discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 托尼·法德尔（Tony Fadell）创造了iPod，参与设计了iPhone，并创立了Nest（后以32亿美元的价格出售给谷歌）。他共同申请了300多项专利，曾是General Magic传奇团队的成员，并撰写了面向创业者最具启发性的著作《Build》。在深度对谈中，我们将探讨：

summary.en: Tony shares hard-won lessons from creating some of the most iconic products in history, emphasizing that great products come from relentless iteration, taste, and the courage to say no. He discusses the importance of building the right team, learning from failure, and maintaining conviction through years of uncertainty. The episode is an inspiring, story-rich masterclass from one of the greatest product minds alive.
summary.zh: Tony 分享了从创造史上最具标志性产品中锤炼出的来之不易的经验，强调伟大产品源于不懈的迭代、品味，以及说“不”的勇气。他讨论了组建正确团队的重要性、从失败中学习，以及在经年累月的未知中保持信念。本期是当今最伟大产品头脑之一带来的、富含故事的鼓舞人心的大师课。

episodeTitle.en: The most rational take on AI you’ll hear this year
episodeTitle.zh: 今年你将听到的关于AI最理性的观点

bio.en: Benedict Evans is a long-time analyst (formerly in-house at a16z) and independent thinker who has tracked the most important shifts in tech and now writes about where the industry is heading.
bio.zh: Benedict Evans 是资深分析师（曾为 a16z 驻场分析师）和独立思想家，长期追踪科技行业最重要的变化，如今撰写关于行业走向的文章。

guestBioOfficial.en: Benedict Evans is an independent analyst and former partner at Andreessen Horowitz, where he spent years as their in-house “thinker” tracking the most important technology trends. For the past six years, he’s been publishing deeply researched presentations on where tech is heading, most recently focused on AI’s transformation of the economy. His work is read by founders, investors, and operators trying to make sense of a noisy field. His most controversial opinion: AI is as big a deal as the internet or mobile—and only as big. *In our in-depth conversation, we discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 本尼迪克特·埃文斯（Benedict Evans）是一位独立分析师，也是安德森·霍洛维茨的前合伙人。在安德森·霍洛维茨，他曾担任内部"思想家"数年，追踪最重要的技术趋势。在过去的六年里，他一直在发布关于科技发展方向的深度研究报告，最近的重点是AI对经济的变革。他的工作被试图理解这个混乱领域的创始人、投资者和运营者所阅读。他最具争议的观点是：AI的重要性与互联网或移动设备相当——而且仅此而已。*在我们的深度对话中，我们讨论了：*

summary.en: Benedict argues AI is as big a deal as the internet or mobile—but only that big—and pushes back on “job apocalypse” panic, noting every new technology automates some jobs while unlocking new ones we can't yet imagine. He cautions against head-in-the-sand denial and advises people to dive in and learn what AI can actually do. The conversation is a clear-eyed take on hype, history, and how to position yourself for an AI-shaped future.
summary.zh: Benedict 认为 AI 与互联网或移动端同等重要——但也“仅此而已”——并反驳“就业末日”的恐慌，指出每项新技术在自动化部分工作的同时，也会解锁我们尚无法想象的新工作。他警示不要掩耳盗铃式地否认，并建议人们深入其中、学习 AI 真正能做什么。对话对炒作、历史以及如何在 AI 塑造的未来中定位自己给出了清醒的判断。

episodeTitle.en: AI predictions: Job markets, Codex beats Claude, and the death of org charts | Dan Shipper
episodeTitle.zh: AI预测：就业市场、Codex击败Claude，以及组织结构图的终结 | Dan Shipper

bio.en: Dan Shipper is co-founder and CEO of Every, a company at the bleeding edge of AI adoption, and returns to predict where AI and work are heading after his earlier correct call on Claude Code.
bio.zh: Dan Shipper 是 Every 的联合创始人兼 CEO，一家处于 AI 应用最前沿的公司，继此前准确预言 Claude Code 后，他再度做客预测 AI 与工作将走向何方。

guestBioOfficial.en: Dan Shipper is the co-founder and CEO of Every, a media and software company that’s become a living laboratory for the future of work. Everyone at his company of about 30 people is an AI early adopter; from editors to ops people, they use AI to do much of their work, giving Every a unique lens into where the world is heading. A year ago on this show, Dan predicted that people were sleeping on Claude Code for nontechnical work, which proved to be remarkably prescient. Today he’s back with another set of calls: the SaaS apocalypse is dumb, CLIs are over, the forward deployed engineer is the most valuable new hire, and the only thing you need to do to stay employed is ride the models. *Dan’s predictions:*
guestBioOfficial.zh:
丹·希珀（Dan Shipper）是媒体与软件公司Every的联合创始人兼首席执行官。Every已成为未来职场发展的活体实验室。公司约30名员工全都是AI早期采用者——从编辑到运营人员，日常工作中大量借助AI技术。这为Every提供了独特视角，洞察全球职场发展趋势。一年前在本节目中，丹曾预言非技术岗位正在忽视Claude Code的潜力，这一预测后来被证明极具洞察力。如今他带来了新一轮预言：SaaS末日论是无稽之谈，CLI已成历史，驻场工程师是新晋最具价值人才，而保持就业的唯一秘诀就是紧跟模型趋势。

*丹的预测：*

summary.en: Dan pushes back on “AI jobpocalypse” panic, arguing he's bullish on PMs and full-stack designers because models commoditize yesterday's competence while humans create something new. He predicts work bifurcates into everyone having at least one agent and most work happening inside environments like Codex or Claude Code. The conversation covers why creativity becomes more valuable and why he's both extremely AI-pilled and bullish on humans.
summary.zh: Dan 反驳“AI 就业末日”的恐慌，认为他看好 PM 和全栈设计师，因为模型把“昨天的人的能力”商品化，而人类创造新东西。他预测工作将一分为二：人人至少有一个智能体，且多数工作在 Codex 或 Claude Code 这类环境中发生。对话涵盖为何创造力更值钱，以及他为何既极度 AI 化又看好人类。

episodeTitle.en: Why the next AI boom is physical AI | Caitlin Kalinowski (ex-OpenAI, Meta, Apple)
episodeTitle.zh: 下一场AI热潮将是物理AI | 凯特琳·卡利诺夫斯基（曾任OpenAI、Meta、苹果公司）

bio.en: Caitlin Kalinowski is a sought-after builder who has worked with legendary makers like Steve Jobs, Mark Zuckerberg, and Sam Altman, and is focused on robotics, manufacturing, and physical-world AI.
bio.zh: Caitlin Kalinowski 是一位备受追捧的构建者，曾与 Steve Jobs、Mark Zuckerberg、Sam Altman 等传奇人物共事，目前专注于机器人、制造和物理世界的 AI。

guestBioOfficial.en: Caitlin Kalinowski was most recently at OpenAI helping build their robotics and hardware teams from scratch. Prior to that, she was head of AR glasses and VR hardware at Meta, where she led the teams building every generation of the Quest, Rift, and Orion, and was Meta’s first consumer electronics hire. Before this, she was  technical lead on MacBook Air and Mac Pro at Apple, and helped engineer the original unibody MacBook Pro. She’s designed and engineered some of the hardest and most beloved consumer hardware products in history and is now focused on the next frontier: robotics. *In our in-depth conversation, we discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 凯特琳·卡利诺夫斯基最近在OpenAI工作，帮助从零开始组建其机器人与硬件团队。在此之前，她曾担任Meta公司的AR眼镜和VR硬件部门负责人，领导团队开发了每一代Quest、Rift和Orion产品，也是Meta公司首位消费电子产品领域的招聘人员。此前，她在苹果公司担任MacBook Air和Mac Pro的技术主管，并参与设计了首款一体式MacBook Pro。她设计并开发了历史上一些最具挑战性和最受欢迎的消费硬件产品，如今专注于下一个前沿领域——机器人技术。在我们的深度对话中，我们探讨了：

summary.en: Caitlin argues that as what's possible behind a keyboard with AI saturates, the next frontier is the physical world—robotics, manufacturing, and reindustrialization. She shares what made Steve Jobs' bar for talent and excellence unwavering and how Sam Altman pushes people to think 100x bigger. The conversation covers why design for physical AI matters, the coming “meteor” of memory-price constraints, and national security implications of reindustrialization.
summary.zh: Caitlin 认为，当键盘后靠 AI 能做的事趋于饱和，下一个前沿是物理世界——机器人、制造和再工业化。她分享了 Steve Jobs 对人才与卓越毫不退让的标准，以及 Sam Altman 如何逼人把想法放大 100 倍。对话涵盖物理 AI 的设计为何重要、即将到来的“内存价格流星”约束，以及再工业化的国家安全含义。

episodeTitle.en: How Anthropic, Costco, and Patagonia all build incorruptible companies  | Eric Ries
episodeTitle.zh: 人类中心主义、好市多和巴塔哥尼亚如何打造廉洁公司 | 埃里克·里斯

bio.en: Eric Ries is the author of The Lean Startup—the most influential startup book of the past 15 years—and now of Incorruptible: Why Good Companies Go Bad and How Great Companies Stay Great, on protecting what founders build.
bio.zh: Eric Ries 是《精益创业》（过去 15 年最具影响力的创业著作）的作者，如今又推出《Incorruptible: Why Good Companies Go Bad and How Great Companies Stay Great》，讲述如何守护创始人所建立的事业。

guestBioOfficial.en: Eric Ries is the author of The Lean Startup, a book that reshaped how a generation of founders think about building companies. His new book, Incorruptible, explains how successful companies are destroyed by failing to protect what makes them valuable, and how to change it. *In our in-depth conversation, we discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 埃里克·里斯是《精益创业》的作者，这本书重塑了一代创业者对公司建设的思考。他的新书《廉洁》解释了成功的公司如何因未能保护其价值所在而被毁，以及如何改变这种局面。在今天的深度对话中，我们讨论了：• 《精益创业》方法论的现状

summary.en: Eric connects his new book Incorruptible to The Lean Startup by framing the first as about building a successful company and the second as about protecting it from the 'force that no one controls'—the drift toward mediocrity that corrupts even winning organizations. He shares how he advised Anthropic's founders to bake AI-safety accountability into their charter, and argues that principled, harder-than-easy decision-making yields unexpected rewards while ROI-only thinking leads astray. The episode is a practical guide for founders on keeping control of what they've built and avoiding the fate of companies destroyed by their own success.
summary.zh: Eric 将新书《Incorruptible》与《精益创业》联系起来：前者讲如何打造一家成功的公司，后者讲如何保护它免遭“无人掌控、人人服从”的力量——那种把即便成功的组织也拖向平庸的引力。他分享了如何建议 Anthropic 的创始人把 AI 安全问责写入公司章程，并主张坚持原则、选择“更难但更对”的决策会带来意外回报，而只算 ROI 的思维会把人带偏。这期节目是为创始人提供的实用指南：守住自己建立的事业，避免被自身成功反噬的命运。

episodeTitle.en: AI era skills: Why cultivating agency matters more than job titles | Max Schoening (Notion)
episodeTitle.zh: AI时代技能：为何培养自主性比职位头衔更重要 | 马克斯·肖宁（Max Schoening，Notion）

bio.en: Max Schoenig is Head of Product at Notion, and has been a PM at Google, ran design at Heroku, and was an engineering and design leader at GitHub.
bio.zh: 马克斯·舍宁（Max Schoenig）是 Notion 的产品负责人，曾在 Google 任 PM、在 Heroku 领导设计，并在 GitHub 担任工程与设计领导。

guestBioOfficial.en: Max Schoening is head of product at Notion, where he’s been especially effective at getting designers and PMs to ship code, prototype in the terminal, and launch extremely successful AI products. He was previously a PM at Google, ran design at Heroku, was VP of Design (and a part-time engineer) at GitHub, and is a two-time founder. He’s one of the most AI-forward product leaders out there and one of the deepest thinkers on how AI changes how we build and use software. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 马克斯·肖宁（Max Schoening）是Notion的产品负责人，尤其擅长推动设计师和产品经理编写代码、在终端进行原型设计，并推出极其成功的AI产品。他曾在谷歌担任产品经理，在Heroku负责设计工作，担任GitHub的副总裁兼兼职工程师，还是两次创业的创始人。他是AI领域最前沿的产品领导者之一，也是对AI如何改变我们构建和使用软件方式思考最深刻的人士之一。我们讨论了：

summary.en: Max argues that in the AI era, skill gaps matter less than agency - the belief that you can change things. He notes the first 10% of every project is now nearly free, lowering the cost of starting. The episode explores how taste and agency, not just technical skill, define modern builders.
summary.zh: 马克斯认为，在 AI 时代，技能差距的重要性低于"自驱力"——即相信自己能改变事物。他指出，如今每个项目的前 10% 几乎免费，降低了启动成本。本期探讨了在现代构建者身上，真正定义价值的为何是品味与自驱力，而非单纯的技术技能。

episodeTitle.en: How to win when software is not a moat | Evan Spiegel (Snapchat CEO)
episodeTitle.zh: 当软件不再是护城河时如何取胜 | 埃文·斯皮格尔（Snapchat CEO）

bio.en: Evan Spiegel is the co-founder and CEO of Snap, the company behind Snapchat—one of the very few durable consumer social apps ever built, with over one billion monthly active users and more than $6 billion in annual revenue.
bio.zh: Evan Spiegel 是 Snap 的联合创始人兼 CEO；Snap 是 Snapchat 的母公司——Snapchat 是有史以来极少数真正长期存活的消费者社交应用之一，月活用户超 10 亿，年收入超 60 亿美元。

guestBioOfficial.en: Evan Spiegel, the co-founder and CEO of Snap, is one of the very few people in the world who has successfully built and scaled a lasting consumer social product. Snapchat has nearly 1 billion MAUs, and Evan and his team invented some of the most important consumer products and features, including Stories, AR glasses, swipe-based navigation, the camera as the primary UX, and a lot more. *In our in-depth conversation, we discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: Snap的联合创始人兼CEO埃文·斯皮格尔是世界上为数不多成功打造并扩展持久消费级社交产品的人之一。Snapchat拥有近10亿月活用户，埃文及其团队发明了许多重要的消费级产品和功能，包括Stories、AR眼镜、滑动式导航、以摄像头为核心的用户体验等。在我们的深度对话中，我们将探讨：

summary.en: Evan argues the hardest part of consumer products isn't product-market fit but distribution, and that Snap's relentless innovation (Stories, AR glasses, swipe navigation) comes from a deliberately tiny design team that presents work on day one. He reflects on 15 years of being copied by the industry and why 'software is not a moat'—a lesson the AI world is now rediscovering. Framing the year as a 'crucible moment,' he stresses that humanity, not technology, dictates adoption, and warns of major societal pushback against careless AI deployment.
summary.zh: Evan 认为消费品最难的部分不是产品市场契合，而是分发；Snap 持续不断的创新（Stories、AR 眼镜、滑动导航）来自一支刻意保持精简、入职第一天就要展示作品的设计团队。他回顾了 15 年来被全行业抄袭的经历，以及为何“软件不是护城河”——这正是如今 AI 界正在重新学到的教训。他把这一年称为“熔炉时刻”，强调决定技术能否被采用的终究是人，而非技术本身，并警示对草率部署 AI 将会出现巨大的社会反弹。

episodeTitle.en: How Anthropic’s product team moves faster than anyone else | Cat Wu (Head of Product, Claude Code)
episodeTitle.zh: Anthropic产品团队如何比任何人都更快行动 | 吴佳佳（Cat Wu，产品负责人）

bio.en: Cat Wu is Head of Product for Claude Code and Cowork at Anthropic, at the center of how AI is changing the way products are built.
bio.zh: Cat Wu 是 Anthropic 的 Claude Code 与 Cowork 产品负责人，正处于 AI 改变产品构建方式的核心。

guestBioOfficial.en: Cat Wu is Head of Product for Claude Code and Cowork at Anthropic, building one of the most important AI products of this generation. Before joining Anthropic, Cat spent years as an engineer and briefly worked in VC. Today, she’s interviewing hundreds of product managers who are trying to break into AI—and seeing firsthand what separates those who thrive from those who fall behind. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh:
吴佳佳（Cat Wu）是Anthropic公司Claude Code和Cowork部门的产品负责人，致力于打造这一代最重要的AI产品。在加入Anthropic之前，吴佳佳曾担任工程师多年，还曾短暂涉足风险投资领域。如今，她正在采访数百名试图进军AI领域的产品经理，亲眼见证了哪些人能在行业中脱颖而出，哪些人会被淘汰。  
*我们将探讨：*

summary.en: Cat argues the hardest part isn't building for a future superintelligent model but eliciting maximum capability from today's models, and that shipping timelines at Anthropic have collapsed from six months to as little as a day. She says the PM role is changing fast—what matters most now is product taste, since code is cheap and deciding what to build is the scarce skill. The conversation covers what emerging PM skills look like in an AI-native world.
summary.zh: Cat 认为，难点不在于为未来的超级智能模型构建，而在于从今天的模型中“逼出”最大能力，且 Anthropic 的功能交付周期已从六个月缩短到最短一天。她说 PM 角色正快速变化——如今最重要的是产品品味，因为代码廉价，而“决定造什么”才是稀缺技能。对话涵盖了在 AI 原生世界里新兴 PM 技能的样子。

episodeTitle.en: Why half of product managers are in trouble | Nikhyl Singhal (Meta, Google)
episodeTitle.zh: 为何半数产品经理深陷困境 | 尼克尔·辛格尔（Meta、Google）

bio.en: Nikhyl Singhal is a veteran product executive who spent years at Meta and Google, served as CPO of Credit Karma, founded four companies, and now leads the leading communities for heads of product (Skip).
bio.zh: Nikhyl Singhal 是一位资深产品高管，曾长期任职于 Meta 和 Google，担任过 Credit Karma 的 CPO，是四家公司的创始人，如今运营着面向产品负责人与 CPO 的顶尖社区 Skip。

guestBioOfficial.en: Nikhyl Singhal is the founder of The Skip, a community for senior product leaders; a former product exec at Meta, Google, and Credit Karma; and a many-time founder. He’s also one of the most honest, unfiltered voices on what’s actually happening in product management right now. *In our in-depth conversation, we discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 尼基尔·辛格尔（Nikhyl Singhal）是资深产品领导者社区The Skip的创始人，也是Meta、谷歌和Credit Karma的前产品高管，还是一位多次创业的成功人士。他还是当下产品管理领域最真诚、最直言不讳的发声者之一。在本次深度对谈中，我们将探讨：

summary.en: Nikhyl argues that AI is radically reshaping product management, with information-movers being displaced by builders who can ship quickly. He predicts a near-term wave of layoffs followed by rehiring of AI-first talent, and stresses that PMs must develop judgment, pace, and hands-on building skills to stay relevant. The episode reframes career advice around becoming a builder rather than a coordinator.
summary.zh: Nikhyl 认为，在 AI 的冲击下，产品管理的角色正在被彻底重塑，单纯传递信息的“信息搬运工”将被能够亲手快速构建产品的“建造者”取代。他预测短期内会出现大规模裁员，随后企业会以 AI 优先的方式重新招人，并强调产品经理必须培养判断力、节奏感和动手构建的能力才能保持竞争力。本期将职业建议重新定义为：成为建造者，而非协调者。

episodeTitle.en: Hard truths about building in the AI era | Keith Rabois (Khosla Ventures)
episodeTitle.zh: 关于AI时代构建的硬道理 | 基思·拉博伊斯（Khosla Ventures）

bio.en: Keith Rabois is a veteran operator and investor, part of the PayPal Mafia, and an early backer of Stripe, Palantir, Airbnb, YouTube, DoorDash, Ramp, and many others.
bio.zh: 基思·拉博伊斯（Keith Rabois）是一位资深运营者与投资人，属于"PayPal 黑帮"成员，并早期投资了 Stripe、Palantir、Airbnb、YouTube、DoorDash、Ramp 等数十家公司。

guestBioOfficial.en: Keith Rabois was an early executive at PayPal (part of the famous PayPal Mafia), COO at Square, VP of Corporate Development at LinkedIn, and an early investor in Stripe, DoorDash, Airbnb, YouTube, Ramp, and Palantir. Currently he’s managing director at Khosla Ventures. Also, he hasn’t touched a computer since September 2010 (he does everything from an iPad). *In our in-depth conversation, Keith shares:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 基思·拉博伊斯曾是PayPal（属于著名的"PayPal黑手党"）的早期高管、Square的COO、LinkedIn的企业发展副总裁，也是Stripe、DoorDash、Airbnb、YouTube、Ramp和Palantir的早期投资者。目前，他是Khosla Ventures的董事总经理。此外，他自2010年9月以来就再也没有碰过电脑了（他现在用iPad处理所有事务）。在我们的深度对话中，基思将分享：

summary.en: Keith shares contrarian takes, including that the traditional product manager role makes less sense as AI handles more building and that founders should rarely talk to customers directly. He argues the modern PM skill is increasingly CEO-like - defining what to build and why. The episode is full of sharp, provocative views on talent, org design, and leveraging AI.
summary.zh: 基思分享了许多反共识观点，包括：随着 AI 承担更多构建工作，传统的产品经理角色意义变小；创始人不应亲自去和用户交谈。他认为，现代 PM 的技能越来越像 CEO——定义要构建什么以及为什么。本期充满关于人才、组织设计与运用 AI 的犀利而具挑衅性的见解。

episodeTitle.en: Head of Growth (Anthropic): Anthropic is automating its own growth
episodeTitle.zh: 增长负责人（Anthropic）：Anthropic正在自动化自身的增长

bio.en: Amol Avasare is Head of Growth at Anthropic, which grew from $1 billion to over $19 billion in annual recurring revenue in roughly 14 months—one of the fastest growth runs in history.
bio.zh: Amol Avasare 是 Anthropic 的增长负责人，该公司在约 14 个月内将年度经常性收入从 10 亿美元增长到超过 190 亿美元，是史上增长最快的纪录之一。

guestBioOfficial.en: Amol Avasare is Head of Growth at Anthropic, which is going through the most unprecedented growth trajectory in history—scaling from $1 billion to over $19 billion in ARR in just 14 months. Previously, Amol worked on the growth teams at Mercury and MasterClass. Before that he was a founder, and he cold emailed his way into the Anthropic role when no job listing existed. Most remarkably, he overcame a traumatic brain injury from a Muay Thai match that meant he couldn't work for nearly a year. *In our in-depth discussion, Amol shares:*
guestBioOfficial.zh:
阿莫尔·阿瓦萨雷（Amol Avasare）是Anthropic公司的增长部门主管，该公司正经历着史无前例的增长轨迹——在短短14个月内，其年度经常性收入（ARR）从10亿美元攀升至超过19亿美元。此前，他曾在Mercury和MasterClass的增长团队工作。在此之前，他还是一位创始人，在没有职位招聘信息的情况下通过冷邮件成功获得了Anthropic的职位。最引人注目的是，他克服了泰拳比赛导致的创伤性脑损伤，这场伤病使他近一年无法工作。

在我们的深度对谈中，阿莫尔分享了：

summary.en: Amol describes the unique challenge of leading growth inside Anthropic, where much past playbook knowledge no longer applies and activation is a core hurdle. He shares clever growth moves like importing memory from ChatGPT and an internal effort called CASH (Claude Accelerate Sustainable Hypergrowth) to automate growth experimentation with Claude. The conversation covers why linear charts have given way to log-linear thinking and how the product's value may be 1000x greater within two years.
summary.zh: Amol 描述了在 Anthropic 领导增长的独特挑战——过去大量的增长方法论不再适用，而激活是核心难题。他分享了诸如“从 ChatGPT 导入记忆”等巧妙的增长动作，以及一个名为 CASH（Claude 加速可持续超增长）的内部项目，用 Claude 自动化增长实验。对话还涵盖为何线性图表已被对数线性思维取代，以及产品价值可能在两年内提升 1000 倍。

episodeTitle.en: An AI state of the union: We’ve passed the inflection point & dark factories are coming
episodeTitle.zh: 《AI现状报告：我们已越过临界点，暗工厂即将来临》

bio.en: Simon Willison is a renowned engineer and one of the most useful voices on how AI is changing software and knowledge work; he co-created Django, coined 'prompt injection,' popularized 'AI slop' and 'agentic engineering,' and maintains 100+ open-source projects.
bio.zh: Simon Willison 是一位知名的工程师，也是关于“AI 如何改变软件与知识工作”最具实用价值的声音之一；他共同创造了 Django 框架、提出了“提示注入（prompt injection）”一词、普及了“AI slop”与“智能体工程（agentic engineering）”，并维护着 100 多个开源项目。

guestBioOfficial.en: Simon Willison is a prolific independent software developer, a blogger, and one of the most visible and trusted voices on the impact AI is having on builders. He co-created Django, the web framework that powers Instagram, Pinterest, and tens of thousands of other websites. He coined the term “prompt injection,” popularized the terms “AI slop” and “agentic engineering,” and has built over 100 open source projects, including Datasette, a data analysis tool used by investigative journalists worldwide. What makes Simon unique is that he’s made the leap from traditional software engineering to AI-native development more fully and visibly than almost anyone—and he’s been documenting everything he learns in real time on his blog, SimonWillison.net. *In our in-depth conversation, Simon shares:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 西蒙·威利森（Simon Willison）是一位多产的独立软件开发者、博主，也是AI对开发者影响方面最具影响力和公信力的声音之一。他共同创建了Django框架，该框架为Instagram、Pinterest等数万个网站提供支持。他创造了“提示注入”一词，推广了“AI糊状物”和“代理式工程”等术语，并开发了100多个开源项目，包括Datasette——全球调查记者使用的数据分析工具。西蒙的独特之处在于，他比几乎任何人都更彻底、更明显地从传统软件工程跨越到AI原生开发——并在自己的博客SimonWillison.net上实时记录所学内容。在我们的深度对话中，西蒙分享了：

summary.en: Simon shares a pragmatic, builder's view of the AI shift, emphasizing that the real unlock is using LLMs as tools in your own workflow rather than waiting for magic. He discusses local and open models, the rise of AI agents, and why data and UX still decide whether an AI product actually works. The conversation is grounded, skeptical in the best way, and full of concrete habits for engineers and knowledge workers.
summary.zh: Simon 分享了对 AI 变革的、务实的“构建者视角”，强调真正的突破口是把大语言模型当作自己工作流中的工具来用，而非坐等魔法降临。他讨论了本地与开源模型、AI 智能体的兴起，以及为何数据与用户体验仍决定一款 AI 产品是否真的好用。对话立足现实、以最佳方式保持怀疑，并充满了面向工程师与知识工作者的具体习惯。

episodeTitle.en: From skeptic to true believer: How OpenClaw changed my life | Claire Vo
episodeTitle.zh: 从怀疑者到忠实信徒：OpenClaw如何改变我的生活 | 克莱尔·沃

bio.en: Claire Vo is a three-time chief product officer (Color, Optimizely, LaunchDarkly) and creator of ChatPRD, likely the most-used PM-specific AI product, which she builds nights and weekends.
bio.zh: Claire Vo 是三度首席产品官（Color、Optimizely、LaunchDarkly），也是 ChatPRD 的创造者——这大概是使用最广的 PM 专用 AI 产品，由她在业余时间打造。

guestBioOfficial.en: Claire Vo is the host of our sister podcast, “How I AI,” a former product executive and engineer, and founder of an AI startup called ChatPRD. Claire now runs her business, podcast, and family life with the help of nine OpenClaw agents running on multiple Mac Minis and old laptops. In this episode, Claire shares her journey from OpenClaw skeptic (it deleted her family calendar the first time she tried it) to true believer, and gives a masterclass in using AI agents in real life. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 克莱尔·沃是我们姊妹播客《How I AI》的主持人，曾任产品高管和工程师，也是AI初创公司ChatPRD的创始人。如今，她借助九台OpenClaw智能助手，在多台Mac Mini和旧笔记本电脑上运营业务、主持播客并打理家庭生活。在本期节目中，克莱尔分享了自己从OpenClaw怀疑者（首次尝试时删掉了家庭日历）到忠实信徒的转变历程，并传授如何在现实生活中运用AI助手的秘籍。*我们将探讨：*

summary.en: Claire discusses which PM skills AI will complement or replace, the story behind ChatPRD, and how to stay ahead of the curve on AI within the PM role. She emphasizes retaining agency over your career and “bending the arc” toward what you want, plus insights on being a successful woman in tech and the rise of the combined CPTO role. The conversation is rich with career advice for both early and senior product people.
summary.zh: Claire 讨论了哪些 PM 技能会被 AI 补充或替代、ChatPRD 背后的故事，以及如何在 PM 角色中保持对 AI 的领先。她强调要对职业生涯保留“主动权”并“扭转弧线”朝向自己想要的方向，以及身为科技行业成功女性、CPTO 角色崛起的洞见。对话富含对早期与资深产品人的职业建议。

episodeTitle.en: The art of influence: The single most important skill left that AI can’t replace | Jessica Fain
episodeTitle.zh: 影响力的艺术：AI无法替代的关键技能 | 杰西卡·费恩（Jessica Fain）

bio.en: Jessica Fain is a product leader who has held roles at Box, Slack, Brightwheel, and now Webflow, and who has become uniquely skilled at the art and science of influencing executives—arguably the highest-leverage skill for product leaders.
bio.zh: Jessica Fain 是一位产品负责人，曾在 Box、Slack、Brightwheel 任职，如今在 Webflow，她在“影响高管”这门艺术与科学上练就了独到的功力——这可以说是产品领导者杠杆率最高的技能。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jessica Fain is a product leader at Webflow and former Chief of Staff to the CPO at Slack, where she worked alongside April Underwood and many past podcast guests including Stewart Butterfield, Annie Pearl, Tamar Yehoshua, and Noah Weiss. She’s spent her career learning how executives actually make decisions—and why most people completely misunderstand the process. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 杰西卡·费恩（Jessica Fain）是Webflow的产品负责人，曾任Slack首席产品官的幕僚长。她与安普尔·安德伍德（April Underwood）及多位往期播客嘉宾（包括斯图尔特·巴特菲尔德（Stewart Butterfield）、安妮·珀尔（Annie Pearl）、塔玛·耶霍舒亚（Tamar Yehoshua）和诺亚·韦斯（Noah Weiss））共事。她职业生涯致力于研究高管决策机制，并揭示多数人对此的误解。*我们讨论了：*

summary.en: Jessica argues that when PMs talk to executives they inexplicably drop the curiosity and empathy they use with users—yet influence is the highest-leverage skill after AI. She explains how executives actually make decisions (picture a strobe light of urgent demands), why you must connect your pitch to their goals and metrics, how asking 'what is the board pushing you on?' builds trust, and why killing and deprioritizing work signals senior leadership. The episode gets tactically deep on how to change minds and the mistakes people make trying to influence up.
summary.zh: Jessica 指出，PM 一和 executives 谈话，就会莫名其妙地丢掉面对用户时的好奇心与同理心——然而影响力是仅次于 AI 的、杠杆率最高的技能。她解释了高管究竟如何做决策（想象一盏不断闪烁的紧急事项信号灯）、为何你必须把自己的提案与他们的目标和指标相连、问“董事会在逼你做什么？”如何建立信任，以及为何砍掉和降优先级的工作反而彰显资深领导力。这期节目就“如何改变他人想法”以及向上管理时常犯的错误给出了极具战术深度的内容。

episodeTitle.en: He's negotiated $1B+ in executive compensation. Here's his playbook. | Jacob Warwick
episodeTitle.zh: 他谈判了超过10亿美元的高管薪酬。这是他的谈判秘籍。| 雅各布·沃里克

bio.en: Jacob Warwick is a professional negotiator who works behind the scenes with senior tech execs, pro athletes, and celebrities to navigate complex comp, M&A, and enterprise-sales negotiations, having helped clients secure over $1 billion in additional compensation.
bio.zh: Jacob Warwick 是一位职业谈判专家，在幕后为科技高管、职业运动员和名人处理复杂的薪酬、并购与企业销售谈判，已帮助客户额外争取到超 10 亿美元的补偿。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jacob Warwick is an executive negotiation coach who helps senior operators negotiate better salary, equity, titles, and severance packages. He has worked with leaders across tech and Hollywood, was previously a founder and CEO himself, and has helped clients secure millions in additional compensation. His approach focuses on collaboration over confrontation, understanding motivations, and treating job searches like enterprise sales processes. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 雅各布·沃里克是一位高管谈判教练，帮助高级运营者更好地协商薪资、股权、职位和离职补偿。他曾与科技和好莱坞领域的领导者合作，曾亲自担任创始人兼CEO，并帮助客户成功获得数百万美元额外薪酬。他的方法侧重于合作而非对抗，理解动机，并将求职视为企业销售流程。*我们讨论：*

summary.en: Jacob gets tactical about comp negotiation: never do it over email (you can't control tone, and context like an annoyed CEO in an airport line can poison it), and lead with the value you'll create, not just demands. He covers who should speak first when comp comes up, the costly mistakes people unknowingly make, and how to ask for more without seeming greedy ('What's the chance there could be a little more?'). The episode is a rare, under-the-radar masterclass in the psychology and mechanics of getting paid what you're worth.
summary.zh: Jacob 就薪酬谈判给出具体战法：绝不用邮件谈（你无法控制语气，而像机场排队中正恼火的 CEO 这样的语境会毁掉谈判），并应先讲你将创造的价值，而非只提要求。他讲到了薪酬话题出现时该谁先开口、人们不知不觉犯下的昂贵错误，以及如何在不显得贪婪的前提下要求加薪（“有没有可能稍微多一点点？”）。这期节目是一场地地道道、鲜为人知的、关于“如何拿到与你价值匹配报酬”的心理与技巧的公开课。

episodeTitle.en: A behind-the-scenes interview with Lenny Rachitsky on building his newsletter and podcast
episodeTitle.zh: Lenny Rachitsky关于如何打造新闻通讯和播客的幕后访谈

bio.en: Michelle Rial is a writer, illustrator, and data journalist whose newsletter grew past a million subscribers, and author of books like Am I Overthinking This?
bio.zh: 米歇尔·里尔（Michelle Rial）是一位作家、插画师与数据新闻工作者，她的新闻通讯订阅者超过百万，并著有《我是不是想太多了？》（Am I Overthinking This?）等书。

guestBioOfficial.en: People have been asking me to sit on the other side of the mic for a long time. With my wife’s debut children’s book, Charts for Babies, coming out next month, we figured: why not do it together? What followed was one of the most honest conversations I’ve had on this podcast. Michelle asked things no one else would think to ask—and many things I’ve never shared publicly. You’ll hear about the specific moments that pushed me to start the newsletter, how I think about quality and iteration, what most stresses me out, and the scariest moment of my life. This was so fun, and so special, and I hope you like it. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh:
很久以来，人们一直邀请我坐到麦克风的另一边。随着我妻子创作的儿童读物《宝宝图表》下个月出版，我们想：何不一起做呢？接下来的，是我在这个播客上进行过的最坦诚的对话之一。米歇尔问了一些别人想不到的问题——还有许多我从未公开分享过的内容。你会听到那些促使我创办新闻通讯的具体时刻，我如何看待质量和迭代，最让我焦虑的事情，以及我生命中最可怕的时刻。这次访谈非常有趣，也很特别，希望你们会喜欢。  
*我们讨论了：*

summary.en: Michelle describes the surreal moment she received the message "I have wisdom to share" that launched her newsletter, now over a million subscribers. She talks about turning anxiety and overthinking into accessible, illustrated essays. The episode is a warm, creative conversation about building an audience by being genuinely yourself.
summary.zh: 米歇尔描述了她收到"我有智慧要分享"这一讯息、从而开启新闻通讯的奇妙时刻——如今订阅已超百万。她谈到如何把焦虑与过度思考变成易懂的插图随笔。本期是一场温暖的创意对话，关于如何以真实的自己做大受众。

episodeTitle.en: The real AI revolution isn’t software. It’s farms, mines, and trucks. | Qasar Younis
episodeTitle.zh: 真正的AI革命并非软件，而是农场、矿山和卡车。| Qasar Younis

bio.en: Qasar Younis is co-founder and CEO of Applied Intuition, a ~$15 billion company that adds AI to vehicles, mining rigs, construction equipment, and more, and is one of the most important under-the-radar AI companies in the world.
bio.zh: Qasar Younis 是 Applied Intuition 的联合创始人兼 CEO，这家估值约 150 亿美元的公司将 AI 应用于汽车、采矿设备、工程机械等领域，是全球最重要却低调隐秘的 AI 公司之一。

guestBioOfficial.en: Qasar Younis is the co-founder and CEO of Applied Intuition, a $15 billion AI company that adds intelligence to cars, tractors, planes, submarines, and other vehicles—essentially, Tesla or Waymo without the hardware. He was previously COO of Y Combinator, started his career as an engineer at GM and Bosch, and was born on a farm in Pakistan. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: Qasar Younis是Applied Intuition的联合创始人兼首席执行官，这家估值150亿美元的AI公司为汽车、拖拉机、飞机、潜艇等车辆增添智能——本质上就是没有硬件的特斯拉或Waymo。他曾担任Y Combinator的首席运营官，职业生涯始于通用汽车和博世的工程师，并出生于巴基斯坦的一个农场。*我们讨论了：*

summary.en: Qasar frames the AI and physical-AI revolution as akin to the Industrial Revolution, with the biggest near-term impact in farming, mining, construction, and self-driving trucks rather than consumer software. He argues that fear of AI stems from misunderstanding, and that the best antidote is to learn the technology and apply it for good. The conversation also covers why self-driving cars are fundamentally robots, and why autonomy can't arrive soon enough for aging workforces.
summary.zh: Qasar 将 AI 与“物理 AI”革命类比为工业革命，认为其近期最大影响将出现在农业、采矿、建筑和自动驾驶卡车，而非消费级软件。他指出对 AI 的恐惧源于误解，而最好的解药就是去学习这项技术并把它用于善处。对话还探讨了为什么自动驾驶汽车本质上就是机器人，以及为什么对于日益老龄化的劳动力来说，自动化来得再快也不为过。

episodeTitle.en: The design process is dead. Here’s what’s replacing it. | Jenny Wen (head of design at Claude)
episodeTitle.zh: 设计流程已死。以下是取代它的东西。 | 温佳妮（Claude设计负责人）

bio.en: Jenny Wen leads design for Claude Cowork at Anthropic, and was previously director of design at Figma (leading the FigJam and Slides teams) and a designer at Dropbox, Square, and Shopify; she offers a glimpse of where the design profession is heading.
bio.zh: Jenny Wen 在 Anthropic 领导 Claude Cowork 的设计，此前是 Figma 的设计总监（领导 FigJam 和 Slides 团队），并在 Dropbox、Square 和 Shopify 担任设计师；她向我们展示了设计职业正走向何方。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jenny Wen leads design for Claude at Anthropic. Prior to this, she was Director of Design at Figma, where she led the teams behind FigJam and Slides. Before that, she was a designer at Dropbox, Square, and Shopify. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 温佳妮在Anthropic领导Claude的设计工作。此前，她在Figma担任设计总监，领导了FigJam和Slides团队。在此之前，她曾在Dropbox、Square和Shopify担任设计师。*我们讨论了：*

summary.en: Jenny argues the old design-process gospel is dead: with AI, designers no longer have time to make beautiful mocks (prototyping has dropped from 60–70% to 30–40% of the role), and the job is now helping engineers and teams execute. Design visions have compressed from multi-year decks to three-to-six-month prototypes, and even engineers struggle to keep up with their own agents. She shares what she now looks for when hiring (three emerging designer archetypes) and where human judgment, taste, and accountability still matter most. It's a wild, practical look at the near future of design.
summary.zh: Jenny 主张旧的设计流程“圣经”已死：在 AI 时代，设计师不再有时间为每个方案做精美 mock（原型工作从占角色的 60%–70% 降到 30%–40%），工作变成了帮助工程师和团队去执行。设计愿景也从多年期的精美 deck 压缩成三到六个月的原型，连工程师都难以跟上自己那一堆智能体的节奏。她分享了如今招聘设计师时看重的点（三种新兴设计师画像），以及人类的判断、品味与责任在哪里依然最关键。这期节目是对设计近未来一次大胆又务实的窥探。

episodeTitle.en: AI is critical for humanity’s survival: Cisco President on the AI revolution | Jeetu Patel
episodeTitle.zh: AI对人类生存至关重要：思科总裁谈AI革命 | 吉图·帕特尔

bio.en: Jeetu Patel is Chief Product Officer and President at Cisco, where he has led a remarkable internal transformation to make a traditionally slow enterprise giant operate in an AI-first way.
bio.zh: Jeetu Patel 是 Cisco 的首席产品官兼总裁，他在内部推动了一场显著的转型，让这家传统上偏慢的企业巨头以“AI 优先”的方式运作。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jeetu Patel is the president and chief product officer at Cisco, where he leads a team of 30,000 people and is playing a central role in the massive AI infrastructure buildout happening right now. Previously, he spent five years as CPO at Box and 17 years running his own startup. Recently Jeetu organized an AI summit featuring industry leaders like Jensen Huang, Sam Altman, Marc Andreessen, and Fei-Fei Li. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 吉图·帕特尔是思科的总裁兼首席产品官，领导着30,000人的团队，在当前大规模AI基础设施建设中发挥着核心作用。此前，他在Box担任了五年CPO，并经营了自己的创业公司17年。最近，吉图组织了一场AI峰会，邀请了詹森·黄、山姆·奥尔特曼、马克·安德森和李飞飞等行业领袖。*我们讨论：*

summary.en: Jeetu argues AI is a megatrend, not a hype cycle—one of the most foundational movements in human history—and that survival (think falling birth rates and caring for aging populations) may depend on successful AI. He shares how he's turning Cisco AI-first, why you should 'fast-forward six months' to prepare for the world to come, and why he rejects the 'praise in public, criticize in private' rule in favor of enough trust to debate in public. He also stresses that stamina trumps intellect—you can't teach hunger, curiosity, and persistence. The episode is a masterclass in leading change at enterprise scale.
summary.zh: Jeetu 主张 AI 是“大趋势”而非炒作周期——是人类历史上最具基础性的运动之一，并认为人类存续（想想下降的出生率与照护老龄人口）可能取决于 AI 的成功。他分享了如何把 Cisco 转型为 AI 优先、为何要“快进六个月”为未来的世界做准备，以及他为何反对“公开表扬、私下批评”、主张建立足够信任以公开辩论。他还强调“耐力胜过智力”——饥饿感、好奇心与毅力无法被教会。这期节目是关于在企业规模上领导变革的公开课。

episodeTitle.en: Head of Claude Code: What happens after coding is solved | Boris Cherny
episodeTitle.zh: Claude Code负责人：编码问题解决后的挑战 | 鲍里斯·切尔尼

bio.en: Boris Cherny is Head of Claude Code at Anthropic, whose tool has transformed how software engineers work and become a major driver of Anthropic's growth.
bio.zh: Boris Cherny 是 Anthropic 的 Claude Code 负责人，该工具彻底改变了软件工程师的工作方式，也成为 Anthropic 增长的重要驱动力。

guestBioOfficial.en: Boris Cherny is the creator and head of Claude Code at Anthropic. What began as a simple terminal-based prototype just a year ago has transformed the role of software engineering and is increasingly transforming all professional work. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 鲍里斯·切尔尼是Anthropic公司的创始人兼Claude Code负责人。在一年前还是一个简单的终端原型时，Claude Code已经改变了软件工程的角色，并正日益改变所有专业工作。 *我们讨论：*

summary.en: Boris reveals he hasn't hand-edited a single line of code since November, shipping 10–30 pull requests a day with multiple agents running, and estimates engineer productivity is up ~200%. He argues coding is “virtually solved” and that soon everyone will both code and be a product manager, with the title “software engineer” giving way to “builder.” The conversation covers why taste and product sense—not implementation—are becoming the scarce, valuable skill.
summary.zh: Boris 透露自去年 11 月起他没手动改过一行代码，每天靠多个智能体运行提交 10–30 个 PR，并估计工程师生产力提升了约 200%。他认为编程已“基本被解决”，很快人人都会既写代码又当产品经理，“软件工程师”头衔将让位于“构建者”。对话涵盖为何品味与产品感——而非实现——正成为稀缺而有价值的技能。

episodeTitle.en: OpenAI’s head of platform engineering on the next 12-24 months of AI | Sherwin Wu
episodeTitle.zh: OpenAI平台工程主管谈未来12-24个月AI发展 | 吴胜文

bio.en: Sherwin Wu is Head of Engineering for OpenAI's API and Developer Platform, giving him a uniquely broad view into the AI startup ecosystem since nearly every AI company integrates with OpenAI's APIs.
bio.zh: Sherwin Wu 是 OpenAI API 与开发者平台工程负责人，由于几乎每一家 AI 公司都接入 OpenAI 的 API，这让他对 AI 创业生态拥有极其独特而广博的视野。

guestBioOfficial.en: Sherwin Wu leads engineering for OpenAI’s API platform, where roughly 95% of engineers use Codex, often working with fleets of 10 to 20 parallel AI agents. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 吴胜文（Sherwin Wu）负责OpenAI API平台的工程工作，该平台约95%的工程师使用Codex，通常同时运行10到20个并行AI代理。*我们讨论了：*

summary.en: Sherwin discusses what he sees across the thousands of teams building on OpenAI's APIs, from common architectural patterns to the mistakes that sink AI products. He shares how developers should think about evaluation, reliability, and cost as models and agents become more capable, and where the platform is heading. The episode is a rare, behind-the-API look at the state and future of AI application development.
summary.zh: Sherwin 讨论了他在数千支基于 OpenAI API 构建的团队中所观察到的现象，从常见的架构模式，到拖垮 AI 产品的那些错误。他分享了随着模型与智能体能力增强，开发者应如何思考评估、可靠性与成本，以及平台的前进方向。本期是一份难得的、API 背后的 AI 应用开发现状与未来透视。

episodeTitle.en: The rise of the professional vibe coder (a new AI-era job)
episodeTitle.zh: 专业编程代码员的崛起（AI时代的新兴职业）

bio.en: Lazar Jovanovic is the first official "vibe coding" engineer at Lovable, having built his role in public by shipping projects and teaching others to code with AI.
bio.zh: 拉扎尔·约万诺维奇（Lazar Jovanovic）是 Lovable 公司首位正式的"氛围编程"（vibe coding）工程师，他通过在公开场合持续构建项目、教他人用 AI 编程，把自己做成了这份工作。

guestBioOfficial.en: Lazar Jovanovic is a full-time professional vibe coder at Lovable. His job is to build both internal tools and customer-facing products purely using AI, while not having a coding background. In this conversation, he breaks down the tactics, workflows, and framework that let him ship production-quality products using only AI. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 拉扎尔·约万诺维奇（Lazar Jovanovic）是Lovable公司的全职专业编程代码员。他的工作是仅通过AI技术构建内部工具和面向客户的产品，尽管他没有编程背景。在本期对话中，他将详细解析如何仅通过AI技术就能交付生产级别的产品所运用的策略、工作流程和框架。*我们将探讨：*

summary.en: Lazar explains that "vibe coding" became a real job by building in public, and that you can effectively hire yourself as a professional vibe coder without waiting for a company. He predicts traditional coding will become rare and artisanal, like calligraphy. The episode captures how the boundaries between engineer, designer, and PM are converging around AI.
summary.zh: 拉扎尔解释说，"氛围编程"之所以成为一份真正的工作，靠的是在公开场合持续构建，而且你无需等公司雇佣，就可以把自己聘为专业的氛围程序员。他预测传统编程将变得稀有而像书法一样具有艺术性。本期展现了工程师、设计师与 PM 的边界如何围绕 AI 融合。

episodeTitle.en: A child psychologist’s guide to working with difficult adults | Dr. Becky Kennedy
episodeTitle.zh: 儿童心理学家指导如何与难相处的成年人共事 | 贝基·肯尼迪博士（Dr. Becky Kennedy）

bio.en: Dr. Becky Kennedy is a clinical psychologist, author, and CEO of Good Inside, one of the most popular parenting platforms, applying attachment and resilience science to both kids and adults at work.
bio.zh: Dr. Becky Kennedy 是一位临床心理学家、作家，也是热门育儿平台 Good Inside 的 CEO，将依恋与韧性科学应用于孩子以及职场中的成年人。

guestBioOfficial.en: Dr. Becky Kennedy is a clinical psychologist, the bestselling author of Good Inside, and the founder of a parenting platform used by millions. Known for her practical, psychology-based approach to parenting, Dr. Becky shares how the same principles that help parents raise resilient children can make you a much more effective leader. In this conversation, she breaks down why all human systems—whether families or companies—operate on the same fundamental principles, and how understanding these dynamics can make you more effective in every relationship. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 贝基·肯尼迪博士是一名临床心理学家、畅销书《内在善良》（Good Inside）的作者，也是拥有数百万用户的育儿平台的创始人。贝基以实用、基于心理学的育儿方法而闻名，她分享了帮助父母培养有韧性的孩子所需的相同原则如何能让你成为更高效的领导者。在对话中，她将剖析为什么所有人类系统——无论是家庭还是公司——都遵循相同的基本原则，以及理解这些动态如何能让你在每一段关系中更高效。*我们将探讨：*

summary.en: Dr. Becky argues most adults in corporate environments behave like “babies in disguise” because all humans need the same things: skills to manage internal difficulty, not just better behavior. She reframes resilience over happiness and separating behavior from identity (“good inside”), and clarifies that boundaries are what you'll do, requiring nothing from the other person. The conversation translates parenting wisdom into practical tools for healthier, more resilient workplaces.
summary.zh: Dr. Becky 认为企业环境中的多数成年人像“伪装成婴儿的成年人”，因为所有人都需要同样的东西：管理内在困境的技能，而非只是更好的行为。她把“韧性优于快乐”、行为与身份分离（“内在是好的”）重新框定，并澄清边界是“你会做什么”、无需对方配合。对话把育儿智慧转化为打造更健康、更有韧性职场的实用工具。

episodeTitle.en: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet
episodeTitle.zh: 马克·安德森：真正的AI热潮尚未真正开启

bio.en: Marc Andreessen is the co-founder of Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and co-author of the Mosaic browser, and one of the most influential venture capitalists and thinkers on technology and AI.
bio.zh: 马克·安德森（Marc Andreessen）是安德森·霍洛维茨（a16z）风投公司的联合创始人、Mosaic 浏览器的联合开发者，也是最具影响力的科技与 AI 风险投资人和思想者之一。

guestBioOfficial.en: Marc Andreessen is a founder, investor, and co-founder of Netscape, as well as co-founder of the venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). In this conversation, we dig into why we’re living through a unique and one of the most incredible times in history, and what comes next. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 马克·安德森是Netscape的创始人、投资者及联合创始人，也是风投公司安德森·霍洛维茨（a16z）的联合创始人。在本次对话中，我们深入探讨为何我们正生活在历史上最独特、最令人惊叹的时代，以及未来将何去何从。*我们将讨论：*

summary.en: Marc frames AI as a "philosopher's stone" that turns the world's most abundant resource - sand - into its rarest - thought. He argues AI arrives just in time to offset declining population growth and labor shortages. The episode explores how the most forward-leaning founders are reimagining companies where a single founder does almost everything.
summary.zh: 马克把 AI 比作"哲人石"——把世界上最丰富的资源（沙）转化为最稀有的资源（思想）。他认为 AI 来得正是时候，足以抵消人口下降与劳动力短缺。本期探讨了最前沿的创始人如何重新构想"一个人几乎包揽所有事"的公司。

episodeTitle.en: The surprising advice from a founder who built 2 unicorns | Jason Cohen (WP Engine)
episodeTitle.zh: 一位打造了两家独角兽企业的创始人给出的惊人建议 | 杰森·科恩（Jason Cohen，WP Engine）

bio.en: Jason Cohen is a four-time founder including two unicorns (one being WP Engine), a prolific writer on product and startups for over 20 years, and the author of the upcoming book Hidden Multipliers.
bio.zh: Jason Cohen 是一位四次创业、打造过两家独角兽（其中之一为 WP Engine）的创始人，二十多年来持续撰写关于产品与创业的文章，并即将出版新作《Hidden Multipliers》。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jason Cohen is a four-time founder (including two unicorns, one being WP Engine) and an investor in over 60 startups, and has been sharing his lessons on company building at A Smart Bear for nearly 20 years. In this episode, Jason shares his methodical five-step framework for diagnosing stalled growth—a problem that faces almost every team. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 杰森·科恩曾四次创业（包括两家独角兽企业WP Engine），是60多家初创企业的投资者，近20年来一直在A Smart Bear分享他关于公司建设的经验。在本期节目中，杰森分享了他诊断停滞增长的五步方法论——这一问题几乎困扰着每个团队。*我们探讨：*

summary.en: Jason lays out a crisp, actionable framework for diagnosing stalled growth: first check if customers are churning after all the effort to acquire them, then scrutinize pricing and positioning (too-low prices can signal 'not good enough' to big buyers), then assess which channels are saturated, and finally question whether you even need to grow. He reframes 'if you're not growing, you're dying' as often investor-driven pressure rather than gospel, and the episode leaves listeners with concrete levers to rekindle or accelerate growth.
summary.zh: Jason 给出了一套清晰、可执行的框架来诊断增长停滞：先检查客户是否在费尽心力获取后又流失，再审视定价与定位（定价过低反而会让大买家觉得“不够好”），接着评估哪些渠道已饱和，最后质疑“你是否真的需要增长”。他把“不增长就等死”重新定义为往往来自投资人的压力、而非金科玉律，让听众带着重新点燃或加速增长的具体抓手离开。

episodeTitle.en: How a Meta PM ships products without ever writing code | Zevi Arnovitz
episodeTitle.zh: Meta产品经理如何无需写代码就能交付产品 | 泽维·阿诺维茨

bio.en: Zevi Arnovitz is a PM at Meta (previously at Wix) who, despite having no technical background, learned to use Cursor and Claude Code to build real products entirely on his own.
bio.zh: Zevi Arnovitz 是 Meta 的产品经理（此前在 Wix），尽管没有技术背景，他却学会了用 Cursor 和 Claude Code 完全靠自己构建出真正的产品。

guestBioOfficial.en: Zevi Arnovitz is a product manager at Meta with no technical background who has figured out how to build and ship real products using AI. His engineering team at Meta asks him to teach them how he does what he does. In this episode, Zevi breaks down his complete AI workflow that allows non-technical people to build sophisticated products with Cursor. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 泽维·阿诺维茨是Meta的产品经理，虽无技术背景，却成功利用AI打造并交付真实产品。他的工程团队请他传授方法。在本期节目中，泽维将解析完整的AI工作流程，让非技术人员也能借助Cursor打造复杂产品。*我们将探讨：*

summary.en: Zevi shares his remarkably practical workflow for building real software as a non-technical PM, using AI coding tools like Cursor and Claude Code. He explains how he scopes, iterates, and ships products solo, and offers a copyable system any non-technical product person can adopt. The episode is an empowering, concrete demonstration that the AI tooling shift has rewritten what a PM without code can do.
summary.zh: Zevi 分享了他作为非技术型 PM、用 Cursor 和 Claude Code 这类 AI 编程工具构建真正软件的、异常务实的工作流。他解释了自己如何界定范围、迭代并独自交付产品，并给出了任何非技术产品人都可复制的系统。本期是一次赋能性的、具体的演示：AI 工具的变革已经重写了“没有代码的 PM”所能做到的事。

episodeTitle.en: How to show up in any room with a low heart rate: Silicon Valley’s missing etiquette playbook
episodeTitle.zh: 如何在任何场合保持冷静：硅谷缺失的社交礼仪指南

bio.en: Sam Lessin is a partner at Slow Ventures, former VP of Product at Facebook, and a two-time founder, who joined Lenny to talk about the surprisingly high-leverage skill of proper etiquette.
bio.zh: Sam Lessin 是 Slow Ventures 的合伙人、Facebook 前产品副总裁、两次创业者，他做客本期，聊的是一个出人意料却极具杠杆效应的技能：得体的社交礼仪。

guestBioOfficial.en: Sam Lessin is a partner at Slow Ventures, a former VP of Product at Facebook, and a two-time founder who’s now teaching etiquette to Silicon Valley’s founders. In this unconventional episode, Sam explains why proper etiquette has become a vital skill for founders in 2026—especially as technology becomes more central to society and trust becomes harder to build. His etiquette book and courses have become surprisingly popular, teaching founders how to “show up in a room with a low heart rate” and quickly build trust. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 山姆·莱辛（Sam Lessin）是Slow Ventures合伙人，曾任Facebook产品副总裁，也是两度创业的成功者，如今他正向硅谷创始人传授社交礼仪。在这期非传统播客中，山姆解释了为何在2026年，恰当的社交礼仪已成为创始人的关键技能——尤其是在科技日益成为社会核心、信任愈发难能可贵的背景下。他创作的礼仪书籍和课程意外走红，教会创始人如何“在任何场合保持冷静”。*我们将探讨：*

summary.en: Sam makes the case that etiquette is a practical skill for showing up in a room with a low heart rate - earning trust and influence without unnecessary friction. He walks through rules for introductions, being early, eye contact, handling late arrivals, and introducing partners, drawn from his book and classes. The episode is an unconventional but genuinely useful guide to the soft skills that quietly shape careers.
summary.zh: Sam 论证了礼仪是一种“以低心率姿态出现在任何场合”的实用技能——无需制造不必要的摩擦，就能赢得信任与影响力。他结合自己的书与课程，逐一讲解了介绍、守时、眼神接触、应对他人迟到、介绍伴侣等规则。本期是一份非传统却真正实用的指南，关乎那些悄悄塑造职业生涯的软技能。

episodeTitle.en: Why most AI products fail: Lessons from 50+ AI deployments at OpenAI, Google & Amazon
episodeTitle.zh: 《为何多数AI产品失败：OpenAI、谷歌和亚马逊50余次AI部署的经验教训》

bio.en: Aishwarya Naresh Reganti and Kiriti Badam are AI product leaders who co-authored a widely-read guest post arguing that building AI products is fundamentally different from building traditional software.
bio.zh: Aishwarya Naresh Reganti 与 Kiriti Badam 是 AI 产品负责人，他们合写了一篇广受关注的客座文章，论述构建 AI 产品与传统软件开发有本质区别。

guestBioOfficial.en: Aishwarya Naresh Reganti and Kiriti Badam have helped build and launch more than 50 enterprise AI products across companies like OpenAI, Google, Amazon, and Databricks. Based on these experiences, they’ve developed a small set of best practices for building and scaling successful AI products. The goal of this conversation is to save you and your team a lot of pain and suffering. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 阿什瓦尔雅·纳雷什·雷甘蒂（Aishwarya Naresh Reganti）和基里蒂·巴达姆（Kiriti Badam）曾在OpenAI、谷歌、亚马逊和Databricks等公司参与开发和推出50余款企业AI产品。基于这些经验，他们总结出了一套构建和扩展成功AI产品的实用方法。本次对话旨在为您和您的团队节省大量摸索成本。*我们将探讨：*

summary.en: They explain that AI products differ from non-AI products primarily through non-determinism—you can't perfectly predict user or model behavior—and the agency-versus-control trade-off when handing decisions to agents. Their advice is to build step-by-step, stay focused on the real problem rather than solution complexity, and establish feedback flywheels that improve over time. They also argue that leaders must get hands-on with AI, accept that their intuition may be wrong, and that “pain is the new moat” for companies learning to build in new areas.
summary.zh: 他们指出，AI 产品与非 AI 产品的核心差异在于“非确定性”——无法准确预测用户或模型的行为——以及在把决策权交给智能体时面临的“能动性 vs 控制”权衡。他们的建议是分步构建、始终聚焦真正的问题而非方案复杂度，并建立能持续改进的反馈飞轮。他们还认为领导者必须亲自上手使用 AI、接受自己的直觉可能出错，并提出了“痛苦即新的护城河”的观点。

episodeTitle.en: “I like being scared”: Molly Graham’s frameworks for rapid career growth | Molly Graham
episodeTitle.zh: “我喜欢被吓到”：莫莉·格雷厄姆的快速职业成长框架 | 莫莉·格雷厄姆

bio.en: Molly Graham is an operating executive who has worked with founder-CEOs like Mark Zuckerberg, Sheryl Sandberg, Larry Page, and Sergey Brin, and coined the "give away your Legos" framework.
bio.zh: 莫莉·格雷厄姆（Molly Graham）是一位运营高管，曾与马克·扎克伯格、谢丽尔·桑德伯格、拉里·佩奇、谢尔盖·布林等创始人型 CEO 共事，并首创了"交出你的乐高"（give away your Legos）框架。

guestBioOfficial.en: Molly Graham has worked for some of tech’s most effective leaders, including Mark Zuckerberg, Sheryl Sandberg, Chamath Palihapitiya, and Bret Taylor. Today she leads Glue Club, a community for leaders navigating rapid scale, growth, and change. She’s best known for her “Give away your Legos” framework and her collection of practical mental models for leading through hypergrowth. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 莫莉·格雷厄姆曾为马克·扎克伯格、谢丽尔·桑德伯格、查马斯·帕利哈皮蒂亚和布雷特·泰勒等科技界最具影响力的领导者工作过。如今，她领导着Glue Club——一个为应对快速扩张、增长和变革的领导者提供支持的社区。她最著名的作品是“Give away your Legos”框架，以及她为在超增长环境中领导团队而收集的实用思维模型。*我们讨论：*

summary.en: Molly argues that ~80% of company culture is defined by the founder's personality, and leaders must articulate and scale it deliberately. She introduces "giving away your Legos" - letting go of what you're good at to take on new challenges as the company grows. The episode also covers the J-curve versus stairs model of career risk and growth.
summary.zh: 莫莉认为，约 80% 的公司文化由创始人的个性决定，领导者必须有意识地去阐释并放大它。她提出"交出你的乐高"——在公司成长时，放下你擅长的事，去迎接新挑战。本期还涵盖了职业风险与成长的"J 曲线 vs 阶梯"模型。

episodeTitle.en: “I deliberately understaff every project” | Leadership lessons from Rippling’s $16B journey
episodeTitle.zh: “我故意让每个项目的人手不足” | 来自Rippling 160亿美元征程的领导力启示

bio.en: Matt MacInnis is the Chief Product Officer at Rippling, where he previously served as COO, and is known for his philosophy that extraordinary results require extraordinary effort.
bio.zh: 马特·麦金尼斯（Matt MacInnis）是 Rippling 的首席产品官，此前担任该公司 COO，以"非凡成果需要非凡投入"的理念而闻名。

guestBioOfficial.en: Matt MacInnis is the chief product officer and former longtime COO at Rippling, a unified workforce management platform valued at over $16 billion. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 马特·麦金尼斯是Rippling的首席产品官兼前长期首席运营官，Rippling是一家估值超过160亿美元的统一员工管理平台。*我们将讨论：*

summary.en: Matt argues you should deliberately understaff projects to avoid politics, cruft, and slowness that come with overstaffing. He insists the most selfish act is withholding feedback, because it optimizes for your own comfort at the team's expense. The episode is a demanding but energizing view of high-performance product culture.
summary.zh: 马特认为，应当刻意让项目"人手不足"，以避免过度配置带来的政治、冗余与迟缓。他坚持，最自私的行为就是隐瞒反馈，因为那是以团队为代价、优化自己的舒适。本期呈现了一种严苛却振奋人心的高绩效产品文化观。

episodeTitle.en: Why securing AI is harder than anyone expected and guardrails are failing | HackAPrompt CEO
episodeTitle.zh: 为何保障AI安全比任何人预期的都困难，防护措施为何失效 | HackAPrompt首席执行官

bio.en: Sander Schulhoff is a leading researcher in adversarial robustness and AI red-teaming - the art of getting AI systems to do things they shouldn't - who runs the field's first and largest AI red-teaming competition and partners with frontier labs.
bio.zh: Sander Schulhoff 是对抗鲁棒性与 AI 红队（让 AI 系统做出不该做之事的艺术）领域的顶尖研究者，他运营着该领域首个也是规模最大的 AI 红队竞赛，并与前沿 AI 实验室合作。

guestBioOfficial.en: Sander Schulhoff is an AI researcher specializing in AI security, prompt injection, and red teaming. He wrote the first comprehensive guide on prompt engineering and ran the first-ever prompt injection competition, working with top AI labs and companies. His dataset is now used by Fortune 500 companies to benchmark their AI systems security, he’s spent more time than anyone alive studying how attackers break AI systems, and what he’s found isn’t reassuring: the guardrails companies are buying don’t actually work, and we’ve been lucky we haven’t seen more harm so far, only because AI agents aren’t capable enough yet to do real damage. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 桑德·舒尔霍夫是一位专注于AI安全、提示注入和红队技术的研究员。他撰写了首份提示工程综合指南，并举办了首届提示注入竞赛，与顶尖AI实验室和公司合作。他的数据集现已被《财富》500强公司用于基准测试其AI系统安全性。他比任何在世的人都花费了更多时间研究攻击者如何攻破AI系统，而他的发现并不令人安心：公司购买的防护措施实际上并不奏效，我们至今尚未看到更多危害，仅仅是因为AI智能体尚未具备足够的能力造成的。*我们将探讨：*

summary.en: Sander delivers a serious, practical look at AI security: how attackers manipulate models into leaking data or taking harmful actions, and how defenders should harden their systems. He covers the rise of prompt injection, the importance of red-teaming before deployment, and what everyone building with LLMs needs to know to avoid catastrophic failures. The episode is a wake-up call on the real risks of deploying AI.
summary.zh: Sander 对 AI 安全给出了严肃而实用的审视：攻击者如何操纵模型泄露数据或采取有害行动，以及防御者应当如何加固系统。他涵盖了提示注入（prompt injection）的兴起、部署前红队测试的重要性，以及每个用 LLM 构建产品的人为避免灾难性失败所必需了解的知识。本期是对部署 AI 真实风险的一记警钟。

episodeTitle.en: Inside OpenAI: 2026 is the year of agents, AI’s biggest bottleneck, and why compute isn’t the issue
episodeTitle.zh: OpenAI内部视角：2026年是智能体之年，AI的最大瓶颈，以及为何计算资源不是问题

bio.en: Alexander Embiricos leads work on Codex, OpenAI's coding agent, and views it as the beginning of an AI software-engineering teammate.
bio.zh: Alexander Embiricos 负责 OpenAI 编程智能体 Codex 的相关工作，并将其视为 AI 软件工程“队友”的开端。

guestBioOfficial.en: Alexander Embiricos leads product on Codex, OpenAI’s powerful coding agent, which has grown 20x since August and now serves trillions of tokens weekly. Before joining OpenAI, Alexander spent five years building a pair programming product for engineers. He now works at the frontier of AI-led software development, building what he describes as a software engineering teammate—an AI agent designed to participate across the entire development lifecycle. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 亚历山大·恩比里科斯（Alexander Embiricos）负责OpenAI强大编码智能体Codex的产品，该产品自8月以来已增长20倍，目前每周处理数万亿个令牌。在加入OpenAI之前，亚历山大花了五年时间为工程师开发对程式设计的支持产品。如今，他在AI主导的软件开发前沿工作，打造了他所描述的软件工程团队伙伴——一个旨在参与整个开发生命周期的AI智能体。*我们将探讨：*

summary.en: Alex explains how Codex functions like a very smart intern that can be put on call for its own training and even writes much of the infrastructure code behind its training runs. He shares a striking example: the Sora Android app was built in 18 days and publicly launched 10 days later, becoming the number-one app in the store. The conversation covers OpenAI's goal of making Codex proactive, why writing code is the best way for models to use computers, and how the product team uses user feedback from Reddit to keep improving.
summary.zh: Alex 解释了 Codex 如何像一个非常聪明的实习生，可以被安排去“值班”维护自己的训练，甚至编写其训练运行背后的大量基础设施代码。他分享了一个惊人案例：Sora 的安卓应用仅用 18 天构建、10 天后公开发布，并成为应用商店排名第一的应用。对话还涵盖 OpenAI 让 Codex 变得“主动”的目标、为何代码是模型使用计算机的最佳方式，以及产品团队如何利用 Reddit 上的用户反馈持续改进。

episodeTitle.en: The $1B Al company training ChatGPT, Claude & Gemini on the path to responsible AGI | Edwin Chen
episodeTitle.zh: 价值100亿美元的AI公司训练ChatGPT、Claude和Gemini，踏上负责任的通用人工智能之路 | 陈宇轩

bio.en: Edwin Chen is the founder and CEO of Surge AI, the leading AI data company that powers training at every frontier AI lab and became the fastest company ever to reach $1 billion in revenue—bootstrapped, with under 100 people, and profitable from day one.
bio.zh: Edwin Chen 是 Surge AI 的创始人兼 CEO；Surge AI 是领先的 AI 数据公司，为每一家前沿 AI 实验室的训练提供支撑，并以最快速度在四年内依靠不到 100 人、零融资、自第一天起盈利的模式跻身十亿美元营收俱乐部。

guestBioOfficial.en: Edwin Chen is the founder and CEO of Surge AI, the company that teaches AI what’s good vs. what’s bad, powering frontier labs with elite data, environments, and evaluations. Surge surpassed $1 billion in revenue with under 100 employees last year, completely bootstrapped—the fastest company in history to reach this milestone. Before founding Surge, Edwin was a research scientist at Google, Facebook, and Twitter and studied mathematics, computer science, and linguistics at MIT. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh:
陈宇轩是Surge AI的创始人兼首席执行官。这家公司教会AI区分善恶，为前沿实验室提供精英数据、环境和评估。Surge去年营收超过10亿美元，员工不足100人，完全自力更生——这是史上最快达到这一里程碑的公司。在创立Surge之前，陈宇轩曾在谷歌、Facebook和Twitter担任研究科学家，并在麻省理工学院学习数学、计算机科学和语言学。  
*我们探讨：*

summary.en: Edwin explains why data quality—not just model architecture—is the real bottleneck in building great AI, and how Surge trains models on what 'good' actually means with a tiny, elite, bootstrapped team. He argues many labs are optimizing for engagement and 'AI slop' rather than truth and human progress, and warns against a Silicon Valley game that mistakes throwing bodies at problems for real capability. The conversation also covers how to choose the right model behavior, why values shape models, and what it takes to build an important company differently.
summary.zh: Edwin 阐释了为何数据质量（而非仅仅是模型架构）才是打造优秀 AI 的真正瓶颈，以及 Surge 如何用一支精悍、精英化、自筹资金的小团队来训练模型理解何为“好”。他认为许多实验室在优化“engagement”和“AI 垃圾内容”而非真相与人类进步，并警示那种以为“堆人”就能提升能力的硅谷游戏。对话还涉及如何选择正确的模型行为、价值观如何塑造模型，以及以不同方式打造一家重要公司需要什么。

episodeTitle.en: Why AI is disrupting traditional product management | Tomer Cohen (LinkedIn CPO)
episodeTitle.zh: 《为什么人工智能正在颠覆传统产品管理 | 托默·科恩（领英首席产品官）》

bio.en: Tomer Cohen is LinkedIn's longtime Chief Product Officer, piloting the 'Full Stack Builder' program that lets anyone take products from idea to launch regardless of function.
bio.zh: Tomer Cohen 是 LinkedIn 任职已久的首席产品官（CPO），他正在推行“全栈构建者（Full Stack Builder）”计划，让任何人无论职能都能将产品从想法推进到上线。

guestBioOfficial.en: Tomer Cohen is the longtime chief product officer at LinkedIn, where he’s pioneering the Full Stack Builder program, a radical new approach to product development that fully embraces what AI makes possible. Under his leadership, LinkedIn has scrapped its traditional Associate Product Manager program and replaced it with an Associate Product Builder program that teaches coding, design, and PM skills together. He’s also introduced a formal “Full Stack Builder” title and career ladder, enabling anyone from any function to take products from idea to launch. In this conversation, Tomer explains why product development has become too complex at most companies and how LinkedIn is building an AI-powered product team that can move faster, adapt more quickly, and do more with less. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 托默·科恩（Tomer Cohen）长期担任领英的首席产品官，他正在开创“全栈构建者”计划，这是一项彻底拥抱人工智能可能性的全新产品开发方法。在他的领导下，领英废除了传统的副产品经理项目，取而代之的是副产品构建者项目，该项目将编程、设计和产品管理技能融为一体。他还引入了正式的“全栈构建者”头衔和职业晋升通道，使来自任何职能的人员都能将产品从构思推向上线。在本次对话中，托默将解释为何大多数公司的产品开发已变得过于复杂，以及领英如何通过人工智能驱动的产品团队实现更快的响应、更灵活的适应和更高效的成果。*我们将讨论：*

summary.en: Tomer explains LinkedIn's Full Stack Builder program, which scraps the traditional APM track in favor of an associate builder path where people from any function take products from idea to launch. He discusses why this broadens the talent pool, creates a new career ladder, and reflects on leading product at LinkedIn's scale. The episode is a forward-looking model for how companies may organize product building in the AI era.
summary.zh: Tomer 解释了 LinkedIn 的“全栈构建者”计划：它废除了传统的 APM（助理产品经理）通道，代之以一个“副构建者”路径，让来自任何职能的人都能将产品从想法推进到上线。他讨论了这为何能拓宽人才池、创造新的职业阶梯，并反思了在 LinkedIn 这种规模下领导产品的体会。本期是关于企业在 AI 时代可能如何组织产品构建的、前瞻性的样板。

episodeTitle.en: What world-class GTM looks like in 2026 | Jeanne DeWitt Grosser (Vercel, Stripe, Google)
episodeTitle.zh: 《2026年世界级GTM的模样》 | 珍妮·德威特·格罗瑟（Jeanne DeWitt Grosser，Vercel、Stripe、Google）

bio.en: Jeanne Grosser is the COO of Vercel, where she oversees marketing, sales, customer success, revenue operations, and field engineering, and she previously built Stripe's earliest sales team from the ground up as its Chief Product Officer.
bio.zh: Jeanne Grosser 是 Vercel 的首席运营官（COO），负责市场营销、销售、客户成功、营收运营和现场工程；此前她曾在 Stripe 担任首席产品官，从零搭建起 Stripe 最早的销售团队。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jeanne DeWitt Grosser built world-class GTM teams at Stripe, Google, and, most recently, Vercel, where she serves as COO and oversees marketing, sales, customer success, revenue operations, and field engineering. She transformed Stripe’s early sales organization from the ground up and advises founders on GTM strategy. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 珍妮·德威特·格罗瑟曾在Stripe、Google以及最近的Vercel建立世界级GTM团队，她目前在Vercel担任首席运营官，负责市场营销、销售、客户成功、收入运营和现场工程。她从零开始重建了Stripe的早期销售组织，并为创始人提供GTM战略建议。*我们讨论了：*

summary.en: Jeanne reframes go-to-market as a product problem, arguing that with AI intensifying competition, the ability to actually bring a product to market now matters more than ever. She explains that most enterprise buying is driven by avoiding pain and reducing risk rather than chasing upside, and that the buying experience itself is becoming a key differentiator between otherwise similar products. A standout idea is the 'go-to-market engineer'—a role on her team that lets them operate roughly ten times faster—and her litmus test that a great salesperson should be nearly indistinguishable from a product manager to engineers. The episode is a deep, tactical primer on segmentation, GTM process, tooling, and her hot takes on PLG, sales compensation, and sales hiring.
summary.zh: Jeanne 把“走向市场（go-to-market）”重新定义成一个产品问题，她认为在 AI 加剧竞争的当下，真正把产品推向市场的能力比以往任何时候都更重要。她解释说，企业采购大多是为了规避痛苦、降低风险，而不是为了追逐上行空间，而且当产品本身差异不大时，购买体验本身正在成为关键差异化因素。一个特别亮眼的想法是“走向市场工程师”（go-to-market engineer）这个角色——它让她的团队运转速度快了大约十倍——以及她那条“黄金标准”：优秀的销售在工程师面前应该几乎 indistinguishable（难以分辨）于产品经理。整期是对市场细分、GTM 流程、工具链的深入实战讲解，也包含了她对 PLG、销售薪酬和销售招聘的犀利观点。

episodeTitle.en: A guide to difficult conversations, building high-trust teams, and designing a life you love
episodeTitle.zh: 《艰难对话指南：如何建立高度信任的团队，设计理想生活》

bio.en: Rachel Lockett is an executive coach and former longtime HR leader at Pinterest and at Stripe who helps CEOs, founders, and tech leaders with emotional intelligence, resilience, and building trusted, accountable teams.
bio.zh: Rachel Lockett 是一位高管教练，也曾长期担任 Pinterest 与 Stripe 的人力资源负责人，她帮助 CEO、创始人和科技领导者提升情商、韧性，并打造值得信赖、各负其责的团队。

guestBioOfficial.en: Rachel Lockett is a sought-after executive coach and former HR leader at Stripe and Pinterest who now works with CEOs, founders, and tech leaders on emotional intelligence, resilience, and leadership skills. In this episode, Rachel shares powerful frameworks for coaching reports, having difficult conversations, avoiding burnout, and strengthening co-founder relationships. She also demonstrates these techniques through a live coaching session with me. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 瑞秋·洛克特（Rachel Lockett）是备受追捧的高管教练，曾任Stripe和Pinterest的人力资源负责人，如今为首席执行官、创始人及科技领袖提供情商、韧性与领导力方面的指导。在本期节目中，瑞秋分享了指导汇报、进行艰难对话、避免职业倦怠以及加强联合创始人关系的实用框架。她还通过与我的现场指导环节现场演示了这些技巧。*我们讨论了：*

summary.en: Rachel argues that great leaders don't need to have all the answers; instead they equip their teams by attuning to context and coaching rather than dictating. She shares how to make difficult conversations easier, how technical leaders can avoid burnout by operating in their gifts and strengths, and why seeking help is a vulnerable but necessary step. The episode reframes the 'human side' of building companies as both fun and high-leverage.
summary.zh: Rachel 认为，杰出的领导者不需要掌握所有答案；相反，他们通过体察情境、以教练方式赋能团队，而非发号施令。她分享了如何让艰难对话变轻松、技术型领导者如何借助自身天赋与优势避免职业倦怠，以及为什么寻求帮助虽令人脆弱却是必经的一步。本期将“打造公司的人的一面”重新定义为既有趣又高杠杆的事。

episodeTitle.en: Mental models for building products people love ft. Stewart Butterfield
episodeTitle.zh: 打造人们喜爱的产品的心智模型，嘉宾斯图尔特·巴特菲尔德（Stewart Butterfield）

bio.en: Stewart Butterfield is a legendary founder who created Flickr and Slack (sold to Salesforce in one of tech's biggest deals), known for deep product, craft, and taste.
bio.zh: Stewart Butterfield 是一位传奇创始人，他创造了 Flickr 和 Slack（被 Salesforce 以科技圈最大交易之一收购），以深厚的产品功力、工艺与品味著称。

guestBioOfficial.en: Stewart Butterfield is the co-founder of Slack and Flickr, two of the most influential products in internet history. After selling Slack to Salesforce in one of tech’s biggest acquisitions, he’s been focused on family, philanthropy, and creative projects. In this rare podcast appearance, Stewart shares the product frameworks and leadership principles that most contributed to his success. From “utility curves” to “the owner’s delusion” to “hyper-realistic work-like activities,” his thoughts on craft, strategy, and leadership apply to anyone building products or leading teams. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 斯图尔特·巴特菲尔德（Stewart Butterfield）是Slack和Flickr的联合创始人，这两款产品是互联网历史上最具影响力的产品之一。在将Slack以科技界最大收购之一出售给Salesforce后，他一直专注于家庭、慈善事业和创意项目。在这次难得的播客亮相中，斯图尔特分享了对他成功贡献最大的产品框架和领导原则。从“效用曲线”到“所有者错觉”再到“超现实的工作般活动”，他对工艺、战略和领导力的见解适用于任何开发产品或领导团队的人。

summary.en: Stewart shares hard-won product and leadership wisdom, including his concept of 'utility curves,' the 'owner's delusion' that makes founders overestimate their product, and the hilarious 'hyperrealistic work-like activities' he sees at companies. He discusses Parkinson's law, why craft and taste matter, and what he's learned about building things people love. The episode only scratches the surface of the wisdom locked in his head.
summary.zh: Stewart 分享了来之不易的产品与领导力智慧，包括他的“效用曲线（utility curves）”概念、让创始人高估自己产品的“所有者妄想（owner's delusion）”，以及他在公司里观察到的滑稽的“超现实工作式活动（hyperrealistic work-like activities）”。他讨论了帕金森定律、为什么工艺与品味重要，以及他在打造受人喜爱之物中学到的东西。本期仅仅触及了他脑海中封存智慧的冰山一角。

episodeTitle.en: The Godmother of AI on jobs, robots & why world models are next | Dr. Fei-Fei Li
episodeTitle.zh: 人工智能教母谈就业、机器人及为何世界模型是下一个风口 | 李飞飞博士（Dr. Fei-Fei Li）

bio.en: Dr. Fei-Fei Li, known as the “godmother of AI,” sparked the deep-learning revolution with ImageNet and now works on world models, including launching the large world model “Marble.”
bio.zh: 被誉为“AI 教母”的李飞飞（Dr. Fei-Fei Li）以 ImageNet 点燃了深度学习革命，如今致力于世界模型，并发布了大型世界模型 “Marble”。

guestBioOfficial.en: Dr. Fei-Fei Li is known as the “godmother of AI.” She’s been at the center of AI’s biggest breakthroughs for over two decades. She spearheaded ImageNet, the dataset that sparked the deep-learning revolution we’re living right now, served as Google Cloud’s Chief AI Scientist, directed Stanford’s Artificial Intelligence Lab, and co-founded Stanford’s Institute for Human-Centered AI. In this conversation, Fei-Fei shares the rarely told history of how we got here—including the wild fact that just nine years ago, calling yourself an AI company was basically a death sentence. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 李飞飞博士被誉为“人工智能教母”。二十多年来，她一直处于人工智能最大突破的核心。她牵头创建了ImageNet数据集，引发了我们如今所处的深度学习革命，曾担任谷歌云首席人工智能科学家，领导斯坦福大学人工智能实验室，并共同创立了斯坦福大学以人为本的人工智能研究所。在对话中，李飞飞分享了我们如何走到今天这一步的鲜为人知的历史——包括一个令人惊讶的事实：就在九年前，自称是人工智能公司几乎等于被判了死刑。*我们将探讨：*

summary.en: Fei-Fei recounts how calling yourself an AI company was a death knell just 9–10 years ago and how that flipped completely, and shares her view that technology is a double-edged sword whose impact is up to people. She explains why she's passionate about building world models and what they are, and announces the launch of Marble, the world's first large world model. The conversation is an inspiring tour of AI history, responsibility, and the road ahead.
summary.zh: 李飞飞回顾了仅仅 9–10 年前“自称 AI 公司”还是品牌死刑、而如今彻底反转的历程，并表达了她“技术是把双刃剑、影响取决于人”的观点。她解释了为何热衷构建世界模型及其含义，并宣布发布全球首个大型世界模型 “Marble”。对话是一场关于 AI 历史、责任与未来之路的鼓舞人心的巡礼。

episodeTitle.en: “Dumbest idea I’ve heard” to $100M ARR: Inside the rise of Gamma | Grant Lee (co-founder)
episodeTitle.zh: “我听过最愚蠢的主意”到1亿美元年营收：Gamma崛起记 | 格兰特·李（联合创始人）

bio.en: Grant Lee is the co-founder and CEO of Gamma, the profitable AI-powered presentation and website design tool that reached $100M ARR in just over two years with a ~30-person team and is valued at over $2 billion.
bio.zh: Grant Lee 是 Gamma 的联合创始人兼 CEO；Gamma 是一款盈利的 AI 演示与网站设计工具，仅用 30 人左右的团队在两年多内达到 1 亿美元 ARR，估值超 20 亿美元。

guestBioOfficial.en: Grant Lee is the co-founder of Gamma, the AI-powered presentation tool that’s one of the hottest and most interesting AI startups in the world right now. They’re valued at over $2 billion, and they hit $100 million ARR in just over two years, with a lean team of just around 30 people. Unlike many fast-growing AI startups, Gamma has been profitable for most of its history, has not raised significant funding, and they built a massive business in a category most investors dismissed. In fact, one investor told Grant his idea was “the dumbest idea he had ever heard.” *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 格兰特·李是AI驱动演示工具Gamma的联合创始人，该公司目前是全球最热门、最具创新性的AI初创企业之一。他们估值超过20亿美元，仅用两年多时间就达成1亿美元年营收目标，团队仅有约30人。与许多快速发展的AI初创公司不同，Gamma在大部分发展历程中都是盈利的，没有筹集大量资金，却在大多数投资者视为冷门的领域建立了庞大业务。事实上，一位投资者曾告诉格兰特，他的想法是“他听过最愚蠢的主意”。*我们探讨了：*

summary.en: Grant tells the story of building Gamma as a small, profitable team serving 50M+ users—despite one investor calling it the 'worst idea' he'd ever heard—and how they grew through hands-on influencer marketing, onboarding micro-influencers manually rather than paying for big creators to read scripts. He shares a relentlessly experimental cadence (idea in the morning, live experiment by afternoon, iterate by evening) and why most people wrongly dismiss the presentation category as a real business. The episode is a tactical masterclass in profitable, sustainable AI-startup growth.
summary.zh: Grant 讲述了用一支精干、盈利的团队服务 5000 万以上用户、打造 Gamma 的故事——尽管有投资人说这是他听过“最烂的点子”，以及他们如何通过亲力亲为的影响者营销实现增长：手动 onboard 微影响者，而非花钱让大网红念脚本。他分享了毫不松懈的实验节奏（早上出点子、下午跑实验、晚上迭代），以及为何大多数人都错误地低估了“演示”这个品类能做成大生意。这期节目是关于盈利、可持续的 AI 创业公司增长的战术公开课。

episodeTitle.en: $1M to $10M: The enterprise sales playbook with Jen Abel
episodeTitle.zh: 从100万到1000万美元：与珍·阿贝尔探讨企业销售攻略

bio.en: Jen Abel is co-founder of JJELLYFISH, where she helps early-stage founders learn to sell, and now GM of Enterprise at a high-growth company; this episode is the tactical follow-up to her first, on going from ~$1M to ~$10M ARR in enterprise sales.
bio.zh: Jen Abel 是 JJELLYFISH 的联合创始人，帮助早期创始人学会销售，如今在某高成长公司担任企业业务 GM；这期节目是她首期节目（如何从 0 到 100 万美元 ARR 的创始人式销售）的战术续集，聚焦如何从约 100 万做到约 1000 万美元 ARR 的企业销售。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jen Abel is GM of Enterprise at State Affairs and co-founded Jellyfish, a consultancy that helps founders learn zero-to-one enterprise sales. She’s one of the smartest people I’ve ever met on learning enterprise sales, and in this follow-up to our first chat two years ago (covering the zero to $1 million ARR founder-led sales phase), we focus on the skills founders need to learn to go from $1M to $10M ARR. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 珍·阿贝尔（Jen Abel）是State Affairs公司的企业业务总经理，也是Jellyfish咨询公司的联合创始人。Jellyfish致力于帮助初创企业掌握从0到1的企业销售技巧。她是我见过最擅长研究企业销售的人之一。在我们两年前首次对话（聚焦创始人主导销售的0到100万美元ARR阶段）的基础上，本次对话聚焦于创始人从100万到1000万美元ARR所需掌握的技能。*我们讨论了：*

summary.en: Jen goes deep on enterprise sales as a creative, relationship-driven art: sell to a gap and an opportunity, not just a problem; stop discounting to win deals (it signals buyers aren't bought in and fake product-market fit); and avoid becoming 'one of three' being tested, because differentiation is everything. She explains how enterprise deals get done through trust and mutual back-scratching, why she skips outbound sales tools (everyone pulls from the same databases) in favor of unconventional back-door approaches, and how to craft deals that make buyers want to move mountains for you. It's the most in-the-weeds enterprise-sales playbook you'll find for free.
