summary.zh: Jen 深入剖析企业销售这门“创造性、以关系驱动”的艺术：卖的是“缺口”与“机会”，而不只是问题；别靠打折赢单（那说明买家并未真的心动，还会伪造产品市场契合的假象）；更要避免沦为你被拿去“三选一”测试的对象，因为差异化就是一切。她解释了企业交易如何通过信任与互相帮忙达成、为何她不用外呼销售工具（大家都在同一批数据库里），而改用非传统的“后门”打法，以及如何设计让买家愿意为你移山的交易。这是你能免费找到的最深入的企业销售实战手册。

episodeTitle.en: She turned 100+ rejections into a $42B company | Melanie Perkins
episodeTitle.zh: 《她将100多次拒绝转化为价值420亿美元的公司 | 梅兰妮·珀金斯》

bio.en: Melanie Perkins is the co-founder and CEO of Canva, the design platform valued at over $42 billion, on track to be one of the most successful founders in tech history.
bio.zh: 梅兰妮·珀金斯（Melanie Perkins）是 Canva 的联合创始人兼 CEO，这家设计平台估值超过 420 亿美元，有望成为科技史上最成功的创始人之一。

guestBioOfficial.en: Melanie Perkins is CEO and co-founder of Canva, currently valued at over $42 billion, generating over $3 billion in annual revenue, with more than 240 million monthly active users and, incredibly, eight consecutive years of profitability. But the journey was far from smooth. Melanie was rejected by over 100 investors during her first fundraising round, her team spent two years without being able to ship a new feature during a technical rewrite, and the company pivoted early from a yearbook publishing platform to become the design powerhouse it is today. Through it all, she maintained what she calls “column B” thinking: building toward a dream future rather than just using the bricks around you. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 梅兰妮·珀金斯（Melanie Perkins）是市值超420亿美元的Canva公司的首席执行官兼联合创始人，该公司年营收超过30亿美元，月活跃用户超过2.4亿，最令人惊叹的是已连续八年实现盈利。但这条创业之路绝非一帆风顺：在首轮融资中，她被100多位投资者拒绝；团队在技术重构期间耗时两年未能推出新功能；公司还曾提前转型，从年鉴出版平台转向如今的顶级设计平台。历经种种挫折，她始终秉持所谓的“B列思维”——即不局限于现有资源，而是朝着梦想未来不断前行。

summary.en: Melanie recounts pitching over 100 investors who all said no, and turning each rejection into a new slide that sharpened her market thesis. She champions "crazy big goals" that make you feel inadequate and thus work harder to will them into existence. The episode is an inspiring founder story about persistence, vision, and betting on yourself.
summary.zh: 梅兰妮讲述了她向 100 多位投资人 pitch 却全部被拒，并把每一次拒绝变成一张新幻灯片、从而打磨出更清晰市场论点的经历。她推崇能让你自觉不足、从而更拼命去实现的"疯狂大目标"。本期是一则关于坚持、远见与押注自己的励志创始人故事。

episodeTitle.en: How Block is becoming the most AI-native enterprise in the world | Dhanji R. Prasanna
episodeTitle.zh: Block如何正成为全球最具AI原生性的企业 | 丹吉·R·普拉萨纳（Dhanji R. Prasanna）

bio.en: Dhanji R. Prasanna leads applied AI efforts and open-source agents at a major AI lab, where internal tools like their “Goose” agent are saving employees 8–10 hours a week.
bio.zh: Dhanji R. Prasanna 在一家顶级 AI 实验室领导应用 AI 与开源智能体工作，其内部工具（如开源智能体 “Goose”）每周为员工节省 8–10 小时。

guestBioOfficial.en: Dhanji R. Prasanna is the chief technology officer at Block (formerly Square), where he’s managed more than 4,000 engineers over the past two years. Under his leadership, Block has become one of the most AI-native large companies in the world. Before becoming CTO, Dhanji wrote an “AI manifesto” to CEO Jack Dorsey that sparked a company-wide transformation (and his promotion to CTO). *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 丹吉·R·普拉萨纳（Dhanji R. Prasanna）是Block（前身为Square）的首席技术官，过去两年间他管理着4,000多名工程师。在他的领导下，Block已成为全球最擅长人工智能应用的大型公司之一。在成为CTO之前，丹吉曾为首席执行官杰克·多西（Jack Dorsey）撰写一份《人工智能宣言》，由此引发了公司范围内的变革（并助他晋升为CTO）。*我们将探讨：*

summary.en: Dhanji shares that engineering teams using AI heavily report 8–10 hours saved per week, and that “this is the worst it will ever be”—the baseline only improves. He tells the story of Goose watching Slack conversations and opening a PR to build a discussed feature hours later, and notes non-technical people are showing the biggest impact by optimizing their own workday. The conversation looks ahead to agents working overnight and anticipating our needs.
summary.zh: Dhanji 分享道，重度使用 AI 的工程团队每周节省 8–10 小时，且“这已经是它最差的样子”——基线只会更好。他讲述了 Goose 监听 Slack 对话、几小时后就开 PR 构建被讨论的功能的故事，并指出非技术人员通过优化自身工作日展现出最大影响。对话展望了智能体在夜间工作、预判我们需求的未来。

episodeTitle.en: Al Engineering 101 with Chip Huyen (Nvidia, Stanford, Netflix)
episodeTitle.zh: Al工程入门：与奇普·许（Chip Huyen，Nvidia、斯坦福大学、Netflix）对话

bio.en: Chip Huyen is an AI expert, author of Designing Machine Learning Systems, and founder focused on helping companies build great AI products, with deep experience in ML fundamentals and production.
bio.zh: Chip Huyen 是一位 AI 专家、《设计机器学习系统》（Designing Machine Learning Systems）作者，也是致力于帮助企业打造优秀 AI 产品的创始人，在机器学习基础与生产化方面有深厚经验。

guestBioOfficial.en: Chip Huyen is a core developer on Nvidia’s Nemo platform, a former AI researcher at Netflix, and taught machine learning at Stanford. She’s a two-time founder and the author of two widely read books on AI, including AI Engineering, which has been the most-read book on the O’Reilly platform since its launch. Unlike many AI commentators, Chip has built multiple successful AI products and platforms and works directly with enterprises on their AI strategies, giving her unique visibility into what’s actually happening inside companies building AI products. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh:
奇普·许恩（Chip Huyen）是英伟达Nemo平台的核心开发者、曾任网飞（Netflix）人工智能研究员，并在斯坦福大学教授机器学习。她曾两次创业，并著有两本广受欢迎的人工智能书籍，包括《AI工程》（AI Engineering），该书自上线以来便成为O'Reilly平台上阅读量最高的书籍。与许多人工智能评论员不同，奇普亲手打造了多个成功的人工智能产品和平台，并直接与企业合作制定人工智能战略，这让她对构建人工智能产品的企业内部运作有着独特的洞察力。  
*我们讨论：*

summary.en: Chip explains ML basics accessibly—pretraining, post-training, RAG, reinforcement learning, RLHF—and then gets into what it actually takes to build great AI products versus what people assume. She argues most companies stall not for lack of tools but because they don't understand their users' real needs and can't measure productivity gains. The conversation is a clear, practical guide to avoiding the “AI hype gap” and shipping products that work.
summary.zh: Chip 以易懂的方式讲解机器学习基础——预训练、后训练、RAG、强化学习、RLHF——并深入探讨打造优秀 AI 产品真正需要什么，而非人们想当然的。她认为多数公司停滞不是因为缺工具，而是不理解用户真实需求、无法衡量生产力提升。对话是避开“AI 炒作鸿沟”、交付真正可用产品的清晰实用指南。

episodeTitle.en: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren
episodeTitle.zh: 2025年如何衡量AI开发者生产力 | 妮可·福斯格伦

bio.en: Nicole Forsgren is the leading expert on developer productivity and author of Accelerate, who now researches how AI is changing how engineering teams work.
bio.zh: 妮可·福斯格伦（Nicole Forsgren）是开发者生产力领域的顶尖专家、《Accelerate》一书的作者，如今研究 AI 如何改变工程团队的工作方式。

guestBioOfficial.en: Nicole Forsgren created the most widely used frameworks for measuring developer productivity—DORA and SPACE. She wrote the foundational book Accelerate and is about to release her newest book, Frictionless, a practical guide for helping teams move faster in the AI era. She’s currently Senior Director of Developer Intelligence at Google. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 妮可·福斯格伦创造了最广泛应用的开发者生产力衡量框架——DORA和SPACE。她撰写了奠基性著作《精益软件与DevOps实战》，并即将推出新作《无摩擦》，这是一本关于AI时代帮助团队加速的实用指南。她目前是谷歌开发者情报高级总监。*我们将讨论：*

summary.en: Nicole argues most productivity metrics are a lie - lines of code are trivially gameable and shipping faster only matters if you ship the right thing. She stresses evaluating AI-generated code for reliability, style, and hallucinations rather than accepting it blindly. The episode is a clear-eyed guide to measuring real productivity in the AI era.
summary.zh: 妮可认为，大多数生产力指标都是谎言——代码行数极易被操纵，而"更快交付"只有在交付正确的东西时才有意义。她强调要评估 AI 生成代码的可靠性、风格与是否存在幻觉，而非盲目接受。本期是一份在 AI 时代衡量真实生产力的清醒指南。

episodeTitle.en: Figma’s CEO: Why AI makes design, craft, and quality the new moat for startups | Dylan Field
episodeTitle.zh: Figma首席执行官：为何人工智能让设计、工艺和质量成为初创公司的新护城河 | Dylan Field

bio.en: Dylan Field is the co-founder and CEO of Figma, the collaborative design tool used by virtually every product team in the world, and is now leading the company's push into AI-native product building with Figma Make.
bio.zh: Dylan Field 是 Figma 的联合创始人兼 CEO；Figma 是全球几乎每个产品团队都在使用的协作设计工具，他目前正带领公司借助 Figma Make 进军 AI 原生产品构建领域。

guestBioOfficial.en: Dylan Field is co-founder and CEO of Figma, a beloved tool used by every modern product team. Founded in 2012, Figma has expanded from a single design tool to a comprehensive platform including FigJam, Slides, Dev Mode, and, most recently, Figma Make. After a $20 billion acquisition by Adobe fell through due to regulatory pushback, Dylan led the company to a successful IPO in 2025. *What you’ll learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh:
迪伦·菲尔德（Dylan Field）是Figma的联合创始人兼首席执行官，Figma是每个现代产品团队都喜爱的工具。Figma成立于2012年，从单一设计工具发展为一个综合平台，涵盖FigJam、Slides、Dev Mode以及最近推出的Figma Make。在Adobe以200亿美元收购Figma因监管阻力而失败后，迪伦于2025年成功带领公司完成IPO。  
*你将学到：*

summary.en: Dylan reflects on how Figma stayed focused and motivated after the failed Adobe acquisition, and how his own leadership has evolved over 13 years. He shares the counterintuitive bet behind FigJam—making 'fun' the differentiator—and lays out his vision for Figma Make as a way to let anyone prototype and shape product direction. He argues that craft and design are now essential to winning in software, that market-size thinking is the wrong lens for new product lines, and that organizations should expect to get better as AI models improve rather than shrink headcount.
summary.zh: Dylan 回顾了在 Adobe 收购告吹后，Figma 如何保持专注与动力，以及他本人在 13 年间的领导力蜕变。他分享了 FigJam 背后那个反直觉的赌注——把“有趣”作为差异化卖点，并阐述了 Figma Make 的愿景：让任何人都能参与原型设计与产品方向的塑造。他认为，在软件行业取胜的关键在于工艺与设计，用市场规模来思考新产品线是错误的方式，而组织应期待随着 AI 模型进步变得更强，而不是缩减人手。

episodeTitle.en: Inside Google's AI turnaround: AI Mode, AI Overviews, and vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein
episodeTitle.zh: 谷歌AI转型内幕：AI模式、AI概览及AI驱动搜索愿景 | 罗比·斯坦

bio.en: Robby Stein is VP of Product for Google Search, responsible for the entire search experience including AI Overviews, AI Mode, Google Lens, and the ranking algorithm, and previously led the launch of Instagram Stories, Reels, and Close Friends as Head of Product at Instagram.
bio.zh: Robby Stein 是 Google 搜索的产品副总裁，负责包括 AI Overviews、AI Mode、Google Lens 与排序算法在内的整个搜索体验，此前作为 Instagram 产品负责人主导推出了 Stories、Reels 与 Close Friends。

guestBioOfficial.en: Robby Stein is VP of Product at Google, where he oversees the core products of Google Search—including the new AI Overviews, AI Mode, search ranking, Google Lens, and more. Previously, he led consumer products at Instagram, where he and his teams built Stories, Reels, Close Friends, and other key features now used by billions. *What you’ll learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 罗比·斯坦是谷歌的产品副总裁，负责谷歌搜索的核心产品，包括新推出的AI概览、AI模式、搜索排名、谷歌Lens等。此前，他曾在Instagram领导消费者产品团队，带领团队开发了如今被数十亿用户使用的故事、短视频、亲密好友等核心功能。*您将学到：*

summary.en: Robby explains why search isn't dying but expanding with AI, and breaks down Google's three-pronged approach: AI Overviews, the new AI Mode, and multimodal experiences like Lens. He describes the renewed focus and urgency inside Google behind Gemini's rise, and why the vast, everyday breadth of search queries is underappreciated by skeptics. The episode offers a front-row view of one of the biggest shifts in Google's history.
summary.zh: Robby 解释了为什么搜索不会消亡，反而正随 AI 扩张，并拆解了 Google 的三叉策略：AI Overviews、全新的 AI Mode，以及以 Lens 为代表的多模态体验。他描述了 Gemini 崛起背后 Google 内部焕然一新的专注与紧迫感，以及为何怀疑者低估了搜索查询在日常上的海量广度。本期提供了 Google 史上最大变革之一的前排视角。

episodeTitle.en: Scale AI CEO on Meta’s $14B deal, scaling Uber Eats to $80B, & what frontier labs are building next
episodeTitle.zh: Scale AI CEO谈元宇宙140亿美元交易、Uber Eats如何扩张至800亿美元，以及前沿实验室的未来方向

bio.en: Jason Droege is the CEO of Scale AI—his first interview since succeeding founder Alexandr Wang after the Meta deal—and previously co-founded Uber Eats, which grew into a multi-billion-dollar business that helped save Uber during the pandemic.
bio.zh: Jason Droege 是 Scale AI 的 CEO——这是他接替创始人 Alexandr Wang（赴 Meta 后）后的首次采访，他此前联合创办了 Uber Eats，将其发展为价值数十亿美元的业务，并在疫情期间拯救了 Uber。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jason Droege is the CEO of Scale AI, a company that provides foundational training data to every major AI lab. He previously co-founded Scour with Travis Kalanick and built Uber Eats from idea to $20 billion in revenue. In this conversation, Jason shares lessons from getting sued for $250 billion, discovering restaurant economics by weighing sandwich ingredients, and over 25 years of launching transformative technology businesses. *What you’ll learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 杰森·德罗格（Jason Droege）是Scale AI的首席执行官，该公司为各大AI实验室提供基础训练数据。此前，他与特拉维斯·卡兰尼克（Travis Kalanick）共同创立了Scour，并将Uber Eats从一个创意发展为年营收200亿美元的业务。在本次对谈中，杰森分享了被索赔2500亿美元的教训、通过称量三明治配料探索餐厅经济学的经验，以及25年多来创立变革性科技企业的心得。 *您将学到：*

summary.en: Jason explains why enterprise AI takes 6–12 months to become robust enough to automate real processes, and why the trend is shifting from models that 'know things' to models that 'do things' via agents. He describes Scale's pioneering role in data labeling, training data, and evals—work that increasingly requires PhDs and professionals doing tasks that take hours—and how that is what actually makes frontier models smarter. The conversation also covers the high bar he sets for new businesses and what unique insight justifies starting one.
summary.zh: Jason 解释了为何企业级 AI 需要 6–12 个月才能足够稳健到自动化真实流程，以及为何趋势正从“知道事情”的模型转向通过智能体“做事”的模型。他描述了 Scale 在数据标注、训练数据和 evals 领域的开创性角色——这类工作越来越需要博士和专业人士完成耗时数小时的任务，而这正是前沿模型变聪明的真正来源。对话还涵盖他对新业务设定的高门槛，以及何种独特洞见才值得去创业。

episodeTitle.en: Finding hidden growth opportunities in your product | Albert Cheng (Duolingo, Grammarly, Chess.com)
episodeTitle.zh: 在产品中发现隐藏的增长机遇 | 阿尔伯特·程（Albert Cheng，Duolingo、Grammarly、Chess.com）

bio.en: Albert Cheng is one of the world's leading consumer growth leaders, having led growth and monetization at Duolingo, Grammarly, and Chess.com, where he applies an experiment-driven, user-value-focused approach to scaling beloved products.
bio.zh: Albert Cheng 是全球顶尖的消费增长领导者之一，曾在 Duolingo、Grammarly 和 Chess.com 主导增长与变现，用实验驱动、聚焦用户价值的方式规模化打造受人喜爱的产品。

guestBioOfficial.en: Albert Cheng has led growth at three of the world’s most successful consumer subscription companies: Duolingo, Grammarly, and Chess.com. A former Google product manager (and serious pianist!), Albert developed a unique approach to finding and scaling growth opportunities through rapid experimentation and deep user psychology. His teams run 1,000/year, discovering counterintuitive insights that have driven tens of millions in revenue. *What you’ll learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 阿尔伯特·程曾在全球三家最成功的消费者订阅公司——Duolingo、Grammarly和Chess.com——领导增长团队。作为前谷歌产品经理（兼认真的钢琴家！），阿尔伯特开发了一种独特的方法，通过快速实验和深入的用户心理分析来发现和扩展增长机遇。他的团队每年进行1000次实验，发现了推动数千万美元收入的反直觉洞察。*您将学到：*

summary.en: Albert defines growth as "connecting users to the value of your product" and uses an explore-and-exploit framework to balance finding the right mountain with climbing it well—surfacing a single insight across the product compounds wins, and while experiment win rates are often just 30–50%, breakthrough wins deserve a company-wide swarm. For freemium and consumer subscriptions, retention is gold: make the free product reflect the full value (Grammarly's sampled paid suggestions nearly doubled upgrades) and invest in resurrecting dormant users. AI accelerates growth work (text-to-SQL bots, AI prototyping), and chess.com pairs engines with LLMs for coaching; brand and mascots (Duo the owl) plus word-of-mouth virality (screenshot hotspots) combine powerfully with experimentation. Shifting a culture from zero to "1,000 experiments a year" relies on CEO buy-in, early wins, and a system (instrumentation, growth model) that matters more than the number itself.
summary.zh: Albert 把增长定义为「把用户连接到产品价值」，并用「探索与利用」框架平衡「找对要爬的山」与「有效爬那座山」——把单个洞察跨产品复利，胜率通常只有 30–50%，但突破性的赢要全公司 swarm。对 freemium/消费订阅，留存是金：让免费产品反映全部价值（Grammarly 抽样穿插付费建议让升级率近翻倍），并投资「复活」休眠用户。AI 加速增长工作（text-to-SQL 机器人、AI 原型），chess.com 用引擎+LLM 做教练；品牌与吉祥物（Duo 猫头鹰）和口碑病毒（截图热点）与实验结合是火箭燃料。把文化从零实验推向「一年一千实验」靠的是 CEO 支持、早期胜利，以及比数字本身更重要的系统（埋点、增长模型）。

episodeTitle.en: Why AI evals are the hottest new skill for product builders | Hamel Husain & Shreya Shankar
episodeTitle.zh: 为何AI评估是产品构建者最热门的新技能 | 哈梅尔·胡赛因 & 施瑞娅·尚卡尔

bio.en: Hamel Husain and Shreya Shankar are the leading voices on AI evals—Hamel a veteran ML engineer (formerly at GitHub and Airbnb) and Shreya a PhD researcher at Stanford—who teach the definitive online course that has trained over 2,000 PMs and engineers across 500 companies, including the teams at OpenAI and Anthropic.
bio.zh: Hamel Husain 与 Shreya Shankar 是 AI 评估（evals）领域最具代表性的声音——Hamel 是一位资深机器学习工程师（曾任职于 GitHub 和 Airbnb），Shreya 是斯坦福的博士研究员——他们开设的权威在线课程已培训超过 2000 名 PM 与工程师、覆盖 500 家公司，其中包括 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的团队。

guestBioOfficial.en: Hamel Husain and Shreya Shankar teach the world’s most popular course on AI evals and have trained over 2,000 PMs and engineers (including many teams at OpenAI and Anthropic). In this conversation, they demystify the process of developing effective evals, walk through real examples, and share practical techniques that’ll help you improve your AI product. *What you’ll learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 哈梅尔·胡赛因和施瑞娅·尚卡尔教授全球最受欢迎的AI评估课程，已培训了2,000多名产品经理和工程师（包括OpenAI和Anthropic的许多团队）。在本次对话中，他们揭开开发有效评估的神秘面纱，分享真实案例，并传授实用技巧，助您提升AI产品质量。*您将学到：*

summary.en: Hamel and Shreya make the case that building evals is the highest-ROI activity for any AI product team, and that you only need to do the process once to build on it—not perfectly, but actionably. They dismantle common misconceptions (no, the AI can't just eval itself; no, you don't need a committee—appoint one trusted 'benevolent dictator' with domain expertise). The episode is a show-and-tell primer: walking through how to build an effective eval, the first steps to start, and battle-tested best practices, leaving even non-technical listeners excited to write their own.
summary.zh: Hamel 和 Shreya 提出，构建 evals 是任何 AI 产品团队投资回报率最高的活动，而且你只需做一次就能在其上迭代——不求完美，但求能真正改进产品。他们戳破了常见误解（不，AI 不能自己评估自己；不，你不需要一个委员会——指派一位你信任、具备领域专长的“仁慈的独裁者”即可）。这期节目是“做给你看”的入门课：手把手讲解如何构建一个有效的 eval、从哪几步开始，以及经过实战检验的最佳实践，让即便非技术的听众也跃跃欲试想写自己的 eval。

episodeTitle.en: From managing people to managing AI: The leadership skills everyone needs now | Julie Zhuo
episodeTitle.zh: 从管理人到管理AI：当下每个人都需要的领导力技能 | 朱莉·卓

bio.en: Julie Zhuo is the co-founder and President of Sundial, a leadership and AI tooling company, and previously spent 13 years at Facebook rising from designer to VP of Product Design.
bio.zh: 朱莉·卓（Julie Zhuo）是 Sundial 公司的联合创始人兼总裁，该公司专注于领导力与 AI 工具；她此前在 Facebook 工作了 13 年，从设计师一路晋升为产品设计副总裁。

guestBioOfficial.en: Julie Zhuo is the former VP and Head of Design at Facebook (now Meta), author of the bestselling book The Making of a Manager, and co-founder of Sundial, an AI-powered data analysis company. Also, my first-ever podcast guest over 3 years ago! *In our conversation, we discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 朱莉·卓曾是Facebook（现元宇宙公司Meta）的副总裁兼设计主管，畅销书《经理人修炼之道》的作者，也是AI驱动数据分析公司Sundial的联合创始人。三年前，她还是我首位播客嘉宾！*在我们的对话中，我们探讨了：*

summary.en: Julie argues that AI is dissolving traditional role boundaries, turning everyone into generalist "builders" who can do many jobs themselves. She describes modern management as being sturdy while staying flexible, like a willow tree that survives storms. The conversation explores how managers should adapt as the rate of change accelerates and models become core resources.
summary.zh: 朱莉认为，AI 正在消解传统的角色边界，让每个人都变成能做多种工作的通才型"构建者"。她把现代管理形容为"柔中带刚"——像柳树一样既能挺过风暴又保持灵活。本期探讨了在变化速度加快、模型成为核心资源之际，管理者应如何调整自身。

episodeTitle.en: Why experts writing AI evals is creating the fastest-growing companies in history | Brendan Foody
episodeTitle.zh: 为何AI评估专家正在创造史上增长最快的公司 | 布伦丹·福迪

bio.en: Brendan Foody is CEO and co-founder of Mercor, the fastest-growing company in history to reach $500M in revenue (in 17 months) and the youngest unicorn founder, building a marketplace for AI training labor.
bio.zh: Brendan Foody 是 Mercor 的 CEO 兼联合创始人，该公司是史上最快达到 5 亿美元收入（仅 17 个月）的公司，他也是最年轻的独角兽创始人，正在打造一个 AI 训练劳动力的市场。

guestBioOfficial.en: Brendan Foody is the CEO and co-founder of Mercor, the fastest-growing company in history to go from $1M to $500M in revenue (in just 17 months!). At 22, he is also the youngest American unicorn founder ever. Mercor works with 6 of the Magnificent 7 and all top 5 AI labs to help them hire experts to create evaluations and training data that improve their models. In this conversation, Brendan explains why evals have become the critical bottleneck for AI progress, how he discovered this massive opportunity, and what the future of work might look like in an AI-driven economy. _Big thank you to Peter Deng for introducing me to Brendan._
guestBioOfficial.zh: 布伦丹·福迪是Mercor公司的首席执行官兼联合创始人，Mercor是史上增长最快的公司之一，从100万美元营收增长至5亿美元（仅用17个月！）。22岁的他也是美国最年轻的独角兽创始人。Mercor与Magnificent 7中的6家公司以及所有前5名的AI实验室合作，帮助他们聘请专家创建评估和训练数据以改进模型。在本次对话中，布伦丹解释了为何评估已成为AI进步的关键瓶颈，他是如何发现这一巨大机遇的，以及AI驱动的经济中未来的工作可能是什么样子。 _非常感谢邓鹏向我介绍布伦丹。_

summary.en: Brendan explains the rise of “evals”—measuring model capabilities—as possibly the biggest business opportunity in history, with Mercor supplying extraordinary professionals to top AI labs. He covers what product-market fit looks like for this new category, the tenets that enabled such extreme growth, and what evaluators actually do day to day. The conversation also explores which skills and jobs will last longest with AI and why he doesn't expect AGI soon.
summary.zh: Brendan 解释了“评估”（evals，即衡量模型能力）的崛起——可能是史上最大的商业机会——Mercor 正为顶尖 AI 实验室提供顶尖专业人才。他讲述了这一新品类产品市场匹配的样子、支撑极端增长的原则，以及评估者每天实际在做什么。对话还探讨了在 AI 时代哪些技能和工作最持久，以及他为何不认为 AGI 会很快到来。

episodeTitle.en: $46B of hard truths: Why founders fail and why you need to run toward fear | Ben Horowitz (a16z)
episodeTitle.zh: 《460亿美元的残酷真相：为何创始人会失败，以及为何你需要直面恐惧》 | 本·霍洛维茨（Ben Horowitz，a16z）

bio.en: Ben Horowitz is the co-founder of Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), one of the world's largest venture capital firms, and author of the New York Times bestsellers The Hard Thing About Hard Things and The CEO Within.
bio.zh: Ben Horowitz 是安德森·霍洛维茨（a16z）的联合创始人，该公司是全球最大的风险投资机构之一，也是《创业维艰》（The Hard Thing About Hard Things）和《掌舵》（The CEO Within）等纽约时报畅销书作者。

guestBioOfficial.en: Ben Horowitz is the co-founder of Andreessen Horowitz, Silicon Valley’s largest and most influential venture capital firm, with over $46B in committed capital across multiple funds. He took Loudcloud public with just $2 million in revenue (dubbed “the IPO from hell”), sold it for $1.6 billion, and has backed companies from Facebook to Stripe to Airbnb to OpenAI to Databricks (now worth more than $100 billion). His management philosophy—forged through near-death experiences and refined through coaching hundreds of CEOs—contradicts most conventional startup wisdom. *In our conversation, Ben shares:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 班·霍洛维茨（Ben Horowitz）是硅谷规模最大、最具影响力的风险投资公司安德森·霍洛维茨（Andreessen Horowitz）的联合创始人，该公司旗下多个基金管理的承诺投资额超过460亿美元。他曾以仅200万美元营收（被称为"地狱般的IPO"）将Loudcloud公司成功上市，随后以16亿美元售出，并投资了从Facebook到Stripe、Airbnb、OpenAI再到Databricks等多家公司（目前估值超1000亿美元）。他的管理理念——历经濒死经历磨砺，并通过指导数百位CEO不断完善——与大多数传统创业智慧背道而驰。*在我们的对话中，班分享了：*

summary.en: Ben argues the worst thing a leader can do is hesitate on the next decision, and that your only real added value comes when you make a call most people disagree with. He reflects on his famous essay “Good Product Manager, Bad Product Manager,” insisting the PM role is fundamentally a leadership job—the “mini-CEO”—where what matters is that the product works. The conversation is full of stories and insights on CEO-ing, decision-making under pressure, and building enduring companies.
summary.zh: Ben 认为领导者最糟糕的事就是在下一个决策上犹豫，而你真正增加的价值只来自做出大多数人反对的决定。他回顾了那篇著名文章《好产品经理，坏产品经理》，坚持 PM 本质上是领导角色——“迷你 CEO”——关键在产品真正奏效。对话充满了关于当 CEO、在压力下决策和打造持久公司的故事与洞见。

episodeTitle.en: How we restructured Airtable's entire org for AI | Howie Liu (co-founder and CEO)
episodeTitle.zh: 我们如何为AI重组Airtable的整个组织 | 豪伊·刘（联合创始人兼CEO）

bio.en: Howie Liu is the co-founder and CEO of Airtable, the flexible low-code application platform, and is part of a wave of founders reinventing decade-old software businesses for the AI era.
bio.zh: Howie Liu 是 Airtable 的联合创始人兼 CEO；Airtable 是一款灵活的低代码应用平台，他也是将成立十余年的软件公司重新改造以迎接 AI 时代的创始人之一。

guestBioOfficial.en: Howie Liu is the co-founder and CEO of Airtable, the no-code platform valued at around $12 billion. After a viral tweet declared “Airtable is dead” based on incorrect data, Howie led a radical transformation: reorganizing the entire company around AI, becoming an “IC CEO” who codes daily, and achieving over $100 million in free cash flow. *What you’ll learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 豪伊·刘是Airtable的联合创始人兼CEO，这家无代码平台估值约120亿美元。在一次基于错误数据的"Airtable已死"病毒式推文后，豪伊领导了一场彻底变革：围绕AI重组整个公司，转变为每天编码的"IC CEO"，并实现了超过1亿美元的自由现金流。*你将学习到：*

summary.en: Howie exemplifies the 'IC CEO' trend—founders diving back into building themselves—and shares the specific skills he believes PMs, engineers, and designers need now (e.g., PMs becoming hybrid prototypers with design sensibility). He explains how he restructured Airtable into a 'fast-thinking' and a 'slow-thinking' group to accelerate AI investment, and how he encourages his team to cancel meetings and just experiment with AI tools. The episode is a practical playbook for navigating the existential AI transition every company is facing.
summary.zh: Howie 是“IC CEO”（创始人重新下场做具体工作）趋势的代表——他分享了认为 PM、工程师和设计师当下需要的具体技能（例如 PM 要变成兼具设计感的混合原型师）。他解释了如何把 Airtable 重组成“快思考”和“慢思考”两个组以加速 AI 投入，以及他如何鼓励团队取消会议、去亲手试用 AI 工具。这期节目是应对每家公司都在经历的 AI 生存转型的实用手册。

episodeTitle.en: How 80,000 companies build with AI: Products as organisms and the death of org charts | Asha Sharma
episodeTitle.zh: 8万家公司如何借助AI进行建设：产品如有机体，组织结构图已死 | 阿莎·夏尔马

bio.en: Asha Sharma is Corporate Vice President of AI Platform at Microsoft, leading the company's AI product strategy and platform, previously COO of Instacart and VP of Product & Engineering at Meta (Messenger, Instagram Direct).
bio.zh: Asha Sharma 是微软 AI 平台企业副总裁，领导公司的 AI 产品战略与平台，此前曾任 Instacart 首席运营官，以及 Meta（Messenger、Instagram Direct）产品与工程副总裁。

guestBioOfficial.en: Asha Sharma leads AI product strategy at Microsoft, where she works with thousands of companies building AI products and has unique visibility into what’s working (and what’s not) across more than 15,000 startups and enterprises. Before Microsoft, Asha was COO at Instacart, and VP of Product & Engineering at Meta, notably leading product for Messenger. *What you’ll learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 阿莎·夏尔马（Asha Sharma）在微软领导人工智能产品战略，负责与数千家开发AI产品的公司合作，并对超过15,000家初创企业和企业的做法有独特的洞察力。在加入微软之前，阿莎曾是Instacart的首席运营官，并在Meta担任产品与工程副总裁，特别是在Messenger方面负责产品。在本期节目中，我们讨论了： • Cash App如何突破重围，成为消费者应用的成功案例

summary.en: Asha frames modern AI products as living “organisms” that think, learn, and evolve, and predicts the death of traditional org charts as agent-based teams become the norm. She draws on working with 80,000+ companies building with AI to explain what separates the successes from the failures. The conversation covers how enterprises should reorganize around AI and why products must be designed for continuous, adaptive intelligence.
summary.zh: Asha 把现代 AI 产品比作会思考、学习、进化的“有机体”，并预测随着智能体团队成为常态，传统组织架构将走向消亡。她基于与 8 万多家用 AI 构建产品的公司合作的经验，解释了成败之分。对话涵盖企业应如何围绕 AI 重新组织，以及为何产品必须为持续、自适应的智能而设计。

episodeTitle.en: Inside the expert network training every frontier AI model | Garrett Lord
episodeTitle.zh: 专家网络如何训练每一款前沿AI模型 | 加勒特·洛德

bio.en: Garrett Lord is the co-founder and CEO of Handshake, the 'LinkedIn for college students' used by every Fortune 500 company to hire graduates, who turned the platform's proprietary student network into a new AI training-data business that hit $50M ARR in four months.
bio.zh: Garrett Lord 是 Handshake 的联合创始人兼 CEO；Handshake 被称为“大学生的 LinkedIn”，每一家财富 500 强公司都用它来招聘毕业生。他把平台独有的学生网络变成了全新的 AI 训练数据业务，仅用四个月就达到了 5000 万美元 ARR。

guestBioOfficial.en: Garrett Lord is co-founder and CEO of Handshake, which started as a career network for college students and new grads but recently discovered something extraordinary: they were sitting on the world’s largest network of academic experts—exactly what frontier AI labs desperately needed. With 500,000 PhDs and 3 million advanced degree holders creating training data, in just eight months they’ve built a new business that hit $50 million in revenue in its first four months and is on track to blow past $100M in the first 12 months. *What you’ll learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 加勒特·洛德是Handshake的联合创始人兼首席执行官。Handshake最初是为大学生和应届毕业生打造的职业社交平台，但最近他们发现了一个惊人机遇：手中掌握着全球最大的学术专家网络——这正是前沿AI实验室迫切需要的资源。凭借50万名博士和300万名高学历人才生成的训练数据，仅用八个月时间，他们就打造出了一项业务，首四个月营收达5000万美元，首12个月有望突破1亿美元大关。*你将学到：*

summary.en: Garrett tells the rare story of a decade-old company disrupting itself: seeing that Handshake's network of millions of students (including tens of thousands of PhDs) was uniquely valuable to AI labs, they launched a data-labeling business from zero and hit $50M ARR in four months. He argues the only real moat in human data is access to an audience, and that as models improve, generalist labelers are replaced by domain experts. The episode is a primer on what data labeling actually involves and a lesson in seizing AI opportunity while protecting against disruption.
summary.zh: Garrett 讲述了一个老公司自我颠覆的罕见故事：他意识到 Handshake 数百万学生（包括数万名博士）的网络对 AI 实验室极具价值，于是从零创办了一个数据标注业务，四个月就达到 5000 万美元 ARR。他主张人类数据领域真正的护城河只有“触达受众的能力”，并认为随着模型进步，通用标注员会被领域专家取代。这期节目既讲解了数据标注究竟涉及什么，也上了一课：如何抓住 AI 机遇、同时抵御被颠覆的风险。

episodeTitle.en: How Intercom rose from the ashes by betting everything on AI | Eoghan McCabe (founder and CEO)
episodeTitle.zh: Intercom如何从灰烬中崛起，押注一切于AI | Eoghan McCabe（创始人兼首席执行官）

bio.en: Eoghan McCabe is the co-founder and CEO of Intercom, the customer-service platform that he steered from a plateauing SaaS business into an AI-first company via its Fin AI agent, now on track to surpass $100 million in ARR.
bio.zh: Eoghan McCabe 是 Intercom 的联合创始人兼 CEO；他将这家客服平台从增长停滞的 SaaS 业务，通过 Fin AI 智能体转型为 AI 优先的公司，目前 Fin 的 ARR 正迈向 1 亿美元。

guestBioOfficial.en: Eoghan McCabe is the founder and CEO of Intercom, a customer service platform that has successfully pivoted to become an AI-first company with its agent product, Fin. After stepping away from the CEO role in 2020 due to health issues, Eoghan returned to find the company’s growth had stalled. Just one month after his return, ChatGPT launched, and within six weeks, Intercom had a working prototype of what would become Fin. In this conversation, Eoghan shares the brutal reality of transforming a late-stage SaaS business valued at multiple billions into an AI-first company that’s now growing faster than most public software companies. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: Eoghan McCabe是Intercom的创始人兼首席执行官，Intercom是一家客户服务平台，成功转型为以AI为先的公司，推出了其代理产品Fin。在2020年因健康问题卸任CEO职位后，Eoghan回归时发现公司的增长停滞。就在他回归的一个月后，ChatGPT发布，六周内，Intercom就开发出了Fin产品的原型。在这次对话中，Eoghan分享了将一家价值数十亿美元的晚期SaaS公司转型为以AI为先的公司的残酷现实。*我们讨论了：*

summary.en: Eoghan gets brutally honest about transforming Intercom into an AI-first company after growth nearly went negative, describing how he declared a 'wartime' mode and rewrote the company's values to cut out what wouldn't work in an AI era. He recounts pushing through intense resistance—including a soft coup attempt and roughly 40% staff turnover—to bet everything on Fin, an AI agent that hit eight figures in ARR within quarters. His core message: AI will disrupt your industry violently, so you must disrupt yourself first, and that requires a founder willing to make brave, hard decisions and own the results.
summary.zh: Eoghan 毫无保留地讲述了在增长几乎转负后，如何将 Intercom 转型为 AI 优先的公司：他宣布进入“战时”状态，并重写公司价值观，以剔除在 AI 时代不再有效的部分。他回顾了顶住巨大阻力（包括一次“软性政变”和约 40% 的人员更替）押注 Fin 的过程——这个 AI 智能体在几个季度内就达到八位数 ARR。他的核心观点是：AI 将以最猛烈的方式颠覆你的行业，所以你必须先自我革命，而这需要一个愿意做出勇敢、艰难决定并承担结果的创始人。

episodeTitle.en: Why ChatGPT will be the next big growth channel (and how to capitalize on it) | Brian Balfour
episodeTitle.zh: 《为什么ChatGPT将成为下一个重大增长渠道（以及如何从中获利）》|布莱恩·巴尔弗

bio.en: Brian Halligan is co-founder and longtime CEO of HubSpot and now the in-house CEO coach at Sequoia, where he brings top CEOs together and coaches them one-on-one.
bio.zh: Brian Halligan 是 HubSpot 的联合创始人兼长期 CEO，现任红杉资本的驻场 CEO 教练，将顶尖 CEO 们聚集一堂并一对一带教。

guestBioOfficial.en: Brian Balfour is the founder of Reforge, the former VP of Growth at HubSpot, and a student (and teacher) of product growth. Brian has studied every major platform shift—from Facebook to Apple to Google—and he’s spotted a pattern that’s about to repeat with ChatGPT. *In this conversation, you’ll learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 布莱恩·巴尔弗是Reforge的创始人，也是HubSpot的前增长副总裁，同时也是产品增长领域的学生（和导师）。布莱恩研究了从Facebook到苹果再到谷歌的每一次重大平台变革，并发现了一个即将在ChatGPT上重演的模式。在本对话中，你将了解：

summary.en: Brian argues that while starting a company has never been easier, scaling it into a durable, high-impact organization has never been harder, putting pressure on founders to decide faster. He shares the traits and “lock algorithm” he looks for in successful CEOs and what it's really like to carry that lonely responsibility. The conversation unpacks what it takes to be a successful CEO in today's faster-moving era.
summary.zh: Brian 认为，虽然创办公司从未如此容易，但把它扩展为持久、高影响力的组织却从未如此困难，这给创始人带来了更快决策的压力。他分享了成功 CEO 所需具备的特质和他寻找人才的“锁定算法”，以及承担这份孤独责任到底是什么滋味。对话拆解了在当今节奏更快的时代，成为成功 CEO 需要什么。

episodeTitle.en: The one question that saves product careers | Matt LeMay
episodeTitle.zh: 《那个挽救产品职业生涯的问题 | 马特·勒梅》

bio.en: Matt LeMay is a longtime product leader and author of Product Management in Practice, a practical guide used by hundreds of product teams.
bio.zh: 马特·勒梅（Matt LeMay）是一位资深产品负责人，也是实用指南《Product Management in Practice》的作者，该书被数百个产品团队使用。

guestBioOfficial.en: Matt LeMay spent 13 years as a music critic at Pitchfork before becoming one of product management’s most influential voices. He’s consulted with companies from startups to Fortune 500s and authored two essential PM books, including Impact-First Product Teams. After watching countless product teams get laid off despite “doing everything right,” he discovered a harsh truth: most PMs are optimizing for the wrong things. *In this conversation, you’ll learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 马特·勒梅在担任Pitchfork音乐评论家13年后，成为产品管理领域最具影响力的人物之一。他曾为从初创公司到《财富》500强企业的各类公司提供咨询服务，并著有两本重要的产品管理书籍，包括《以影响力为先的产品团队》。在目睹无数产品团队尽管“一切都做对了”却仍被裁员后，他发现了一个残酷的真相：大多数产品经理都在优化错误的方面。*在本次对话中，你将学习到：*

summary.en: Matt warns that too many teams are "doing work around the work," a dynamic he calls the low-impact PM death spiral. He urges PMs to ask whether they'd fully fund their own team if they were CEO. The episode offers a three-step path toward becoming a higher-impact product team focused on outcomes.
summary.zh: 马特警示，太多团队在"围绕工作做工作"，他把这种状态称为"低影响力 PM 的死亡螺旋"。他敦促 PM 自问：如果自己是 CEO，是否会全额资助自己的团队？本期提供了一条三步路径，帮助团队转向聚焦成果、更高影响力的产品运作。

episodeTitle.en: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest growing product in history  | Nick Turley (OpenAI)
episodeTitle.zh: 《深入ChatGPT：史上增长最快的产品》 | 尼克·特利（OpenAI）

bio.en: Nick Turley is the product lead for ChatGPT at OpenAI, having joined from Dropbox and Instacart, and helped turn a research project into the most consequential product in history.
bio.zh: 尼克·特利（Nick Turley）是 OpenAI 旗下 ChatGPT 的产品负责人，此前来自 Dropbox 和 Instacart，他帮助把一个研究项目变成了史上最具影响力的产品。

guestBioOfficial.en: Nick Turley is Head of ChatGPT, the fastest-growing product in history, with 700 million weekly active users (10% of the world’s population). He was part of the original hackathon team that shipped ChatGPT in just 10 days, helped it grow from zero to billions in revenue, and leads product for what may be the most consequential product of our time. We recorded this the day before GPT-5 launched. *We discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 尼克·特利（Nick Turley）：ChatGPT团队负责人

summary.en: Nick recalls joining OpenAI when it was a research lab and his first task was almost trivial, before helping build what became ChatGPT from a hackathon codebase. He shares the scrappy origin of a product initially expected to fail. The episode offers a behind-the-scenes look at shipping and scaling ChatGPT.
summary.zh: 尼克回忆，自己加入 OpenAI 时它还只是研究实验室，第一个任务近乎琐碎，之后才参与把一个黑客松代码库做成了 ChatGPT。他分享了这款最初被认为会失败的产品——ChatGPT——的草创起源。本期提供了 ChatGPT 上线与规模化的幕后视角。

episodeTitle.en: Brian Chesky's secret mentor who scaled Airbnb (after dying 9 times & building a hotel empire)
episodeTitle.zh: 布莱恩·切斯基背后的“秘密导师”：如何将Airbnb扩展至全球（历经九次失败后建立酒店帝国）

bio.en: Chip Conley is a hospitality entrepreneur (founder of Joie de Vivre Hotels), former strategic advisor to Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky, founder of the Modern Elder Academy, and author on thriving at work as you age.
bio.zh: Chip Conley 是一位酒店业创业者（Joie de Vivre Hotels 创始人）、Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky 的前战略顾问、现代长者学院（Modern Elder Academy）创始人，也是关于“年长者在职场中茁壮成长”的作者。

guestBioOfficial.en: Chip Conley is the founder of Joie de Vivre hotels, the second-largest boutique hotel brand in the world. At age 52, he joined Airbnb as Head of Global Hospitality and Strategy, reporting to CEO Brian Chesky, who was 21 years younger. He earned the title of Airbnb’s “Modern Elder” by guiding the young founders on leadership and culture while learning Silicon Valley’s tech mindset himself. Today, Chip leads the Modern Elder Academy, the world’s first midlife wisdom school, and is the author of best-selling books like Wisdom@Work and Peak. He champions the idea that age and experience are assets—and that midlife can be a launchpad for renewed purpose and impact. *In this conversation, we discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 奇普·康利是Joie de Vivre酒店的创始人，该品牌是全球第二大精品酒店连锁。52岁时，他加入Airbnb担任全球酒店与战略负责人，向比他小21岁的CEO布莱恩·切斯基汇报工作。凭借在领导力和文化方面的指导，以及亲自学习硅谷科技思维模式，他赢得了Airbnb“现代长者”的称号。如今，奇普领导着全球首家中年智慧学院Modern Elder Academy，并著有《职场智慧》和《巅峰时刻》等畅销书。他倡导年龄和经验是宝贵资产的观点，认为中年可以成为重新追寻人生目标和产生影响力的跳板。 *在本次对话中，我们将探讨：*

summary.en: Chip shares what it was like joining Airbnb in his fifties as both mentor and subordinate to Brian Chesky, and why older brains connecting dots alongside fast young teammates is a superpower. He discusses founding the Modern Elder Academy, how a near-death experience changed his life trajectory, and how to build a great culture. The conversation is about success, meaning, and contribution in tech as you age.
summary.zh: Chip 分享了五十多岁加入 Airbnb、既当 Brian Chesky 的导师又当部下的经历，以及为何“年长大脑”与飞速的年轻队友连线是一种超能力。他谈到了创办现代长者学院、一次濒死体验如何改变人生轨迹，以及如何打造优秀文化。对话关于在年岁增长时，于科技行业中获得成功、意义与贡献。

episodeTitle.en: He saved OpenAI, invented the “Like” button, and built Google Maps: Bret Taylor (Sierra)
episodeTitle.zh: 他拯救了OpenAI，发明了“点赞”按钮，并打造了谷歌地图：Bret Taylor（Sierra）

bio.en: Bret Taylor is a legendary builder—co-creator of Google Maps, inventor of the Like button and real-time News Feed (sold to Facebook), former CTO of Facebook, co-CEO of Salesforce, and current co-founder/CEO of Sierra, an AI agent company, plus chairman of OpenAI's board.
bio.zh: Bret Taylor 是一位传奇构建者——Google Maps 联合创造者、Like 按钮与实时动态消息（卖给 Facebook）的发明者、Facebook 前 CTO、Salesforce 联席 CEO，现任 AI 智能体公司 Sierra 的联合创始人兼 CEO，并任 OpenAI 董事会主席。

guestBioOfficial.en: Bret Taylor’s legendary career includes being CTO of Meta, co-CEO of Salesforce, chairman of the board at OpenAI (yes, during that drama), co-creating both Google Maps and the Like button, and founding three companies. Today he’s the founder and CEO of Sierra, an AI agent company transforming customer service. He’s one of the few people I’ve met who’s been wildly successful at every level—from engineer to C-suite executive to founder—and across almost every discipline, including PM, engineer, CTO, COO, CPO, CEO, and board member. *In this conversation, you’ll learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: Bret Taylor传奇的职业生涯包括担任Meta的CTO、Salesforce的联席CEO、OpenAI董事会主席（是的，在那场风波期间）、共同创造谷歌地图和点赞按钮，以及创立三家公司。如今，他是AI智能体公司Sierra的创始人兼CEO，该公司正在变革客户服务。作为我见过的为数不多在每个层级——从工程师到高管，再到创始人——以及几乎所有领域（包括产品经理、工程师、CTO、COO、CPO、CEO和董事会成员）都取得巨大成功的人之一，在这次对话中，你将了解到：

summary.en: Bret predicts the whole software market will shift toward agents and outcome-based pricing, and reflects on lessons from creating Google Maps after an early product failure. He shares the mindset—“what's the most impactful thing I could do today?”—that powered success across wildly different roles. The conversation covers the skills and mindsets behind his range and why we're all still underestimating agents' impact on business.
summary.zh: Bret 预测整个软件市场将转向智能体和“按结果付费”，并回顾了在早期产品失败后打造 Google Maps 的教训。他分享了“今天我能做的最有影响力的事是什么？”这一心态，它支撑了他在截然不同角色中的成功。对话涵盖其多元成就背后的技能与心态，以及为何我们都仍低估了智能体对商业的影响。

episodeTitle.en: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam
episodeTitle.zh: 《为AI产品定价：400+家公司与50家独角兽的经验之谈 | 马德哈万·拉马努贾姆》

bio.en: Madhavan Ramanujam is one of the world's leading pricing and monetization strategists, a former managing partner at Simon-Kucher who has advised over 250 companies including 30 unicorns, author of Monetizing Innovation and its sequel Scaling Innovation, and now invests full-time in early-stage AI companies through his own fund.
bio.zh: Madhavan Ramanujam 是全球顶尖的定价与变现战略专家，曾任 Simon-Kucher 的管理合伙人，为包括 30 家独角兽在内的 250 多家公司提供顾问服务；他是《Monetizing Innovation》及其续作《Scaling Innovation》的作者，目前通过自己的基金全职投资早期 AI 公司。

guestBioOfficial.en: Madhavan Ramanujam is the world’s foremost expert on pricing and monetization strategy. As managing partner at Simon-Kucher, he helped over 250 companies, including 30 unicorns, architect their pricing strategies. He’s the author of the definitive book on pricing, Monetizing Innovation. Now he’s back with a sequel, Scaling Innovation, which reveals how to build enduring businesses by dominating both market share and wallet share. He recently left Simon-Kucher to launch his own fund, 49 Palms, focused on helping early-stage AI companies. *In this conversation, we discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 马德哈万·拉马努贾姆是全球定价与货币化策略领域的顶尖专家。作为西蒙-库彻管理合伙人，他曾为包括30家独角兽在内的250多家公司设计定价策略。他是定价领域权威著作《货币化创新》的作者，如今他推出续作《扩展创新》，揭示如何通过主导市场份额与用户忠诚度双重优势打造持久商业帝国。他近期离开西蒙-库彻，创立专注于助力早期AI公司的基金49 Palms。*在本次对话中，我们将探讨：*

summary.en: Madhavan argues that in the AI era, winners must master monetization from day one and resist anchoring customers on low price points like $20/month, because 20% of what you build drives 80% of willingness to pay. He introduces a simple two-by-two for picking a pricing model and explains why the coveted top-right quadrant is true outcome-based pricing, where you have both autonomy and attribution. The conversation covers how to gain pricing power, tactical negotiation advice, and the most common traps founders fall into that prevent durable, profitable businesses. He stresses that great founders must dominate both market share and wallet share—and that getting pricing right early is far cheaper than fixing it later.
summary.zh: Madhavan 认为，在 AI 时代，赢家必须从第一天起就精通变现，不能把客户锚定在每月 20 美元这样的低价上，因为你构建的东西里，有 20% 决定了 80% 的支付意愿。他介绍了一个用来选择定价模型的简单四象限，并解释了为什么大家都想要的那个右上角，是真正的“基于结果的定价”——既拥有自主权，又能清晰归因。对话涵盖了如何获得定价权、具体的谈判建议，以及创始人最常掉进去、导致无法建立持久盈利业务的那些陷阱。他强调，优秀的创始人必须同时拿下市场份额和钱包份额，而且尽早把定价做对，远比日后返工便宜得多。

episodeTitle.en: Anthropic co-founder: AGI predictions, leaving OpenAI, what keeps him up at night | Ben Mann
episodeTitle.zh: Anthropic联合创始人：AGI预测、离开OpenAI、让他夜不能寐的难题 | 本·曼（Ben Mann）

bio.en: Benjamin Mann is a co-founder of Anthropic, where he serves as tech lead for product engineering and focuses on aligning AI to be helpful, harmless, and honest.
bio.zh: Benjamin Mann 是 Anthropic 的联合创始人，担任产品工程技术负责人，专注于让 AI 做到有用、无害、诚实。

guestBioOfficial.en: Benjamin Mann is a co-founder of Anthropic, an AI startup dedicated to building aligned, safety-first AI systems. Prior to Anthropic, Ben was one of the architects of GPT-3 at OpenAI. He left OpenAI driven by the mission to ensure that AI benefits humanity. In this episode, Ben opens up about the accelerating progress in AI and the urgent need to steer it responsibly. *In this conversation, we discuss:*
guestBioOfficial.zh:
本·曼（Ben Mann）是致力于构建安全至上的AI系统的AI初创公司Anthropic的联合创始人。在创立Anthropic之前，本是OpenAI GPT-3的核心开发者之一。他因致力于确保AI造福人类的使命而离开OpenAI。在本期节目中，本将畅谈AI领域的加速发展以及负责任引导AI的重要性。
*本期对谈讨论议题：*

summary.en: Ben discusses why he left OpenAI—believing safety wasn't the top priority—and the urgency of aligning superintelligence before it's too late. He estimates a meaningful chance of hitting some form of superintelligence around 2028 and gives a non-zero probability of a very bad outcome, arguing we must “keep God in a box.” The conversation covers the war for AI researchers, how soon AGI might arrive, and candid advice for navigating a rapidly automating world.
summary.zh: Ben 讨论了为何离开 OpenAI——认为安全并非最高优先级——以及在为时已晚之前对齐超级智能的紧迫性。他估计在 2028 年前后达到某种形式超级智能的概率不小，并给出“极坏结果”非零的可能性，主张必须“把上帝关在盒子里”。对话涵盖 AI 人才的争夺、AGI 何时到来，以及应对快速自动化世界的坦诚建议。

episodeTitle.en: The AI-native startup: 5 products, 7-figure revenue, 100% AI-written code. | Dan Shipper (Every)
episodeTitle.zh: 《AI原生初创公司：5款产品、7位数收入、100%AI编写代码》| Dan Shipper（Every）

bio.en: Dan Shipper is co-founder and CEO of Every, a 15-person company building four products at the bleeding edge of what's possible with AI, with a head of AI operations automating the team's workflows.
bio.zh: Dan Shipper 是 Every 的联合创始人兼 CEO，这家仅 15 人的公司在 AI 可能性的最前沿打造了四款产品，并设有 AI 运营负责人来自动化团队工作流。

guestBioOfficial.en: Dan Shipper is the co-founder and CEO of Every. With just 15 people, Every publishes a daily AI newsletter, ships multiple AI products, and operates a million-dollar-a-year consulting arm—all while their engineers write virtually zero code. It’s the most radical example of AI-first operations, and Dan is a prolific writer who has become a leading voice on how AI is transforming the way we build and work. *Learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: Dan Shipper是Every的联合创始人兼CEO。仅用15人，Every每日发布AI新闻简报，推出多款AI产品，并运营着年营收百万美元的咨询业务——而其工程师几乎无需编写代码。这是AI优先运营的最极端案例，Dan也是一位多产作家，已成为AI如何改变我们构建与工作方式的领军人物。*学习：*

summary.en: Dan shares how his team operates at the edge of AI adoption, with a head of AI operations constantly building prompts and workflows that the whole team automates. He argues entry-level jobs aren't being taken—kids with ChatGPT will simply move far faster—and that organizations playing at the edge today are doing what everyone else will in three years. The conversation is a window into a near-future way of building companies.
summary.zh: Dan 分享了团队如何在 AI 应用的最前沿运作——设有 AI 运营负责人不断构建提示词与工作流，全员自动化。他认为初级岗位并未被夺走——用 ChatGPT 的孩子只会快得多——而今天在边缘探索的组织，正做着别人三年后的事。对话是一扇窥见“近未来公司运作方式”的窗口。

episodeTitle.en: Rapidly test and validate any startup idea with the 2-day Foundation Sprint
episodeTitle.zh: 通过为期两天的基础冲刺，快速测试并验证任何初创想法

bio.en: Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky are the co-creators of the Design Sprint and authors of Sprint and Make Time; in this conversation they share the 'Foundation Sprint,' a framework (from their book Click) for founders to clarify and test a startup idea before building.
bio.zh: Jake Knapp 与 John Zeratsky 是“设计冲刺”（Design Sprint）的共同创造者，也是《Sprint》和《Make Time》的作者；在本期对话中，他们分享了“基础冲刺”（Foundation Sprint）——出自其著作《Click》的一个框架，帮助创始人在动手之前厘清并验证创业点子。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky are the co-creators of the Design Sprint (the famous five-day product innovation process) and authors of the bestselling book Sprint. After decades of working with over 300 startups in the earliest stages, they discovered that most startups fail not because they can’t build, but because they build the wrong thing. The very beginning of a startup is your highest-leverage moment, and most teams waste months or years by skipping a few critical early questions. Jake and John developed the Foundation Sprint to help startups validate ideas and compress months of work into just two days. *What you’ll learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 杰克·纳普（Jake Knapp）和约翰·泽拉特斯基（John Zeratsky）是设计冲刺（著名的五天产品创新流程）的联合创始人，也是畅销书《冲刺》的作者。经过数十年与300多家初创企业的合作，他们发现大多数初创企业失败的原因不是因为无法构建产品，而是因为构建了错误的产品。初创企业的起始阶段是最高效的创新时刻，但大多数团队却因忽略关键早期问题而浪费数月或数年时间。杰克和约翰开发了基础冲刺，帮助初创企业验证创意，将数月工作压缩至仅需两天。*你将学到：*

summary.en: Jake and JZ present the Foundation Sprint as the missing manual for founders: a roughly two-day, 10-hour sprint where the core team aligns on who the customer is, what they're building, how it differentiates, and how to test it quickly with real prospects. They argue that the more AI-generated a product is, the more generic it becomes—so slowing down to think deeply about what makes it unique actually saves time long-term. Drawing on 300+ teams (Google, Microsoft, Uber, and more), they make the case that two days of focused alignment may be the highest-ROI days in your product's history.
summary.zh: Jake 和 JZ 把“基础冲刺”称作创始人的“缺失手册”：一个约两天、10 小时的冲刺，让核心团队就“客户是谁、在造什么、差异化何在、如何用真实潜客快速验证”达成一致。他们主张：产品越依赖 AI 生成，就越容易变得千篇一律——所以慢下来深度思考“独特之处”长期反而省时间。结合 300 多个团队（Google、Microsoft、Uber 等）的经验，他们认为这两天的聚焦对齐可能是你产品史上投资回报率最高的两天。

episodeTitle.en: I’ve run 75+ businesses. Here’s why you’re probably chasing the wrong idea. | Andrew Wilkinson
episodeTitle.zh: 我经营过 75 家以上的企业。以下是为什么你可能在追逐错误理念的原因。 | 安德鲁·威尔金森

bio.en: Andrew Wilkinson is co-founder and CEO of Tiny, a holding company often called the Berkshire Hathaway of the internet that owns over 40 businesses, and has started and run more companies than almost anyone.
bio.zh: Andrew Wilkinson 是 Tiny 的联合创始人兼 CEO，这家控股公司常被称为“互联网界的伯克希尔·哈撒韦”，旗下拥有 40 多家企业，他创办并运营过的公司数量几乎无人能及。

guestBioOfficial.en: Andrew Wilkinson is the co‑founder of Tiny, a holding company that quietly owns more than three dozen profitable internet and consumer brands, including Dribbble and the AeroPress coffee maker. Starting as a teenage barista and web designer, he’s created a portfolio approaching $300 million in yearly sales (and he was personally worth over $1 billion at one point)—all without ever raising venture capital. *In this conversation, you’ll learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 安德鲁·威尔金森是 Tiny 的联合创始人，Tiny 是一家控股公司，旗下拥有 30 多个盈利的互联网和消费品牌，包括 Dribbble 和 AeroPress 咖啡机。他从十几岁时担任咖啡师和网页设计师起步，如今创建的投资组合年销售额接近 3 亿美元（他个人财富一度超过 10 亿美元）。*在本次对话中，你将了解到：*

summary.en: Andrew shares strategies for coming up with a great business idea—advising first-time founders not to swing for the fences immediately and to “fish where the fish are” rather than enter repeatedly failed business models. He describes AI as a tireless $200-a-month employee that will massively change knowledge work, and grapples with whether all jobs eventually become a single prompt. The conversation also covers what he's learned about happiness, money, and building durable businesses.
summary.zh: Andrew 分享了想出优秀商业点子的策略——建议首次创业者不要一开始就全力冲刺，要“到有鱼的地方钓鱼”，而非进入那些反复失败的模式。他把 AI 形容为每月 200 美元、永不疲倦的员工，将极大改变知识工作，并思考所有工作是否最终都变成一句提示词。对话还涵盖他在幸福、金钱和打造持久业务方面的心得。

episodeTitle.en: Naming expert shares process for creating billion-dollar brands: Vercel, Azure, Windsurf, Sonos
episodeTitle.zh: 命名专家分享打造十亿美元品牌的流程：Vercel、Azure、Windsurf、Sonos

bio.en: David Placek is the founder of Lexicon Branding, the firm that pioneered the discipline of brand naming and created iconic names including BlackBerry, Pentium, Swiffer, and the Impossible Burger.
bio.zh: David Placek 是 Lexicon Branding 的创始人，该公司开创了品牌命名这门行当，并创造了包括 BlackBerry、Pentium、Swiffer 和 Impossible Burger 在内的标志性名称。

guestBioOfficial.en: David Placek is the founder of Lexicon Branding, a company that focuses exclusively on the development of brand names for competitive advantage. Lexicon is behind iconic names such as Sonos, Microsoft’s Azure, Windsurf, Vercel, Impossible Foods, BlackBerry, Intel’s Pentium, Apple’s PowerBook, and Swiffer. Over 40 years, David’s team has named nearly 4,000 brands and companies, employing over 250 linguists and pioneering naming innovation. *What you’ll learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 大卫·普拉塞克（David Placek）是Lexicon Branding公司的创始人，该公司专注于通过品牌命名为竞争优势而努力。Lexicon为Sonos、微软的Azure、Windsurf、Vercel、Impossible Foods、黑莓、英特尔的Pentium、苹果的PowerBook和Swiffer等知名品牌命名。在40多年的时间里，David的团队为近4,000个品牌和公司命名，雇佣了250多名语言学家，并开创了命名创新领域。*您将了解到：*

summary.en: A great brand name outlasts every other element of a company, so it deserves serious investment rather than a last-minute afterthought. Placek's team deliberately seeks names that provoke tension and polarization within a client's team, because comfort with a name usually signals it is not distinctive enough. He breaks the naming process into three steps—identify, invent, implement—and relies on small creative teams, linguists, and a proprietary "sound symbolism" engine rather than big brainstorms. For founders without those resources, he recommends a simple "diamond" exercise focused on behavior and experience, generating 1,000-plus directions without judging them, and choosing a bold name you won't immediately love. He also stresses that the .com is no longer critical and that the right name creates asymmetric and cumulative advantage in the market.
summary.zh: 一个伟大的品牌名比公司的其他一切元素都更长久，所以它值得认真投入，而不是临上线前才草草了事。普拉塞克的团队会刻意寻找能在客户团队内部引发张力和两极分化的名字，因为对一个名字感到舒服，通常意味着它不够独特。他把命名流程拆成三步——识别、发明、落地——依靠的是小创意团队、语言学家，以及一套专有的"语音象征"引擎，而非大型头脑风暴。对于没有这些资源的创始人，他建议做一个简单的"菱形"练习，聚焦行为和体验，先生成上千个方向、先别评判，最后选一个大胆、你不会一眼爱上的名字。他还强调 .com 已不再关键，而对的名字能在市场上带来不对称优势和累积优势。

episodeTitle.en: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products
episodeTitle.zh: 从ChatGPT到Instagram再到Uber：全球最受欢迎产品的幕后默默耕耘者

bio.en: Peter Deng is one of the most under-the-radar impactful product leaders in tech, having been VP of Product at OpenAI - where he oversaw ChatGPT Enterprise, voice, memory, and custom GPTs - and the first Head of Product at Instagram, plus leadership roles at Meta, Uber, and AOL.
bio.zh: Peter Deng 是科技圈最低调却最具影响力的产品领袖之一：曾任 OpenAI 产品副总裁（统管 ChatGPT Enterprise、语音、记忆与自定义 GPT），也是 Instagram 首任产品负责人，并曾在 Meta、Uber 和 AOL 担任领导职务。

guestBioOfficial.en: Peter Deng has led product teams at OpenAI, Instagram, Uber, Facebook, Airtable, and Oculus and helped build products used by billions—including Facebook’s News Feed, the standalone Messenger app, Instagram filters, Uber Reserve, ChatGPT, and more. Currently he’s investing in early-stage founders at Felicis. In this episode, Peter dives into his most valuable lessons from building and scaling some of tech’s most iconic products and companies. *What you’ll learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 邓波（Peter Deng）曾在OpenAI、Instagram、Uber、Facebook、Airtable和Oculus等公司领导产品团队，助力数十亿用户使用的产品问世——包括Facebook的News Feed、独立Messenger应用、Instagram滤镜、Uber Reserve、ChatGPT等。目前，他在Felicis投资早期阶段的创业者。在本期节目中，邓波深入分享了他在打造和扩展科技界最具标志性的产品与公司过程中收获的最宝贵经验。*你将学到：*

summary.en: Peter reflects on what it takes to build products from idea to billions of users, arguing that sometimes the product doesn't matter as much as price and ETA did at Uber. He shares his view that the best product people operate autonomously - if he's still telling you what to do in six months, he hired the wrong person - and discusses the five types of product managers. The conversation also covers the rising importance of AI integrations and what founders should know about building agentic products.
summary.zh: Peter 反思了如何将一个产品从想法做到数十亿用户，提出在 Uber 时真正决定成败的往往是价格与到达时间，而非产品本身。他分享了自己的理念：最优秀的产品人才能够自主运作——如果六个月后他还在告诉你该做什么，那就说明招错了人——并讨论了产品经理的五种类型。对话还涉及日益重要的 AI 集成，以及创始人构建智能体（agentic）产品时必须了解的事。

episodeTitle.en: AI prompt engineering in 2025: What works and what doesn’t | Sander Schulhoff
episodeTitle.zh: 2025年AI提示工程：哪些有效，哪些无效 | 桑德·舒尔霍夫

bio.en: Sander Schulhoff is the OG prompt engineer - creator of the first prompt-engineering guide on the internet - who partnered with OpenAI on the first and largest AI red-teaming competition, HackAPrompt, and now works with frontier labs on model security.
bio.zh: Sander Schulhoff 是“元老级提示工程师（OG prompt engineer）”——互联网上第一份提示工程指南的创作者——他曾与 OpenAI 合作发起首个也是规模最大的 AI 红队竞赛 HackAPrompt，如今与前缘实验室合作研究模型安全。

guestBioOfficial.en: Sander Schulhoff is the OG prompt engineer. He created the very first prompt engineering guide on the internet (two months before ChatGPT’s release) and recently wrote the most comprehensive study of prompt engineering ever conducted (co-authored with OpenAI, Microsoft, Google, Princeton, and Stanford), analyzing over 1,500 academic papers and covering more than 200 prompting techniques. He also partners with OpenAI to run what was the first and is the largest AI red teaming competition, HackAPrompt, which helps discover the most state-of-the-art prompt injection techniques (i.e. ways to get LLMS to do things it shouldn’t). Sander teaches AI red teaming on Maven, advises AI companies on security, and has educated millions of people on the most state-of-the-art prompt engineering techniques. *In this episode, you’ll learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 桑德·舒尔霍夫是AI提示工程领域的先驱。他在ChatGPT发布前两个月就撰写了互联网上首个提示工程指南，最近与OpenAI、微软、谷歌、普林斯顿大学和斯坦福大学合作完成了迄今最全面的提示工程研究，分析了1,500多篇学术论文，涵盖200多种提示技术。他还与OpenAI合作举办了首届也是规模最大的AI红队竞赛HackAPrompt，帮助发现最先进的提示注入技术（即让大语言模型做不该做的事情的方法）。桑德在Maven上教授AI红队技术，为AI公司提供安全咨询，并向数百万人传授最先进的提示工程技术。*在本期节目中，您将学到：*

summary.en: Sander explains how prompt engineering actually works and how his thinking has evolved, sharing lessons from building the first prompt-engineering guide and running HackAPrompt. He discusses the future of AI agents, why red-teaming and security matter more as models get more capable, and practical habits for getting dramatically better results from LLMs. The episode changed how Lenny himself uses large language models.
summary.zh: Sander 解释了提示工程究竟如何运作、以及他的思考如何演进，并分享了打造首份提示工程指南、运营 HackAPrompt 的经验。他讨论了 AI 智能体的未来、为何随着模型能力增强，红队与安全愈发重要，以及从 LLM 获得显著更好结果的实用习惯。本期改变了 Lenny 本人使用大语言模型的方式。

episodeTitle.en: How to build a team that can “take a punch” | Hilary Gridley (Head of Core Product, Whoop)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何打造一支能“承受打击”的团队 | 希拉里·格里德利（Whoop公司核心产品负责人）

bio.en: Hilary Gridley is head of core product at Whoop and the author of the sixth most popular post ever in Lenny's newsletter, 'How to Become a Super Manager with AI'; she previously held product leadership roles at Big Health and Dropbox.
bio.zh: Hilary Gridley 是 Whoop 的核心产品负责人，也是 Lenny newsletter 史上第六受欢迎的文章《如何用 AI 成为超级管理者》（How to Become a Super Manager with AI）的作者；她此前曾在 Big Health 和 Dropbox 担任产品领导职务。

guestBioOfficial.en: Hilary Gridley is the Head of Core Product at WHOOP and a passionate thought leader in leveraging AI to elevate product teams and management practices. With extensive experience tackling challenging problems in regulated industries and high-stakes environments, Hilary emphasizes the importance of building resilience and adaptability within teams. Previously, she was a senior director of product at Big Health and a senior product marketing manager at Dropbox. *In this episode, you’ll learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 希拉里·格里德利是Whoop公司的核心产品负责人，她热衷于利用人工智能提升产品团队和管理实践的水平。凭借在受监管行业和高风险环境中解决挑战性问题的丰富经验，希拉里强调团队培养韧性和适应能力的重要性。此前，她曾在Big Health担任高级产品总监，并在Dropbox担任高级产品营销经理。*在本期节目中，你将学习到：*

summary.en: Hilary gets deeply personal about the mental game of product leadership—how to keep the voices in your head from 'eating you alive,' how to help your team 'take a punch' and counter-program a feared narrative with action. She teaches tactics for dealing with hardship, why you should sometimes do the thing that will probably fail because it's important, and a reframe that at work you're usually not the protagonist. The conversation is packed with advice that makes you a better product leader, builder, and human.
summary.zh: Hilary 非常坦诚地聊了产品领导的“心理战”——如何不让脑中的声音“把你生吞活剥”、如何帮团队“挨一拳”并用行动去改写你害怕别人对你的叙事。她传授了面对困境的具体方法、为何有时你应该去做那件很可能会失败但很重要的事，以及一个重新框架：在工作中你通常并不是主角。这期对话充满能让你成为更好产品领导者、建设者和人的建议。

episodeTitle.en: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest and beyond | Bob Baxley
episodeTitle.zh: 来自苹果、迪士尼、Pinterest等公司的35年产品设计智慧 | 鲍勃·巴克斯利

bio.en: Bob Baxley is a designer and executive who built and led design teams at Apple, Pinterest, Yahoo, and ThoughtSpot over a three-decade career, shaping products used by hundreds of millions.
bio.zh: Bob Baxley 是一位设计师和高管，在三十年的职业生涯中于 Apple、Pinterest、Yahoo 和 ThoughtSpot 构建并领导设计团队，塑造了数亿人使用的产品。

guestBioOfficial.en: Bob Baxley is a design leader who has shaped products used by billions at Apple, Pinterest, Yahoo, and ThoughtSpot. During his eight years at Apple, he led design for the online store and the App Store, and witnessed the iPhone’s transformative launch while working under Steve Jobs. A student of history turned software craftsman, Bob discovered his calling after exploring photography, filmmaking, and music, ultimately recognizing software as the most powerful creative medium of our time. Bob champions the moral obligation designers have to reduce frustration in people’s daily digital interactions. *What you’ll learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 鲍勃·巴克斯利是一位设计领袖，曾在苹果、Pinterest、雅虎和ThoughtSpot等公司参与设计数十亿用户使用的产品。在苹果工作的八年间，他领导了在线商店和App Store的设计团队，并在史蒂夫·乔布斯手下见证了iPhone的变革性发布。作为一名从历史学者转变为软件工匠的鲍勃，在探索摄影、电影和音乐后，最终发现软件是我们这个时代最强大的创意媒介。他主张设计师有道德义务减少人们在日常数字交互中的挫败感。 *你将学到：*

summary.en: Bob offers a unique perspective that design is “imagining the future you want to live in and taking steps to make it real,” and that being design-led is different from being designer-led. He reflects on why Apple's design DNA had to be present from the start and the lessons of witnessing history there. The conversation covers why product people have an obligation to put positive emotional energy back into people's lives and how to build a lasting design culture.
summary.zh: Bob 提出独特观点：设计是“想象你想生活的未来，并采取措施使之成真”，且“设计驱动”不同于“设计师驱动”。他反思了为何 Apple 的设计基因必须从一开始就存在，以及在那里见证历史的教训。对话涵盖为何产品人有义务把积极的情感能量归还给用户生活，以及如何建立持久的设计文化。

episodeTitle.en: Anthropic's CPO on what comes next | Mike Krieger (co-founder of Instagram)
episodeTitle.zh: Anthropic公司的首席产品官谈未来发展 | 迈克·克里格（Instagram联合创始人）

bio.en: Mike Krieger is the Chief Product Officer at Anthropic, maker of Claude, and the co-founder of Instagram, one of the most influential product thinkers in tech.
bio.zh: 迈克·克里格（Mike Krieger）是 Anthropic（Claude 的开发者）的首席产品官，也是 Instagram 的联合创始人，是科技界最具影响力的产品思考者之一。

guestBioOfficial.en: Mike Krieger is the chief product officer of Anthropic and the co-founder of Instagram. After leaving Meta, he co-founded Artifact, an AI-powered news app that I absolutely loved, and joined Anthropic to lead product in 2024. *In this episode, you'll learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 迈克·克里格（Mike Krieger）是Anthropic的首席产品官，也是Instagram的联合创始人。离开Meta后，他联合创立了由人工智能驱动的新闻应用Artifact（我对这款应用赞不绝口），并于2024年加入Anthropic负责产品管理。*在本期节目中，您将学习到：*

summary.en: Mike reveals that over half - now ~70% - of Anthropic's pull requests are generated by Claude Code, forcing a re-architecture of their merge queue. He describes the Claude Code team building Claude Code in a self-improving loop as the most futuristic way of working. The episode offers a front-row view of product-building inside a leading AI lab.
summary.zh: 迈克透露，Anthropic 超过一半（如今约 70%）的合并请求由 Claude Code 生成，迫使他们重新架构合并队列。他描述 Claude Code 团队用 Claude Code 自我迭代地构建自身，是"最具未来感"的工作方式。本期让人近距离看到领先 AI 实验室内部的产品构建。

episodeTitle.en: Growth tactics from OpenAI and Stripe’s first marketer | Krithika Shankarraman
episodeTitle.zh: OpenAI和Stripe首位营销人员的增长策略 | Krithika Shankarraman

bio.en: Krithika Shankarraman was the first marketing hire and VP of Marketing at OpenAI, the first marketing hire at Stripe, and an early marketing leader at Retool, Dropbox, and Android at Google; she is now an Executive in Residence at Thrive Capital advising founders on marketing.
bio.zh: Krithika Shankarraman 是 OpenAI 的首位市场负责人兼市场副总裁、Stripe 的首位市场负责人，也是 Retool、Dropbox 以及 Google Android 的早期市场领袖；她目前是 Thrive Capital 的驻场高管（Executive in Residence），为创始人提供市场方面的顾问支持。

guestBioOfficial.en: Krithika Shankarraman was the first marketing hire at OpenAI and Stripe and led marketing at Retool. At OpenAI, she established marketing foundations for ChatGPT for consumers and enterprises, as well as their developer API platform. While at Stripe, she spent over eight years building and scaling their marketing function from scratch. An engineer turned marketer, Krithika brings a uniquely analytical approach to marketing. She currently serves as Entrepreneur in Residence at Thrive Capital, where she helps portfolio companies on all things marketing. *What you will learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh:
克里提卡·尚卡拉曼（Krithika Shankarraman）曾是OpenAI和Stripe的首位营销招聘人员，并曾在Retool负责营销工作。在OpenAI，她为面向消费者和企业的ChatGPT产品以及开发者API平台奠定了营销基础。在Stripe，她历经八年从零开始构建并扩展营销团队。作为从工程师转型为营销者的专业人士，克里提卡为营销工作带来了独特的分析思维。她目前在Thrive Capital担任驻场创业导师，助力投资组合公司解决各类营销难题。

*您将学到什么：*

summary.en: Krithika argues that while playbooks and frameworks exist for everything, real marketing still requires putting in the hours to deeply understand your customer rather than blindly copying what others do. Drawing on her time as the first marketing hire at OpenAI and Stripe, she explains that even for a product as magical as ChatGPT, marketing's job is to create 'use-case epiphany'—helping people realize what the product is actually for. She shares a four-step diagnostic approach to marketing, an 'anti-playbook playbook,' and what B2B companies can learn from consumer marketing. The episode also covers career advice for aspiring marketers and the essential marketing literacy that every non-marketer needs to build successful products.
summary.zh: Krithika 认为，尽管到处都有现成的打法和框架，但真正的市场营销仍然需要投入大量时间去深度理解你的客户，而不是盲目照搬别人的做法。结合她在 OpenAI 和 Stripe 担任首位市场负责人的经历，她解释说，即便像 ChatGPT 这样神奇的产品，市场营销的工作也是创造“用例顿悟”——帮助人们想清楚这个产品到底能用来做什么。她分享了一套四步诊断式的营销方法、一个“反套路手册”，以及 B2B 公司能从消费级营销中学到什么。这一期还涵盖了给有志于做市场的人的职业建议，以及每个非市场人员都需要具备、才能做出成功产品的市场常识。

episodeTitle.en: Unconventional product lessons from Binance, N26, Google, more | Mayur Kamat (CPO at N26)
episodeTitle.zh: 来自币安、N26、谷歌等公司的非传统产品经验 | 梅尤尔·卡马特（N26首席产品官）

bio.en: Mayur Kamat is the Chief Product Officer at N26, one of the world's top fintech startups, and was previously Global Head of Growth at Google and the first PM on Hangouts.
bio.zh: 马尤尔·卡马特（Mayur Kamat）是 N26 的首席产品官，N26 是全球顶尖的金融科技初创公司之一，他此前是 Google 的全球增长负责人、也是 Hangouts 的第一位 PM。

guestBioOfficial.en: Mayur Kamat is the chief product officer at N26—a $9 billion neobank serving over 7 million customers in 25 countries—where he leads product, design, data, and research. Prior to N26, Mayur was Head of Product at Binance, growing the crypto exchange to a peak $400 billion valuation. Earlier in his career, he built and scaled products at Google (Gmail Mobile, Hangouts), Microsoft, and travel unicorn Agoda. Learn:
guestBioOfficial.zh: 梅尤尔·卡马特是N26的首席产品官——这家市值90亿美元的新型银行在25个国家拥有超过700万客户，提供超过125,000种产品，是全球最受欢迎的项目管理工具。在加入N26之前，梅尤尔曾在币安担任产品主管，将这家加密货币交易所发展至市值400亿美元的巅峰。在职业生涯早期，他曾在谷歌（Gmail移动版、Hangouts）、微软和旅游独角兽Agoda开发和管理产品。学习：

summary.en: Mayur shares his biggest failure - leading Hangouts at Google with vast resources yet failing to build a great messaging product - and the lesson that strategy is overrated versus speed from hypothesis to data. He advises PMs to make experimentation scientific rather than opinion-driven. The episode is a candid look at product leadership at hyper-scale.
summary.zh: 马尤尔分享了他最大的失败——在 Google 手握海量资源领导 Hangouts，却没能做出一款出色的通讯产品——并得出教训：相比"从假设到数据"的速度，战略往往被高估。他建议 PM 把实验变得科学化，而非靠观点驱动。本期坦诚呈现了超大规模下的产品领导力。

episodeTitle.en: Microsoft CPO: If you aren’t prototyping with AI you’re doing it wrong | Aparna Chennapragada
episodeTitle.zh: 微软首席产品官：如果你没有用AI做原型，那你就做错了 | 阿帕纳·陈纳普拉加达

bio.en: Aparna Chennapragada is Chief Product Officer at Microsoft overseeing AI product strategy for productivity tools and agents, previously CPO at Robinhood and a long-time VP at Google (Lens, Search, Shopping, AR).
bio.zh: Aparna Chennapragada 是微软首席产品官，负责生产力工具与智能体的 AI 产品战略，此前曾任 Robinhood 首席产品官，以及 Google 长期副总裁（负责 Lens、搜索、购物、AR 等）。

guestBioOfficial.en: Aparna Chennapragada is the chief product officer of experiences and devices at Microsoft, where she oversees AI product strategy for their productivity tools and work on agents. Previously, she was the CPO at Robinhood, spent 12 years at Google, and is also on the board of eBay and Capital One. *What you’ll learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 阿帕纳·陈纳普拉加达（Aparna Chennapragada）是微软体验与设备业务的首席产品官，负责其生产力工具的人工智能产品战略，并参与智能助手的相关工作。此前，她曾在Robinhood担任首席产品官，在谷歌工作了12年，并担任eBay和Capital One的董事会成员。 *你将学到：*

summary.en: Aparna argues that even as models “eat” products, design and taste remain central, and introduces NLX—natural language as the new UX—with its own grammars and invisible UI elements. She describes B2B as like Jean-Claude Van Damme doing the splits across two moving trucks, and why PMs should still learn to code. The conversation covers why the PM role isn't going anywhere and how her team “lives in the future” to build toward what's coming.
summary.zh: Aparna 认为，即便模型“吃掉”产品，设计与品味依然核心，并提出 NLX——自然语言即新的用户体验——它自有语法和看不见的 UI 元素。她把 B2B 比作“让·克洛德·范·达姆在两辆行驶卡车间劈叉”，并解释了 PM 为何仍该学编程。对话涵盖为何 PM 角色不会消失，以及她的团队如何“活在未来”以面向将要到来的东西而构建。

episodeTitle.en: How Revolut trains world-class PMs: The “Local CEO” model, raw intellect & building wow products
episodeTitle.zh: Revolut如何培养世界级的产品经理："本地CEO"模式、原始智力与打造惊艳产品

bio.en: Dmitry Zlokazov is Global Head of Product at Revolut, the $60B+ finance super app, known for hiring and incubating some of the best product managers in the industry.
bio.zh: Dmitry Zlokazov 是 Revolut 的全球产品负责人，Revolut 是一家估值超 600 亿美元的金融超级应用，以招聘和培养业内最优秀的产品经理而闻名。

guestBioOfficial.en: Dmitry Zlokazov is the head of product at Revolut, the $45 billion fintech giant operating in over 50 countries, serving more than 50 million customers, and producing some of the world’s top product leaders. Dmitry shares his hard-won lessons, contrarian org design principles, and day-to-day practices that power Revolut’s relentless shipping velocity, culture of ownership, and unparalleled “wow” product experience. *What you’ll learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: 德米特里·兹洛卡佐夫（Dmitry Zlokazov）是Revolut的产品负责人。Revolut是一家市值450亿美元的金融科技巨头，业务遍及50多个国家，拥有超过5000万客户，并培养了全球一些顶尖的产品领导者。德米特里分享了他来之不易的经验、反常规的组织设计原则以及日常实践，这些为Revolut持续的高效交付速度、自主权文化和无与伦比的"惊艳"产品体验提供了支撑。*您将学到：*

summary.en: Dmitry explains Revolut's product philosophy: valuing raw intellect and unquenched hunger over experience, and never compromising on quality, UX, and aesthetics even when cutting features. He argues if a product is 99% done it's closer to 0% than 100%, and shares how the company produces and hires great product leaders. The conversation centers on ownership, solving painful problems, and making experiences “wow and lovable.”
summary.zh: Dmitry 解释了 Revolut 的产品哲学：看重原始智力和不屈的饥饿感甚于经验，即便砍功能也绝不妥协质量、UX 与美感。他认为若产品“完成 99%”反而更接近 0% 而非 100%，并分享了公司如何培养与招聘优秀产品领导者。对话聚焦拥有感、解决痛点，以及打造“惊艳且讨人喜欢”的体验。

episodeTitle.en: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)
episodeTitle.zh: Palantir如何打造终极创始人工厂 | 纳比尔·S·库雷希（创始人、作家、前Palantir员工）

bio.en: Nabeel S. Qureshi is a writer, researcher, and engineer who studied AI policy at the Mercatus Center and documented Palantir's distinctive product-management model.
bio.zh: 纳比尔·S·库雷希（Nabeel S. Qureshi）是一位作家、研究员与工程师，曾在 Mercatus Center 研究 AI 政策，并系统记录过 Palantir 独特的产品管理模式。

guestBioOfficial.en: *Nabeel Qureshi* is an entrepreneur, writer, researcher, and visiting scholar of AI policy at the Mercatus Center (alongside Tyler Cowen). Previously, he spent nearly eight years at Palantir, working as a forward-deployed engineer. His work at Palantir ranged from accelerating the Covid-19 response to applying AI to drug discovery to optimizing aircraft manufacturing at Airbus. Nabeel was also a founding employee and VP of business development at GoCardless, a leading European fintech unicorn. *What you’ll learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: *纳比尔·库雷希*是一位企业家、作家、研究员，也是Mercatus中心人工智能政策领域的访问学者（与泰勒·考恩共事）。此前，他在Palantir工作了近八年，担任前沿部署工程师。他在Palantir的工作范围广泛，从加速新冠疫情响应到将AI应用于药物发现，再到优化空客的飞机制造。纳比尔还是GoCardless（欧洲领先的金融科技独角兽）的创始员工和业务发展副总裁。*您将学到：*

summary.en: Nabeel explains Palantir's unusual PM model: only proven "forward-deployed engineers" could become PMs, screening for independent thinking and broad intellectual curiosity. He describes how these engineers embedded with customers to deeply understand problems before productizing. The episode is a fascinating study of a PM culture very different from the mainstream.
summary.zh: 纳比尔解释了 Palantir 非同寻常的 PM 模式：只有证明了自己的"前沿部署工程师"才能成为 PM，以此筛选出独立思考与广博智识好奇心的人。他描述了这些工程师如何深入客户现场、在产品化之前深度理解问题。本期是对一种迥异于主流的 PM 文化的精彩研究。

episodeTitle.en: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna
episodeTitle.zh: 我为何会默许自己创造了厌恶的环境？ | 杰瑞·科隆纳（Jerry Colonna）

bio.en: Jerry Colonna is one of the world's most respected executive coaches, co-founder and CEO of Reboot, and a former venture capitalist (Flatiron Partners) and author of Reboot and Reunion; he helps leaders do the inner work of becoming better humans.
bio.zh: Jerry Colonna 是全球最受尊敬的髙管教练之一，也是 Reboot 的联合创始人兼 CEO、前风险投资家（Flatiron Partners）以及《Reboot》《Reunion》的作者；他帮助领导者通过内在修炼成为更好的人。

guestBioOfficial.en: *Jerry Colonna* is a world-renowned executive coach, a former venture capitalist, and the co-founder and CEO of Reboot, an executive coaching firm that combines practical leadership development with deeper self-inquiry. With over 27 years of coaching experience, he has guided countless leaders through the challenges of scaling companies, building teams, and navigating the emotional complexities of leadership. Known for his radical-self-inquiry approach, Jerry helps leaders uncover the unconscious patterns that hold them back and empowers them to lead with authenticity, compassion, and clarity. *In our conversation, we cover:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: *杰瑞·科隆纳*是世界知名的执行教练，曾任风险投资家，现为Reboot公司的联合创始人兼CEO。Reboot将实用领导力发展与深度自我探索相结合。凭借27年的教练经验，他帮助无数领导者应对公司扩张、团队建设及领导力情感挑战。以激进的自我探索方法著称，杰瑞帮助领导者发现阻碍他们的无意识模式，助力他们以真诚、同理心和清晰的思维进行领导。*在对话中，我们讨论了：*

summary.en: Jerry challenges the entrepreneurial culture of bullshitting ourselves that 'everything's up and to the right,' and offers his piercing question—'how have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don't want?'—as a way to reclaim agency. He discusses the dangers of an unexamined 'growth mindset,' why self-inquiry and busyness are worth confronting, and a simple equation his team uses to cultivate great leaders. The conversation is unusually raw and human, and aimed at making you a better person, partner, and leader.
summary.zh: Jerry 质疑创业圈里“一切都在向右上增长”的自我欺骗，并抛出一个犀利的问题——“我如何共谋创造了那些我说自己不想要的局面？”——以此重新拿回主动权。他谈到了不加检视的“成长型思维”的危险、为何值得直面自我审视与忙碌，以及他的团队用来培养卓越领导者的一个简单公式。这期对话出奇地真实、有人情味，目标是让你成为更好的人、更好的伴侣与更好的领导者。

episodeTitle.en: Inside Devin: The AI engineer that's set to write 50% of its company’s code this year | Scott Wu
episodeTitle.zh: 深入德文：这位AI工程师今年将为公司编写50%的代码 | 吴斯科特

bio.en: Scott Wu is co-founder and CEO of Cognition, maker of Devin, the world's first autonomous AI software engineer that works like a remote engineer you collaborate with through Slack and a dedicated site.
bio.zh: Scott Wu 是 Cognition 的联合创始人兼 CEO，该公司打造了 Devin——全球首个自主式 AI 软件工程师，它像一个远程工程师，可通过 Slack 和专用网站与人协作。

guestBioOfficial.en: *Scott Wu* is the co-founder and CEO of Cognition, the company behind Devin—the world’s first autonomous AI software engineer. Unlike other AI coding tools, Devin works like an autonomous engineer that you can interact with through Slack, Linear, and GitHub, just like with a remote engineer. With Scott’s background in competitive programming and a previous AI-powered startup, Lunchclub, teaching AI to code has become his ultimate passion.What you’ll learn: • How a team of “Devins” are already producing 25% of Cognition’s pull requests, and they are on track to hit 50% by year’s end
guestBioOfficial.zh:
吴斯科（Scott Wu）是Cognition公司的联合创始人兼首席执行官，该公司推出了全球首款自主AI软件工程师——Devin。与其他AI编码工具不同，Devin就像一个可以通过Slack、Linear和GitHub与你互动的自主工程师，就像远程工程师一样。凭借吴斯科在竞技编程方面的背景，以及他之前创立的AI驱动初创公司Lunchclub，将AI教会编程已成为他毕生热爱的事业。

你将学到：• “Devin团队”已为Cognition贡献了25%的代码请求，预计到年底将达到50%

summary.en: Scott explains how Devin evolved from a junior-engineer-level tool into a production system used by many companies, and what building and managing AI agents teaches us about the future of software. He shares Cognition's philosophy on autonomy, the human-in-the-loop workflows that work, and why agentic engineering is becoming a must-have skill. The episode is a front-row view of the autonomous-software-engineer frontier.
summary.zh: Scott 解释了 Devin 如何从一个“初级工程师水平”的工具，演进为被众多公司投入生产的系统，以及构建与管理 AI 智能体为我们揭示了软件未来的什么。他分享了 Cognition 关于自主性的理念、行之有效的“人在回路”工作流，以及为什么“智能体工程（agentic engineering）”正成为一项必备技能。本期是对“自主式 AI 软件工程师”前沿的前排透视。

episodeTitle.en: The rise of Cursor: The $300M ARR AI tool that engineers can’t stop using | Michael Truell
episodeTitle.zh: Cursor的崛起：这款年营收3亿美元的AR/AI工具让工程师爱不释手 | 迈克尔·特鲁尔

bio.en: Michael Truell is the co-founder and CEO of Anysphere, the company behind Cursor, the AI code editor that reached $100M ARR in about a year and a half.
bio.zh: 迈克尔·特鲁埃尔（Michael Truell）是 Anysphere 的联合创始人兼 CEO，该公司打造了 AI 代码编辑器 Cursor，约在一年半内达到 1 亿美元 ARR。

guestBioOfficial.en: *Michael Truell* is the co-founder and CEO of Anysphere, the company behind Cursor—the fastest-growing AI code editor in the world, reaching $300 million in annual recurring revenue just two years after its launch. In this conversation, Michael shares his vision for the future, lessons learned, and advice for preparing for the fast-approaching AI future. *What you’ll learn:*
guestBioOfficial.zh: *迈克尔·特鲁尔*是Anysphere的联合创始人兼CEO，Anysphere是Cursor背后的公司——Cursor是全球增长最快的AI代码编辑器，仅在推出两年后就达到了3亿美元的年营收。在本次对话中，迈克尔将分享他对未来的愿景、经验教训以及为迎接即将到来的AI时代做准备的建议。*你将学到：*

summary.en: Michael describes Cursor's goal of inventing a new way to build software where engineers become "logic designers" specifying intent. He shares the counterintuitive finding that custom models power every magic moment, and that they initially hired too slowly. The episode is a candid founder's view of building the fastest-growing AI developer tool.
summary.zh: 迈克尔描述了 Cursor 的目标：发明一种构建软件的新方式，让工程师变成"逻辑设计者"，只需明确意图。他分享了一个反直觉的发现——每一个魔法时刻背后都有定制模型的支撑，且他们起初招人太慢。本期以坦诚的创始人视角，讲述了如何打造增长最快的 AI 开发者工具。

episodeTitle.en: Inside monday.com’s transformation: Radical transparency, impact over output, & the path to $1B ARR
episodeTitle.zh: monday.com内部转型启示：彻底透明、以影响力而非产出为导向，以及如何实现10亿美元年营收目标的路径

bio.en: Daniel Lereya is Chief Product and Technology Officer at Monday.com, having joined when the company was around 40 people and helped scale it to a public company with hundreds of thousands of customers.
bio.zh: Daniel Lereya 是 Monday.com 首席产品与技术官，在公司约 40 人时加入，助其扩展为拥有数十万客户的上市公司。

guestBioOfficial.en: Daniel Lereya, the Chief Product and Technology Officer at monday.com, shares how he and his team realized they were being outpaced by competitors and how that realization completely transformed how they operate and allowed them to build a global powerhouse, doing over $1 billion in ARR, with 245,000 customers worldwide. What you’ll learn:
guestBioOfficial.zh: monday.com首席产品与技术官丹尼尔·勒雷亚（Daniel Lereya）分享了他与团队如何意识到被竞争对手超越，以及这一认知如何彻底改变了他们的运营方式，最终帮助他们打造了全球巨头，实现了超过10亿美元的年营收目标，全球拥有24.5万名客户。您将了解到：

summary.en: Daniel shares the most counterintuitive lesson from scaling Monday.com: realizing competitors moved faster forced a shift in how the team thinks about product and operations. He advocates radical transparency—sharing everything with employees—which deepens partnership rather than demoralizing, and orienting all teams around impact. The conversation covers how a gift from competitors (“they showed us it's possible”) can reset ambition and execution.
summary.zh: Daniel 分享了扩展 Monday.com 最反直觉的一课：意识到竞争对手更快，倒逼团队改变对产品与运营的思维方式。他主张彻底透明——与员工共享一切——这反而加深伙伴关系而非打击士气，并让所有团队围绕“影响力”对齐。对话涵盖竞争对手的“礼物”（“他们让我们看到可能”）如何重设野心与执行。

episodeTitle.en: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1m developers in 4 months: Inside Windsurf
episodeTitle.zh: 如何在4个月内打造吸引超过100万开发者的神奇AI代码编辑器：Windsurf内部故事

bio.en: Varun Mohan is co-founder and CEO of Windsurf, a leading AI coding tool and main competitor to Cursor, which reached 1 million users within four months.
bio.zh: Varun Mohan 是 Windsurf 的联合创始人兼 CEO，Windsurf 是一款领先的 AI 编程工具、也是 Cursor 的主要竞争者，它在四个月内就达到了 100 万用户。

guestBioOfficial.en: Varun Mohan is the co-founder and CEO of Windsurf (formerly Codeium), an AI-powered development environment (IDE) that has been used by over 1 million developers in just four months and has quickly emerged as a leader in transforming how developers build software. Prior to finding success with Windsurf, the company pivoted twice—first from GPU virtualization infrastructure to an IDE plugin, and then to their own standalone IDE. In this conversation, you'll learn:
guestBioOfficial.zh: 瓦伦·莫汉（Varun Mohan）是Windsurf（前身为Codeium）的联合创始人兼首席执行官。这款由人工智能驱动的开发环境（IDE）在短短四个月内就吸引了超过100万名开发者，并迅速成为变革开发者软件构建方式的领军者。Windsurf取得成功之前，公司曾两次转型——先是从GPU虚拟化基础设施转向IDE插件，再转向自主研发的独立IDE。在本次对话中，您将了解：

summary.en: Varun shares what makes Windsurf unique, why they invested heavily in enterprise sales unusually early, and why agency is becoming the most important skill for engineers and product builders. He tells the origin story of pivoting from a GPU infrastructure company to a much bigger opportunity in AI coding tools. The episode is a sharp look at building a category-defining developer product in the AI era.
summary.zh: Varun 分享了 Windsurf 的独特之处、为何他们在很早阶段就异乎寻常地重投企业销售，以及为什么“能动性（agency）”正成为工程师与产品构建者最重要的技能。他讲述了从一家 GPU 基础设施公司，转向 AI 编程工具这一更大机会的起源故事。本期是在 AI 时代打造定义品类之开发者产品的犀利透视。
