episodeTitle.en: Everyone’s an engineer now: Inside v0’s mission to create 100 million builders | Guillermo Rauch
episodeTitle.zh: 如今人人都是工程师：v0如何致力于培养1亿名创客 | 吉列尔莫·劳奇

bio.en: Guillermo Rauch is the founder and CEO of Vercel, whose AI website builder v0 is one of the most popular in the world, and a legendary open-source engineer behind frameworks like Next.js and Socket.IO.
bio.zh: Guillermo Rauch 是 Vercel 的创始人兼 CEO；其 AI 建站工具 v0 是全球最流行的同类产品之一，他也是 Next.js、Socket.IO 等开源框架背后的传奇工程师。

guestBioOfficial.en: Guillermo Rauch is the founder and CEO of Vercel, creators of v0 (one of the most popular AI app building tools), and the mind behind foundational JavaScript frameworks like Next.js and Socket.io. An open source pioneer and legendary engineer, Guillermo has built tools that power some of the internet’s most innovative products, including Midjourney, Grok, and Notion. His mission is to democratize product creation, expanding the pool of potential builders from 5 million developers to over 100 million people worldwide. In this episode, you’ll learn: 1. How AI will radically speed up product development—and the three critical skills PMs and engineers should master now to stay ahead
guestBioOfficial.zh: 吉列尔莫·劳奇（Guillermo Rauch）是Vercel的创始人兼首席执行官，Vercel是v0（最受欢迎的人工智能应用构建工具之一）的开发者，也是Next.js和Socket.io等基础JavaScript框架背后的核心人物。作为开源领域的先驱和传奇工程师，吉列尔莫开发的工具为包括Midjourney、Grok和Notion在内的互联网最具创新性的产品提供了支持。他的使命是推动产品创作民主化，将潜在开发者的数量从500万增加到全球超过1亿。在本期节目中，您将了解：1. 人工智能将如何极大地加速产品开发进程——以及产品经理和工程师现在应掌握的三项关键技能，以保持领先地位

summary.en: Guillermo explains how AI is dissolving the line between roles—designers who can ship full products, PMs who can prototype to production—and why understanding how things work 'under the hood' still matters for steering models. He reframes taste as a developable skill built through 'exposure hours' trying lots of products, and predicts a future where 'AI becomes synonymous with software.' The episode is essential listening for understanding which skills to focus on as product development is reshaped by AI.
summary.zh: Guillermo 解释了 AI 如何消融角色边界——设计师能交付完整产品、PM 能做出可上线的原型——以及为何理解“底层原理”对驾驭模型依然重要。他把“品味”重新定义为一种可通过“沉浸时长”（大量试用各种产品）来培养的能力，并预言未来“AI 将成为软件的代名词”。这期节目对于理解在 AI 重塑产品开发之际该聚焦哪些技能，是不可错过的必听内容。

episodeTitle.en: OpenAI’s CPO on how AI changes must-have skills, moats, coding, startup playbooks, more | Kevin Weil
episodeTitle.zh: OpenAI首席产品官Kevin Weil解析AI如何重塑必备技能、护城河、编程、创业路径等 | Kevin Weil

bio.en: Kevin Weil is the Chief Product Officer of OpenAI, maker of ChatGPT, and has previously led product at Twitter, Meta's Novi, and Planet Labs.
bio.zh: 凯文·韦尔（Kevin Weil）是 OpenAI（ChatGPT 的开发者）的首席产品官，此前曾领导 Twitter、Meta 的 Novi 以及 Planet Labs 的产品。

guestBioOfficial.en: Kevin Weil is the chief product officer at OpenAI, where he oversees the development of ChatGPT, enterprise products, and the OpenAI API. Prior to OpenAI, Kevin was head of product at Twitter, Instagram, and Planet, and was instrumental in the development of the Libra (later Novi) cryptocurrency project at Facebook.
guestBioOfficial.zh: Kevin Weil是OpenAI的首席产品官，负责ChatGPT、企业产品和OpenAI API的开发。在加入OpenAI之前，Kevin曾在推特、Instagram和Planet担任产品负责人，还参与了Facebook Libra（后更名为Novi）加密货币项目的开发。

summary.en: Kevin argues the AI model you use today is the worst you'll ever use, because capabilities improve every couple of months. He describes OpenAI's mindset of building for the edge of current model abilities, knowing they'll soon be surpassed. The episode also reflects on his earlier Libra project and what it means to build inside the center of the AI storm.
summary.zh: 凯文认为，你今天使用的 AI 模型将是你这辈子用过最差的，因为能力每隔几个月就会提升。他描述了 OpenAI 紧贴当前模型能力边界去构建产品的思路，因为知道这些能力很快会被超越。本期还回顾了他早年的 Libra 项目，以及身处 AI 风暴中心意味着什么。

episodeTitle.en: Become a better communicator: Specific frameworks to improve your clarity, influence, and impact
episodeTitle.zh: 成为更出色的沟通者：提升清晰度、影响力和成果的具体框架

bio.en: Wes Kao co-created the Alt-MBA with Seth Godin, co-founded Maven (live cohort-based courses), and now runs her own course on Executive Communication and Influence.
bio.zh: Wes Kao 与 Seth Godin 共同创造了 Alt-MBA，联合创立了 Maven（实时 cohort 制课程平台），如今运营着自己关于“高管沟通与影响力”的课程。

guestBioOfficial.en: Wes Kao is an entrepreneur, coach, and advisor. She co-founded the live learning platform Maven, backed by First Round and a16z. Before Maven, Wes co-created the altMBA with best-selling author Seth Godin. Today, Wes teaches a popular course on executive communication and influence. Through her course and one-on-one coaching, she’s helped thousands of operators, founders, and product leaders master the art of influence through clear, compelling communication. Known for her surgical writing style and no-BS frameworks, Wes returns to the pod to deliver a tactical master class on becoming a sharper, more persuasive communicator—at work, in meetings, and across your career. What you’ll learn:
guestBioOfficial.zh: 韦斯·考（Wes Kao）是一位企业家、教练和顾问。她与First Round和a16z合作创立了实时学习平台Maven。在创立Maven之前，韦斯与畅销书作家赛斯·高丁（Seth Godin）共同创建了altMBA项目。如今，韦斯教授一门关于高管沟通与影响力的热门课程。通过她的课程和一对一辅导，她帮助数千名运营者、创始人和产品负责人掌握通过清晰、有说服力的沟通来提升影响力的艺术。韦斯以其精准的写作风格和直击要害的框架而闻名，她重返播客，为听众带来一堂关于如何成为更敏锐、更有说服力的沟通者的战术大师课——无论是在职场、会议中，还是在整个职业生涯中。你将学到：

summary.en: Wes shares how to communicate as an executive and increase your influence, built around George Bernard Shaw's line that the single biggest problem in communication is the illusion that it has taken place. She covers being specific instead of vague, earning trust through clarity, and why strong communication compounds across a career. The episode is a practical guide to a high-leverage skill most people underinvest in.
summary.zh: Wes 分享了如何以高管的方式沟通、提升影响力，其核心是萧伯纳那句名言：沟通中最大的单一问题，就是“以为沟通已经发生”的错觉。她涵盖了用具体取代含糊、通过清晰赢得信任，以及为什么出色的沟通会在整个职业生涯中产生复利。本期是关于一项大多数人投入不足的高杠杆技能的务实指南。

episodeTitle.en: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up")
episodeTitle.zh: 规划、构建和交付产品的更佳之道 | 瑞安·辛格（Ryan Singer，“Shape Up”创始人）

bio.en: Ryan Singer is one of the first hires at 37signals and, through 17 years building Basecamp, authored Shape Up, a distinctive alternative approach to building software centered on appetites rather than deadlines.
bio.zh: Ryan Singer 是 37signals 最早的一批员工之一，在 17 年打造 Basecamp 的过程中写就了《Shape Up》——一种以“胃口（appetite）”而非截止日期为中心的、别具一格的软件开发方法。

guestBioOfficial.en: Ryan Singer is one of the earliest employees and the former Head of Strategy at 37signals (the makers of Basecamp), where he spent nearly two decades refining a product development approach that helped the company build super-successful products with small teams. Based on these lessons, he wrote "Shape Up: Stop Running in Circles and Ship Work that Matters," and Ryan now works with companies of all sizes to help them escape the cycle of endless sprints, missed deadlines, and dragging projects. What you’ll learn:
guestBioOfficial.zh: 瑞安·辛格是37signals（Basecamp创始团队）的早期员工之一，曾担任战略主管近二十年。他在那里完善了一种产品开发方法，帮助公司用小团队打造出超级成功的产品。基于这些经验，他撰写了《Shape Up：停止无意义循环，交付有价值成果》一书。如今，瑞安为各类规模的公司提供支持，帮助他们摆脱无休止的冲刺周期、错过截止日期和拖延项目的困境。您将收获：

summary.en: Ryan explains how Shape Up differs from Scrum/Agile by using fixed appetites instead of deadlines, bringing design, engineering, and product together to shape a plan before building. He traces the method's origins in the early days of Basecamp and David Heinemeier Hansson's 10-hours-a-week constraint, and why it helps maintain a startup way of working as a company grows. The episode is essential listening for teams exploring alternatives to traditional agile.
summary.zh: Ryan 解释了 Shape Up 与 Scrum/敏捷的区别：它用固定的“胃口”而非截止日期，并在动手前让设计、工程与产品共同“塑形”方案。他追溯了这一方法在 Basecamp 早期、以及 David Heinemeier Hansson 每周仅 10 小时约束下的起源，并说明它如何帮助公司在成长过程中保持创业式的工作方式。对于探索传统敏捷之外替代方案的团队，本期是必听内容。

episodeTitle.en: How to win in the AI era: Ship weekly, embrace technical debt, ruthlessly cut scope, and more
episodeTitle.zh: 如何在AI时代胜出：每周发布产品、接受技术债务、无情地缩减范围等

bio.en: Gaurav Misra is the co-founder and CEO of Captions, a leading consumer AI app for generating and editing talking videos with over 10 million users, and was previously an early employee at Snap who led its design engineering team.
bio.zh: Gaurav Misra 是 Captions 的联合创始人兼 CEO；Captions 是一款领先的消费级 AI 应用，可用 AI 生成和编辑口播视频，用户超 1000 万，他此前是 Snap 的早期员工并领导其设计工程团队。

guestBioOfficial.en: Gaurav Misra is the co-founder and CEO of Captions, an AI-powered video creation company and one of the most successful consumer AI products in the world today. Previously he was a product leader at Snap, where he created the design engineering function and spent years helping develop features used by hundreds of millions of users worldwide. With a background in both engineering and design, Gaurav brings a unique cross-functional perspective to product development. What you’ll learn:
guestBioOfficial.zh: 加瓦尔·米斯拉是Captions的联合创始人兼CEO，Captions是一家AI驱动的视频创作公司，也是当今全球最成功的消费级AI产品之一。此前，他曾在Snap担任产品负责人，创建了设计工程部门，并花费数年时间帮助开发了全球数亿用户使用的功能。凭借工程和设计背景，加瓦尔为产品开发带来了独特的跨职能视角。你将学到：

summary.en: Gaurav walks through how a modern AI-native startup actually operates: every engineer ships a marketable product or feature every single week, they deliberately take on technical debt to move faster than big companies, and they run a hidden 'secret roadmap' alongside the public one because user-requested features are rarely a competitive edge. He reflects on what Snap taught him about building consumer/social apps—running with no PMs and letting designers run the show—and grapples with a world where AI-generated video is indistinguishable from real. The episode is packed with operating lessons for anyone building on top of AI.
summary.zh: Gaurav 拆解了一家现代 AI 原生创业公司的真实运作方式：每位工程师每周都要交付一个可上市的产品或功能；他们刻意承担技术债务，以比大公司更快的速度前进；并在公开路线图之外另设一条“秘密路线图”，因为用户提出的功能很少构成竞争优势。他回顾了 Snap 教给他的关于打造消费/社交应用的经验——不设 PM、由设计师主导，也直面了“AI 视频真假难辨”的世界。这期节目充满面向所有在 AI 之上构建产品者的运营经验。

episodeTitle.en: Superhuman's secret to success | Rahul Vohra (CEO and founder)
episodeTitle.zh: 《超人成功秘诀》| 拉胡尔·沃赫拉（CEO兼创始人）

bio.en: Rahul Vohra is the founder and CEO of Superhuman, the AI-powered email client, and a famously thoughtful and articulate builder who previously founded Rapportive, the first Gmail extension to scale to millions of users.
bio.zh: Rahul Vohra 是 AI 驱动电子邮件客户端 Superhuman 的创始人兼 CEO，也是一位以深思熟虑、表达清晰著称的构建者，此前曾创立首个规模化至数百万用户的 Gmail 插件 Rapportive。

guestBioOfficial.en: Rahul Vohra is the founder and CEO of Superhuman. Prior to Superhuman, Rahul founded Rapportive, the first Gmail plug-in to scale to millions of users, which he sold to LinkedIn in 2012. He is also a prominent angel investor, and his fund has invested $50 million in over 120 companies, including Placer, Supabase, Mercury, Zip, ClassDojo, and Writer. What you’ll learn:
guestBioOfficial.zh: 拉胡尔·沃赫拉是Superhuman的创始人兼CEO。在创立Superhuman之前，拉胡尔创立了Rapportive，这是首款扩展至数百万用户的Gmail插件，并于2012年将其出售给LinkedIn。他还是一位著名的天使投资人，其基金已向Placer、Supabase、Mercury、Zip、ClassDojo和Writer等120多家公司投资5000万美元。你将学到：

summary.en: Rahul reveals that there is no such thing as a truly viral product - only word-of-mouth and remarkability - and that great products deliberately ignore much early feedback to serve a narrow, passionate wedge. He shares his 'switch log' technique for reclaiming time from calendar tyranny, his long-time Transcendental Meditation practice, and why he hired a president to offload operations. The episode is a masterclass in deliberate, taste-driven building.
summary.zh: Rahul 揭示：并不存在真正“病毒式”的产品——有的只是口碑与“值得被谈论（remarkability）”，而伟大的产品会刻意忽略大量早期反馈，只为服务一个狭窄而狂热的小切口。他分享了自己挣脱日历暴政的“切换日志（switch log）”技巧、长期的超觉冥想（TM）练习，以及为何聘请一位总裁来卸下运营重担。本期是一堂关于刻意、凭品味驱动的建设的大师课。

episodeTitle.en: Inside Bolt: From near-death to one of the fastest-growing products in history | Eric Simons
episodeTitle.zh: Bolt内部视角：从濒临倒闭到史上增长最快的产品之一 | 埃里克·西蒙斯

bio.en: Eric Simons is the co-founder and CEO of StackBlitz, whose AI coding app Bolt became one of the fastest-growing products in history—hitting roughly $20M ARR within two months of launch and approaching $40M—after seven years of building the underlying WebContainer technology.
bio.zh: Eric Simons 是 StackBlitz 的联合创始人兼 CEO；其 AI 编程应用 Bolt 成为史上增长最快的产品之一——上线两个月即达到约 2000 万美元 ARR、并逼近 4000 万美元——而这建立在历时七年打磨的 WebContainer 底层技术之上。

guestBioOfficial.en: Eric Simons is the founder and CEO of StackBlitz, the company behind Bolt—the #1 web-based AI coding agent and one of the fastest-growing products in history. After nearly shutting down, StackBlitz launched Bolt on Twitter and exploded from zero to $40 million ARR and 1 million monthly active users in about five months. What you’ll learn:
guestBioOfficial.zh: 埃里克·西蒙斯是StackBlitz的创始人兼CEO，Bolt背后的公司——排名第一的基于Web的AI编码代理，也是史上增长最快的产品之一。在几乎倒闭后，StackBlitz在Twitter上推出Bolt，并在约五个月内从零用户跃升至4000万美元的年度经常性收入和100万月活跃用户。你将学到：

summary.en: Eric tells the story of Bolt as an 'overnight success seven years in the making': StackBlitz was nearly out of money until they realized their browser-based WebContainer tech was perfectly suited for AI products and launched with a single tweet. He credits the small, long-tenured core team as the real engine of their absurd growth, and argues that building technology first and finding the problem later was the right call for them despite conventional wisdom. The conversation is a window into the cutting edge of AI coding tools and where AI-native product building is heading.
summary.zh: Eric 把 Bolt 的故事称为“七年磨一剑的一夜成功”：StackBlitz 一度濒临破产，直到他们意识到自己在浏览器中打造的 WebContainer 技术特别适合 AI 产品，并用一条推文就发布了产品。他把这种惊人的增长归功于一支规模很小、共事多年的核心团队，并主张“先造技术、后找问题”尽管违背常规、对他们却是正确的选择。这期对话是观察 AI 编程工具前沿、以及 AI 原生产品构建走向的一扇窗口。

episodeTitle.en: Building Lovable: $10M ARR in 60 days with 15 people | Anton Osika (CEO and co-founder)
episodeTitle.zh: 打造可爱的产品：15人团队60天内创收1000万美元年营收 | 安东·奥西卡（CEO兼联合创始人）

bio.en: Anton Osika is co-founder and CEO of Lovable, an AI engineer that turns an English prompt into a working product in minutes, and the fastest-growing startup in Europe's history.
bio.zh: Anton Osika 是 Lovable 的联合创始人兼 CEO，Lovable 是一个把英文提示词在几分钟内变成可用产品的 AI“软件工程师”，也是欧洲史上增长最快的创业公司。

guestBioOfficial.en: Anton Osika is the co-founder and CEO of Lovable, which is building what they call “the last piece of software”—an AI-powered tool that turns descriptions into working products without requiring any coding knowledge. Since launching three months ago, Lovable hit $4 million ARR in the first four weeks and $10 million ARR in two months with a team of just 15 people, making it Europe’s fastest-growing startup ever. What you’ll learn:
guestBioOfficial.zh: 安东·奥西卡（Anton Osika）是Lovable的联合创始人兼CEO。Lovable致力于打造一款被称为"最后一块软件"的AI驱动工具——无需任何编码知识即可将产品描述转化为可用的成品。自三个月前推出以来，Lovable仅用15人团队就实现了首周400万美元年营收，两个月内达1000万美元年营收，成为欧洲发展最快的初创公司。您将了解：

summary.en: Anton explains Lovable's origin and his philosophy of the “minimum lovable product,” arguing that being loved by users—not just used—is the real growth driver. He hit $10M ARR in two months with just 15 people by obsessing over generalist, multi-skilled hires rather than narrow roles. The conversation covers a live demo, how the team operates and hires, and which skills will matter more or less as AI product-building goes mainstream.
summary.zh: Anton 讲述了 Lovable 的由来，以及他“最小可爱产品”的理念，认为被用户喜爱（而非仅仅使用）才是真正的增长引擎。他用 15 个人在两个月内做到 1000 万美元 ARR，秘诀是痴迷于招“通才”而非窄角色。对话包含现场演示、团队运作与招聘方式，以及在 AI 制造成主流后哪些技能更重要或更不重要。

episodeTitle.en: Notion's lost years, near collapse during COVID, staying small to move fast, building horizontal
episodeTitle.zh: Notion的迷失岁月、在新冠疫情期间濒临倒闭、保持小规模以快速发展、构建横向

bio.en: Ivan Zhao is the co-founder and CEO of Notion, the beloved all-in-one productivity and workspace tool used by millions, and a famously philosophical founder who rarely does interviews.
bio.zh: Ivan Zhao 是 Notion 的联合创始人兼 CEO；Notion 是一款被数百万人喜爱的“一体化”生产力与协作空间工具，他本人是一位以富有哲学思考著称、极少接受采访的创始人。

guestBioOfficial.en: Ivan Zhao is the co-founder and CEO of Notion. Ivan shares the untold story of Notion, from nearly running out of database space during Covid to finding product-market fit after several “lost years,” and the hard-won lessons along the way. What you’ll learn:
guestBioOfficial.zh: 伊万·赵是Notion的联合创始人兼CEO。伊万分享了Notion不为人知的幕后故事——从新冠疫情期间数据库空间告急，到历经“迷茫岁月”后最终找到产品-市场契合点，以及一路走来得来不易的经验教训。您将了解到：

summary.en: Ivan reflects on Notion's first three to four 'lost years'—pivoting from a too-ambitious 'everyone can build software' tool to a productivity app he calls 'sugar-coated broccoli'—and how hiding a big vision inside a form people cared about was the key. He shares the joy and suffering of building a horizontal product, his lean-and-craft approach and hard trade-offs, and a wild near-death story where Notion's single master database almost ran out of space during COVID. The conversation frames tools as extensions of ourselves that, once shaped, shape us back.
summary.zh: Ivan 回顾了 Notion 前三四年的“迷失岁月”——从过于宏大的“人人都能造软件”工具，转向他称之为“裹了糖衣的西兰花”的生产力应用，并认为把宏大愿景藏进人们真正关心的形态是关键。他分享了打造横向产品的喜悦与痛苦、精益与工艺的方法论及艰难取舍，以及一个惊险的濒死故事：疫情期间 Notion 唯一的主数据库差点空间耗尽。整场对话把工具视为自我的延伸——一旦被塑造，反过来也会塑造我们。

episodeTitle.en: Matt Mullenweg on the future of open source and why he’s taking a stand
episodeTitle.zh: 马特·马伦威格谈论开源的未来及他的立场

bio.en: Matt Mullenweg is the co-creator of WordPress, which powers about 40% of the internet, and the CEO of Automattic, the company behind WordPress.com, Tumblr, and WooCommerce.
bio.zh: 马特·穆伦韦格（Matt Mullenweg）是 WordPress 的联合创始人，该产品支撑了约 40% 的互联网，他也是 Automattic 的 CEO，该公司旗下有 WordPress.com、Tumblr 和 WooCommerce。

guestBioOfficial.en: Matt Mullenweg is the co-founder of WordPress, the open source platform powering a staggering 43% of the internet. He also serves as CEO of Automattic—the parent company of brands like WordPress.com, WooCommerce, and Tumblr—which is worth over $7 billion, with over 1,700 employees across 90 countries. In this episode, he discusses some of the most controversial topics surrounding WordPress, Automattic, and the broader open source community. What you’ll learn:
guestBioOfficial.zh: 马特·马伦威格是WordPress的联合创始人，WordPress是为互联网提供支持的开源平台，占据了惊人的43%的市场份额。他还担任Automattic的首席执行官——Automattic是WordPress.com、WooCommerce和Tumblr等品牌的母公司，市值超过70亿美元，员工超过1700人，分布在90个国家。在本期节目中，他讨论了围绕WordPress、Automattic和更广泛的开源社区的一些最具争议的话题。你将学到：

summary.en: Matt defends open-source ideals in his public battle with WP Engine, arguing the company diluted the WordPress brand through a "bastardized" managed version. He reflects on how 20+ years of goodwill were tested and why protecting the commons matters. The episode offers a candid look at the politics and principles of the open-source world.
summary.zh: 马特在他与 WP Engine 的公开较量中捍卫开源理念，认为后者通过"被篡改"的托管版本稀释了 WordPress 品牌。他反思了二十多年的口碑如何受到考验，以及保护"公共品"为何重要。本期坦诚呈现了开源世界的政治与原则。

episodeTitle.en: An inside look at X’s Community Notes | Keith Coleman & Jay Baxter
episodeTitle.zh: X社区笔记内幕解析 | 基思·科尔曼与杰伊·巴克斯特

bio.en: Keith Coleman and Jay Baxter lead Community Notes at X (formerly Twitter), the crowdsourced system that adds context and flags misleading posts across the platform.
bio.zh: 基思·科尔曼（Keith Coleman）和杰伊·巴克斯特（Jay Baxter）负责 X（原 Twitter）的 Community Notes 功能，这是一个通过众包方式为帖子补充背景、标记误导信息的系统。

guestBioOfficial.en: Keith Coleman (VP of Product) and Jay Baxter (founding ML engineer), the minds behind Community Notes, reveal how a small, scrappy team inside Twitter/X built the most trusted crowdsourced information system on the internet—one that’s changing the way we understand truth online. What you'll learn: 1. How Community Notes actually works—a deep dive into the groundbreaking algorithm that rewards “bridging agreement” instead of majority rule
guestBioOfficial.zh: 推特/X内部的Keith Coleman（产品副总裁）和Jay Baxter（创始ML工程师）——Community Notes背后的智囊团，揭秘如何在推特内部打造互联网上最受信任的众包信息系统，并彻底改变我们理解网络真相的方式。您将学习：1. 社区笔记的实际运作机制——深入解析开创性算法如何奖励“桥梁共识”而非多数规则

summary.en: Keith and Jay explain how Community Notes works: anyone can propose a note, and notes are rated by people who have historically disagreed, which keeps them neutral and accurate. They insist all of humanity should be eligible to participate - including elites, advertisers, and government figures. Independent studies show notes genuinely shift users' agreement with misleading claims.
summary.zh: 基思和杰伊解释了 Community Notes 的运作方式：任何人都可以提议备注，而备注由历史上观点相左的人来评分，从而保持中立与准确。他们坚持认为全人类都应可参与——包括精英、广告主和政府人士。独立研究表明，这些备注确实能改变用户对误导内容的认同。

episodeTitle.en: How to find work you love | Bob Moesta (Jobs-to-be-Done co-creator, author of "Job Moves”)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何找到热爱的工作 | Bob Moesta（Jobs-to-be-Done框架联合创始人、《Job Moves》作者）

bio.en: Bob Moesta is co-creator of the Jobs-to-be-Done framework (with Clay Christensen) and author of Job Moves, focused on helping people find careers and jobs that truly fit them.
bio.zh: Bob Moesta 是与 Clay Christensen 共同创立“待办任务”（Jobs-to-be-Done）框架的人，也是《Job Moves》一书的作者，专注于帮助人们找到真正适合自己的职业与工作。

guestBioOfficial.en: Bob Moesta, co-creator of the Jobs to Be Done framework, recently published a new book, Job Moves. Drawing from interviews with over 1,000 people about their career transitions, it offers a practical playbook for career development. In our conversation, we discuss: • The four different “quests” that drive career changes
guestBioOfficial.zh: Bob Moesta，Jobs to Be Done框架的联合创始人，近期出版了新书《Job Moves》。通过对1000多位职业转型者的访谈，该书为职业发展提供了实用指南。在对话中，我们探讨了：• 推动职业变迁的四种不同“探索之旅”

summary.en: Bob introduces his book Job Moves, built on interviewing over a thousand people who switched jobs and finding most ended up worse because they didn't know themselves well enough. He shares the tactic of taking a “jobcation” to reset between roles and distinguishes job features (salary, title) from job experiences that actually keep people engaged. The conversation reframes career transitions as progress moments and offers a practical lens for making better job changes.
summary.zh: Bob 介绍了他的新书《Job Moves》，基于对上千名跳槽者的访谈，发现大多数人因不够了解自己而跳到了更差的工作。他分享了在角色之间“放个职假”（jobcation）来重置状态的技巧，并区分了工作“特征”（薪资、头衔）与真正让人投入的“体验”。对话把职业转换重新框定为“进步时刻”，并提供了做出更好工作选择的实用视角。

episodeTitle.en: A founder’s guide to crisis management | Uri Levine (Waze co-founder, serial entrepreneur)
episodeTitle.zh: 创始人危机管理指南 | 乌里·莱文（Waze联合创始人、连续创业者）

bio.en: Uri Levine is co-founder of Waze (and nine other companies), has sold two companies for over $1 billion, sits on 20 startup boards, and authored Fall in Love with the Problem, Not the Solution.
bio.zh: Uri Levine 是 Waze 的联合创始人（以及另外九家公司的创始人），曾将两家公司以超 10 亿美元售出，任职于 20 家初创公司董事会，并著有《爱上问题，而非方案》（Fall in Love with the Problem, Not the Solution）。

guestBioOfficial.en: Uri Levine is a co-founder of Waze (which was acquired by Google for $1.3 billion in 2013), along with nine other companies (including another company he sold for over $1 billion). He’s also been on 20 boards and has been an advisor to over 50 startups. He recently released a new chapter of his best-selling book Fall in Love with the Problem, Not the Solution, which provides a guide to surviving crises at your company. In this episode, we cover: • The two types of startup crisis and how to handle them
guestBioOfficial.zh: 乌里·莱文是Waze（2013年被谷歌以13亿美元收购）的联合创始人，还参与了其他九家公司的创立（包括他以超过10亿美元出售的另一家公司）。他曾在20个董事会任职，并为50多家初创公司提供过咨询服务。近期，他发布了畅销书《爱上问题而非解决方案》的新章节，为企业应对危机提供了指南。在本期节目中，我们将探讨：• 两种类型的初创公司危机及其应对之道

summary.en: Uri goes deep on one powerful lesson: fall in love with the problem, not the solution, because the problem outlasts any single answer. Drawing on Waze and his dozen companies, he shares how to validate problems, stay flexible when evidence contradicts your plan, and why great founders are obsessed with the pain they're relieving. The episode is a focused, punchy distillation of hard-won entrepreneurship wisdom.
summary.zh: Uri 深入讲解了一条有力经验：爱上问题，而非方案，因为问题比任何单一答案都更长久。依托 Waze 和他的十余家公司，他分享了如何验证问题、在证据与计划相悖时保持灵活，以及为什么伟大的创始人痴迷于他们正在缓解的痛苦。本期是对来之不易的创业智慧的一次聚焦、犀利的提炼。

episodeTitle.en: OpenAI researcher on why soft skills are the future of work | Karina Nguyen
episodeTitle.zh: OpenAI研究员谈软技能为何是未来工作的核心 | 卡琳娜·阮

bio.en: Karina Nguyen is a research engineer at Anthropic, where she works on the cutting edge of building and improving Claude, and previously did front-end engineering.
bio.zh: 卡琳娜·阮（Karina Nguyen）是 Anthropic 的研究工程师，在构建与改进 Claude 模型的最前沿工作，此前从事前端工程。

guestBioOfficial.en: Karina Nguyen leads research at OpenAI, where she’s been pivotal in developing groundbreaking products like Canvas, Tasks, and the o1 language model. Before OpenAI, Karina was at Anthropic, where she led post-training and evaluation work for Claude 3 models, created a document upload feature with 100,000 context windows, and contributed to numerous other innovations. With experience as an engineer at the New York Times and as a designer at Dropbox and Square, Karina has a rare firsthand perspective on the cutting edge of AI and large language models. In our conversation, we discuss: • How OpenAI builds product
guestBioOfficial.zh: 卡琳娜·阮在OpenAI领导研究工作，曾在Anthropic为Claude 3模型开发培训后评估工具，创建支持10万个上下文窗口的文档上传功能，并为多项创新做出贡献。她在《纽约时报》担任工程师，以及在Dropbox和Square担任设计师的经历，使她对AI和大语言模型的前沿技术有着难得的第一手视角。在我们的对话中，我们讨论了：• OpenAI如何打造产品

summary.en: Karina explains how her love of front-end engineering evolved into AI research as she realized models could build apps themselves. She argues that creative, aesthetic judgment is still hard to teach models and remains a key human skill. The episode demystifies how large language models are actually created and where human taste still matters most.
summary.zh: 卡琳娜讲述了她对前端工程的热爱如何随着"模型能自己构建应用"的认知而转向 AI 研究。她认为，创造性与审美判断仍难以教给模型，依然是人类的关键能力。本期揭开了大语言模型真实构建过程的神秘面纱，并指出人类品味在何处最为关键。

episodeTitle.en: Tobi Lütke's leadership playbook: First principles, infinite games, and maximizing human potential
episodeTitle.zh: 托比·卢特克（Tobi Lütke）的领导力秘籍：第一性原理、无限游戏与最大化人类潜能

bio.en: Tobi Lutke is the co-founder and CEO of Shopify, one of the most respected operator-founders in tech, known for first-principles, infinite-game thinking.
bio.zh: Tobi Lutke 是 Shopify 的联合创始人兼 CEO，是科技圈最受尊敬、以“运营者—创始人”著称的人物之一，以其第一性原理、无限游戏式的思维闻名。

guestBioOfficial.en: Tobi Lütke is the founder and CEO of Shopify, a $130 billion business that powers over 10% of all U.S. e-commerce. Starting as a snowboard shop in 2004, Shopify has become the leading commerce platform by consistently approaching problems differently. Tobi remains deeply technical, frequently coding alongside his team, and is known for his unique approach to leadership, product development, and company building. In our conversation, we discuss: • Why complexity kills entrepreneurship
guestBioOfficial.zh: 托比·卢特克（Tobi Lütke）是Shopify的创始人兼CEO。Shopify市值达1300亿美元，支撑着美国10%以上的电子商务业务。Shopify最初只是2004年的一家滑雪板店，如今已成为领先的电商平台，始终以不同视角解决问题。托比始终保持着深厚的技术功底，经常与团队一起编码，并以独特的领导力、产品开发和公司建设方法而闻名。在我们的对话中，我们探讨了：•为何复杂性会扼杀创业精神

summary.en: Tobi shares his leadership playbook: thinking from first principles, treating business as an infinite game, and maximizing leverage by using the best tools and agents available. He discusses why craft, simplicity, and developer happiness matter, and how he approaches strategy and hiring at Shopify's scale. The episode is a masterclass in founder-led, conviction-driven operating.
summary.zh: Tobi 分享了他的领导手册：从第一性原理思考、把商业当作无限游戏、并通过使用最佳工具与智能体来最大化杠杆。他讨论了为什么工艺、简洁与开发者的快乐至关重要，以及他在 Shopify 这种规模下如何处理战略与招聘。本期是一堂关于创始人驱动、凭信念运作的大师课。

episodeTitle.en: Linear’s secret to building beloved B2B products | Nan Yu (Head of Product)
episodeTitle.zh: Linear打造备受喜爱的B2B产品的秘诀 | 余南（Nan Yu，产品负责人）

bio.en: Nan Yu is a product leader at Linear known for the team's belief that there is no trade-off between speed and quality when people are truly competent.
bio.zh: 南宇（Nan Yu）是 Linear 的产品负责人，以团队"在真正有能力的状态下，速度与质量之间并无折中"的信念而闻名。

guestBioOfficial.en: Nan Yu is the head of product at Linear, one of the most beloved and fastest-growing B2B SaaS products out there today, and the gold standard for high-performing tech teams. In our conversation, we discuss: • Why speed and quality aren’t actually at odds
guestBioOfficial.zh: 余南是Linear的产品负责人，Linear是当今最受欢迎、发展最快的B2B SaaS产品之一，也是高绩效技术团队的标杆。在对谈中，我们讨论了：• 速度与质量为何并非矛盾

summary.en: Nan argues speed and quality are not a trade-off - top crafters' output quality is visible in how fast they move. He describes having a working hypothesis tested internally within the first ~10% of a project's time. The episode covers how Linear says no to features to avoid bloat and keep ICs happy.
summary.zh: 南认为速度与质量并非折中关系——顶尖匠人的产出质量，正体现在他们推进的速度上。他描述了一个做法：在项目前约 10% 的时间内，就拿出可工作的版本、在内部验证关键假设。本期涵盖了 Linear 如何通过拒绝功能来避免臃肿、让一线工程师满意。

episodeTitle.en: An operator’s guide to product strategy | Chandra Janakiraman (CPO at VRChat, ex-Meta, Headspace)
episodeTitle.zh: 《产品战略操作指南》 | 钱德拉·贾纳基拉曼（Chandra Janakiraman，VRChat首席产品官，前Meta、Headspace高管）

bio.en: Chandra Janakiraman is Chief Product Officer and EVP at VRChat, formerly a product leader at Meta, CPO at Headspace, GM at Zynga, and senior PM at Amazon.
bio.zh: Chandra Janakiraman 是 VRChat 首席产品官兼执行副总裁，曾任 Meta 产品负责人、Headspace 首席产品官、Zynga 总经理，以及亚马逊高级产品经理。

guestBioOfficial.en: Chandra Janakiraman is the chief product officer, executive vice president, and a board member at VRChat. Previously, he was a product leader at Meta, where he led Facebook’s social experience interfaces and Reality Labs’ growth; served as CPO at Headspace, where he helped relaunch the platform, driving a 4x subscriber boost; and was a GM at Zynga, delivering massive hit games that reached hundreds of millions. In our conversation, Chandra shares: • His playbook for developing a product strategy
guestBioOfficial.zh:
钱德拉·贾纳基拉曼是VRChat的首席产品官、执行副总裁兼董事会成员。此前，他曾在Meta担任产品负责人，负责Facebook的社交体验界面和Reality Labs的业务增长；在Headspace担任首席产品官，助力该平台重启并推动订阅用户数增长四倍；还曾在Zynga担任总经理，打造了数亿用户的大型热门游戏。在对话中，钱德拉分享：  
• 制定产品战略的实用指南

summary.en: Chandra demystifies product strategy, arguing it isn't a born talent but a learnable process, and breaks it into “present-forward” problem-solving (2-year horizon) and big-“S” aspirational strategy (5–10 years). He shares a five-stage process to build alignment and why strategy must include an exciting view of the future. The conversation is a practical method for anyone who wants to get better at strategy.
summary.zh: Chandra 揭开了产品战略的神秘面纱，认为它并非天赋，而是可习得的过程，并将其拆为“面向当下”的问题解决（两年视野）与宏大的“aspirational”战略（5–10 年）。他分享了一个建立对齐的五阶段流程，以及为何战略必须包含对未来的激动人心的愿景。对话是任何想提升战略能力者的实用方法。

episodeTitle.en: 10 growth tactics that never work | Elena Verna (Amplitude, Miro, Dropbox, SurveyMonkey)
episodeTitle.zh: 十种永远行不通的增长策略 | 埃琳娜·维尔纳（曾任Amplitude、Miro、Dropbox、SurveyMonkey等公司增长负责人）

bio.en: Elena Verna is the Head of Growth at Lovable, the AI vibe-coding platform that surpassed $200 million in ARR within roughly a year of launch with a team of about 100 people.
bio.zh: Elena Verna 是 Lovable 的增长负责人，Lovable 是一个 AI vibe coding 平台，在发布约一年内、以约 100 人的团队实现了超过 2 亿美元的年度经常性收入（ARR）。

guestBioOfficial.en: Elena Verna is one of Silicon Valley’s most sought-after growth advisors and operators. She previously led growth at companies like Amplitude, Miro, Dropbox, and SurveyMonkey and is currently doing full-time advising for high-growth tech companies. In our conversation, Elena and I discuss: • 10 growth tactics that never work
guestBioOfficial.zh: 埃琳娜·维尔纳是硅谷最受追捧的增长顾问和运营专家之一。她曾在Amplitude、Miro、Dropbox和SurveyMonkey等公司领导增长团队，目前全职为高增长科技公司提供咨询服务。在我们的对话中，埃琳娜和我讨论了：• 十种永远行不通的增长策略

summary.en: Elena explains that in the AI era, product-market fit is no longer a one-time milestone but a recurring fight you must recapture every three months as both the underlying technology and consumer expectations shift rapidly. She shares Lovable's growth playbook: giving the product away for free and treating LLM costs as marketing spend, building a lively community on Discord, building in public, and embedding activation inside the product/AI team rather than a separate growth team. On hiring and culture, she argues AI-native new grads and failed founders are now the hottest talent, and that women risk being left behind in the AI wave unless we deliberately create on-ramps like Lovable's SheBuilds hackathons. She also reflects on work-life balance at a hyper-growth startup and why ruthlessly protecting personal boundaries is essential to doing your best work.
summary.zh: Elena 指出，在 AI 时代，产品市场契合不再是一次性的里程碑，而是一场每三个月就得重新抓住的持久战——因为底层技术和消费者期望都在快速变化。她分享了 Lovable 的增长打法：把产品免费送出去、把 LLM 成本当作营销开支，在 Discord 上建设活跃的社区，公开构建，以及把"激活"嵌入产品/AI 团队而不是单独的增长团队。在招聘和文化上，她认为 AI 原生的新毕业生和失败过的创始人现在是抢手人才，而女性若不加以刻意铺路（如 Lovable 的 SheBuilds 黑客松）很容易在这波 AI 浪潮中被落下。她还聊了超高速增长创业公司的工作生活平衡，以及为什么 ruthlessly 地保护个人边界，是把工作做到最好的前提。

episodeTitle.en: How to break out of autopilot and create the life you want | Graham Weaver (Stanford GSB professor)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何摆脱自动驾驶模式，创造理想生活 | 格雷厄姆·威弗（斯坦福商学院教授）

bio.en: Graham Weaver teaches a top-rated course at Stanford's Graduate School of Business and is the founder and CEO of Alpine Investors, one of the world's top-performing private equity firms; he helps people get off 'autopilot' and figure out what to do with their lives.
bio.zh: Graham Weaver 在斯坦福商学院开设一门高评分课程，同时是 Alpine Investors（全球表现最顶尖的私募股权基金之一）的创始人兼 CEO；他帮助人们摆脱“自动驾驶模式”，想清楚自己这辈子该做什么。

guestBioOfficial.en: Graham Weaver teaches a top-rated course at Stanford’s Graduate School of Business (GSB), where he often unexpectedly ends up helping students figure out what to do with their lives. He is also the founder and CEO of Alpine Investors, a people-driven private equity firm. In our conversation, we discuss: • Why everything worthwhile requires suffering
guestBioOfficial.zh: 格雷厄姆·威弗在斯坦福商学院（GSB）教授一门备受欢迎的课程，他经常在课堂上帮助学生找到人生的方向。他同时也是Alpine Investors的创始人兼CEO，这是一家以人为本的私募股权公司。在本次对话中，我们探讨了：•为何一切有价值的事物都需要经历磨难

summary.en: Graham shares practical frameworks for finding your path, including the 'genie' thought experiment (what would you wish for if any wholehearted pursuit were guaranteed to succeed?) and the 'nine lives' exercise. He argues that life is suffering, so you may as well choose something meaningful, and that everything you want lies on the other side of 'worse first'—the hard early days you must push through. The conversation also covers when to actually quit, and how to escape the autopilot mode most people live in. His advice comes from someone actively doing the work, not just teaching it.
summary.zh: Graham 分享了找到人生方向的实用框架，包括“神灯精灵”思维实验（如果任何全身心的追求都 guaranteed 成功，你会许什么愿？）和“九条命”练习。他主张人生本就充满苦难，所以不如选择有意义的事；你想要的一切都在“先苦后甜”的另一侧——你必须熬过那些艰难的开头。对话还涵盖了究竟何时该放弃，以及如何摆脱大多数人都在过的“自动驾驶”模式。他的建议来自一个真正在做事、而非只教书的人。

episodeTitle.en: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)
episodeTitle.zh: 创始人背后的故事：德鲁·休斯顿（Drew Houston，Dropbox）

bio.en: Drew Houston is co-founder and CEO of Dropbox, which he's built over 18 years through three eras—hypergrowth, attacks from Big Tech incumbents, and a painful reinvention toward productivity.
bio.zh: Drew Houston 是 Dropbox 联合创始人兼 CEO，18 年来他将公司经历了三个时代——超高速增长、来自科技巨头的围剿，以及痛苦地向生产力方向重塑。

guestBioOfficial.en: Drew Houston is the co-founder and CEO of Dropbox. Under his leadership, Dropbox has grown from a simple idea to a service used by over 700 million registered users globally, with a valuation exceeding $9 billion. Drew has led Dropbox through multiple phases, from explosive viral growth, to battling all the tech giants at once, to reinventing the company for the future of work. In our conversation, he opens up about: •  The three eras of Dropbox’s growth and evolution
guestBioOfficial.zh:
德鲁·休斯顿是Dropbox的联合创始人兼首席执行官。在他的领导下，Dropbox从一个简单的想法发展成为全球7亿多注册用户使用的服务，估值超过90亿美元。德鲁带领Dropbox经历了多个阶段，从爆炸式病毒式增长，到同时与所有科技巨头竞争，再到为未来的工作重塑公司。在我们的对话中，他将畅谈：
• Dropbox增长和演进的三个时代

summary.en: Drew reflects on Dropbox's three eras: early 10x hypergrowth, then near-death competition as Apple, Microsoft, and Google launched rival products (Google Photos' free storage “nuked” their model), and a forced pivot to productivity. He shares the emotional toll—employees not wanting to wear the shirt, the narrative flipping—and the lessons of resilience and reinvention under existential threat. The conversation is a candid founder's story of surviving platform shifts and staying alive.
summary.zh: Drew 回顾了 Dropbox 的三个时代：早期十倍超增长，接着是苹果、微软、谷歌推出竞品带来的濒死竞争（Google Photos 的免费存储“核平”了他们的模式），以及被迫向生产力转型。他分享了其中的情感代价——员工不愿穿公司 T 恤、叙事反转——以及在生存威胁下韧性与重塑的教训。对话是一位创始人坦诚讲述如何在平台变迁中存活下来。

episodeTitle.en: Scripts for navigating difficult conversations | Alisa Cohn (executive coach)
episodeTitle.zh: 应对艰难对话的剧本 | 阿莉莎·科恩（Alisa Cohn，执行教练）

bio.en: Alisa Cohn is an executive coach who has worked with C-suite leaders at startups like Etsy, Venmo, and DraftKings as well as Fortune 500s like Microsoft and Google, and has been named one of the world's top startup coaches.
bio.zh: Alisa Cohn 是一位高管教练，曾辅导 Etsy、Venmo、DraftKings 等初创公司以及微软、谷歌等世界 500 强企业的高管，被誉为全球顶尖的初创公司教练之一。

guestBioOfficial.en: Alisa Cohn is an executive coach who has worked with C-suite executives at startups like Venmo, Etsy, Wirecutter, and DraftKings, and Fortune 500 companies like Microsoft, Google, Pfizer, Dell, and IBM. Inc. Magazine named Alisa one of the top 100 leadership speakers, and she was named one of the Top 50 coaches in the world by Thinkers50 and the #1 startup coach for the past four years by Global Gurus. She is also the author of From Start-Up to Grown-Up, which won the 2022 Independent Press Award and the American Book Fest 2023 Best Book Award for Entrepreneurship, and is the creator and host of a podcast of the same name. In our conversation, we discuss: • The psychology behind why we avoid difficult conversations
guestBioOfficial.zh:
艾丽莎·科恩（Alisa Cohn）是一位高管教练，曾与Venmo、Etsy、Wirecutter和DraftKings等初创公司的高管，以及微软、谷歌、辉瑞、戴尔和IBM等《财富》500强公司的C级高管合作。《Inc.》杂志将艾丽莎评为全球百位领导力演讲者之一，Thinkers50将她列为全球前50位教练，而Global Gurus则连续四年将她评为头号初创公司教练。她还著有《从初创到成熟》一书，该书荣获2022年独立出版社奖和2023年美国图书节创业类最佳图书奖，并创办了同名播客节目。在我们的对谈中，我们将探讨：  
• 我们为何回避艰难对话的心理机制

summary.en: Alisa shares specific language for having difficult conversations, such as delivering a tough “no promotion” message while preserving hope and the employee's growth. She pushes back on the idea that a leader's job is to make everyone happy, arguing that driving toward results sometimes requires uncomfortable feedback. The conversation also covers practical tactics for running more effective meetings and a simple three-question routine to close them well.
summary.zh: Alisa 分享了进行困难对话的具体话术，例如在告知“不予晋升”时如何保留希望与员工的成长空间。她反对“领导的工作是让所有人开心”的观念，认为达成结果有时需要让人不适的反馈。对话还包含让会议更高效的实用技巧，以及用三个问题漂亮收尾会议的方法。

episodeTitle.en: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO at Confluent)
episodeTitle.zh: 优秀的AI产品为何都离不开数据 | 肖恩·克洛斯（Confluent首席产品官）

bio.en: Shaun Clowes is Chief Product Officer at Confluent, previously CPO at MuleSoft (a billion-dollar business within Salesforce), CPO at Metromile, and a six-year Atlassian veteran who built the first-ever B2B growth team and created two popular Reforge courses.
bio.zh: Shaun Clowes 是 Confluent 的首席产品官（CPO），此前曾任 MuleSoft（Salesforce 内部一家十亿美元级企业）的 CPO、Metromile 的 CPO，并在 Atlassian 任职六年，打造了史上首个 B2B 增长团队，还创建了两门广受欢迎的 Reforge 课程。

guestBioOfficial.en: Shaun Clowes is the chief product officer at Confluent and former CPO at Salesforce’s MuleSoft and at Metromile. He was also the first head of growth at Atlassian, where he led product for Jira Agile and built the first-ever B2B growth team. In our conversation, we discuss: • Why most PMs are bad, and how to fix this
guestBioOfficial.zh: 肖恩·克洛斯（Shaun Clowes）是Confluent的首席产品官，曾任Salesforce旗下MuleSoft和Metromile的首席产品官。他还是Atlassian首位增长业务负责人，负责Jira Agile产品并组建了首个B2B增长团队。在我们的对话中，我们探讨了：•为何大多数产品经理表现不佳，以及如何改善这一现状

summary.en: Shaun combines tactical execution with strategic framing, sharing lessons from building retention/engagement and data-for-PMs courses and leading product at multiple enterprises. He discusses how to think about retention and engagement as systems, the role of data in product decisions, and how to operate effectively as a CPO across very different company stages. The episode is packed with frameworks for product leaders scaling complex B2B businesses.
summary.zh: Shaun 将战术执行与战略框架相结合，分享了他在打造“留存/参与”与“面向 PM 的数据”课程、并在多家企业领导产品中的经验。他讨论了如何将留存与参与视为系统、数据在产品决策中的作用，以及作为 CPO 如何在不同阶段的公司中有效运作。本期为正在规模化复杂 B2B 业务的产品领导者，提供了满满的框架。

episodeTitle.en: Behind the founder: Marc Benioff
episodeTitle.zh: 创始人背后的故事：马克·贝尼奥夫

bio.en: Marc Benioff is the founder, chairman, and CEO of Salesforce, the cloud CRM pioneer he started in 1999 that grew into one of the world's largest enterprise software companies.
bio.zh: 马克·贝尼奥夫（Marc Benioff）是 Salesforce 的创始人、董事长兼 CEO，这家云 CRM 先驱公司始于 1999 年，已成长为全球最大的企业软件公司之一。

guestBioOfficial.en: Marc Benioff is the co-founder and CEO of Salesforce, the second-largest software company in the world. He started programming at age 15, selling his first program for $75, and went on to build Salesforce into a company worth more than $300 billion that also owns Slack, Tableau, Quip, and MuleSoft. Marc is known as a marketing legend, and is now leading Salesforce into the era of AI agents. In our conversation, we discuss: • The importance of maintaining a beginner’s mind
guestBioOfficial.zh: 马克·贝尼奥夫是Salesforce的联合创始人兼CEO，Salesforce是全球第二大软件公司。他15岁开始编程，首次出售程序时售价75美元，后来将Salesforce打造为市值超3000亿美元的公司，旗下还拥有Slack、Tableau、Quip和MuleSoft等产品。马克被誉为营销传奇人物，如今正引领Salesforce迈入AI智能助手时代。在对话中，我们将探讨：•保持初学者心态的重要性

summary.en: Marc shares his philosophy of compassionate, stakeholder-centered capitalism and how Salesforce pioneered cloud software and the "1-1-1" philanthropy model. He discusses leading through massive scale, the role of trust as the #1 value, and how to keep innovating as a large company. The episode is a rare look at building and running an enduring tech institution.
summary.zh: 马克分享了他"以人为本、兼顾各方利益相关者"的资本主义理念，以及 Salesforce 如何开创云软件与"1-1-1"慈善模式。他探讨了在巨大规模下如何领导、为何把"信任"作为第一价值观，以及大公司如何持续创新。本期罕见地展示了如何构建并运营一家经久不衰的科技机构。

episodeTitle.en: How Shopify builds a high-intensity culture | Farhan Thawar (VP and Head of Eng)
episodeTitle.zh: Shopify如何打造高强度文化 | 法尔汉·塔瓦尔（VP兼工程总监）

bio.en: Farhan Thawar is Vice President and Head of Engineering at Shopify, where he helps run a 10,000-person fully-remote engineering organization known for its urgency, velocity, and first-principles thinking.
bio.zh: Farhan Thawar 是 Shopify 的工程副总裁兼工程负责人，管理着一支 1 万人、完全远程的工程组织，该组织以紧迫感、高速执行和第一性原理式的思考著称。

guestBioOfficial.en: Farhan Thawar is the head of engineering at Shopify, where he oversees more than 1,000 engineers and a platform that powers over 10% of all U.S. e-commerce. Before Shopify, he was VP of engineering at Pivotal Labs and Xtreme Labs, and co-founder of Helpful.com. In our conversation, Farhan shares: • Why choosing the harder path leads to better outcomes
guestBioOfficial.zh: 法尔汉·塔瓦尔是Shopify的工程总监，负责管理1,000多名工程师和一个为美国10%以上电商提供支持的平台。在加入Shopify之前，他曾在Pivotal Labs和Xtreme Labs担任工程副总裁，并是Helpful.com的联合创始人。在我们的对话中，法尔汉分享了：•为何选择更艰难的道路会带来更好的结果

summary.en: Farhan shares concrete tactics for maintaining intensity and urgency at scale, including unusual meeting cadences, a constant drive to delete code (their 'Delete Code Club'), and the counterintuitive power of pair programming. He advocates 'creating intensity' by doing more per minute rather than more hours, and explains why he defaults to the harder option when choosing between paths because it ultimately makes life easier. He also offers sharp hiring advice—including how Shopify plans to bring on over a thousand engineering interns—and reflects on a career of working alongside a different billionaire each decade.
summary.zh: Farhan 分享了在规模化下保持强度与紧迫感的具体做法，包括独特的会议节奏、持续删代码的“删代码俱乐部”，以及结对编程那种反直觉的力量。他主张通过“每分钟做更多”而非“工时更长”来制造强度，并解释为何在两个选项之间他默认选择更难的那条路，因为它最终让人生更轻松。他还给出了犀利的招聘建议——包括 Shopify 计划招募上千名工程实习生，并回顾了自己“每十年换一位亿万富翁老板”的职业生涯。

episodeTitle.en: Behind the product: Duolingo streaks | Jackson Shuttleworth (Group PM, Retention Team)
episodeTitle.zh: 产品背后的故事：Duolingo的学习连胜 | 杰克逊·沙特尔沃斯（Group PM，留存团队）

bio.en: Jackson Shuttleworth is a group product manager at Duolingo, where he leads the retention team and owns the streaks feature—arguably the single most impactful driver of Duolingo's growth into a $14B business.
bio.zh: Jackson Shuttleworth 是 Duolingo 的集团产品经理，领导留存团队并负责“连续打卡”（streaks）功能——这可以说是推动 Duolingo 成长为 140 亿美元公司的最具影响力的单一功能。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jackson Shuttleworth is a Group PM at Duolingo, where he leads the retention team and the powerful streak feature. The streak feature, which gamifies consecutive days of learning, has been Duolingo’s most important and innovative growth lever and a key driver of their growth to a $14 billion business with almost 600 million users. In our conversation, we dive deep into the history and lessons of this feature: • The evolution of the streak feature
guestBioOfficial.zh: 杰克逊·沙特尔沃斯是Duolingo的Group PM，负责领导留存团队和强大的学习连胜功能。学习连胜功能通过将连续学习天数游戏化，为Duolingo提供了最重要且最具创新性的增长杠杆，也是其发展至市值140亿美元、拥有近6亿用户的关键驱动力。我们的对话深入探讨了该功能的演变历程及经验教训：• 学习连胜功能的演变

summary.en: Jackson walks through the entire journey of Duolingo's streaks feature—the wins, the wrong turns, and the 600+ experiments his team has run on it over four years—showing why it became the company's biggest growth lever (9M+ users now hold year-plus streaks). He shares what they learned about human motivation, the copy-testing infrastructure that lets them experiment constantly, and the psychology of habit-forming design. It's a deep, single-feature case study in how one mechanic can create billions in value.
summary.zh: Jackson 完整复盘了 Duolingo “连续打卡”功能的历程——成功、走错的弯路，以及团队四年里在它身上跑过的 600 多次实验，说明了为何它成了公司最大的增长杠杆（如今 900 多万用户保持着一年以上的连续打卡）。他分享了关于人类动机的洞见、让他们能持续实验的文案测试基础设施，以及习惯养成设计背后的心理学。这是一期关于“一个机制如何创造数十亿美元价值”的、聚焦单一功能的深度案例研究。

episodeTitle.en: Seth Godin's best tactics for building remarkable products, strategies, brands and more
episodeTitle.zh: 赛斯·戈丁（Seth Godin）打造卓越产品、战略、品牌等的绝佳策略

bio.en: Seth Godin is a marketer, teacher, entrepreneur, and author of more than 20 books, including Purple Cow, Permission Marketing, and Linchpin.
bio.zh: 赛斯·戈丁（Seth Godin）是营销思想家、教育者和创业者，著有《紫牛》《许可营销》《支点》等 20 余部作品，并通过长期写作持续影响人们对营销、品牌、产品与改变的理解。

guestBioOfficial.en: Seth Godin is a legend. He’s a marketer, teacher, entrepreneur, and author of more than 20 books, including Purple Cow, Permission Marketing, and Linchpin. He also writes one of the most popular and longest-running blogs in the world (approaching publishing 10,000 in a row!) and continues to shape how we think about marketing, brand, product, and creating lasting change in the world. In our conversation, we discuss: • How to build remarkable products that spread
guestBioOfficial.zh: 赛斯·戈丁（Seth Godin）堪称传奇人物。他既是营销专家、教育者，也是《紫牛》《许可营销》《支点》等20余部著作的作者。他还运营着全球最受欢迎且持续更新的博客（已连续发布近万篇文章！），持续重塑我们对营销、品牌、产品以及如何在世界上创造持久变革的认知。在对话中，我们探讨了：• 如何打造能自我传播的卓越产品

summary.en: This episode explores how to build remarkable products that spread, create a strategy with productive tension, make a meaningful promise to users, and build brands that remain distinctive as AI becomes ubiquitous.
summary.zh: 本期围绕如何打造值得主动传播的产品、如何让策略保有有效张力、如何向用户作出并兑现一个有意义的承诺，以及当 AI 逐渐成为基础能力后，品牌怎样继续保持差异化展开。

episodeTitle.en: How a great founder becomes a great CEO | Jonathan Lowenhar (co-founder of Enjoy The Work)
episodeTitle.zh: 伟大创始人如何成为卓越CEO | 乔纳森·洛文哈尔（Enjoy The Work联合创始人）

bio.en: Jonathan Lowenhar runs Enjoy The Work, a firm whose singular mission is to help founders become great CEOs, through mentoring and advising rooted in the study of how the best startups operate.
bio.zh: Jonathan Lowenhar 经营着 Enjoy The Work，这家公司唯一的使命是帮助创始人成为杰出的 CEO，其辅导与咨询建立在“研究最优秀初创公司如何运作”之上。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jonathan Lowenhar is the co-founder of Enjoy The Work, an executive coaching firm that helps founders become great CEOs. Over the past decade, Enjoy The Work has supported over 165 founders on their journey to becoming better leaders. In our conversation, we discuss: • The difference between being a founder and being a CEO
guestBioOfficial.zh: 乔纳森·洛文哈尔（Jonathan Lowenhar）是Enjoy The Work的联合创始人，这是一家帮助创始人成长为卓越CEO的执行力教练公司。在过去十年间，Enjoy The Work已为超过165位创始人提供了支持，助力他们成为更出色的领导者。在我们的对谈中，我们探讨了：• 创始人与CEO身份的差异

summary.en: Jonathan draws a sharp line between being a founder (a state of being) and being a CEO (a craft), and pushes back on 'founder mode' as an excuse for not learning the job—the best CEOs know when to calibrate between the two. He walks through the two phases of a startup (build something people want; then build a company around it), the most common CEO failure modes, and his 'Magic Box' paradigm for a successful exit (never be 'for sale'—seduce the buyer instead). The episode is full of advice on hiring, building a repeatable go-to-market motion, and trusting your intuition as a founder.
summary.zh: Jonathan 划清了“创始人”（一种存在状态）与“CEO”（一门手艺）的界限，并批评“创始人模式”成了不学本分的借口——最优秀的 CEO 知道何时在两者间切换。他拆解了创业的两个阶段（做出人们想买的东西；再围绕它建一家公司）、最常见的 CEO 失败模式，以及他用于成功退出的“Magic Box”范式（永远不要“待售”——而要 seduce 买方）。这期节目充满关于招聘、打造可复制的上市动作、以及作为创始人学会信任直觉的建议。

episodeTitle.en: The ultimate guide to founder-led sales | Jen Abel (co-founder of JJELLYFISH)
episodeTitle.zh: 创始人主导销售的终极指南 | 珍·阿贝尔（JJELLYFISH联合创始人）

bio.en: Jen Abel is the co-founder of Jellyfish (JJELLYFISH), where she and her team help early-stage founders learn how to sell, do customer discovery, and build a repeatable sales motion; this episode is an ultra-tactical guide to founder-led sales from zero to one.
bio.zh: Jen Abel 是 Jellyfish（JJELLYFISH）的联合创始人，她和团队帮助早期创始人学习如何销售、做客户探索并建立起可复制的销售动作；这期节目是关于从 0 到 1 的“创始人式销售”的极致实战指南。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jen Abel is the co-founder of JJELLYFISH, where she and her team have worked with over 300 early-stage founders to learn how to sell, do early customer discovery, and set up a repeatable sales motion on the way to their first $1M ARR. In our conversation, Jen shares: • Why founder-led sales is so crucial early on
guestBioOfficial.zh:
珍·阿贝尔（Jen Abel）是JJELLYFISH的联合创始人，她与团队合作，帮助300多位初创企业创始人学习如何销售、进行早期客户探索，并在迈向首个100万美元年度经常性收入（ARR）的道路上建立可重复的销售模式。在我们的对话中，珍分享了：  
• 创始人主导销售在早期为何如此关键

summary.en: Jen gets extremely tactical on founder-led sales, treating the founder as the product and the goal as learning as fast as possible rather than revenue on day one. She covers how to craft counterintuitive, shock-value messaging that earns a read, how to structure the first sales call with vulnerability ('I'm early-stage, help me learn'), how to find and reach leads, get through procurement, and close. With actual words, phrases, and pitfalls at every step, it's an episode packed with advice you can put into practice tomorrow—the most hands-on sales conversation you'll find.
summary.zh: Jen 就“创始人式销售”给出极其具体的建议，把创始人本身当作产品，把目标定为“尽可能快地学习”而非第一天就要收入。她讲了如何写出反直觉、有冲击力的信息以赢得一读、如何在第一次销售电话中以坦诚示弱（“我们很早期，请帮我看看这个问题在你们那边是怎么发生的”）、如何找到并触达线索、通过采购流程并签约。每一步都附上真实话术、措辞与坑，这期节目充满了你明天就能用上的建议——是你所能找到最手把手的销售对话。

episodeTitle.en: Behind the product: Replit | Amjad Masad (co-founder and CEO)
episodeTitle.zh: 产品背后的故事：Replit | 阿米贾德·马萨德（联合创始人兼CEO）

bio.en: Amjad Masad is the co-founder of Replit, an AI-powered platform for building and shipping software with over 34 million users, on a mission to make creating software dramatically easier.
bio.zh: Amjad Masad 是 Replit 的联合创始人，这是一个拥有超 3400 万用户的 AI 软件开发与部署平台，使命是让创建软件变得容易得多。

guestBioOfficial.en: Amjad Masad is the co-founder and CEO of Replit, a browser-based coding environment that allows anyone to write and deploy code. Replit has 34 million users globally and is one of the fastest-growing developer communities in the world. Prior to Replit, Amjad worked at Facebook, where he led the JavaScript infrastructure team and contributed to popular open-source developer tools. Additionally, he played a key role as a founding engineer at the online coding school Codecademy. In our conversation, Amjad shares: • A live demo of Replit in action
guestBioOfficial.zh: 阿米贾德·马萨德是Replit的联合创始人兼CEO，这是一款基于浏览器的编码环境，允许任何人编写和部署代码。Replit在全球拥有3400万用户，是全球发展最快的开发者社区之一。在加入Replit之前，阿米贾德曾在Facebook工作，领导JavaScript基础设施团队，并为流行的开源开发者工具做出贡献。此外，他还在在线编程学校Codecademy担任创始工程师。在我们的对谈中，阿米贾德将分享：• Replit实时演示

summary.en: Amjad demos what Replit can do today—letting anyone build and ship software, including full startups, with minimal technical skill—which he argues will blow people's minds. He predicts the bottleneck shifts from making things to generating ideas, and imagines a future where someone runs a billion-dollar company with zero employees. The conversation explores the profound implications for the future of product development, product management, and founders as AI lowers the cost of building.
summary.zh: Amjad 演示了 Replit 今天的能力——让任何人都能用极少的技术技能构建并发布软件（包括完整的创业项目），他认为这会让人大开眼界。他预测瓶颈将从“做出来”转向“想出来”，并想象未来有人用零员工运营一家十亿美元公司。对话深入探讨了 AI 降低构建成本后，对产品开发、产品管理和创始人的深远影响。

episodeTitle.en: Building Wiz: The fastest-growing startup in history | Raaz Herzberg (CMO & VP Product Strategy)
episodeTitle.zh: Building Wiz：史上发展最快的初创公司 | 拉兹·赫茨伯格（CMO兼产品战略副总裁）

bio.en: You're one of the first 10 employees, you're the first product manager. It was when you joined, the founders didn't really have an idea figured out yet. When they landed on an idea, and then ended up being wrong, ended up not working. Six weeks after you joined, there was a pivot.
bio.zh: 你是前10名员工之一，是首位产品经理。当时你加入时，创始人们还没有想清楚主意。他们确定了一个想法，结果却发现方向错误，最终失败了。你加入六周后，公司进行了转型。

summary.en: At the time, we didn't really have a solid product yet. We would have 10 to 15 meetings every day with potential customers. I was hired as the first product manager. I sat in on those calls. (00:07:01): I still did not exactly understand what we were going to build, which was confusing, because I was a product manager,
summary.zh: 当时，我们还没有一个成熟的产品。我们每天会与潜在客户进行10到15次会议。我被聘为首位产品经理。我参加了这些会议。（00:07:01）：我仍然不完全明白我们要构建什么，这很令人困惑，因为我是一名产品经理，

episodeTitle.en: Everything you’ve ever wanted to know about SAFe and the product owner role | Melissa Perri
episodeTitle.zh: 关于SAFe和产品负责人的角色，你想知道的一切 | 梅利莎·佩里

bio.en: Melissa is a product leader and guest on Lenny's podcast discussing product management, company building, and team leadership.
bio.zh: 梅丽莎（Melissa）是一位产品负责人，作为嘉宾做客 Lenny 的播客，探讨产品管理、公司建设与团队领导等话题。

guestBioOfficial.en: Melissa Perri is the founder of Product Institute, author of Escaping the Build Trap, and host of the Product Thinking Podcast. She has worked with startups, Fortune 50 companies, and everything in between to help them build better products and level up their product teams. In our conversation, we discuss: • The history of the product owner role
guestBioOfficial.zh:
梅利莎·佩里（Melissa Perri）是Product Institute的创始人，《摆脱构建陷阱》（Escaping the Build Trap）一书的作者，以及Product Thinking播客的主持人。她曾与初创企业、财富50强公司及介于两者之间的各类企业合作，助力它们打造更优质的产品，并提升产品团队的专业水平。在我们的对谈中，我们探讨了以下内容：  
• 产品负责人的角色发展历程

summary.en: In this episode, Melissa shares practical perspectives on product management and building effective teams. She discusses how strong product culture and clear priorities help organizations move faster. The conversation offers actionable takeaways for product leaders navigating growth and execution.
summary.zh: 在本期节目中，梅丽莎分享了关于产品管理与打造高效团队的务实观点。她探讨了强大的产品文化与清晰优先级如何让组织跑得更快。本期为在产品增长与执行中探索的领导者提供了可落地的要点。

episodeTitle.en: Breaking the rules of growth: Why Shopify bans KPIs, optimizes for churn, and prioritizes intuition
episodeTitle.zh: 打破增长规则：为何Shopify禁用KPI、优化客户流失并优先考虑直觉

bio.en: Archie Abrams is VP of Product and Head of Growth at Shopify, leading a 600+ person org (product, design, engineering, data ops, growth marketing) and formerly a long-time leader at Udemy; he turned Shopify's "build a 100-year company" long-termism, its long-horizon holdout experiments, and its use of absolute numbers over conversion rates into an operational growth practice.
bio.zh: Archie Abrams 是 Shopify 的产品 VP 兼增长负责人，领导一个 600 多人的组织（产品、设计、工程、数据运营、增长营销），曾长期任职于 Udemy；他把 Shopify「为 100 年建公司」的长期主义、用长期 holdout 实验衡量真实影响、以及用绝对数而非转化率做增长指标的方法，变成了可执行的增长实践。

guestBioOfficial.en: Archie Abrams is the VP of Product and Head of Growth at Shopify, where he leads a 600+ person growth org across product, design, engineering, data, ops, and growth marketing. Shopify powers over 10% of e-commerce in the United States, with $235 billion in GMV in 2023 (roughly the size of Finland’s economy). He previously led Consumer product and growth at Lyft and was at Udemy for 8 years as SVP of Product having joined the company when it was 10 people. In our conversation, we discuss: • Why Shopify optimizes for churn
guestBioOfficial.zh: 阿奇·艾布拉姆斯（Archie Abrams）是Shopify产品副总裁兼增长部门负责人，领导着由600多人组成的增长团队，涵盖产品、设计、工程、数据、运营和增长营销等领域。Shopify为美国超过10%的电商交易提供支持，2023年GMV达2350亿美元（相当于芬兰经济规模）。他此前曾在Lyft领导消费者产品与增长团队，并在Udemy任职8年，担任产品高级副总裁，当时Udemy仅有10名员工。在对话中，我们将探讨：• Shopify为何优化客户流失

summary.en: Archie Abrams shares Shopify's counterintuitive growth philosophy: because revenue comes mostly from payments tied to merchant success (not subscriptions), they don't optimize for retention/churn but lower the barrier to starting a business and let a few huge winners (a power law) carry each cohort's value. They keep 1–3 year holdouts on every experiment and found ~30–40% of short-term "wins" have no long-term lift (mostly pull-forward effects) — so teams still ship short-term wins and even "neutral" experiments. On metrics, Shopify uses absolute counts, not conversion rates, to stop teams from tightening the upstream funnel just to flatter their local rate. The org splits into core product (decided by Tobi/Glen on taste, no KPIs), growth R&D, growth marketing, and customer support; growth and core collaborate through healthy tension and trust. He also covers the attribution mess of blending sales and self-serve funnels, Shopify's CMO-less embedded marketing, and how Udemy used discounts to signal value through price and trigger an emotional sense of progress.
summary.zh: Archie Abrams 分享了 Shopify 反直觉的增长哲学：因为收入主要来自商家成功后的支付分成（而非订阅），所以他们不优化「留存/流失」，而是降低创业门槛、让更多商家进门，靠少数大成商家（幂律）撑起整批价值。他们为跑过的每个实验保留 1–3 年的长期 holdout，发现约 30–40% 短期显示 lift 的实验长期其实没增量（多为「提前拉动」效应）——所以团队仍会 ship 短期有效的改动，甚至 ship「中性」实验。指标上，Shopify 用绝对人数而非转化率，避免团队为美化局部转化率而收紧上游漏斗。组织上分核心产品（由 Tobi/Glen 凭品味决策、无 KPI）、增长 R&D、增长营销、客户支持；增长与核心靠「健康张力」和信任协作。他还聊了销售+自助混合漏斗的归因难题、无 CMO 的嵌入式营销，以及 Udemy 用折扣「用价格 signal 价值+触发情感进步」的打法。

episodeTitle.en: 4 questions Shreyas wishes he’d asked himself sooner | Former PM leader at Stripe, Twitter, Google
episodeTitle.zh: 施雷亚斯希望自己能早点问自己的4个问题 | 曾任Stripe、Twitter、Google产品经理的领导者

bio.en: Shreyas Doshi is a product leader and one of today's most consistently insightful voices on the craft of product management, drawing on senior product roles at Google, Twitter, Yahoo, and Stripe; this is a live-recorded edition of his conversation.
bio.zh: Shreyas Doshi 是一位产品领导者，也是当下对产品管理手艺最具持续洞察力的声音之一，其经验来自在 Google、Twitter、Yahoo 和 Stripe 的高级产品职务；本期为其对话的现场录制版。

guestBioOfficial.en: Shreyas Doshi is a former product leader at Stripe, Twitter, Google, and Yahoo. He’s now a full-time advisor and coach to founders and executives. Shreyas is known for his incredibly insightful writing on products, which has garnered him a passionate following in the PM and startup community. Last week, we sat down together at the very first Lenny and Friends Summit in San Francisco for a special live episode. We covered: • Why product leaders often feel overwhelmed with work, and how to combat it
guestBioOfficial.zh: 施雷亚斯·多希曾是Stripe、Twitter、Google和雅虎的产品负责人。如今，他全职为创始人和高管提供顾问及指导服务。施雷亚斯以其对产品领域极具洞察力的文章而闻名，在产品管理和创业社区收获了热情追随者。上周，我们在旧金山首届Lenny和朋友们峰会上进行了特别的现场访谈，内容包括：• 产品负责人为何常感工作负担过重，以及如何应对这一挑战

summary.en: Shreyas shares his philosophy of high-leverage product work, including the art of saying no, focusing on outcomes over output, and protecting cognitive bandwidth for the few things that matter. He discusses how to develop product taste, the discipline of ignoring most requests, and why great PMs think in terms of leverage and systems. The episode is a dense, actionable masterclass in the craft of product management.
summary.zh: Shreyas 分享了他关于高杠杆产品工作的理念，包括说“不”的艺术、聚焦产出之上的成果、以及为少数要事保护认知带宽。他讨论了如何培养产品品味、忽略大多数请求的自律，以及为什么优秀的产品经理以杠杆与系统的方式思考。本期是关于产品管理手艺的、信息密集且可落地的导师课。

episodeTitle.en: Meta’s head of product on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, and more | Naomi Gleit
episodeTitle.zh: Meta产品主管谈与马克·扎克伯格共事、早期增长策略等 | 娜奥米·格莱特

bio.en: Naomi Gleit is Head of Product at Meta and, apart from Mark Zuckerberg, the longest-serving executive, having joined as employee #29 and scaled the company for nearly 20 years.
bio.zh: 娜奥米·格莱特（Naomi Gleit）是 Meta 的产品负责人，除马克·扎克伯格外任职最久的高管，她以第 29 号员工身份加入，伴随公司成长近 20 年。

guestBioOfficial.en: Naomi Gleit is head of product at Meta, joined as employee #29, and is the longest-serving executive at Meta other than Mark Zuckerberg. She’s been at the center of some of the company’s most foundational products, including Facebook’s early growth team. In our conversation, we discuss: • How she originally landed at Facebook
guestBioOfficial.zh: 娜奥米·格莱特是Meta的产品主管，曾以第29号员工的身份加入公司，是除马克·扎克伯格外在Meta任职时间最长的高管。她参与了该公司最基础的产品开发，包括Facebook的早期增长团队。在我们的对话中，我们将讨论：•她最初如何进入Facebook

summary.en: Naomi stresses creating a single "canonical doc" for every project to drive extreme clarity and avoid conflicting answers. She shares lessons from Meta's legendary early growth team and how to ramp up fast on any new initiative. The episode is a rare, practical master class in product leadership from inside Meta's senior ranks.
summary.zh: 娜奥米强调为每个项目建立唯一的"权威文档"（canonical doc），以实现极度清晰、避免答案相互矛盾。她分享了 Meta 传奇早期增长团队的经验，以及如何快速上手任何新项目。本期是一份来自 Meta 高层的罕见而实用的产品领导力大师课。

episodeTitle.en: How to see like a designer: The hidden power of typography and logos | Jessica Hische
episodeTitle.zh: 如何像设计师一样思考：字体与标志的隐藏力量 | 杰西卡·希舍（Jessica Hische）

bio.en: Jessica Hische is a renowned custom typographer and lettering artist (and bestselling children's book author) whose work—logos for Mailchimp, Eventbrite, Philz Coffee, and more—has shaped how a generation thinks about brand and craft.
bio.zh: Jessica Hische 是一位知名的定制字体与字母设计艺术家（也是畅销童书作者），她的作品——为 Mailchimp、Eventbrite、Philz Coffee 等设计的标志——塑造了一代人对于品牌与工艺的认知。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jessica Hische is a lettering artist and New York Times bestselling author based in Oakland, California. She specializes in typographical work for logos, film, books, and other commercial applications. Her clients include Wes Anderson, The United States Postal Service, Target, Hallmark, and Penguin Books, and her work has been featured in design and illustration annuals both in the U.S. and internationally. She’s been named a Print Magazine New Visual Artist (20 under 30), one of Forbes 30 under 30 in Art and Design, an ADC Young Gun, a “Person to Watch” by GD USA, and an Adweek “Creative 100.” In our conversation, we discuss: • My new logo and brand!
guestBioOfficial.zh: 杰西卡·希舍（Jessica Hische）是字体艺术家，现居加利福尼亚州奥克兰。她专攻字体设计，服务于标志、电影、书籍及其他商业应用。客户包括韦斯·安德森（Wes Anderson）、美国邮政服务（USPS）、塔吉特（Target）、贺卡（Hallmark）和企鹅图书（Penguin Books），其作品多次入选美国及国际设计与插画年鉴。她曾获《印刷杂志》“新视觉艺术家”（20位30岁以下艺术家）、福布斯“30位30岁以下艺术与设计人才”、ADC青年才俊及GD USA“值得关注人物”等称号。在对话中，我们讨论了：• 我的新标志和品牌！

summary.en: Jessica walks through the process of refreshing Lenny's own logo and brand, and explains which specific elements of a logo actually affect how people feel about a brand. She makes the case that a 'good enough' logo can serve most startups for a long time, when it makes sense to refresh your look, and shares clever productivity tips, design advice, and fun stories from the illustration world. It's a rare, accessible peek into the craft of brand and lettering from a master.
summary.zh: Jessica 完整讲述了为 Lenny 本人刷新 logo 与品牌的过程，并解释了 logo 的哪些具体元素真正影响人们对品牌的感受。她主张“够好”的 logo 往往能让大多数初创公司用很久，以及何时才值得刷新形象，并分享了聪明的效率技巧、设计建议，以及插画圈的有趣故事。这是来自一位大师、难得又通俗易懂的品牌与字体工艺一瞥。

episodeTitle.en: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, founder mode, more | Anneka Gupta
episodeTitle.zh: 变得更具战略眼光、应对难相处的同事、创始人模式等挑战 | 安妮卡·古普塔

bio.en: Anneka Gupta is Chief Product Officer at Rubrik, a lecturer on product management at Stanford's Graduate School of Business, and former President and head of product at LiveRamp, where she spent 11 years.
bio.zh: Anneka Gupta 是 Rubrik 首席产品官、斯坦福商学院产品经理课程讲师，曾任 LiveRamp 总裁兼产品负责人，在那里工作了 11 年。

guestBioOfficial.en: Anneka Gupta is the Chief Product Officer at Rubrik, a leading B2B cybersecurity company. She previously spent 11 years at LiveRamp, where she was the President and Head of Product and Platforms leading product development and go-to-market operations and strategy. Anneka also sits on the board of directors for Tinuiti and teaches product management at Stanford University. In our conversation, we discuss: • Navigating “founder mode” dynamics in organizations
guestBioOfficial.zh: 安妮卡·古普塔（Anneka Gupta）是领先的B2B网络安全公司Rubrik的首席产品官。她此前在LiveRamp工作了11年，担任总裁兼产品与平台部负责人，主导产品开发及市场推广策略。古普塔还担任Tinuiti董事会成员，并在斯坦福大学教授产品管理课程。在我们的对话中，我们探讨了： • 如何在组织中驾驭“创始人模式”动态

summary.en: Anneka reframes what it means to be “strategic”: being able to articulate a compelling why and acting as a change agent for long-term interests even when it's hard. She shares advice on navigating difficult personalities, giving and receiving hard feedback, and bringing humor and gratitude to every situation. The conversation also covers managing your energy versus your time, tactical ways to become more strategic, and how to break into product management.
summary.zh: Anneka 重新定义了“有策略”的含义：能清晰阐述有说服力的“为什么”，并即便艰难也充当推动长期利益的变革者。她分享了应对难缠性格、给予和接受尖锐反馈，以及把幽默与感恩带入每个场景的建议。对话还涵盖管理精力而非时间、变得更有策略的实操方法，以及如何进入产品经理行业。

episodeTitle.en: Why most public speaking advice is wrong—and how to finally overcome anxiety | Tristan de Montebello
episodeTitle.zh: 为何大多数公众演讲建议都是错误的——以及如何最终克服焦虑 | 特里斯坦·德·蒙特贝洛

bio.en: Tristan de Montebello is co-creator of Ultraspeaking, the best public-speaking workshop Lenny has found, and a former world-championship finalist in public speaking.
bio.zh: Tristan de Montebello 是 Ultraspeaking 的联合创造者——这是 Lenny 所见过最好的公开演讲工作坊——他也是世界演讲锦标赛的前决赛选手。

guestBioOfficial.en: Tristan de Montebello is the co-creator of Ultraspeaking, the most effective method I’ve come across for rapidly improving communication and presentation skills. In 2017, Tristan became the fastest person ever to reach the finals of the World Championship of Public Speaking, achieving this feat in just seven months with no prior experience. In our conversation, we discuss: • Why public speaking is a meta skill that can transform your life
guestBioOfficial.zh: 特里斯坦·德·蒙特贝洛是Ultraspeaking的联合创始人，这是我所知晓的提升沟通和演讲技巧最有效的方法。2017年，特里斯坦仅用七个月时间便毫无经验地闯入世界公共演讲锦标赛决赛，成为史上最快达成这一壮举的人。对话中，我们将探讨：• 公众演讲为何是能改变人生的元技能

summary.en: Tristan shares how to become a dramatically better, more comfortable speaker, including speaking on the spot without panic. He explains the mindset and reps that build speaking confidence, why most fear is learned, and how communication accelerates your career. The episode is a practical, energizing guide to a skill that pays compounding dividends.
summary.zh: Tristan 分享了如何成为显著更优秀、更从容的演讲者，包括在毫无准备下临场发言而不慌乱。他解释了构建演讲信心的思维与练习、为何大多数恐惧是习得的，以及沟通如何加速你的职业生涯。本期是一份务实、令人振奋的指南，关乎一项带来复利回报的技能。

episodeTitle.en: Becoming a conscious leader: Leading without fear, finding your life’s objective function, and getting better at vision and strategy | John Mark Nickels (Uber, Waymo, DoorDash)
episodeTitle.zh: 成为有意识的领导者：无所畏惧地领导、找到人生使命函数、提升愿景与战略能力 | John Mark Nickels（优步、Waymo、DoorDash）

bio.en: J.M. Nickels is a product leader who has built and led teams at Waymo, DoorDash, and Uber—launching the first version of Uber Pool and later leading the infrastructure behind Uber's matching and pricing—and now leads product for Uber's mobility team; he speaks on 'conscious leadership.'
bio.zh: J.M. Nickels 是一位产品负责人，曾在 Waymo、DoorDash 和 Uber 打造并领导团队——推出了 Uber Pool 的第一个版本，后来领导支撑 Uber 匹配与定价的底层基础设施——如今领导 Uber 出行（mobility）团队的产品；他常谈“自觉领导力”（conscious leadership）。

summary.en: J.M. weaves a rare blend of hard skills, soft skills, tactics, and raw emotion—including tears—around the theme of conscious leadership: leading as influence anyone can exercise, and getting clear on your 'objective function' by imagining your future self (e.g., your relationship with your daughter matters more than a slightly better deck). He shares lessons from building Uber Pool, scaling DoorDash's platform, and commercializing Waymo's autonomous vehicles, and why an awareness that life ends should reframe your priorities. The episode is a powerful, human conversation for becoming a better leader.
summary.zh: J.M. 围绕“自觉领导力”这一主题，罕见地把硬技能、软技能、战术与真挚情感（包括落泪）交织在一起：把领导视为人人都能施展的影响力，并通过想象未来的自己来厘清你的“目标函数”（例如，与女儿的关系比一份稍好的 deck 重要得多）。他分享了打造 Uber Pool、扩展 DoorDash 平台、将 Waymo 自动驾驶商业化过程中的教训，以及为何“生命终将结束”的觉知应当重塑你的优先级。这期节目是一场强大而有人性的对话，助你成为更好的领导者。

episodeTitle.en: Thinking like a gardener, slime mold, the adjacent possible: Product advice from Alex Komoroske
episodeTitle.zh: 像园丁一样思考、黏菌、邻近可能性：亚历克斯·科莫罗斯基的产品建议

bio.en: Alex Komoroske is a former 13-year Google veteran (Search, Chrome's Open Web Platform, AR at Maps) and ex-head of corporate strategy at Stripe who is founding a startup to reimagine the web for the AI era.
bio.zh: Alex Komoroske 在 Google 工作了 13 年（搜索、Chrome 开放网络平台、地图 AR 等），曾任 Stripe 企业战略负责人，目前正在创办一家旨在为 AI 时代重塑网络的公司。

guestBioOfficial.en: Alex Komoroske is a strategic leader who merges the practice, theory, and mindset necessary to tackle complex problems. He spent 13 years at Google, where he worked on Search and DoubleClick and led Chrome’s Open Web Platform. He also spearheaded Augmented Reality in Google Maps and developed toolkits to align companywide strategy from the ground up. After serving as Head of Corporate Strategy at Stripe, he is now co-founding a startup aimed at reimagining the web for the AI era. Alex created the popular “Slime Molds” deck, which offers fresh insights into organizational dynamics. He is also the author of the widely read “Bits and Bobs,” a collection of thought-provoking reflections.In our conversation, we delve into: • “Organizational kayfabe”
guestBioOfficial.zh: 亚历克斯·科莫罗斯基是一位战略领袖，他融合了应对复杂问题所需的实践、理论和思维模式。他曾在谷歌工作 13 年，先后负责搜索和 DoubleClick 项目，并领导 Chrome 的开放网络平台。他还主导了谷歌地图中的增强现实功能开发，并开发了从零开始构建全公司战略的工具包。在担任 Stripe 企业战略主管后，他目前正与人共同创办一家旨在为人工智能时代重新构想网络的初创公司。亚历克斯创作了广受欢迎的《黏菌》演示文稿，为组织动态提供了全新的洞见。他还是广受欢迎的《零零碎碎》系列文章的作者，该系列文集充满了发人深省的思考。在我们的对话中，我们将深入探讨：• “组织内的‘kayfabe’现象”

summary.en: Alex makes the case for thinking like a gardener rather than a builder—cultivating systems that grow and compound on their own instead of forcing a fixed plan. He explores how LLMs and generative AI will reshape product building, which skills will matter most, and what organizations can learn from slime mold and “the adjacent possible.” The conversation ranges across strategy salons, organizational kayfabe, and why directing emergent behavior beats brute-force control.
summary.zh: Alex 主张像“园丁”而非“建造者”一样思考——培育能自主生长、自我复合的系统，而不是强推既定计划。他探讨了 LLM 和生成式 AI 将如何重塑产品构建、未来哪些技能最关键，以及组织能从黏菌和“邻近可能”中学到什么。对话还涵盖策略沙龙、组织性的 kayfabe，以及为何引导涌现行为优于蛮力控制。

episodeTitle.en: How marketplaces win: Liquidity, growth levers, quality, more | Benjamin Lauzier (Lyft, Thumbtack)
episodeTitle.zh: 市场平台如何取胜：流动性、增长杠杆、质量等 | 本杰明·劳齐尔（Lyft、Thumbtack）

bio.en: Ben Lauzier was VP of Product and Growth at Thumbtack (3x growth in three years) and an early Lyft employee (#30) who led driver-side product and growth, and now advises marketplace teams and founded healthcare startup Nurra.
bio.zh: Ben Lauzier 曾任 Thumbtack 产品与增长副总裁（三年内增长 3 倍），也是 Lyft 早期员工（第 30 号），负责司机端产品与增长，现为正念市场团队顾问，并创办了医疗创业公司 Nurra。

guestBioOfficial.en: Benjamin Lauzier has been building and scaling marketplaces for almost 15 years. He was the VP of product and growth at Thumbtack, where he rebuilt the product team and Thumbtack’s growth levers, re-architected their revenue model, and helped double the company’s growth within three years. Prior to Thumbtack, Ben was at Lyft for six years, where he led the supply side of the product organization to a point where 1% of U.S. workers were driving for Lyft every month. Currently, he advises marketplace teams and founders, teaches a Reforge course on marketplace growth, and has recently launched a health tech company called Nurra, which connects users with care advocates to navigate the health-care system. In our conversation, we cover: • What defines a marketplace business
guestBioOfficial.zh:
班杰明·劳齐尔（Benjamin Lauzier）过去近15年一直致力于搭建和扩展电商平台。他曾在Thumbtack担任产品与增长副总裁，期间重组了产品团队和增长引擎，重新设计了公司的营收模式，并在三年内助力公司增长率翻倍。在加入Thumbtack之前，班杰明曾在Lyft工作六年，期间他将该公司的供应侧产品部门打造成美国每月有1%劳动者为Lyft平台司机的规模。目前，他为多个电商团队和创始人提供咨询服务，教授Reforge平台关于电商增长的课程，并于近期创立了健康科技公司Nurra，该公司致力于帮助用户与医疗顾问对接，助力其在医疗体系中高效寻医问药。在本次对谈中，我们将探讨：
• 何为电商平台业务

summary.en: Ben goes deep on building and scaling marketplaces: what to focus on pre-product-market fit, which side to prioritize, how to track liquidity, and what causes most marketplaces to fail. He advocates providing guardrails and empowering supply rather than micromanaging from an ivory tower, plus clever supply-side growth tactics. The conversation also contrasts the European and U.S. product markets and what European companies should change.
summary.zh: Ben 深入探讨了构建和扩展双边市场：产品市场匹配前要关注什么、优先哪一侧、如何追踪流动性，以及大多数市场失败的原因。他主张提供护栏、赋能供给侧，而非坐在象牙塔里微观管理，并分享巧妙的供给侧增长策略。对话还对比了欧洲与美国产品市场，以及欧洲公司应做出哪些改变。

episodeTitle.en: Lessons in product leadership and AI strategy from Glean, Google, Amazon, and Slack | Tamar Yehoshua
episodeTitle.zh: 来自Glean、谷歌、亚马逊和Slack的产品领导力与AI战略启示 | 塔玛·耶霍舒亚

bio.en: Tamar Yehoshua is president of product and technology at Glean, previously CPO at Slack (where she 10x'd revenue through IPO and Salesforce acquisition) and a long-time Google leader on Search.
bio.zh: Tamar Yehoshua 是 Glean 的产品与技术总裁，此前曾任 Slack 首席产品官（在她任内营收增长 10 倍，直至 IPO 并被 Salesforce 收购），也是 Google 搜索领域的长期领导者。

guestBioOfficial.en: Tamar Yehoshua is the president of product and technology at Glean. Prior to joining Glean, Tamar was chief product officer at Slack, where she led product, design, and research as the company scaled, including a 10x increase in revenue, its public listing, and an acquisition by Salesforce. She also led product and engineering teams at Google, working on search, identity, and privacy, and at A9.com, an Amazon company. Tamar has served on the board of directors for RetailMeNot, ServiceNow, Snyk, and Yext. In our conversation, we discuss: • Why you don’t need to be a well-run company to win
guestBioOfficial.zh: 塔玛·耶霍舒亚（Tamar Yehoshua）是Glean的产研总裁。在加入Glean之前，塔玛曾担任Slack的首席产品官。在Slack规模扩张的过程中，她领导了产品、设计和研究团队，推动公司营收增长10倍，并成功完成上市及被Salesforce收购。此前，她还曾在谷歌和亚马逊旗下公司A9.com担任产品和工程团队负责人。塔玛现任RetailMeNot、ServiceNow、Snyk和Yext等多家公司的董事会成员。在我们的对话中，我们探讨了：•为何无需成为一家运营完善的公司也能胜出

summary.en: Tamar discusses what it takes to lead product and technology at a fast-scaling enterprise AI company like Glean, and the lessons from scaling Slack 10x and leading Search at Google. She covers how to build trustworthy AI products for enterprises, the interplay of product and engineering leadership, and how to maintain quality and momentum through hypergrowth. The episode is a senior operator's view of building serious enterprise software.
summary.zh: Tamar 探讨了在像 Glean 这样快速扩张的企业级 AI 公司中，领导产品与技术需要什么，以及从 Slack 十倍增长、在 Google 领导搜索中学到的经验。她涵盖了如何为企业打造值得信赖的 AI 产品、产品与工程领导力的相互作用，以及如何在超高速增长中保持品质与势头。本期是一位资深运营者对打造严肃企业级软件的透视。

episodeTitle.en: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)
episodeTitle.zh: AI时代重新思考SEO | 伊莱·施瓦茨（SEO顾问、作家）

bio.en: Eli Schwartz is a growth advisor and SEO strategist who has guided search strategy for companies like Quora, Coinbase, Tinder, LinkedIn, and Zapier, and is the author of the book Product-Led SEO.
bio.zh: Eli Schwartz 是一位增长顾问兼 SEO 策略师，曾为 Quora、Coinbase、Tinder、LinkedIn、Zapier 等公司指导搜索策略，并著有《Product-Led SEO》一书。

guestBioOfficial.en: Eli Schwartz is a leading SEO consultant and the author of Product-Led SEO. He has worked with industry giants like Zapier, Tinder, Coinbase, Quora, LinkedIn, and WordPress to build and execute global SEO strategies that significantly enhanced their organic visibility at scale. In our conversation, Eli shares: • How AI and LLMs are reshaping the SEO landscape
guestBioOfficial.zh: 伊莱·施瓦茨是领先的SEO顾问，也是《产品主导的SEO》一书的作者。他曾与Zapier、Tinder、Coinbase、Quora、LinkedIn和WordPress等行业巨头合作，构建并执行全球SEO战略，显著提升了他们的自然可见度。在对话中，伊莱分享：• AI和LLM如何重塑SEO格局

summary.en: Eli reframes SEO as a product problem that product managers should own, arguing it is simple and not the "dark art" many believe it to be. With AI answer engines and Google's instant answers removing top-of-funnel results, he shows why SEO must shift to the mid-funnel buyer journey and why many SaaS, B2B, and local businesses should not invest in SEO at all. He covers programmatic versus editorial SEO, why link-building is really brand-building, how to forecast SEO upside top-down, and why most keyword research tools are wildly inaccurate. His core message: SEO isn't dying, but success now requires matching the right solution to real user intent rather than chasing rankings and traffic.
summary.zh: Eli 把 SEO 重新框定为产品经理该拥有的产品问题，认为它很简单、并不是很多人以为的“黑魔法”。随着 AI 答案引擎和 Google 的即时答案拿走顶层漏斗结果，他指出 SEO 必须转向中层漏斗的买家旅程，而且很多 SaaS、B2B 和本地商家根本不该投 SEO。他覆盖了程序化 vs 编辑式 SEO、为什么建外链其实是建品牌、怎么自上而下预测 SEO 上升空间、以及为什么大多数关键词工具严重不准。他的核心信息：SEO 没在死，但现在的成功需要把正确方案匹配真实用户意图，而不是追逐排名和流量。

episodeTitle.en: The things engineers are desperate for PMs to understand | Camille Fournier (“The Manager’s Path”)
episodeTitle.zh: 工程师迫切希望产品经理理解的事 | 卡米尔·福尼尔（《管理者之路》）

bio.en: Camille Fournier is a respected technology executive and author of The Manager's Path (a definitive guide to engineering management), formerly CTO of Rent the Runway, VP of Technology at Goldman Sachs, and head of platform engineering at JPMorgan Chase.
bio.zh: Camille Fournier 是一位受人尊敬的技术高管、《经理人之路》（The Manager's Path，工程管理权威指南）的作者，曾任 Rent the Runway 的 CTO、高盛技术副总裁、摩根大通平台工程负责人。

guestBioOfficial.en: Camille Fournier is the author of The Manager’s Path, which many consider the definitive guide for navigating one’s career path in tech. Camille was previously the CTO of Rent the Runway, VP of Technology at Goldman Sachs, Head of Platform Engineering at Two Sigma, and Global Head of Engineering and Architecture at JPMorgan Chase. She is about to release new newest book, Platform Engineering: A Guide for Technical, Product, and People Leaders. In our conversation, we discuss: • What product managers do that annoys engineers
guestBioOfficial.zh: 卡米尔·福尼尔是《管理者之路》的作者，该书被许多人视为科技行业职业发展路径的权威指南。卡米尔曾担任Rent the Runway的首席技术官、高盛公司的技术副总裁、Two Sigma公司的平台工程主管，以及摩根大通的全球工程与架构负责人。她即将出版新书《平台工程：技术、产品与人员领导者的指南》。在对话中，我们讨论了：• 产品经理做哪些事会让工程师感到厌烦

summary.en: Camille tackles what PMs do that annoys engineers—hoarding credit and not understanding technical details—and why the best PMs talk least and encourage others to present. She stresses that engineers want to understand the business and customer problem, not just write code, and that great PMs aren't threatened by others' ideas. The conversation is a frank guide to PM-engineer dynamics and becoming a trusted partner to engineering.
summary.zh: Camille 剖析了产品经理哪些行为惹恼工程师——独吞功劳、不懂技术细节——以及为何最好的 PM 话最少、鼓励别人来展示。她强调工程师想理解业务与客户问题，而非只写代码，而优秀的 PM 不会被他人的想法威胁。对话是关于 PM 与工程师关系的坦率指南，教你成为工程师信赖的伙伴。

episodeTitle.en: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, more | Phyl Terry
episodeTitle.zh: 在当今市场中获得理想工作：谈判技巧、求职建议等 | 菲尔·特里（Phyl Terry）

bio.en: Phyl Terry is the author of Never Search Alone and a veteran operator - he was on the founding team of the first company Amazon acquired and later ran the consulting firm Creative Good - who has reinvented job searching through peer support.
bio.zh: Phyl Terry 是《永远不要独自求职》（Never Search Alone）一书的作者，也是一位资深从业者——他曾是亚马逊收购的第一家公司的创始团队成员，后来运营咨询公司 Creative Good——他通过同伴互助重新发明了求职方式。

guestBioOfficial.en: Phyl Terry is the author of Never Search Alone, which I’ve seen so many people reference as the most impactful guide they read for finding a job. Phyl was on the founding team of the first company Amazon acquired back in the ’90s and then was CEO of pioneering product consulting firm Creative Good, with companies like Apple, Facebook, and Microsoft as customers. Today, Phyl is the founder and CEO of Collaborative Gain, which 20 years ago pioneered bringing councils to senior product leaders and GMs in Silicon Valley. That’s their day job—in addition to that, Phyl runs a free global community for job seekers based on their latest book. In our conversation, we discuss: • Why you should never search for a job alone
guestBioOfficial.zh: 菲尔·特里（Phyl Terry）是《永不独自求职》一书的作者，我见过许多人将这本书视为他们求职过程中最具影响力的指南。菲尔曾是亚马逊在90年代收购的第一家公司的创始团队成员，随后担任开创性产品咨询公司Creative Good的首席执行官，其客户包括苹果、Facebook和微软等公司。如今，菲尔是Collaborative Gain的创始人兼首席执行官，该公司20年前率先为硅谷的高级产品领导者和总经理引入顾问服务。除此之外，菲尔还基于其最新著作为求职者运营了一个免费的全球社区。在我们的对话中，我们探讨了：• 为何你不应独自求职

summary.en: Phyl argues that job searching should be done with others, not alone, and introduces Job Search Councils: free, volunteer-run support groups of six to eight seekers who meet weekly using a structured methodology.
