He explains the 'spear, not a net' approach to candidate-market fit and why treating the search like a product exercise reveals focus. The episode is a compassionate, tactical playbook for finding work you love.
summary.zh: Phyl 主张求职应当与他人同行，而非孤军奋战，并介绍了“求职委员会（Job Search Councils）”：由 6-8 名求职者组成、免费且由志愿者运营的互助小组，每周按结构化方法碰面。他阐释了用“长矛而非渔网”的思路去匹配“候选人—市场”契合度，以及为何把求职当作产品练习能让人聚焦。本期是一份充满同理心、可落地的“找到热爱的工作”实战手册。

episodeTitle.en: How LinkedIn became interesting: The inside story | Tomer Cohen (CPO at LinkedIn)
episodeTitle.zh: 《领英如何变得引人入胜：内部故事 | 托默·科恩（领英首席产品官）》

bio.en: Tomer Cohen is Chief Product Officer at LinkedIn, overseeing all product teams, previously head of mobile and the revamp of the LinkedIn feed, and a driver of LinkedIn's early AI-first shift.
bio.zh: Tomer Cohen 是 LinkedIn 的首席产品官（CPO），统管所有产品团队，此前曾任移动端负责人、主导 LinkedIn 信息流的改版，也是 LinkedIn 早期“AI 优先”转向的推动者之一。

guestBioOfficial.en: Tomer Cohen is the chief product officer at LinkedIn, responsible for setting the company’s product strategy, leading product development, user experience design, business development, content creation, and customer operations. He also hosts the Building One podcast, where he interviews exceptional builders across various disciplines. In our conversation, we discuss: • How LinkedIn transformed its feed into an engaging content and social platform
guestBioOfficial.zh:
托默·科恩（Tomer Cohen）是领英的首席产品官，负责制定公司的产品战略、领导产品开发、用户体验设计、业务开发、内容创作和客户运营。他还主持《Building One》播客，采访各领域的杰出创新者。在我们的对话中，我们将探讨：
• 领英如何将其动态推送平台转型为引人入胜的内容和社交平台

summary.en: Tomer shares how LinkedIn builds product at scale, from revamping the feed to shifting the company toward an AI-first mindset well before it was fashionable. He discusses the structure of product teams, how to keep a massive surface feeling relevant, and lessons from leading one of the world's largest professional networks. The episode is a senior product leader's look at operating at extreme scale.
summary.zh: Tomer 分享了 LinkedIn 如何在规模化下打造产品，从改版信息流，到在该词流行之前很久就推动公司向“AI 优先”转变。他讨论了产品团队的结构、如何让一个庞大的界面始终让人觉得 relevant，以及领导全球最大职业网络之一的经验。本期是一位资深产品领导者对极致规模化运作的透视。

episodeTitle.en: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)
episodeTitle.zh: 首席增长黑客揭秘秘籍 | 肖恩·埃利斯（《增长黑客》作者）

bio.en: Today, my guest is Sean Ellis. Sean is one of the earliest and most influential thinkers and operators in the world of growth. He coined the term growth hacking, invented the ICE prioritization framework, was one of the earliest people to use freemium as a growth strategy, and maybe most famously de
bio.zh: 今天的嘉宾是 Sean Ellis。Sean 是增长领域最早、最具影响力的思想家和实践者之一。他创造了"增长黑客"（growth hacking）一词，发明了 ICE 优先级排序框架，是最早将免费增值（freemium）作为增长策略的人之一，或许最广为人知的是 de

guestBioOfficial.en: Sean Ellis is one of the earliest and most influential thinkers and operators in growth. He coined the term “growth hacking,” invented the ICE prioritization framework, was one of the earliest people to use freemium as a growth lever, and, most famously, developed the Sean Ellis Test for product-market fit (which a large percentage of founders use today to track if they’ve found PMF). Over the course of his career, Sean was head of growth at Dropbox and Eventbrite; helped companies like Microsoft and Nubank refine their growth strategy; was on the founding team of LogMeIn, which sold for over $4 billion; and is the author of one of the most popular growth books of all time, Hacking Growth, which has sold over 750,000 copies. In our conversation, he shares: • The proper use of the Sean Ellis Test for measuring product-market fit
guestBioOfficial.zh: 肖恩·埃利斯是增长领域最早且最具影响力的思想领袖和实干家之一。他创造了“增长黑客”一词，发明了ICE优先级框架，率先将免费增值模式作为增长杠杆，并最著名的开发了用于验证产品市场契合度的肖恩·埃利斯测试（如今大量创业者借此追踪是否找到了PMF）。职业生涯中，肖恩曾担任Dropbox和Eventbrite的增长负责人，助力微软和Nubank等公司优化增长策略，参与创立了以40亿美元估值出售的LogMeIn，并著有畅销增长类书籍《增长黑客》，该书累计销量超75万册。在对话中，他将分享：• 正确使用肖恩·埃利斯测试衡量产品市场契合度

summary.en: The question is, how would you feel if you could no longer use this product? Once you got a high enough percentage of users saying they'd be very disappointed, most of those products did pretty well. If you felt too low, those products tended to suffer. Just ignore the people who say they'd be somewhat disappointed. Th
summary.zh: 问题是：如果无法再使用这个产品，你会有什么感觉？一旦有够高比例的用户表示"非常失望"，大多数这类产品都表现不错。如果比例太低，这些产品往往就会陷入困境。直接忽略那些说"有点失望"的人。Th

episodeTitle.en: How to consistently go viral: Nikita Bier’s playbook for winning at consumer apps
episodeTitle.zh: 如何持续打造爆款产品：尼基塔·比尔（Nikita Bier）在消费类应用领域的成功秘籍

bio.en: Nikita Bier is a consumer-app builder who has launched more chart-topping apps than almost anyone else, selling tbh to Facebook for over $30 million and Gas to Discord for many millions more with a tiny team.
bio.zh: Nikita Bier 是一位消费级应用高手，他打造并推向排行榜榜首的应用数量几乎无人能及：以超过 3000 万美元将 tbh 出售给 Facebook，又以数千万美元将 Gas 出售给 Discord，且全程只有极小的团队与极少的资金。

guestBioOfficial.en: Nikita Bier is one of the most in-demand consumer, social, and growth experts in the world. He’s the co-founder of TBH (sold to Meta for more than $30 million) and Gas (sold to Discord for millions more) and has helped more consumer apps that have hit #1 in the app stores than any other person I’ve come across. He currently spends his time advising founders on growth, product, and design and is an investor and advisor to some of the best consumer tech companies, including Flo, Locket, Eight Sleep, Citizen, BeReal, Captions, and more. In our conversation, we discuss: • The inside story of how TBH and Gas achieved explosive growth
guestBioOfficial.zh: 尼基塔·比尔（Nikita Bier）是全球最受欢迎的消费、社交和增长领域专家之一。他曾联合创立TBH（以超3000万美元价格出售给Meta）和Gas（以数百万美元出售给Discord），助力多款应用登顶应用商店榜单。如今，他专注于为初创公司提供增长策略咨询，投资了Flo、Locket、Eight Sleep、Citizen、BeReal、Captions等多家消费科技公司。在对谈中，我们将讨论：• TBH和Gas实现爆发式增长的内部秘诀

summary.en: Nikita shares hard-won tactics for building viral consumer apps, emphasizing that you should hunt for latent demand where users jump through hoops to get value. He explains why building for teens (13-18) is the smartest wedge because their invitation rates collapse with age, and why most founders underestimate the chaotic grind of keeping a hit online. The conversation also covers how to recognize when to pivot and why product lives and dies in the pixels, not in documents.
summary.zh: Nikita 分享了打造病毒式消费应用的实战策略，强调要寻找用户愿意“绕远路”也要获得价值的潜在需求。他解释了为什么从青少年（13-18 岁）切入是最聪明的策略——因为随着年龄增长，用户的邀请率会骤降——以及为什么大多数创始人低估了维持一款爆款在线运转的混乱与艰辛。对话还涉及如何判断何时该转型，以及为什么产品的成败在于像素与体验，而非文档。

episodeTitle.en: Succeeding as an introvert, building zero-to-one, and PM’ing your career like a product | Deb Liu
episodeTitle.zh: 作为内向者的成功之道：从0到1的构建，以及像产品经理般规划职业生涯 | 黛布·刘（Deb Liu）

bio.en: Deb Liu was VP of Product at Facebook (creating and leading Facebook Marketplace, used by 1B+ monthly), led its first mobile ad product, and is CEO of Ancestry, with board roles including Intuit.
bio.zh: Deb Liu 曾任 Facebook 产品副总裁（创建并领导月活超 10 亿的 Facebook Marketplace，并主导首个移动广告产品），现任 Ancestry CEO，并在 Intuit 等公司任董事。

guestBioOfficial.en: Deb Liu is the CEO of Ancestry and former longtime VP of Product at Facebook. At Facebook, Deb led the creation of Facebook Marketplace, developed the first mobile ad product for apps, built the company’s games business, and launched Facebook Pay. She’s also held leadership roles at PayPal and eBay, serves on the board of Intuit, and is the author of Take Back Your Power. In our conversation, we discuss: • Why you should PM your career like you PM your product
guestBioOfficial.zh: 黛布·刘（Deb Liu）现任Ancestry首席执行官，曾长期担任Facebook产品副总裁。在Facebook任职期间，她主导了Facebook Marketplace的开发，打造了首款移动应用广告产品，构建了公司的游戏业务，并推出了Facebook Pay。她还曾在PayPal和eBay担任领导职务，现任Intuit董事会成员，并著有《夺回你的力量》一书。在对谈中，我们探讨了：•为何你应该像管理产品一样管理自己的职业生涯

summary.en: Deb shares tactical career advice, including why resilience is key and how to “PM your career like you PM your product.” She discusses succeeding in business as an introvert by reframing self-promotion as “educating others about your team's great work,” and what she learned building multiple zero-to-one billion-dollar businesses inside Facebook. The conversation is full of hard-won wisdom on career, leadership, and impact.
summary.zh: Deb 分享了务实的职业建议，包括为何韧性关键，以及如何“像做产品一样做自己的职业生涯管理”。她讨论了内向者如何在职场成功——把自我推销重新定义为“让他人了解团队的出色工作”，以及在 Facebook 内部打造多个从 0 到 1 的十亿美元业务的所学。对话充满关于职业、领导与影响力的宝贵智慧。

episodeTitle.en: Unorthodox PM tips: Automating user insights, unselling candidates, decision logs, more | Kevin Yien
episodeTitle.zh: 制作和营销

bio.en: Kevin Yien leads merchant product experiences at Stripe, previously built Square's restaurant business, and was Head of Product and Design at Mutiny.
bio.zh: 凯文·叶（Kevin Yien）在 Stripe 负责商户产品体验，此前在 Square 打造了餐饮业务，并曾任 Mutiny 的产品与设计负责人。

guestBioOfficial.en: Kevin Yien leads product for merchant experiences at Stripe. Before that, he meandered his way from being a technical designer to a product manager, built the restaurants business and ecosystem team at Square, and most recently was head of product and design at Mutiny. He also makes ice cream and teaches for fun. In our conversation, we discuss: • Why aspiring PMs should start in engineering, design, or sales
guestBioOfficial.zh: Kevin Yien谈产品管理：自动化用户洞察、拒绝候选人、决策日志等 | Kevin Yien

summary.en: Kevin argues every PM should be able to sell and support their own product, because if you can't, you can't be trusted to build it. He advocates keeping a decision log to build product sense through repeated reps and outcome review. The episode also covers his unconventional "unsell email" hiring tactic and practical uses of AI in PM work.
summary.zh: 凯文认为，每个 PM 都应该能卖、也能支持自己的产品，因为如果做不到，就不该被信任去构建它。他主张用"决策日志"通过反复决策与复盘结果来培养产品感。本期还涵盖了他非传统的"劝退邮件"招聘法，以及 AI 在 PM 工作中的实际应用。

episodeTitle.en: Improve strategy, influence, and decision-making by understanding your brain | Evan LaPointe
episodeTitle.zh: 通过了解大脑来提升战略、影响力和决策力 | 埃文·拉普安特

bio.en: Evan LaPointe is the founder of CORE Sciences, which teaches companies and individuals how the brain actually works and how to apply that understanding to collaborate, build products, and make smarter decisions; a four-time founder, he created Satellite (the fourth-largest analytics product on the internet), later acquired by Adobe where he led product strategy and innovation for Adobe's digital business.
bio.zh: Evan LaPointe 是 CORE Sciences 的创始人，该公司向企业和个人讲解大脑真正的工作方式，并据此帮助人们更好地协作、打造产品、做出更明智的决策；作为连续四次创业的人，他创办了 Satellite（互联网上第四大的分析产品），该公司后被 Adobe 收购，他随后在 Adobe 负责数字业务的产品战略与创新。

guestBioOfficial.en: Evan LaPointe is the founder of CORE Sciences, which teaches companies and individuals how our brains work and how that translates to improved collaboration, better products, faster decision-making, and more growth. Previously, Evan was the co-founder of Satellite, the fourth-largest analytics product on the internet today (it mostly runs behind the scenes, and pretty much everyone listening will have used it today without knowing it), which was acquired by Adobe, where he later ran product strategy, innovation, and long-range thinking for Adobe’s digital experiences business. In our conversation, we discuss: • The three different systems of the brain
guestBioOfficial.zh: 埃文·拉普安特是CORE Sciences的创始人，该公司教会企业和个人我们的大脑如何运作，以及如何将其转化为更好的协作、更优质的产品、更快的决策和更多增长。此前，埃文是Satellite的联合创始人，Satellite是当今互联网上第四大分析产品（它主要在幕后运行，几乎每个听众今天都会在不知情的情况下使用过它），后被Adobe收购，他随后在Adobe的数字体验业务中负责产品战略、创新和长期规划。在我们的对话中，我们讨论了：• 大脑的三个不同系统

summary.en: Evan frames the brain as a college campus with different 'departments,' and argues most people over-rely on the risk-averse 'history department' instead of routing problems to the more experimental, creative parts of the mind for dramatically better answers. He shows how this lens improves concrete work: becoming more influential by choosing the 'character' you play (devil's advocate, stress-tester, and so on), running better meetings, and increasing focus. A central, refreshingly blunt takeaway is that before anything else you must ask whether you are a 'miserable experience' to work with, because a toxic presence undermines everything else. The episode blends neuroscience with highly actionable tactics for building more productive relationships and making faster, smarter decisions.
summary.zh: Evan 把大脑比作一个有大大小小不同“部门”的大学校园，并指出大多数人都过度依赖那个规避风险的“历史系”，而不是把问题交给大脑中更具实验精神、更有创造力的部分，从而错过明显更好的答案。他用这个视角改进具体的工作：通过选择自己扮演的“角色”（比如唱反调的人、压力测试者等）来提升影响力、把会议开得更好、更专注。一个直白又核心的洞见是：在考虑其他一切之前，你必须先问自己是不是一个“让人难受的共事对象”，因为糟糕的个人状态会毁掉其他所有努力。这一期把神经科学和高度可操作的实战方法结合在一起，帮助你建立更高效的人际关系，并做出更快、更明智的决策。

episodeTitle.en: How embracing your emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (Art of Accomplishment)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何拥抱你的情绪将加速你的职业生涯 | 乔·哈德森（成就艺术）

bio.en: Joe Hudson is one of the most sought-after executive coaches among tech leaders, having worked with people from OpenAI, SpaceX, and Apple; his approach blends spiritual, psychological, and neurological practices to help people build a life of enjoyment and ease.
bio.zh: Joe Hudson 是科技圈高管中最抢手的教练之一，曾与来自 OpenAI、SpaceX、Apple 的人士合作；他的方法融合了精神、心理与神经科学的练习，帮助人们打造充满乐趣与从容的人生。

guestBioOfficial.en: Joe Hudson is one of the most sought-after executive coaches in Silicon Valley. He is the founder of Art of Accomplishment, a transformational coaching program that has helped tens of thousands of people, including many tech executives and founders from companies like Apple, OpenAI, and Google. His unique method of transformation comes from over 25 years of exploring neurological, psychological, and spiritual traditions, tested against real-world challenges. In our conversation, Joe shares: • Why the critical voice in your head is always wrong, and how to change your relationship with that voice
guestBioOfficial.zh:
乔·哈德森（Joe Hudson）是硅谷最受追捧的高管教练之一。他创立的"成就艺术"（Art of Accomplishment）转型教练项目已帮助数万人，包括来自苹果、OpenAI和谷歌等公司的许多科技高管和创始人。他独特的转变方法源于25年多来对神经学、心理学和精神传统的探索，并在现实挑战中进行验证。在我们的对话中，乔分享了：  
• 为什么你脑海中的批判声音总是错误的，以及如何改变与这种声音的关系

summary.en: Joe explains what most often keeps people stuck—unfelt and unexpressed emotions, and the critical voice in your head that is always wrong, contradictory, and 'telling you bullshit.' He teaches a playful practice of responding to that voice anew each day ('Oh, I see you're really scared. I've got you'), why falling in love with your emotions is powerful, and why focusing on what you want (and enjoying your work 10% more) boosts both efficiency and quality. The episode also covers a seven-minute gratitude practice that, he promises, will change your life.
summary.zh: Joe 解释了人们最常被困住的原因——未被感受与表达的情绪，以及脑中那个永远错误、自相矛盾、“在胡说八道”的批判性声音。他教了一种 playful 的练习：每天以新的方式回应那个声音（“噢，我看见你真的很害怕，我在这儿陪着你”），为何“爱上你的情绪”很有力量，以及为何聚焦你想要的（并把工作的乐趣提升 10%）能同时提高效率和质量。这期节目还讲了一个七分钟的感恩练习——他保证它会改变你的人生。

episodeTitle.en: Lessons from scaling Uber and Opendoor | Brian Tolkin (Head of Product at Opendoor, ex-Uber)
episodeTitle.zh: Uber和Opendoor扩张的经验教训 | Brian Tolkin（Opendoor产品主管，前Uber员工）

bio.en: Brian Tolkin is Head of Product and Design at Opendoor, previously an early Uber employee (#100) who started in operations, led uberPOOL's launch, and created Uber's product-operations function.
bio.zh: Brian Tolkin 是 Opendoor 产品与设计负责人，此前是 Uber 早期员工（第 100 号），从运营起步，领导了 uberPOOL 的发布，并创立了 Uber 的产品运营职能。

guestBioOfficial.en: Brian Tolkin is the Head of Product at Opendoor. Previously, he was one of the early employees at Uber, where he was instrumental in launching and growing UberPool, UberHop, and UberExpress and started one of the first product operations teams in tech. In our conversation, we dive into: • How to enable product and ops to work well together
guestBioOfficial.zh: Brian Tolkin是Opendoor的产品主管。此前，他是Uber的早期员工之一，在那里他在推出和发展UberPool、UberHop和UberExpress方面发挥了重要作用，并在科技领域创立了首批产品运营团队之一。在对话中，我们深入探讨了：• 如何让产品和运营部门协同高效工作

summary.en: Brian shares lessons on building products with a heavy operational component, arguing that ops experience gives a deep understanding of how the business actually works. He covers how to run great product reviews, how Opendoor applies the Jobs-to-be-Done framework, and the story of Zillow competing with then partnering Opendoor. The conversation is full of stories from the early days of Uber and Opendoor on scaling operationally-heavy tech companies.
summary.zh: Brian 分享了打造“强运营属性”产品的经验，认为运营经历让人深刻理解业务实际如何运转。他讲述了如何做好产品评审、Opendoor 如何应用“待办任务”框架，以及 Zillow 先竞争后合作的故事。对话充满了 Uber 与 Opendoor 早期扩展“重运营”科技公司的故事。

episodeTitle.en: The ultimate guide to paid growth | Timothy Davis (Shopify)
episodeTitle.zh: 《权力掮客：罗伯特·摩西与纽约的衰落》

bio.en: Timothy Davis led performance marketing for all of Shopify for two and a half years and, as a consultant, helped companies like Pinterest, LinkedIn, Redfin, and Eventbrite build and scale their performance marketing teams.
bio.zh: Timothy Davis 在 Shopify 全面负责效果营销长达两年半，并以顾问身份帮助 Pinterest、LinkedIn、Redfin、Eventbrite 等公司搭建并做大了效果营销团队。

guestBioOfficial.en: Timothy Davis has led performance marketing for all of Shopify for the past 2.5 years, and as a consultant has helped companies like Pinterest, LinkedIn, Redfin, and Eventbrite kickstart and scale their performance marketing teams. In every one of those cases, he got them so performant at paid growth that they significantly scale spend and investment in these channels. In our conversation, we cover: • When and how to start investing in performance marketing
guestBioOfficial.zh: 《最终指南：付费增长》 | 蒂莫西·戴维斯（Shopify）

summary.en: Timothy's core thesis is that paid is for everyone at baseline — at minimum paid search, because it's user-driven — but sequencing and evidence matter. He advises starting with Google Search, then Meta, then video/YouTube, and using your own analytics plus small 'signs of life' tests (e.g., 1% lookalikes built from your existing customers) before scaling spend. Critically, don't pour money into ads until you have product-market fit and can actually convert in that market. For team building, hire a data-literate generalist first (someone who finds signal in the noise), then a creative, then a dedicated data scientist; only add headcount when a 'red days' capacity calculator shows the team is genuinely overloaded, and run an 'ops cadence' spreadsheet to stay accountable. Judge performance with platform-native signals (ad strength, click share) and incrementality/Geo experiments rather than vanity metrics, and prefer multi-touch, time-decay attribution. Agencies are fine to start with, but choose partners who plan your exit and dig deep into keyword granularity, landing pages, and conversion paths.
summary.zh: Timothy 的核心观点是：付费广告对每家公司都该做——至少该做付费搜索，因为它是用户主动驱动的——但顺序和证据很重要。他建议先从 Google 搜索做起，再是 Meta，然后是视频/YouTube，并用你自己的分析数据加上小规模的「生命迹象」测试（比如用现有客户建的 1% 类似受众）来验证，再放大投放。关键是，在达成产品市场契合、且能真正在那个市场转化之前，别往广告里砸钱。搭团队时，先招一个懂数据、能从噪音里找信号的通用型人才，再招创意，再招专职数据科学家；只有当「红色天数」容量计算器显示团队真的超负荷时才加人，并用一张「运营节奏」表格来保持问责。评估效果要看平台原生的信号（广告强度、点击份额）和增量性/地理实验，而不是虚荣指标，归因上偏好多触点、时间衰减。代理公司起步时可以用，但要选会为你的退出做规划、并深入到关键词粒度、落地页和转化路径里的人。

episodeTitle.en: 5 essential questions to craft a winning strategy | Roger Martin (author, advisor, speaker)
episodeTitle.zh: 《制定制胜战略的五个关键问题》| 罗杰·马丁（作家、顾问、演讲者）

bio.en: Roger Martin is one of the world's most trusted strategy advisors, professor emeritus at the Rotman School of Management at the University of Toronto, and author of the classic Playing to Win.
bio.zh: Roger Martin 是全球最受信赖的战略顾问之一，多伦多大学罗特曼管理学院荣休教授，也是经典著作《赢得胜利》（Playing to Win）的作者。

guestBioOfficial.en: Roger Martin is one of the world’s leading experts on strategy and the author of Playing to Win, one of the most beloved books on strategy. He’s written extensively for the Harvard Business Review; consulted for dozens of Fortune 500 companies, including P&G, Lego, and Ford; and written 11 other books. In our conversation, we discuss: • The five key questions you need to answer to develop an effective strategy
guestBioOfficial.zh: 罗杰·马丁是战略领域的全球顶尖专家之一，也是最受欢迎的战略著作《Playing to Win》的作者。他为《哈佛商业评论》撰写了大量文章，为包括宝洁、乐高、福特在内的数十家《财富》500强公司提供咨询服务，并著有11本其他书籍。在我们的对话中，我们讨论了：• 制定有效战略需要回答的五个关键问题

summary.en: Roger argues that strategy is an integrative activity answering five questions - winning aspiration, where to play, how to win, required capabilities, and management systems - and that you must choose either differentiation or low cost. He critiques how business schools teach strategy poorly, and insists great strategists are made through practice, not born. The episode gives ground-level PMs and ICs a practical framework for crafting real strategy.
summary.zh: Roger 主张战略是一项“整合性”活动，需回答五个问题——制胜抱负、在何处竞争、如何取胜、所需能力、以及支撑性管理体系——并且必须在“差异化”与“低成本”之间二选一。他批评商学院对战略的教学方式之多谬，并坚称伟大的战略家是练出来的，而非天生的。本期为一线 PM 与独立贡献者提供了一套制定真正战略的实用框架。

episodeTitle.en: Building a world-class data org | Jessica Lachs (VP of Analytics and Data Science at DoorDash)
episodeTitle.zh: 打造世界级数据组织 | 杰西卡·拉克斯（Jessica Lachs，DoorDash分析与数据科学副总裁）

bio.en: Jessica Lachs is Vice President of Analytics and Data Science at DoorDash, where she has built one of the largest and most respected data teams in tech over a 10+-year tenure and was the company's first GM launching new markets; she previously founded the social-gifting startup GiftSimple.
bio.zh: Jessica Lachs 是 DoorDash 的分析与数据科学副总裁，在十余年任期里打造了科技圈规模最大、最受尊敬的数据团队之一，也是公司开拓新市场的第一位 GM；她此前创办了社交送礼初创 GiftSimple。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jessica Lachs is the global head of analytics and data science at DoorDash, where she’s built one of the largest and most respected data organizations in tech. In her more than 10 years at DoorDash, she has served as the first general manager, responsible for launching new markets; the head of business ops and analytics; and the VP of analytics and data science. Previously, Jessica founded GiftSimple, a social gifting startup, and started her career at Lehman Brothers as an investment banking analyst. In our conversation, she shares: • How to structure and scale a high-impact analytics organization
guestBioOfficial.zh:
杰西卡·拉克斯（Jessica Lachs）是DoorDash全球分析与数据科学负责人，她在该公司打造了科技领域规模最大、最受尊敬的数据组织之一。在DoorDash任职的十多年间，她曾担任首位负责新市场拓展的总经理、业务运营与分析部门主管，以及分析与数据科学副总裁。此前，她创立了社交礼品初创公司GiftSimple，并在雷曼兄弟担任投资银行分析师。在对谈中，她分享了：
• 如何构建和扩展高影响力分析组织

summary.en: Jessica makes the case that analytics should be a business-impact function, not a service desk—answering 'what do we do now?' not just 'why?'. She argues for a centralized data org, explains why retention is a terrible metric to goal on (find a short-term measure that drives long-term output), and shares what to look for when hiring data people. The conversation is full of concrete examples of how DoorDash's data team shaped real decisions, plus great stories from the company's scrappy early days.
summary.zh: Jessica 主张分析应当是一个“驱动业务影响”的职能，而非服务台——回答“我们现在该怎么做？”，而不只是“为什么？”。她主张数据团队集中化，解释了为何“留存”是个糟糕的考核指标（应找一个能驱动长期产出的短期指标），并分享了招聘数据人才时看重的点。对话充满了 DoorDash 数据团队如何影响真实决策的具体案例，以及公司草创期的精彩故事。

episodeTitle.en: Building product at Stripe: craft, metrics, and customer obsession | Jeff Weinstein (Product lead)
episodeTitle.zh: 在Stripe构建产品：工艺、指标和以客户为中心 | 杰夫·温斯坦（Jeff Weinstein，产品负责人）

bio.en: Jeff Weinstein spent six-plus years at Stripe, where he led payment-infrastructure product teams, scaled Stripe Payments to hundreds of billions in annual volume, and grew Stripe Atlas—now used to start one in six new Delaware corporations.
bio.zh: Jeff Weinstein 在 Stripe 任职六年多，领导支付基础设施产品团队，将 Stripe Payments 的规模做到每年数千亿交易量，并壮大了 Stripe Atlas——如今全美每六家新成立的特拉华州公司就有一家通过它注册。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jeff Weinstein is a product lead at Stripe, where he helped grow their payment APIs to hundreds of billions in volume and transformed the way founders start companies into a few simple clicks with Atlas. Prior to Stripe, Jeff led several startups and sold companies to Groupon and Box. He’s known for his customer obsession, craft, quality, and building beloved products businesses rely on. In our conversation, we discuss: • The power of customer obsession and how to operationalize it in the product development process
guestBioOfficial.zh: 杰夫·温斯坦是Stripe的产品负责人，曾帮助将其支付API的交易量提升至数千亿美元，并通过Atlas将创始人创办公司的流程简化至几次点击。在加入Stripe之前，杰夫领导了多家初创公司，并将公司出售给Groupon和Box。他以对客户的执着、工艺、质量以及打造深受用户喜爱的产品而闻名。在我们的对话中，我们讨论了： • 客户执着的力量以及如何在产品开发过程中将其付诸实践

summary.en: Jeff breaks down the skills behind his remarkably effective product leadership: a go-go optimism and long-term compounding philosophy, operationalizing product craft and quality, and treating every customer complaint as an 'unbelievable gift' of direct signal. He shares the 'Stripe Study Groups' empathy practice he started (role-play as a customer with no agenda to solve problems), how to talk to customers, how to know you have product-market fit, and how to pick great metrics. The episode is the longest in Lenny's history for good reason—a full archaeology of a beloved product leader's craft.
summary.zh: Jeff 拆解了他极高效率的产品领导力背后的技能：积极进取的乐观主义与长期复利式的理念、把产品工艺与质量落到日常，以及把每条客户抱怨都当作直连信号的“不可思议的礼物”。他分享了发起的“Stripe 学习小组”共情练习（角色扮演成客户、不以解决问题为目的）、如何与客户交谈、如何判断你已找到产品市场契合，以及如何挑选好指标。这期节目成为 Lenny 史上最长的一期并非没有原因——它是对一位备受喜爱的产品领导者“手艺”的完整考古。

episodeTitle.en: Pattern Breakers: How to find a breakthrough startup idea | Mike Maples, Jr. (Partner at Floodgate)
episodeTitle.zh: 《破局者：如何找到突破性创业理念》 | 小迈克·马普尔斯（Mike Maples, Jr.，Floodgate合伙人）

bio.en: Mike Maples Jr is a legendary early-stage investor and co-founder of Floodgate, a seed-investing pioneer that backed Twitter, Lyft, Twitch, and other transformative companies.
bio.zh: 小迈克·梅普尔斯（Mike Maples Jr）是一位传奇的早期投资人、种子投资先驱 Floodgate 的联合创始人，曾投资 Twitter、Lyft、Twitch 等变革性公司。

guestBioOfficial.en: Mike Maples, Jr. is a legendary early-stage startup investor and a co-founder and partner at Floodgate. He’s made early bets on transformative companies like Twitter, Lyft, Twitch, Okta, Rappi, and Applied Intuition and is one of the pioneers of seed-stage investing as a category. He’s been on the Forbes Midas List eight times and enjoys sharing the lessons he’s learned from his years studying iconic companies. In his new book, Pattern Breakers: Why Some Start-Ups Change the Future, co-authored with Peter Ziebelman, he discusses what he’s found separates startups and founders that break through and change the world from those that don’t. After spending years reviewing the notes and decks from the thousands of startups he’s known over the past two decades, he’s uncovered three ways that breakthrough founders think and act differently. In our conversation, Mike talks about: • The three elements of breakthrough startup ideas
guestBioOfficial.zh: 小迈克·马普尔斯（Mike Maples, Jr.）是传奇的早期阶段创业投资人，也是Floodgate的联合创始人及合伙人。他早期投资了推特、Lyft、Twitch、Okta、Rappi和Applied Intuition等变革性公司，是种子期投资领域的先驱。他八次入选《福布斯米达斯榜单》，乐于分享多年研究标志性公司的经验。在与彼得·齐贝尔曼（Peter Ziebelman）合著的新书《破局者：为何有些创业公司能改变未来》中，他剖析了突破性创业公司与未能突破、改变世界的创业公司之间的差异。通过研究过去20年间认识的数千家初创公司的笔记和演示文稿，他发现了突破性创业者在思维和行动上的三个不同之处。在对谈中，迈克探讨了：• 突破性创业理念的三个要素

summary.en: Mike argues breakthrough startups win through asymmetric warfare enabled by inflections, insights, and founder-future-fit, not by out-executing incumbents. He explains that 80% of his biggest returns came from pivots and that startups should propose a radically different future. The episode is a deep framework for spotting and backing category-defining companies.
summary.zh: 迈克认为，突破性的初创公司靠"拐点、洞见与创始人与未来的契合"发起不对称战争取胜，而非靠比巨头执行得更好。他说明，自己 80% 的最高回报来自转型，且初创公司应提出截然不同的未来。本期是一套用于识别并押注"定义品类"公司的深度框架。

episodeTitle.en: Dylan Field live at Figma's Config: Intuition, simplicity, and the future of design
episodeTitle.zh: Dylan Field在Figma Config上的现场演讲：直觉、简洁性与设计的未来

bio.en: Dylan Field is the co-founder and CEO of Figma, the collaborative interface design tool that became one of the most widely used products by design and product teams worldwide.
bio.zh: Dylan Field 是 Figma 的联合创始人兼 CEO；Figma 是一款协作式界面设计工具，已成为全球设计与产品团队使用最广泛的产品之一。

guestBioOfficial.en: Dylan Field is the co-founder and CEO of Figma, the collaborative design platform that has revolutionized how product teams work. In my first-ever live podcast, recorded at Figma Config, Dylan and I dig into:
guestBioOfficial.zh: Dylan Field是协作设计平台Figma的联合创始人兼CEO，该平台彻底改变了产品团队的工作方式。在我首次在Figma Config录制的现场播客中，Dylan和我深入探讨了：

summary.en: In this conversation, Dylan Field shares the story of building Figma from a fledgling browser-based design tool into a category-defining product used across the industry. He discusses why treating design as a first-class, collaborative discipline—rather than a handoff—was core to Figma's differentiation and growth. Dylan also digs into lessons on product taste, hiring elite small teams, and why staying patient and focused on craft ultimately beat chasing every market opportunity.
summary.zh: 在这期对话中，Dylan Field 讲述了如何将 Figma 从一个浏览器端的初创设计工具，打造成被全行业使用的标杆性产品。他谈到，把设计当作一项一等公民、可协作的学科（而非交付环节）是 Figma 实现差异化与增长的核心。Dylan 还深入分享了关于产品品味、组建精悍精英团队的经验，以及为何保持耐心、专注工艺最终胜过追逐每一个市场机会。

episodeTitle.en: The social radar: Y Combinator’s secret weapon | Jessica Livingston (co-founder of YC, author)
episodeTitle.zh: 社交雷达：Y Combinator的秘密武器 | 杰西卡·利文斯顿（YC联合创始人、作家）

bio.en: Jessica Livingston is the co-founder of Y Combinator—the first and most famous startup accelerator, which has funded 5,000+ companies including Airbnb, Stripe, and Coinbase—and author of Founders at Work; she is famed for her 'social radar' for reading people.
bio.zh: Jessica Livingston 是 Y Combinator 的联合创始人——这是第一家也是最著名的创业加速器，已投资 5000 多家公司，包括 Airbnb、Stripe、Coinbase——也是《Founders at Work》的作者；她以善于“读人”的“社交雷达”而闻名。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jessica Livingston is a co-founder of Y Combinator, the first and most successful startup accelerator. Y Combinator has funded over 5,000 companies, 200 of which are now unicorns, including Airbnb, Dropbox, DoorDash, Stripe, Coinbase, and Reddit. Jessica played a crucial role in YC’s early success, when she was nicknamed the “social radar” because of her uncanny ability to quickly evaluate people—an essential skill when investing in early-stage startups. She’s also the host of the popular podcast The Social Radars, where she interviews billion-dollar-startup founders, and the author of the acclaimed book Founders at Work, which captures the origin stories of some of today’s most interesting companies. In our conversation, we discuss: • How Jessica gained the affectionate title of the “social radar”
guestBioOfficial.zh: 杰西卡·利文斯顿是Y Combinator的联合创始人，Y Combinator是首家且最成功的创业加速器。Y Combinator已资助超过5,000家公司，其中200家现已成为独角兽，包括Airbnb、Dropbox、DoorDash、Stripe、Coinbase和Reddit。杰西卡在YC早期成功中发挥了关键作用，当时她被昵称为"社交雷达"，因为她具有快速评估人的非凡能力——这在投资早期初创公司时是一项至关重要的技能。她还是广受欢迎的播客《社交雷达》的主持人，在节目中采访亿万美元初创公司的创始人，并撰写广受好评的《创始人工作手册》，该书记录了当今一些最有趣公司的起源故事。在我们的对话中，我们讨论了：• 杰西卡如何获得"社交雷达"这个亲切称号

summary.en: Jessica reveals the superpower behind her 'Social Radar' nickname: an uncanny ability to read founders (do the co-founders get along? do they get defensive? are they hustlers who'll burn the boat?). She shares wild early YC stories—including how the Airbnb founders won the partners over with their Obama O's and Cap'n McCain's cereal boxes—and how being defensively committed signals trouble. The episode also covers her Social Radars podcast and a fun 'reading the mind in the eyes' test, with tips on developing your own people-reading ability.
summary.zh: Jessica 揭开了她“社交雷达”绰号背后的超能力：一种读创始人的惊人本领（联合创始人处得来吗？他们会防御性地辩解吗？他们是会破釜沉舟的实干家吗？）。她分享了 YC 早期的疯狂故事——包括 Airbnb 创始人如何用“Obama O's”和“Cap'n McCain's”麦片盒征服合伙人，以及“防御性过强”如何预示麻烦。这期节目还涵盖了她的 Social Radars 播客和一个有趣的“读眼识心”测试，并给出培养读人能力的建议。

episodeTitle.en: Making an impact through authenticity and curiosity | Ami Vora (CPO at Faire, ex-WhatsApp, FB, IG)
episodeTitle.zh: 通过真实与好奇心产生影响 | 阿米·沃拉（Faire首席产品官，前WhatsApp、Facebook、Instagram高管）

bio.en: Ami Vora is Chief Product Officer at Faire, the leading B2B marketplace for independent retailers and brands, and was employee #150 at Facebook, where she launched the first developer platform and led global ads and WhatsApp product/design.
bio.zh: Ami Vora 是 Faire（面向独立零售商与品牌的最大 B2B 市场）首席产品官，也是 Facebook 第 150 号员工，曾发布首个开发者平台，并领导全球广告业务及 WhatsApp 的产品与设计。

guestBioOfficial.en: Ami Vora is the Chief Product Officer of Faire, which connects independent retailers and brands around the world. Before Faire, Ami spent over 15 years at Meta, including as VP of Product and Design for WhatsApp (2B+ users), VP of Product for Facebook’s ads system (now $130B of annual revenue), and director at Instagram. She began her career working on developer tools at Microsoft. In our conversation, we discuss: • Why execution eats strategy for breakfast
guestBioOfficial.zh:
阿米·沃拉是Faire的首席产品官，该平台连接全球独立零售商和品牌。在加入Faire之前，阿米在Meta工作了超过15年，曾担任WhatsApp产品与设计副总裁（用户超过20亿）、Facebook广告系统副总裁（年营收现已达1300亿美元）以及Instagram的总监。她职业生涯的开端是在微软开发者工具部门工作。在我们的对谈中，我们将探讨：  
• 执行为何会把战略当早餐吃掉

summary.en: Ami discusses the skill of disagreeing skillfully—subordinating your ego to get to the best outcome—and using metaphors and imagery to rally a team around a shared feeling. She introduces the “hill climb” metaphor to distinguish local from global optima and what sustains you through the valley. The conversation covers building strategy skills, being a successful woman in tech, and setting up effective goals, plus a fun lightning round.
summary.zh: Ami 探讨了“优雅地异议”这门艺术——把自我收起来，只为达成最好的结果——以及用隐喻和意象让团队围绕共同感受团结一致。她提出“爬山”隐喻来区分局部最优与全局最优，以及是什么支撑你穿越低谷。对话涵盖策略能力、身为科技行业女性的成功之道、设定有效目标，以及一轮有趣的快问快答。

episodeTitle.en: Hard-won lessons building 0 to 1 inside Atlassian | Tanguy Crusson (Head of Jira Product Discovery)
episodeTitle.zh: 《在Atlassian内部从0到1的艰辛历程 | 坦古伊·克鲁松（Tanguy Crusson，Jira产品发现负责人）》

bio.en: Tanguy Crusson is a 10+ year Atlassian veteran who has led major internal big bets including HipChat, Statuspage, and Jira Product Discovery, one of the fastest-growing products in Atlassian's history.
bio.zh: Tanguy Crusson 是一位在 Atlassian 任职逾十年的老兵，曾领导多项重大的内部“从零到一”赌注，包括 HipChat、Statuspage，以及 Atlassian 史上增长最快的产品之一 Jira Product Discovery。

guestBioOfficial.en: Tanguy Crusson is the product lead for Jira Product Discovery at Atlassian. In his more than 10 years at the company, he has been instrumental in taking several new products from zero to one, including HipChat, Statuspage, and Jira Product Discovery. In this episode, we dive deep into the struggles of innovating and building new products inside a large company. Tanguy shares candid stories about what worked, what didn’t, and his many hard-won lessons learned about how to successfully build 0 to 1. We cover: • Why large companies with so many advantages still fail at creating new products
guestBioOfficial.zh: 坦吉·克鲁松（Tanguy Crusson）是Atlassian公司Jira产品探索部门的产品负责人。他在该公司的十余年间，成功推动了多款新产品从零到一的成长，包括HipChat、Statuspage和Jira Product Discovery。在本期节目中，我们将深入探讨大型企业内部创新和打造新产品的挑战。坦吉将分享真知灼见，讲述成功经验与失败教训，揭示如何从0到1成功打造新产品。我们将重点探讨：•为何拥有诸多优势的大型企业仍在新产品开发上屡屡碰壁

summary.en: Tanguy shares the real, unglamorous challenges of innovating and building zero-to-one inside a large company like Atlassian. He discusses why some internal big bets worked and others didn't, how to get coverage for ambitious ideas, and what he learned from products like HipChat and Jira Product Discovery. The episode is a candid look at corporate innovation from someone who has actually shipped it.
summary.zh: Tanguy 分享了在 Atlassian 这样的大公司内部推动创新、打造“从零到一”产品的真实且不易的难题。他讨论了为何有些内部大赌注成功了、有些却没有，如何为雄心勃勃的想法争取支持，以及从 HipChat 和 Jira Product Discovery 等产品中学到的东西。本期是一位真正交付过产品的人的、坦诚的企业创新透视。

episodeTitle.en: The paths to power: How to grow your influence and advance your career | Jeffrey Pfeffer (Stanford)
episodeTitle.zh: 通往权力的道路：如何提升你的影响力并推进你的职业生涯 | 杰弗里·普费弗（Jeffrey Pfeffer，斯坦福大学）

bio.en: Jeffrey Pfeffer is a Professor of Organizational Behavior at Stanford Graduate School of Business and the author of The 7 Rules of Power, who teaches that power is a learnable skill—not a personality trait—that advances your career and well-being.
bio.zh: Jeffrey Pfeffer 是斯坦福商学院组织行为学教授、《权力的 7 条法则》（The 7 Rules of Power）的作者，他主张权力是一项可习得的技能——而非性格特质——能推动你的职业生涯与幸福感。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jeffrey Pfeffer teaches the single most popular (and somewhat controversial) class at Stanford’s Graduate School of Business: The Paths to Power. He’s also the author of 16 books, including 7 Rules of Power: Surprising—But True—Advice on How to Get Things Done and Advance Your Career. He has taught at Harvard, the London Business School, and IESE and has written for publications like Fortune and the Washington Post. Recognized by the Academy of Management and listed in the Thinkers50 Hall of Fame, Jeffrey also serves on several corporate and nonprofit boards, bringing his expertise to global audiences through seminars and executive education. In our conversation, we discuss: • Jeffrey’s seven rules of power
guestBioOfficial.zh:
杰弗里·普费弗（Jeffrey Pfeffer）在斯坦福商学院的研究生院教授最受欢迎（但颇具争议）的课程《通往权力的道路》。他还是16本书的作者，包括《权力的七条法则：令人惊讶却真实的建议》和《提升职业生涯》。他曾在哈佛大学、伦敦商学院和IESE商学院任教，并为《财富》杂志和《华盛顿邮报》等媒体撰稿。杰弗里获得了管理学会的认可，并入选Thinkers50名人堂，同时还担任多家企业和非营利组织的董事会成员，通过研讨会和高管教育向全球受众传播专业知识。在我们的对话中，我们讨论了：
• 杰弗里提出的七条权力法则

summary.en: Jeffrey lays out his seven rules of power—get out of your own way, break the rules, show up powerfully, build a brand, network relentlessly, use your power, and accept that how you got it will be forgiven—and insists these are masterable skills, not personality. He argues that if you think power is 'dirty' you'll unconsciously sabotage your own success, and that more good people need power so it's used for good. The conversation walks through each rule with real examples and ends with concrete steps you can start today to build your own power, whether you're an IC or a CEO.
summary.zh: Jeffrey 列出了他的七条权力法则——别挡自己的路、打破规则、以强者的姿态出现、建立个人品牌、不懈地经营人脉、运用你的权力、并接受一个事实：你获取权力的方式终会被原谅——并强调这些都是可掌握的技能，而非性格。他主张，如果你认为权力“肮脏”，就会在潜意识里 sabotage 自己的成功；而需要更多好人掌握权力，权力才能被用于善。对话逐条讲解每条法则并配以真实案例，最后给出你今天就能开始的、建立自身权力的具体步骤——无论你是个人贡献者还是 CEO。

episodeTitle.en: Lessons from a 2-time unicorn builder, 50-time startup advisor and 20-time board member | Uri Levine
episodeTitle.zh: 从两次独角兽公司创始人、50次创业顾问到20次董事会成员的经验谈 | 乌里·莱文

bio.en: Uri Levine is co-founder of Waze and nine other companies, has sold two companies for over $1 billion, advised 50+ founders, and authored Fall in Love with the Problem, Not the Solution.
bio.zh: Uri Levine 是 Waze 与另外九家公司的联合创始人，曾将两家公司以超 10 亿美元售出，为 50 多位创始人提供过顾问服务，并著有《爱上问题，而非方案》（Fall in Love with the Problem, Not the Solution）。

guestBioOfficial.en: Uri Levine is the co-founder of Waze, the world’s largest community-based traffic and navigation app, acquired by Google for over $1 billion. He’s also founded nine other companies, been on the board of 20 companies, and advised more than 50 companies. He’s most recently the author of Fall in Love with the Problem, Not the Solution: A Handbook for Entrepreneurs, hailed by Steve Wozniak as the “Bible for entrepreneurs.” Uri is dedicated to creating impactful startups that solve real-world problems and has seen everything from failure to moderate success to big success. In our conversation, we dig into: • Why falling in love with the problem is key to startup success
guestBioOfficial.zh: 乌里·莱文是全球最大社区导航应用Waze的联合创始人，该应用被谷歌以超过10亿美元的价格收购。他还创立了其他九家公司，担任过20家公司的董事会成员，并为50多家公司提供过咨询服务。他最新著作《爱上问题而非解决方案：创业者手册》被史蒂夫·沃兹尼亚克誉为“创业者的圣经”。乌里致力于打造能解决现实问题的有影响力初创企业，见证了从失败到平庸成功再到巨大成功的全过程。在对话中，我们将深入探讨：• 爱上问题是创业成功的关键

summary.en: Uri distills the biggest lessons from working with dozens of startups into one core idea: fall in love with the problem, not the solution. He shares why founders should validate the pain before building, stay ready to pivot when the data disagrees, and keep the user's problem front and center through every stage. The episode is a founder's field guide to building companies that actually matter.
summary.zh: Uri 将他与数十家初创公司共事所得的最大经验，提炼为一个核心理念：爱上问题，而非方案。他分享了为什么创始人应当在动手前先验证“痛点”、在数据相悖时随时准备转型，以及为何要在每个阶段都把用户的问题置于最前沿。本期是一份创始人的实战指南，关于打造真正有意义的公司。

episodeTitle.en: Inside Canva: Coaches not managers, giving away your Legos, and embracing AI | Cameron Adams
episodeTitle.zh: Canva内部：教练而非管理者，分享乐高积木，拥抱AI | 卡梅伦·亚当斯

bio.en: Cameron “Cam” Adams is co-founder and Chief Product Officer at Canva, the profitable design platform generating billions in ARR and growing 60%+ year over year.
bio.zh: Cameron “Cam” Adams 是 Canva 的联合创始人兼首席产品官，Canva 是一家盈利的设计平台，年经常性收入达数十亿美元，年增速超 60%。

guestBioOfficial.en: Cameron Adams is the co-founder and chief product officer of Canva. Canva is one of the world’s most valuable private software companies, used by 95% of Fortune 500 companies. Since its launch in 2013, Canva has grown to over 150 million monthly users in more than 190 countries, generating $2.3 billion in annual revenue. Prior to Canva, Cameron ran a design consultancy, worked at Google on Google Wave, and founded the email startup Fluent. He is also an author of five web design books and a regular speaker at global conferences. In our conversation, we discuss: • Why they spent a year building their minimum viable product (MVP) before launch
guestBioOfficial.zh:
卡梅伦·亚当斯（Cameron Adams）是Canva的联合创始人兼首席产品官。Canva是全球最具价值的私营软件公司之一，95%的《财富》500强企业都在使用该平台。自2013年推出以来，Canva已在190多个国家发展至每月1.5亿用户，年营收达23亿美元。在加入Canva之前，卡梅伦曾经营一家设计咨询公司，在谷歌参与Google Wave项目开发，并创立了邮件初创公司Fluent。他还是五本网页设计书籍的作者，并经常在全球会议上发言。在本次对谈中，我们探讨了以下内容：
• 他们为何在产品上线前花费一年时间打造最小可行产品（MVP）

summary.en: Cam shares how Canva stays product-obsessed at massive scale, including its freemium strategy and a unique culture where everyone has a coach and people “give away their Lego.” He discusses lessons on building MVPs, how the product team thinks about AI inside the product, and their SEO and growth strategy. The conversation also peeks into Canva's team culture and recent launches.
summary.zh: Cam 分享了 Canva 在超大规模下如何保持“产品痴迷”，包括免费增值策略，以及“人人都有教练、乐于交出手中积木”的独特文化。他讨论了打造 MVP 的教训、产品团队如何看待产品内的 AI，以及他们的 SEO 与增长策略。对话还一窥 Canva 的团队文化与近期发布。

episodeTitle.en: The surprising truth about what closes deals: Insights from 2.5m sales conversations | Matt Dixon
episodeTitle.zh: 《成交背后的惊人真相：250万次销售对话的洞察》|马特·迪克森

bio.en: Matt Dixon is a sales and customer-experience researcher and author of the bestsellers The Challenger Sale and The JOLT Effect, based on studies of millions of sales conversations.
bio.zh: 马特·迪克森（Matt Dixon）是一位销售与客户体验研究专家，也是畅销书《挑战式销售》（The Challenger Sale）与《JOLT 效应》（The JOLT Effect）的作者，其结论基于对数百万次销售对话的研究。

guestBioOfficial.en: Matt Dixon is one of the world’s foremost experts in sales and the author of The Challenger Sale, which sold over a million copies worldwide and was a #1 Amazon and Wall Street Journal bestseller. His most recent book, The JOLT Effect, focuses on overcoming customer indecision—one of the biggest challenges to closing deals. Outside of writing, Matt co-founded DCM Insights, a boutique consultancy helping organizations understand customer behavior, and is a frequent contributor to the Harvard Business Review, with more than 20 print and online articles to his credit. In our conversation, we discuss: • Why 40% to 60% of qualified sales opportunities are lost due to customer indecision
guestBioOfficial.zh: 马特·迪克森是全球销售领域的顶尖专家，《挑战者销售》一书全球销量超百万册，并登上亚马逊和《华尔街日报》畅销书榜单。他最新著作《JOLT效应》聚焦克服客户犹豫不决——这是成交的最大挑战之一。除写作外，马特还联合创立了DCM Insights，这家精品咨询公司帮助组织理解客户行为，并为《哈佛商业评论》撰写20余篇纸质版与网络版文章。在对话中，我们将探讨：•为何40%至60%的合格销售机会因客户犹豫不决而流失

summary.en: Matt reveals that most deals are lost not to competitors but to customer indecision driven by fear of failure, and that dialing up FOMO backfires 87% of the time. He lays out the JOLT method - judge indecision, offer a recommendation, limit exploration, and take risk off the table. The episode also revisits the Challenger Sale's lessons on leading the customer's thinking.
summary.zh: 马特揭示，大多数交易不是输给竞争对手，而是输给由"害怕搞砸"驱动的客户犹豫，且制造紧迫感（FOMO）有 87% 的概率适得其反。他给出了 JOLT 方法——判断犹豫、给出建议、限制选择、消除风险。本期还重温了《挑战式销售》中关于"引领客户思考"的要点。

episodeTitle.en: Unorthodox frameworks for growing your product, career, and impact | Bangaly Kaba (YT, IG, FB)
episodeTitle.zh: 《增长你的产品、职业和影响力的非传统框架 | 班加利·卡巴（YouTube、Instagram、Facebook）》

bio.en: Bangaly Kaba was an early growth PM at Facebook, Head of Growth at Instagram (scaling it past 1 billion users), VP of Product at Instacart, and is Director of Product Management at YouTube, known for his framework on driving organizational change.
bio.zh: Bangaly Kaba 曾是 Facebook 早期增长产品经理、Instagram 增长负责人（将其扩展到超 10 亿用户）、Instacart 产品副总裁，现任 YouTube 产品管理总监，以其推动组织变革的框架闻名。

guestBioOfficial.en: Bangaly Kaba was an early growth PM at Facebook, head of growth at Instagram, and VP of Product at Instacart and is currently Director of Product at YouTube overseeing a global team working on creator monetization. Bangaly has also been a growth advisor to dozens of companies, including Twitter, on the board of multiple companies, and is an active angel investor. In our conversation, we discuss: • A simple framework for choosing where to work and what to work on
guestBioOfficial.zh:
班加利·卡巴（Bangaly Kaba）曾在Facebook担任早期增长产品经理，在Instagram担任增长主管，并在Instacart担任产品副总裁，目前在YouTube担任产品总监，负责监督全球团队的创作者变现工作。班加利还为Twitter等数十家公司提供增长咨询，担任多家公司的董事会成员，并且是一位活跃的天使投资人。在我们的对话中，我们将讨论：  
• 选择工作地点和工作内容的简单框架

summary.en: Bangaly shares a five-component change framework—vision, skills, incentives, resources, action plan—and the discipline of truly understanding a problem before justifying and executing on it. He discusses his legendary “How to Choose Where to Work” essay and how impact depends on the environment and your skills. The conversation is packed with lessons on growth, culture, and making real change inside large organizations.
summary.zh: Bangaly 分享了一个五要素变革框架——愿景、技能、激励、资源、行动计划——以及“先真正理解问题，再论证和执行”的纪律。他谈到了那篇传奇的《如何选择工作与方向》文章，以及影响力如何取决于环境与个人技能。对话充满了关于增长、文化和在大型组织内产生真正变革的洞见。

episodeTitle.en: Why not asking for what you want is holding you back | Kenneth Berger (exec coach, first PM @Slack)
episodeTitle.zh: 为何不主动争取想要的东西会阻碍你前进 | 肯尼斯·伯格（执行教练，Slack首位产品经理）

bio.en: Kenneth Berger was Slack's first product manager and is now an executive coach helping startup leaders make ambitious work sustainable without burning out.
bio.zh: 肯尼斯·伯杰（Kenneth Berger）是 Slack 的第一位产品经理，如今是一位高管教练，帮助初创公司领导者在不透支的前提下持续推进高难度目标。

guestBioOfficial.en: Kenneth Berger coaches startup leaders on how to prevent burnout, advocate for their desired lifestyle, and make a meaningful impact on the world. He’s spent more than  20 years in the tech industry, is a former founder backed by top investors, and was the first product manager at Slack. Kenneth’s core mission is to help startup leaders change the world by learning to ask for what they want, living with integrity, and building genuine relationships even with the people they find most challenging. Currently he is writing a book, Ask for What You Want, in which he aims to share his actionable strategies for creating change in the world. In our conversation, we explore: • Why asking for what you want is so impactful
guestBioOfficial.zh: 肯尼斯·伯格为初创企业领导者提供指导，帮助他们预防职业倦怠、倡导理想生活方式，并为世界创造积极影响。他在科技行业深耕逾20年，曾是获得顶级投资者的初创公司创始人，也是Slack的首位产品经理。肯尼斯的核心使命是帮助初创企业领导者通过学会主动争取想要的东西、秉持诚信原则以及与最具挑战性的人建立真诚关系来改变世界。目前，他正在撰写《勇于争取》一书，旨在分享其推动世界变革的实用策略。在对话中，我们将探讨：• 主动争取想要的东西为何具有深远影响

summary.en: Kenneth centers his coaching on the idea of "ask for what you want," noting that voicing desires out loud dramatically increases the odds of getting them. He frames sustainable startup work as avoiding both burnout and sellout. The episode distills lessons from his decade as an operator and years as a coach into practical advice for ambitious leaders.
summary.zh: 肯尼斯把教练工作的核心放在"开口要你想要的"这一理念上，指出把愿望大声说出来会大幅提高实现的概率。他把可持续的创业工作定义为既不倦怠也不妥协。本期将他十余年运营者与多年教练的经验，提炼成对雄心勃勃的领导者的实用建议。

episodeTitle.en: Be fundamentally different, not incrementally better | Jag Duggal (Nubank, Facebook, Google)
episodeTitle.zh: 像杰克·杜加尔（Nubank、Facebook、谷歌）那样：从根本上与众不同，而非渐进式改进

bio.en: Jag Duggal is Chief Product Officer at Nubank, the massively under-the-radar Brazilian fintech with a fanatical user base that is larger than Coinbase, Robinhood, Affirm, SoFi, and Lemonade combined; before Nubank he led product at Facebook, Google, and Quantcast.
bio.zh: Jag Duggal 是 Nubank 的首席产品官；Nubank 是一家极度低调却庞大的巴西金融科技公司，拥有狂热的用户群，规模超过 Coinbase、Robinhood、Affirm、SoFi 和 Lemonade 之和；加入 Nubank 前，他曾在 Facebook、Google 和 Quantcast 领导产品。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jag Duggal is chief product officer at Nubank, a decacorn neobank founded in Brazil. It’s valued at over $30 billion, is bigger than Coinbase, Robinhood, Affirm, and SoFi combined, has 100 million customers (more than Bank of America!) while only operating in three countries in Latin America, and 80% to 90% of its growth comes through word of mouth. Prior to Nubank, Jag was a director of product management at Facebook, a senior vice president at Quantcast, and a product leader at Google. In our conversation, we discuss: • How Nubank builds a fanatical user base
guestBioOfficial.zh: 杰克·杜加尔是Nubank的首席产品官，Nubank是一家成立于巴西的独角兽新银行。其估值超过300亿美元，规模超过Coinbase、Robinhood、Affirm和SoFi的总和，仅在拉丁美洲三个国家开展业务，80%至90%的增长来自口碑。在加入Nubank之前，杰克曾担任Facebook的产品管理总监、Quantcast的高级副总裁，以及谷歌的产品负责人。在我们的对话中，我们将探讨：• Nubank如何建立狂热的用户基础

summary.en: Jag explains how Nubank wins not by being incrementally better but fundamentally different, earning fanatical love (80–90% of growth is word of mouth) and only scaling a product line once its Sean Ellis score crosses a compelling threshold. He discusses how to develop a clear strategy (channeling Kevin Systrom's 'at least we are clear'), category design, and disciplined product-line expansion into lending, investing, insurance, and small business. The conversation is a masterclass in building products people love and in the future of FinTech out of Latin America.
summary.zh: Jag 解释了 Nubank 何以胜出：不是“好一点”，而是“根本不同”，从而赢得狂热的喜爱（80%–90% 的增长来自口碑），并且只有当某个产品线的 Sean Ellis 分数越过有说服力的门槛后才会扩张。他谈到了如何制定清晰的战略（借鉴 Kevin Systrom 的“至少我们是清晰的”）、品类设计，以及向借贷、投资、保险和小企业业务的有纪律的品类扩张。这期对话是关于“打造人们热爱的产品”以及拉美金融科技未来的公开课。

episodeTitle.en: A framework for PM skill development | Vikrama Dhiman (Gojek)
episodeTitle.zh: 产品经理技能发展框架 | 维克拉马·迪曼（Go-Jek）

bio.en: Vikrama Dhiman heads all product at Gojek - including product management, design, and research across India, Singapore, and Indonesia - and is one of Asia's best-known product leaders.
bio.zh: Vikrama Dhiman 统管 Gojek 的全部产品事务——包括产品管理、设计与研究，团队横跨印度、新加坡与印尼——也是亚洲最知名的产品领导者之一。

guestBioOfficial.en: Vikrama Dhiman heads all things product at Gojek, including product management, design, program management, and research, across Indonesia, Singapore and India. He has over 16 years of experience building internet products, consults with Fortune 500 companies, and is among the most well-known and respected product leaders in all of Asia. In our conversation, we discuss: • The most common traits among successful product managers
guestBioOfficial.zh: 维克拉马·迪曼负责Go-Jek在印度尼西亚、新加坡和印度的所有产品相关事务，包括产品管理、设计、项目管理和研究。他拥有超过16年的互联网产品开发经验，为《财富》500强公司提供咨询服务，是亚洲最知名、最受尊敬的产品领袖之一。在我们的对话中，我们讨论了：• 成功产品经理最常见的特质

summary.en: Vikrama shares a practical framework for PM skill development, how to break into product management, and the common ways PMs shoot themselves in the foot. He discusses operating across diverse Asian markets, balancing breadth and depth as a product leader, and lessons from scaling Gojek's super-app. The episode is a grounded, mentorship-style guide especially useful for product managers in fast-growing markets.
summary.zh: Vikrama 分享了一套务实的“产品经理技能发展”框架、如何进入产品管理领域，以及产品经理常犯的自我挫败式错误。他讨论了横跨多元亚洲市场的运营、作为产品领导者如何平衡广度与深度，以及规模化 Gojek 超级应用中的经验。本期是一份扎根的、导师风格的指南，对快速增长市场中的产品经理尤其有用。

episodeTitle.en: Business strategy with Hamilton Helmer (author of 7 Powers)
episodeTitle.zh: 与汉密尔顿·赫尔默（《7种战略力量》作者）的商业战略对话

bio.en: Hamilton Helmer is a strategy legend and the author of 7 Powers, the widely praised framework for identifying and building sustainable competitive advantage ('moats'), credited by leaders like Peter Thiel and Reed Hastings for helping them build durable companies.
bio.zh: Hamilton Helmer 是战略领域的传奇人物，也是《七种力量》（7 Powers）的作者；这本书提出了识别与构建可持续竞争优势（“护城河”）的广为推崇的框架，被 Peter Thiel、Reed Hastings 等领导者誉为帮助他们打造持久公司的关键。

guestBioOfficial.en: Hamilton Helmer is one of the world’s leading experts on business strategy and the author of the seminal book 7 Powers: The Foundations of Business Strategy, which provides a comprehensive framework for understanding what it really takes to achieve and sustain a competitive advantage. With more than three decades of experience in the strategic consulting industry, Hamilton has advised over 200 companies—from burgeoning startups to Fortune 100 giants—on how to identify, build, and leverage their unique strategic powers. In our conversation, we discuss: • Potential sources of power that startups should develop from an early stage
guestBioOfficial.zh: 汉密尔顿·赫尔默是全球顶尖的商业战略专家，也是开创性著作《7种战略力量：商业战略基础》的作者。该书为理解如何真正获得并维持竞争优势提供了全面的框架。凭借在战略咨询行业超过30年的经验，汉密尔顿曾为200多家公司提供咨询服务——从初创企业到《财富》100强巨头——帮助他们识别、构建并利用独特的战略力量。在我们的对话中，我们讨论了：• 初创企业应从早期阶段就开发的潜在力量来源

summary.en: Hamilton explains that real 'power' requires both a benefit and a barrier—speed or a great team alone is a treadmill, not a moat—and walks through how startups can begin developing sources of power early. He covers which powers companies mistakenly think they have, how power relates to strategy and moats, and what individual PMs (not just leaders) can do with these insights. The conversation also explores how AI is reshaping both market entry and the classic sources of power, plus a preview of his next book.
summary.zh: Hamilton 解释说，真正的“力量”需要同时具备收益与壁垒——光有速度或优秀团队只是 treadmill（跑步机），而非护城河，并讲解了初创公司如何尽早开始培育力量来源。他谈到了公司常误以为自己拥有、实则没有的力量，力量如何与战略和护城河关联，以及普通 PM（不只是领导者）能如何利用这些洞见。对话还探讨了 AI 如何重塑市场进入方式与经典力量来源，并预告了他的下一本书。

episodeTitle.en: This will make you a better decision maker | Annie Duke (Thinking In Bets, former pro poker player)
episodeTitle.zh: 这将让你成为更优秀的决策者 | 安妮·杜克（《在博彩中思考》前职业扑克玩家）

bio.en: Annie Duke is the author of the bestsellers Thinking in Bets and Quit: The Power of Knowing When to Walk Away, a former professional poker player who won over $4 million, and a special partner at First Round Capital.
bio.zh: Annie Duke 是畅销书《赌注思维》（Thinking in Bets）和《退出：懂得何时放手的力量》（Quit）的作者，曾经的职业扑克玩家（赢得超 400 万美元），也是 First Round Capital 的特别合伙人。

guestBioOfficial.en: Annie Duke is a former professional poker player, a decision-making expert, and a special partner at First Round Capital. She is the author of Thinking in Bets (a national bestseller) and Quit: The Power of Knowing When to Walk Away and the co-founder of the Alliance for Decision Education, a nonprofit whose mission is to improve lives by empowering students through decision skills education. In our conversation, we cover: • What Annie learned from the late Daniel Kahneman
guestBioOfficial.zh: 安妮·杜克曾是职业扑克玩家、决策专家，也是First Round Capital的特别合伙人。她是《在博彩中思考》（全国畅销书）和《退出：知难而退的智慧》的作者，同时也是非营利组织“决策教育联盟”的联合创始人，该组织致力于通过决策技能教育提升人们的生活质量。在我们的对谈中，我们探讨了：• 安妮从已故的丹尼尔·卡尼曼那里学到了什么

summary.en: Annie explains the importance of making intuition explicit so you can discover when it's wrong, and reframes meetings around discovery, discussion, and decision rather than just talking. She introduces pre-mortems paired with kill criteria and argues there is no such thing as a long feedback loop if you identify correlated signals. The conversation draws on lessons from her friend Daniel Kahneman about improving decision quality in companies.
summary.zh: Annie 解释了把直觉“显性化”的重要性，这样你才能发现它何时出错，并把会议重新定义为发现、讨论和决策，而非只是空谈。她介绍了配合“终止标准”的事前复盘（pre-mortem），并认为只要你找到相关信号，就不存在“长反馈循环”。对话借用了她已故好友、心理学家 Daniel Kahneman 的洞见，探讨如何提升企业的决策质量。

episodeTitle.en: Twitter’s ex-Head of Product on Elon, consumer products, culture, more | Kayvon Beykpour
episodeTitle.zh: 推特前产品主管谈埃隆、消费产品、文化等 | 凯文·贝克波尔

bio.en: Kayvon Beykpour is a product leader best known for transforming Twitter's product culture from stagnant to ship-driven, and was previously the founder of Periscope.
bio.zh: 凯冯·贝伊科佩（Kayvon Beykpour）是一位产品负责人，以将 Twitter 的产品文化从停滞不前转变为高频发布而闻名，他此前是 Periscope 的创始人。

guestBioOfficial.en: Kayvon Beykpour was the longest-serving head of product at Twitter and was GM of Twitter’s consumer division until the platform was acquired by Elon Musk. He originally joined Twitter in 2015 through the acquisition of his company, Periscope, the largest live video streaming platform at the time. Periscope pioneered technology that inspired Instagram Live, TikTok Live, Facebook Live, and other social networks’ expansion into video streaming. In our conversation, we discuss: • The story of being let go from Twitter after Elon’s acquisition
guestBioOfficial.zh: 凯文·贝克波尔是推特任职时间最长的产品主管，在推特被埃隆·马斯克收购前一直担任消费者部门总经理。他最初于2015年通过收购当时最大的实时视频流媒体平台Periscope加入推特。Periscope开创的技术启发了Instagram Live、TikTok Live、Facebook Live等社交网络在视频流媒体领域的扩展。在我们的对话中，我们讨论了：•被推特解雇后的经历

summary.en: Kayvon describes how he turned Twitter's product team from a stagnant organization into one that shipped constantly by attacking "sacred cows." He shares stories of launching Spaces, Fleets, Twitter Blue, and more, and reflects on his early work with Elon Musk. The episode is a playbook for injecting ambition and momentum into a stuck product culture.
summary.zh: 凯冯讲述了他如何通过攻击"不可动摇的圣牛"，把 Twitter 的产品团队从停滞的组织变成持续发布的团队。他分享了推出 Spaces、Fleets、Twitter Blue 等产品的故事，并回顾了早期与埃隆·马斯克共事的经历。本期是关于如何给陷入停滞的产品文化注入野心与动能的实战手册。

episodeTitle.en: How to build deeper, more robust relationships | Carole Robin (Stanford professor, “Touchy Feely”)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何建立更深厚、更稳固的关系 | 卡罗尔·罗宾（斯坦福大学教授，“触觉感知”）

bio.en: Carole Robin taught the legendary “Touchy Feely” (Interpersonal Dynamics) course at Stanford's Graduate School of Business for over 20 years and wrote Connect, distilling those lessons for leaders.
bio.zh: Carole Robin 在斯坦福商学院讲授传奇的“Touchy Feely”（人际动力学）课程逾 20 年，并著有《Connect》一书，将那些洞见提炼给领导者。

guestBioOfficial.en: Carole Robin spent over 20 years teaching the Stanford Graduate School of Business course Interpersonal Dynamics, affectionately known as “Touchy Feely.” After leaving Stanford, she founded a nonprofit called Leaders in Tech, which applies the Touchy Feely principles to help Silicon Valley executives build their leadership and interpersonal skills. Carole co-authored the popular book Connect: Building Exceptional Relationships with Family, Friends, and Colleagues, which shares key insights from her decades of teaching these courses. In our conversation, we discuss: • The benefits of building robust relationships, in life and work
guestBioOfficial.zh:
卡罗尔·罗宾（Carole Robin）在斯坦福商学院任教逾20年，教授《人际交往动力学》课程，该课程被亲切地称为"感性管理"。离开斯坦福后，她创立了非营利组织"科技领袖"（Leaders in Tech），致力于运用"感性管理"理念，助力硅谷高管提升领导力与人际交往能力。卡罗尔与人合著了畅销书《连接：与家人、朋友和同事建立卓越关系》，从数十年教学经验中提炼出关键洞见。在本次对谈中，我们将探讨：  
• 构建稳固人际关系的益处——无论是在生活还是职场中

summary.en: Carole shares how to give feedback well—staying with “what/when/where/how” questions and avoiding “why,” and recognizing that anger is a secondary emotion hiding fear or hurt. She introduces the “three realities” concept and why separating behavior from identity (“good inside”) transforms relationships and teams. The conversation is a warm, practical guide to building stronger connections and becoming a more effective leader.
summary.zh: Carole 分享了如何好好给予反馈——用“什么/何时/何地/如何”的问题、避开“为什么”，并认识到愤怒是掩盖恐惧或受伤的次级情绪。她提出“三种现实”概念，以及将行为与身份分离（“内在是好的”）如何改变人际关系与团队。对话是建立更强联结、成为更有效领导者的温暖实用指南。

episodeTitle.en: Vision, conviction, and hype: How to build 0 to 1 inside a company | Mihika Kapoor (Product, Figma)
episodeTitle.zh: 《愿景、信念与炒作：如何在公司内部从0到1打造创新》 | 米希卡·卡普尔（Mihika Kapoor，Figma产品经理）

bio.en: Mihika Kapoor is a product manager at Figma renowned for creating a compelling vision and getting teams to see it, and a repeated "best PM" cited by peers.
bio.zh: 米希卡·卡普尔（Mihika Kapoor）是 Figma 的产品经理，以"能创造令人信服的愿景、并让团队看见它"而闻名，被同行多次评为"最佳 PM"。

guestBioOfficial.en: Mihika Kapoor is a design-engineer-PM hybrid at Figma, where she was an early PM on FigJam and is now spearheading development on a new product at the company that’s coming out this June. She’s known as the go-to person at Figma for leading new 0-to-1 products, and, as you’ll hear in our conversation, beloved by everyone she works with. Her background includes founding Design Nation, a national nonprofit focused on democratizing design education for undergraduates; spearheading product launches at Meta; and community building within the NYC AI startup scene. In our conversation, we discuss: • How to effectively take ideas from 0 to 1 at larger companies
guestBioOfficial.zh: 米希卡·卡普尔（Mihika Kapoor）是Figma公司的设计工程师兼产品经理三位一体人才。她曾是FigJam产品的早期产品经理，如今正牵头开发公司将于今年6月推出的新产品。在Figma内部，她被视为引领新产品从0到1开发的核心人物，正如你将在我们的对谈中听到的，她深受同事们的喜爱。她的职业经历包括创立全国性非营利组织"设计国度"（Design Nation），致力于为大学生普及设计教育；在Meta公司主导产品发布；以及参与纽约市人工智能初创企业社区建设。在对谈中，我们将探讨：• 在大型公司如何有效地将创意从0到1落地

summary.en: Mihika argues a PM's scope should be the whole world, with nothing off-limits, and that prototyping before a project is greenlit builds shared vision. She shares Figma's "Maker Week" hackathon as a way to give people space for wildly ambitious ideas. The episode is a master class in vision-setting and entrepreneurial culture.
summary.zh: 米希卡认为，PM 的视野应当是"全世界"，没有什么是禁区；在项目获批前就做设计与原型，能建立共同愿景。她分享了 Figma 的 "Maker Week" 内部黑客松，作为给员工空间去追求狂野想法的做法。本期是关于"设定愿景与创业文化"的大师课。

episodeTitle.en: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (YC)
episodeTitle.zh: 1000+ YC初创企业的经验教训：韧性、停滞不前的想法、转型等 | 达尔顿·考德威尔（YC）

bio.en: Dalton Caldwell is a managing director and group partner at Y Combinator, where he's worked with more startups than nearly anyone alive, and previously co-founded and led imeem and App.net.
bio.zh: Dalton Caldwell 是 Y Combinator 的管理董事兼集团合伙人，他合作过的初创公司数量几乎无人能及，此前曾联合创立并领导 imeem 和 App.net。

guestBioOfficial.en: Dalton Caldwell is Managing Director and Group Partner at Y Combinator. Prior to YC, he was the co-founder and CEO of imeem (acquired by MySpace in 2009) and the co-founder and CEO of App.net. During his time at YC, he’s advised more than 35 YC unicorns, including DoorDash, Amplitude, Webflow, and Retool, and has worked across 21 different YC batches. He’s also racked up more than 6,500 office hours with founders. In our conversation, we discuss: • Why founders need to adopt the mindset “Just don’t die”
guestBioOfficial.zh: 达尔顿·考德威尔（Dalton Caldwell）是Y Combinator的常务董事兼合伙人。加入YC之前，他曾担任imeem（2009年被MySpace收购）的联合创始人兼首席执行官，以及App.net的联合创始人兼首席执行官。在YC期间，他为超过35家YC独角兽公司提供咨询服务，包括DoorDash、Amplitude、Webflow和Retool，并参与了21个不同批次的YC项目。他还为创始人提供了超过6,500个办公小时的支持。在我们的对话中，我们讨论了：•为何创始人需要采取“只要不倒闭就行”的心态

summary.en: Dalton distills startup wisdom from seeing thousands of applications: sell something, make money, and above all “don't die.” He covers what to do when your startup is struggling, how to know when to pivot (a good pivot feels like going home), and why avoiding over-delegation early matters. The conversation also lists startup ideas to avoid and 20 categories of ideas he's actively looking to fund.
summary.zh: Dalton 从审阅数千份申请中提炼出创业智慧：卖东西、赚钱，最重要的是“别死”。他讲述了创业陷入困境时该做什么、何时该转型（好的转型像回家一样），以及早期为何避免过度授权。对话还列出了该避开的创业点子，以及他正积极寻找投资的 20 类点子。

episodeTitle.en: A framework for finding product-market fit | Todd Jackson (First Round Capital)
episodeTitle.zh: 《寻找产品-市场匹配的框架》 | 托德·杰克逊（First Round Capital）

bio.en: Todd Jackson is a partner at First Round Capital and a rare VC who came up as a product leader - PM of Gmail, Facebook News Feed/Photos/Groups, Twitter product director, Dropbox VP of product & design, and a founder.
bio.zh: Todd Jackson 是 First Round Capital 的合伙人，也是一位罕见的、从产品领导者成长起来的投资人——他曾任 Gmail 产品经理、Facebook 动态消息/照片/小组产品负责人、Twitter 产品总监、Dropbox 产品与设计副总裁，同时也是一位创始人。

guestBioOfficial.en: Todd Jackson is a Partner at First Round Capital. Before moving into venture capital, he played a crucial role as VP of Product and Design at Dropbox, guiding the company until its IPO in 2018. Prior to Dropbox, Todd led product management for Twitter’s Content and Discovery teams after selling his startup, Cover, to Twitter in 2014. Before Cover, Todd oversaw product development for Facebook’s Newsfeed, Photos, and Groups. He kickstarted his career at Google as an associate product manager and eventually led product for Gmail, witnessing its growth from beta to 200 million users. In our conversation, we discuss: • Why product-market fit (PMF) matters
guestBioOfficial.zh: 托德·杰克逊（Todd Jackson）是First Round Capital的合伙人。在投身风险投资之前，他曾在Dropbox担任VP of Product和Design，助力公司于2018年成功上市。在Dropbox之前，托德于2014年将自己的初创公司Cover出售给Twitter后，领导Twitter的内容与发现团队的产品管理工作。在Cover之前，托德曾负责Facebook Newsfeed、Photos和Groups的产品开发。他在谷歌的职业生涯始于助理产品经理，最终负责Gmail的产品管理，见证了该产品从测试版到2亿用户的成长历程。在我们的对话中，我们将探讨：•产品-市场匹配（PMF）为何至关重要

summary.en: Todd shares how a product leader thinks as a VC, including what he looks for in founders and teams, and how his operating background shapes his investments. He discusses lessons from building Gmail, the Facebook News Feed redesign, and Dropbox, plus why he believes more operators should move into venture. The episode is a unique blend of product craft and investing wisdom.
summary.zh: Todd 分享了一位产品领导者作为投资人是如何思考的，包括他在创始人与团队身上寻找什么，以及他的运营背景如何塑造其投资。他讨论了打造 Gmail、Facebook 动态消息改版与 Dropbox 的经验，以及为什么他认为更多运营者应当进入风投。本期是产品手艺与投资智慧的独特融合。

episodeTitle.en: Bending the universe in your favor | Claire Vo (LaunchDarkly, Color, Optimizely, ChatPRD)
episodeTitle.zh: “让宇宙为你所用” | Claire Vo（LaunchDarkly、Color、Optimizely、ChatPRD）

bio.en: Claire Vo is the host of the sister podcast How I AI, a three-time CPO, and longtime engineer and founder, sharing her journey from AI skeptic to power user of the OpenClaw agent platform.
bio.zh: Claire Vo 是姊妹播客《How I AI》的主持人、三度首席产品官、长期工程师兼创始人，她分享了自己从 AI 怀疑者到 OpenClaw 智能体平台重度用户的心路历程。

guestBioOfficial.en: Claire Vo is the chief product officer at LaunchDarkly and the founder of ChatPRD, likely the most popular PM-specific AI product out there. Before LaunchDarkly, she was a longtime chief product officer at Color and Optimizely. Claire has founded and managed two other companies, Pretty HQ and Experiment Engine, the latter of which Optimizely acquired in 2017. In our conversation, we discuss: • Knowing what you want in your career and being clear about it
guestBioOfficial.zh:
克莱尔·沃（Claire Vo）是LaunchDarkly的首席产品官，也是ChatPRD的创始人。ChatPRD可能是目前最受PM群体欢迎的AI产品。在加入LaunchDarkly之前，她曾长期担任Color和Optimizely的首席产品官。克莱尔还创立并管理过两家其他公司——Pretty HQ和Experiment Engine，后者于2017年被Optimizely收购。在我们的对话中，我们探讨了以下内容：
• 明确自己的职业发展方向

summary.en: Claire describes going from an eight-hour setup disaster (that deleted her family calendar) to running eight different personal agents that save real economic value, like “Sam” who does sales work she used to pay someone for. She argues the unlock is running multiple specialized agents and pulling the thread long enough to see where the tools are heading. The conversation is a first-hand tour of living with AI agents in daily life.
summary.zh: Claire 描述了自己从一次耗时八小时、还误删家庭日历的糟糕安装，到运行八个不同个人智能体、产生真实经济价值的历程，比如替她做销售工作的“Sam”（以前她每周付费请人做）。她认为关键在于运行多个专业化智能体，并持续拉线足够久以看见工具走向。对话是关于在日常生活中与 AI 智能体共处的一手之旅。

episodeTitle.en: Zigging vs. zagging: How HubSpot built a $30B company | Dharmesh Shah (co-founder/CTO)
episodeTitle.zh: 《曲线求生：HubSpot如何打造市值300亿美元的公司》，达米什·沙阿（Dharmesh Shah，HubSpot联合创始人兼首席技术官）

bio.en: Dharmesh Shah is the co-founder and CTO of HubSpot, the publicly traded CRM and inbound-marketing platform that grew from a scrappy SMB-focused startup into a multi-billion-dollar company serving hundreds of thousands of businesses.
bio.zh: Dharmesh Shah 是 HubSpot 的联合创始人兼 CTO。HubSpot 是一家上市的 CRM 与集客营销平台，从一家专注中小企业的草根创业公司，成长为服务数十万家企业、市值数十亿美元的公司。

guestBioOfficial.en: Dharmesh Shah is the co-founder and CTO of HubSpot (currently valued at $30 billion) and one of the most fascinating founders I’ve ever met. Dharmesh is the keeper of HubSpot’s Culture Code, built ChatSpot (an AI chatbot built on top of HubSpot CRM) and a game called WordPlay (which grew to 16 million users), and also founded and writes for OnStartups, a top-ranking startup blog and community with more than 1M members. He’s also invested in 100+ startups including OpenAI, AngelList, Coinbase, and Dropbox. In our conversation, we discuss: • The biggest lessons he has learned from building HubSpot
guestBioOfficial.zh:
达米什·沙阿是市值300亿美元的科技巨头HubSpot的联合创始人兼首席技术官，也是我见过最令人着迷的创业者之一。达米什是HubSpot文化准则的守护者，创建了ChatSpot（基于HubSpot CRM开发的人工智能聊天机器人）和名为WordPlay的游戏（用户量达1600万），还创立并为OnStartups撰稿——这是一个排名靠前的创业博客和社区，拥有超过100万名会员。他还投资了100多家初创公司，包括OpenAI、AngelList、Coinbase和Dropbox。在我们的对话中，我们将探讨：
• 他从创建HubSpot中汲取的最大教训

summary.en: Dharmesh Shah shares the contrarian, systems-minded playbook behind building HubSpot. He argues most "first principles" thinking is misused, and instead favors "high-conviction, low-consensus bets" — decisions like focusing on SMBs when everyone said it was impossible. A recurring theme is fighting complexity: he treats simplicity as something you must actively fight for, because entropy (the second law of thermodynamics) always increases in companies and code. He explains HubSpot's "flash tags" (FYI → suggestion → recommendation → plea) for calibrated communication, the "debate, decide, unite" decision model, and an Excel-style framework for evaluating ideas by potential, probability, passion, and prowess. On culture, his breakthrough insight is that "culture is a product" you build for your team and must iterate like software rather than freeze. He closes with why AI excites him more than any prior platform shift — it delivers cognition at scale and moves software from imperative to declarative interfaces.
summary.zh: Dharmesh Shah 分享了打造 HubSpot 那套反共识、系统化思维的玩法。他认为大多数"第一性原理"是被误用的，转而推崇"高信念、低共识的赌注"——比如在所有人都说不可能时，押注中小企业市场。贯穿全场的主题是"对抗复杂度"：他把"简单"当作必须主动去争取的东西，因为熵（热力学第二定律）在公司与代码里只会不断增加。他讲解了 HubSpot 用于精准沟通的"闪电标签"（FYI → 建议 → 推荐 → 恳求）、"辩论、决定、团结"的决策模型，以及用潜力、概率、热情、实力来给点子打分的 Excel 式框架。谈到文化，他最突破的洞见是"文化即产品"——你是为团队造产品，必须像软件一样迭代，而不是冻结它。最后他讲为何 AI 比以往任何平台变革都让他兴奋：它带来"规模化的认知"，把软件从命令式界面推向声明式界面。

episodeTitle.en: How to speak more confidently and persuasively | Matt Abrahams (professor, speaker, author)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何更自信、更有说服力地表达 | 马特·亚伯拉罕斯（教授、演讲家、作家）

bio.en: Matt Abrahams is a Stanford Graduate School of Business lecturer on communication and the host of the Think Fast, Talk Smart podcast, and author of a popular book on speaking confidently.
bio.zh: 马特·亚伯拉罕斯（Matt Abrahams）是斯坦福商学院的沟通课程讲师、Think Fast, Talk Smart 播客的主持人，也是一本关于自信演讲的畅销书作者。

guestBioOfficial.en: Matt Abrahams is a renowned communication expert, with decades of teaching, coaching, and consulting experience. At Stanford University, he teaches a business school class on strategic communication. Beyond academia, he’s a sought-after keynote speaker and consultant, guiding presenters from IPO road shows to prestigious platforms like TED, the World Economic Forum, and the United Nations. His acclaimed podcast, Think Fast, Talk Smart, garners millions of listeners, and his book, Think Faster, Talk Smarter, equips speakers with practical skills for impromptu success. With a previous bestseller, Speaking Up Without Freaking Out, Matt has empowered countless individuals to speak confidently and authentically. In our conversation, we discuss: • The concept of “daring to be dull”
guestBioOfficial.zh: 马特·亚伯拉罕斯是知名的沟通专家，拥有数十年的教学、指导和咨询经验。在斯坦福大学，他教授战略沟通方面的商学院课程。除学术领域外，他还是备受追捧的主题演讲者和顾问，指导过从IPO路演到TED、世界经济论坛和联合国等知名平台的演讲者。他的广受好评的播客《快速思考，明智表达》吸引了数百万听众，他的著作《更快思考，更聪明表达》为演讲者提供了即兴成功的实用技能。凭借此前畅销书《无惧发声》，马特帮助无数人自信而真实地表达。在我们的对谈中，我们将探讨：• “敢于平庸”的概念

summary.en: Matt teaches that you must "prepare to be spontaneous" through practice, just like athletes or jazz musicians. He recommends visualization to calm anxiety and striving for connection over perfection by "daring to be dull." The episode is a practical toolkit for communicating clearly and confidently in the moment.
summary.zh: 马特指出，你必须像运动员或爵士乐手那样，通过练习来"为即兴做准备"。他推荐用可视化来缓解焦虑，并通过"敢于平淡"来追求连接而非完美。本期是一套关于在当下清晰、自信沟通的实用工具箱。

episodeTitle.en: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more
episodeTitle.zh: 库纳尔·沙阿谈在印度取胜、二阶思维、创业哲学等

bio.en: Kunal Shah is the founder and CEO of CRED, the Indian fintech app for credit-card bill payments, and a widely followed thinker on why products succeed in India.
bio.zh: 库纳尔·沙阿（Kunal Shah）是 CRED 的创始人兼 CEO，CRED 是一款印度信用卡还款金融科技应用，他也是关于"产品为何能在印度成功"的广受关注的思考者。

guestBioOfficial.en: Kunal Shah is one of the most well-known and admired product leaders in India. He is the CEO and founder of CRED, an Indian-based fintech startup valued at over $6 billion. Prior to CRED, he founded three other startups, including Freecharge, which he sold for over $400 million to Snapdeal. He has also been an advisor to India’s most influential organizations. In our conversation, we discuss: • The prevalence of successful Indian immigrants in top CEO roles across the tech industry
guestBioOfficial.zh: 库纳尔·沙阿是印度最知名且备受尊敬的产品领袖之一。他是印度金融科技初创公司CRED的首席执行官兼创始人，该公司估值超过60亿美元。在创立CRED之前，他还创立了其他三家初创公司，包括以4亿多美元价格出售给Snapdeal的Freecharge。他还曾为印度最具影响力的组织担任顾问。在我们的对话中，我们探讨了：• 印度成功移民在科技行业高层CEO职位中的普遍性

summary.en: Kunal observes that many top global CEOs were India-born immigrants who faithfully scaled their founders' "dharma," or core principles. He argues Indian users relate to time and money differently - for instance, no Indian has been paid by the hour. The episode is a fascinating lens on building products for the Indian market and its distinct cultural logic.
summary.zh: 库纳尔观察到，许多全球顶级 CEO 都是印度裔移民，他们忠实地放大了创始人的"达摩"（dharma，即核心原则）。他认为印度用户对待时间与金钱的方式不同——例如，没有印度人按小时计薪。本期提供了一个迷人的视角，来看待如何为印度市场打造产品及其独特的文化逻辑。

episodeTitle.en: The ultimate guide to PR | Emilie Gerber (founder of Six Eastern)
episodeTitle.zh: 《公关终极指南》| Emilie Gerber（Six Eastern创始人）

bio.en: Emilie Gerber is the founder and CEO of Six Eastern, a PR agency that has worked with over 100 tech companies—from stealth startups to public companies—to earn press, build awareness, and sharpen their communications strategy.
bio.zh: Emilie Gerber 是 Six Eastern 的创始人兼 CEO；这是一家公关机构，已与 100 多家科技公司（从隐身期初创到上市公司）合作，帮助它们获得媒体曝光、建立认知并打磨传播策略。

guestBioOfficial.en: Emilie Gerber is the founder and CEO of Six Eastern, a top PR agency that’s worked with over 100 tech companies, from stealth startups to publicly traded companies. Before starting her own firm, she worked at Uber, where she led PR for the business development team and B2B programs. Prior to that, she worked at Box on product communications, with a focus on product launches and partnership announcements. In our conversation, we discuss: • Why, and when, getting press is worth your time
guestBioOfficial.zh: Emilie Gerber是Six Eastern的创始人兼首席执行官，这是一家顶级公关公司，曾为100多家科技公司提供服务，从隐形初创企业到上市公司。在创立自己的公司之前，她曾在Uber工作，负责业务开发团队和B2B项目的公关工作。此前，她在Box负责产品传播工作，重点关注产品发布和合作伙伴公告。在我们的对话中，我们讨论了：• 为什么以及何时值得花时间获取媒体报道

summary.en: Emilie gets concrete about how startups can actually earn press, covering which publications to target based on your market and story, how to craft and send pitches that reporters will open, and why warm introductions matter less than people think. She explains how to find a compelling nugget in your own messaging, where podcasts and newsletters can outperform traditional media, and what it realistically costs and how much lead time you need to work with a PR agency. The episode also walks through real pitch examples—both strong and weak—to show what works.
summary.zh: Emilie 非常具体地讲了一家初创公司究竟如何获得媒体关注：根据你的市场和故事该 targeting 哪些媒体、如何撰写并发送记者愿意打开的 Pitch、以及为何“熟人引荐”没有人们想象的那么重要。她解释了如何在自己的信息中提炼出有吸引力的“金点子”，播客和 Newsletter 为何可能比传统媒体更有效，以及聘请公关机构的真实成本与所需时间。节目还逐一点评了真实 Pitch 案例（有优有劣），展示什么才有效。

episodeTitle.en: The happiness and pain of product management | Noam Lovinsky (Grammarly, FB, Thumbtack, YT)
episodeTitle.zh: 产品管理的幸福与痛苦 | 诺姆·洛文斯基（Grammarly、Facebook、Thumbtack、YouTube）

bio.en: When you were at Facebook, you built what is called the New Product Experimentation team trying to create a startup within a startup.
bio.zh: 你在Facebook工作时，组建了所谓的新产品实验团队，试图在公司内部创建一家初创公司。

guestBioOfficial.en: Noam Lovinsky has had a distinguished career in product, leaving an indelible mark at Facebook, YouTube, Thumbtack, and currently as the chief product officer at Grammarly. At Facebook, Noam helped establish the New Product Experimentation team; at Thumbtack, he was chief product officer; and at YouTube, he was one of the early product leaders overseeing the consumer experience. In our conversation, we discuss: • Challenges and lessons from reviving growth at YouTube and Thumbtack
guestBioOfficial.zh: 诺姆·洛文斯基在产品领域拥有辉煌的职业生涯，曾在Facebook、YouTube、Thumbtack等公司留下深刻印记，目前担任Grammarly的首席产品官。在Facebook，诺姆帮助组建了新产品实验团队；在Thumbtack，他担任首席产品官；在YouTube，他是早期负责用户体验的产品负责人之一。在我们的对谈中，我们探讨了：• 在YouTube和Thumbtack重振增长的挑战与经验教训

summary.en: There were many times where Google leadership reconsidered the acquisition and, "Should we sell YouTube?" if you can believe it or not. I remember in a board meeting, the new model really started to show legs and one of the board members, Brian Schreier at Sequoia, said it was the prettiest smile graph that he had ever
summary.zh: 有很多时候，谷歌高层重新考虑收购事宜，甚至考虑“我们是否应该出售YouTube？”。信不信由你，我记得在一次董事会会议上，新模型开始显现成效，董事会成员Brian Schreier说，这是他见过最漂亮的曲线图。

episodeTitle.en: Product management theater | Marty Cagan (Silicon Valley Product Group)
episodeTitle.zh: 产品管理戏码 | 马蒂·卡根（硅谷产品集团）

bio.en: Marty Cagan is the author of Inspired and Empowered and a partner at SVPG, who has coached more product teams and PMs than almost anyone, and recently released a new book on modern product practice.
bio.zh: 马蒂·卡根（Marty Cagan）是《Inspired》与《Empowered》的作者、SVPG 的合伙人，他辅导过的产品团队与 PM 几乎无人能及，近期又推出了一本关于现代产品实践的新书。

guestBioOfficial.en: Marty Cagan is a luminary in the world of product. He’s the author of two of the most foundational books for product teams and product leaders (Inspired and Empowered), he’s the founder of Silicon Valley Product Group (one of the longest-running product advisory groups), and he’s almost certainly worked with more product leaders and teams than any human alive. Now he’s releasing his newest book, Transformed, which is sure to become a staple of tech-powered companies worldwide. Marty’s previous appearance on our show remains one of the most popular episodes to date. In this conversation, we discuss: • The rise of “product management theater”
guestBioOfficial.zh: 马蒂·卡根是产品界的泰斗人物。他著有两本面向产品团队和产品负责人的基础读物（《启发》和《赋能》），创立了运营时间最长的产品顾问团体之一——硅谷产品集团，并且与全球众多产品负责人及团队合作的次数比其他任何人都多。如今，他即将推出新作《蜕变》，必将成为全球科技型企业的必备读物。马蒂此前在我们节目中的亮相仍是迄今最受欢迎的剧集之一。在本次对谈中，我们将探讨：• “产品管理戏码”的兴起

summary.en: Marty argues many companies overhired during the pandemic, creating fake product roles like agile coaches and product owners that deliver output, not outcomes. He pushes back on the "victim" mindset, insisting individual contributors can drive real change from within. The episode is a bracing call to rediscover what true product management looks like.
summary.zh: 马蒂认为，许多公司在疫情期间过度招聘，制造出敏捷教练、产品负责人等"假产品角色"，它们只交付产出而非成果。他反对"受害者"心态，坚持一线产品人也能从内部推动真正的改变。本期是一次令人警醒的呼吁：重新发现真正产品管理的模样。

episodeTitle.en: Inside TikTok: Culture, strategy, monetization, and more | Ray Cao
episodeTitle.zh: TikTok内幕：文化、战略、变现等 | 曹睿（Ray Cao）

bio.en: Ray Cao is the global Head of Monetization Product Strategy & Operations at TikTok, where he has been for over four years, after spending six years at Google helping scale Google Shopping globally.
bio.zh: Ray Cao 是 TikTok 全球变现产品战略与运营负责人，已在公司四年有余，此前曾在 Google 工作六年，帮助 Google Shopping 在全球范围规模化。

guestBioOfficial.en: Ray (Jiayi) Cao is the global head of product strategy and operations for monetization product at TikTok. Prior to TikTok, Ray spent six years at Google helping scale Google Shopping globally. In our conversation, we discuss: • TikTok’s internal culture and core values
guestBioOfficial.zh: 曹睿（曹佳仪）是TikTok变现产品全球产品战略与运营负责人。加入TikTok之前，曹睿曾在谷歌工作六年，助力Google Shopping在全球范围内扩展规模。在我们的对话中，我们探讨了：• TikTok的内部文化和核心价值观

summary.en: Ray pulls back the curtain on how TikTok operates, explaining its 'context, no control' culture that gives people full information and autonomy while expecting ownership. He discusses how TikTok fine-tunes its algorithm and product for different cultures, why it maintains a 'always day one' startup hunger, and what it takes to succeed as a creator or advertiser on the platform. The episode is a rare inside look at one of the most successful businesses in history.
summary.zh: Ray 揭开了 TikTok 的运作内幕，阐释了其“给背景、不给控制（context, no control）”的文化：在授予充分信息与自主权的同时，要求员工具备主人翁意识。他探讨了 TikTok 如何针对不同文化微调算法与产品、为何保持“永远第一天”的创业饥渴，以及作为创作者或广告主在该平台取得成功的关键。本期是对史上最成功企业之一难得的内部透视。

episodeTitle.en: Making Meta | Andrew ‘Boz’ Bosworth (CTO)
episodeTitle.zh: 打造元宇宙 | Andrew ‘Boz’ Bosworth（首席技术官）

bio.en: Andrew “Boz” Bosworth is CTO of Meta, one of its first engineers (2006), and creator of landmark products including the Facebook News Feed, mobile ads platform, and Messenger.
bio.zh: Andrew “Boz” Bosworth 是 Meta 首席技术官，公司最早的工程师之一（2006 年加入），并打造了 Facebook 动态消息、移动广告平台和 Messenger 等标志性产品。
