guestBioOfficial.en: Andrew Bosworth—or Boz, as most people know him—is the chief technology officer at Meta and head of Reality Labs, the company’s augmented reality/virtual reality (AR/VR) organization, which he created in 2017. Boz joined Facebook in 2006 as their approximately 10th engineer, and in his 18-year tenure he built the original News Feed, Messenger, and Groups, as well as many early anti-abuse and infrastructure systems. At various times he has been the engineering director overseeing Events, Places, Photos, Videos, Timeline, Privacy, and more. Before Reality Labs, he ran the Ads and Business Platform product group, where he led engineering, product, research, analytics, and design, taking annual revenue from $4 billion to $40 billion in five years. Andrew currently leads Meta’s efforts in AR, VR, AI, and consumer hardware across Quest, Ray-Ban Meta glasses, and more. In our conversation, we discuss: • Stories from the early days of Facebook
guestBioOfficial.zh: Andrew Bosworth——大多数人熟知的Boz——是Meta的首席技术官，也是Reality Labs（该公司的增强现实/虚拟现实（AR/VR）组织）的负责人，该组织由他于2017年创立。Boz于2006年加入Facebook，担任约第10位工程师。在18年的任期内，他开发了原始的新闻推送、Messenger和群组功能，以及许多早期反滥用和基础设施系统。他曾担任工程总监，负责活动、地点、照片、视频、时间线、隐私等多个部门。在Reality Labs之前，他负责广告和商业平台产品组，领导工程、产品、研究、分析和设计团队，在五年内将年收入从40亿美元提升至400亿美元。Andrew目前负责Meta在Quest、Ray-Ban Meta眼镜等产品上的AR、VR、AI和消费硬件业务。在对话中，我们探讨了：• Facebook早期阶段的故事

summary.en: Boz reflects on the brutal early days of Facebook—120-hour weeks, no hobbies—and why the romantic founder story hides the grind. He shares lessons on asking your manager for help, why communication is the job, and stories from building the very first News Feed (which users hated yet immediately doubled usage). The conversation also covers Meta's recent turnaround, his thoughts on Apple Vision Pro, and broad leadership and career advice.
summary.zh: Boz 回顾了 Facebook 早期残酷的日子——每周 120 小时、没有爱好——以及为何浪漫的创始人故事掩盖了其中的煎熬。他分享了向经理求助、为何“沟通就是工作”的经验，以及打造第一个动态消息（用户讨厌却立即令使用量翻倍）的故事。对话还涵盖 Meta 近期的扭亏为盈、对 Apple Vision Pro 的看法，以及广泛的领导与职业建议。

episodeTitle.en: How to discover your superpowers, own your story, and unlock personal growth | Donna Lichaw
episodeTitle.zh: 如何发现你的超能力、掌控自己的故事并开启个人成长之旅 | 唐娜·利查沃（Donna Lichaw）

bio.en: Donna Lichaw is an executive coach, speaker, and bestselling author of The Leader's Journey, helping founders, CEOs, and executives scale their impact while staying true to themselves.
bio.zh: Donna Lichaw 是一位高管教练、演讲者和畅销书《领导者的旅程》（The Leader's Journey）作者，帮助创始人、CEO 和高管在忠于自我的同时放大影响力。

guestBioOfficial.en: Donna Lichaw is an internationally sought-after executive coach, keynote speaker, and best-selling author. She helps visionary founders, CEOs, and executive teams level up their leadership and scale their impact while staying true to their mission, purpose, and themselves. Donna works with leaders at companies like Google, Disney, Twitter, Microsoft, Mailchimp, and Adobe, as well as a plethora of mission-driven startups and nonprofits. In our conversation, we discuss: • How our personal narratives influence our success and failure
guestBioOfficial.zh: 唐娜·利查沃是备受国际追捧的高管教练、主题演讲者和畅销书作家。她帮助有远见的创始人、CEO和高管团队提升领导力并扩大影响力，同时忠实于他们的使命、愿景和自我。在对话中，我们将讨论：• 个人叙事如何影响我们的成功与失败

summary.en: Donna explains how the stories we tell ourselves shape our success or failure, and how identifying your superpowers and your “kryptonite” is essential to career growth. She offers ways to reframe imposter syndrome as an advantage and to surface life goals even when you have no idea what they are. The conversation is full of frameworks and coaching examples for unlocking your leadership through self-narrative.
summary.zh: Donna 解释了“我们对自己讲的故事”如何塑造成败，以及识别自己的超能力与被“氪石”弱点对职业成长的关键作用。她提供了把冒名顶替综合征重新框定为优势、以及在毫无头绪时找到人生目标的方法。对话充满了通过自我叙事释放领导力的框架与教练案例。

episodeTitle.en: How Netflix builds a culture of excellence | Elizabeth Stone (CTO)
episodeTitle.zh: Netflix如何构建卓越文化 | 伊丽莎白·斯通（CTO）

bio.en: Elizabeth Stone is the chief technology officer at Netflix—reportedly the first economist ever named CTO of a Fortune 500 company—and previously held leadership roles in data and science at Netflix, Lyft, and Nuna.
bio.zh: Elizabeth Stone 是 Netflix 的首席技术官——据称是有史以来第一位出任财富 500 强公司 CTO 的经济学家，此前曾在 Netflix、Lyft 和 Nuna 担任数据与研究领域的领导职务。

guestBioOfficial.en: Elizabeth Stone is the chief technology officer of Netflix. She previously served as vice president of product data science and engineering, and as vice president of data and insights, at Netflix. Before Netflix, Elizabeth was vice president of science at Lyft, chief operating officer at Nuna, a trader at Merrill Lynch, and an economist at Analysis Group. In our conversation, we discuss: • Elizabeth’s advice for career advancement
guestBioOfficial.zh: 伊丽莎白·斯通（Elizabeth Stone）是Netflix的首席技术官。她此前曾在Netflix担任产品数据科学与工程副总裁，以及数据与洞察副总裁。在加入Netflix之前，伊丽莎白曾担任Lyft的科学副总裁、Nuna的首席运营官，以及美林证券的交易员和Analysis Group的经济学家。在我们的对话中，我们讨论了：• 伊丽莎白对职业发展的建议

summary.en: Elizabeth explains how her economics background shaped her career and why she expects more economists to rise in tech leadership, and shares her 'secret sauce' for consistently climbing quickly across companies. She walks through Netflix's distinctive culture of high talent density, radical candor, and freedom and responsibility, and how that culture is the foundation everything else rests on. The conversation also covers how Netflix structures its data and user-research teams, and what endurance sports like triathlons have taught her about work and life.
summary.zh: Elizabeth 解释了经济学背景如何塑造了她的职业生涯，以及为何她预计会有更多经济学家进入科技公司的领导层，并分享了她能在多家公司快速晋升的“秘诀”。她梳理了 Netflix 以高人才密度、极致坦诚、自由与责任为核心的特殊文化，以及为何这种文化是其他一切的根基。对话还涵盖了 Netflix 如何组织其数据与用户研究团队，以及铁人三项等耐力运动教会她的关于工作与人生的道理。

episodeTitle.en: Building a world-class sales org | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)
episodeTitle.zh: 《打造世界级销售团队》 | 杰森·莱姆金（Jason Lemkin，SaaStr）

bio.en: Jason M. Lemkin is the founder of EchoSign (grown past $100M ARR and sold to Adobe) and the creator of SaaStr, the largest community for SaaS founders and executives; he is one of the most quoted voices on building and scaling SaaS go-to-market.
bio.zh: Jason M. Lemkin 是 EchoSign 的创始人（ARR 做到超 1 亿美元后出售给 Adobe），也是 SaaStr（最大的 SaaS 创始人与高管社区）的创办者；他是关于打造与扩展 SaaS 上市策略被引用最多的声音之一。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jason Lemkin created and runs SaaStr, the world’s largest community for B2B/SaaS founders, and is the managing director of SaaStr Fund, a $90 million venture capital firm specializing in early-stage enterprise investments. He is also the mastermind behind two major tech conferences each year—one in the Bay Area, drawing in over 15,000 people, and another in Europe, with a crowd of more than 3,000 SaaS executives, founders, and entrepreneurs. Before SaaStr, Jason wore many hats: CEO and co-founder of EchoSign (later bought by Adobe), vice president at Adobe Systems, co-founder and president of NanoGram Devices Corp., vice president of NeoPhotonics, and a senior director at BabyCenter. In our conversation, we discuss: • How far you should go without a salesperson
guestBioOfficial.zh:
杰森·莱姆金创立并运营着全球最大的B2B/SaaS创始人社区SaaStr，同时担任SaaStr Fund的董事总经理——这家规模达9000万美元的风投公司专注于早期企业投资。此外，他每年还主办两场大型科技会议：一场在湾区，吸引超过15,000人参与；另一场在欧洲，吸引了3,000多名SaaS高管、创始人和创业者。SaaStr之前，杰森曾担任过多个职位：EchoSign（后被Adobe收购）的首席执行官兼联合创始人、Adobe Systems的副总裁、NanoGram Devices Corp.的联合创始人兼总裁、NeoPhotonics的副总裁，以及BabyCenter的高级总监。在我们的对话中，我们探讨了以下内容：
• 何时应该在没有销售人员的情况下全力推进

summary.en: Jason gets extremely tactical about building a sales team—the area most product leaders lack experience in: how long to wait before hiring your first salesperson, why you should actually hire two, how to comp and interview them, and when to bring on a VP of sales. He covers how to keep reps from flaming out and burning cash, how to make the product–sales relationship healthier (with your head of product deeply involved), how long trials should be, and why to avoid annual contracts. The episode is a rich, extended masterclass drawn from Jason's hard-won SaaS experience.
summary.zh: Jason 就“组建销售团队”给出了极其具体的建议——这是大多数产品领导者最缺经验的领域：该等多久才招第一名销售、为何其实应该一次招两人、如何给他们定薪酬与面试、何时引入销售副总裁。他讲了如何避免销售员快速熄火、烧光现金，如何让产品与销售的关系更健康（让产品负责人深度参与），试用以期多长，以及为何要避免年度合同。这期节目是基于 Jason 来之不易的 SaaS 经验、内容极为丰富的长版公开课。

episodeTitle.en: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (Authors of Make Time, Character VC)
episodeTitle.zh: 为重要之事腾出时间 | 杰克·纳普和约翰·泽拉斯基（《腾出时间》作者）

bio.en: Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky are the co-creators of the Design Sprint and authors of Sprint and Make Time; they now run the venture firm Character and its Character Labs accelerator.
bio.zh: Jake Knapp 与 John Zeratsky 是“设计冲刺”（Design Sprint）的共同创造者，也是《Sprint》和《Make Time》的作者；他们如今经营着风险投资公司 Character 及其 Character Labs 加速器。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky are bestselling authors of the books Sprint and Make Time. They have helped more than 300 teams design new products and bring them to market, including those at YouTube, Gusto, One Medical Group, and Slack. Jake and JZ are co-founders of the venture capital firm Character, where they support startups with capital and sprints. Previously, they were operating partners at Google Ventures and, before that, design leaders at Google, where JZ worked on Google Ads and YouTube and Jake helped build Gmail and co-founded Google Meet. In our conversation, we discuss: • “Busy bandwagon” and “infinity pools”
guestBioOfficial.zh:
杰克·纳普（Jake Knapp）和约翰·泽拉特斯基（John Zeratsky）是《冲刺》（Sprint）和《把握时间》（Make Time）两本书的畅销作者。他们曾帮助300多个团队设计新产品并将其推向市场，其中包括YouTube、Gusto、One Medical Group和Slack等公司。杰克和约翰是风险投资公司Character的联合创始人，通过资金和冲刺计划为初创企业提供支持。此前，他们曾在Google Ventures担任运营合伙人，更早之前则在谷歌担任设计主管，约翰曾参与Google Ads和YouTube的开发，杰克则协助开发Gmail并参与创立Google Meet。在对话中，我们探讨了以下内容：
• “忙碌的从众心理”和“无边泳池”

summary.en: Jake and JZ focus on their book Make Time, arguing productivity is really about protecting one peak-attention moment a day—the 'highlight' you'd be proud to name at day's end—rather than time management. They share a ton of practical, immediately actionable tactics for product leaders and founders to spend their energy better and feel good about their days. The episode is a welcome, grounding counterpoint to hustle culture, and Lenny guarantees you'll leave with at least three things to change starting tomorrow.
summary.zh: Jake 和 JZ 聚焦他们的书《Make Time》，主张“生产力”真正关乎保护每天一段注意力巅峰的时刻——即你在一天结束时能骄傲地说出的“高光时刻”，而非时间管理。他们为产品领导者和创始人分享了大量可立刻落地、能更好分配精力并让日子过得更有成就感的实用方法。这期节目是对“拼搏文化”的一剂令人舒心的清醒剂，Lenny 保证你至少能带走三件明天就能改变的事。

episodeTitle.en: Inside OpenAI | Logan Kilpatrick (head of developer relations)
episodeTitle.zh: 《OpenAI内幕》

bio.en: Logan Kilpatrick is the Head of Developer Relations at OpenAI, supporting developers building on its APIs and ChatGPT, and previously was an ML engineer at Apple.
bio.zh: 洛根·基尔帕特里克（Logan Kilpatrick）是 OpenAI 的开发者关系负责人，支持基于其 API 与 ChatGPT 构建应用的开发者，此前是 Apple 的机器学习工程师。

guestBioOfficial.en: Logan Kilpatrick leads developer relations at OpenAI, supporting developers building with the OpenAI API and ChatGPT. He is also on the board of directors at NumFOCUS, the nonprofit organization that supports open source projects like Jupyter, Pandas, NumPy, and more. Before OpenAI, Logan was a machine-learning engineer at Apple and advised NASA on open source policy. In our conversation, we discuss: • OpenAI’s fast-paced and innovative work environment
guestBioOfficial.zh: 洛根·基尔帕特里克（Logan Kilpatrick）在OpenAI负责开发者关系工作，支持开发者使用OpenAI API和ChatGPT进行开发。他同时也是非营利组织NumFOCUS的董事会成员，该组织支持Jupyter、Pandas、NumPy等开源项目。在加入OpenAI之前，洛根曾在苹果担任机器学习工程师，并为NASA提供开源政策咨询。在我们的对谈中，我们探讨了：• OpenAI快节奏且富有创新性的工作环境

summary.en: Logan says the top traits he looks for when hiring are high agency and urgency - people who act without needing consensus. He describes being on the front lines as developers figure out how to use AI superpowers in real products. The episode offers a window into OpenAI's developer ecosystem and what makes builders effective in the AI era.
summary.zh: 洛根说，他招聘时最看重的特质是高自驱力与紧迫感——即无需达成共识就能行动的人。他描述了自己身处一线的经历：开发者们正在弄清如何把 AI 的超能力用在真实产品中。本期让我们一窥 OpenAI 的开发者生态，以及在 AI 时代什么让构建者高效。

episodeTitle.en: Lessons from Atlassian | Megan Cook (Head of Product, Jira)
episodeTitle.zh: Atlassian的经验教训 | 梅根·库克（Jira产品负责人）

bio.en: Megan Cook is Head of Product for Jira at Atlassian, used by 75% of Fortune 500 companies, and has spent nearly 11 years at the company.
bio.zh: 梅根·库克（Megan Cook）是 Atlassian 公司 Jira 的产品负责人，Jira 被 75% 的财富 500 强企业使用，她在公司近 11 年。

guestBioOfficial.en: Megan Cook is the head of product for Atlassian’s Jira software, which is used by 75% of Fortune 500 companies, has over 125,000 customers globally, over 15 different products, and is by far the most popular project management tool in the world. Megan has been at Atlassian for just under 11 years, and before this role, she was an analyst, a developer, and an Agile coach. In our conversation, we discuss: • How to get buy-in for your ideas
guestBioOfficial.zh: 梅根·库克是Atlassian Jira软件的产品负责人，该软件被75%的《财富》500强公司使用，全球拥有超过125,000名客户，涵盖15款不同产品，是目前全球最受欢迎的项目管理工具。梅根在Atlassian工作了近11年，此前曾担任分析师、开发人员和敏捷教练。在本次对话中，我们探讨了：• 如何为你的想法争取支持

summary.en: Megan describes "Fight Club," a weekly 30-minute slot where she, engineering, and design deliberately surface and resolve conflict early. She argues naming and addressing disagreement prevents it from festering into bigger problems. The episode is a practical guide to healthy conflict and alignment on large product teams.
summary.zh: 梅根描述了"搏击俱乐部"——每周 30 分钟，她与工程、设计负责人刻意把冲突摆上台面、尽早解决。她认为，正视并处理分歧，能防止其恶化成更大的问题。本期是关于大型产品团队中"健康冲突与对齐"的实用指南。

episodeTitle.en: Managing nerves, anxiety, and burnout | Jonny Miller (Nervous Systems Mastery)
episodeTitle.zh: 管理紧张、焦虑与职业倦怠 | 乔尼·米勒（Nervous Systems Mastery）

bio.en: Jonny Miller is a coach and educator who created Nervous System Mastery, a program that teaches tech professionals practical tools to build calm, resilience, and sustained high performance.
bio.zh: 乔尼·米勒（Jonny Miller）是一位教练与教育工作者，他创立了"神经系统掌控力"（Nervous System Mastery）项目，向科技从业者传授培养内心平静、提升抗压能力与持续高效状态的实用工具。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jonny Miller is the founder of ⁠Nervous System Mastery⁠, a course that has helped hundreds of founders and tech leaders cultivate calm, reduce nervousness, enhance resilience, and elevate their sense of aliveness. Having personally benefited from Jonny’s teachings, I’m especially excited to have him on the show. In this episode, we discuss: • How shifting your focus from the mind to the body can help ease nervousness
guestBioOfficial.zh: 乔尼·米勒（Jonny Miller）是Nervous System Mastery的创始人，这门课程已帮助数百位创始人和科技领袖培养冷静心态、减轻紧张情绪、增强韧性并提升生命活力感。亲身受益于乔尼的教导，我特别高兴能邀请他参与节目。在本期节目中，我们探讨了：• 将注意力从大脑转向身体如何帮助缓解紧张情绪

summary.en: Jonny shares his "feather, brick, dump truck" framework, which shows that burnout begins with subtle bodily signals that escalate into crises if ignored. He argues that learning to notice early feedback lets people course-correct long before a breakdown. The conversation offers concrete techniques for regulating the nervous system, reframing burnout prevention as a trainable, body-based skill.
summary.zh: 乔尼提出了"羽毛、砖头、自卸卡车"框架，说明职业倦怠往往从细微的身体信号开始，若被忽视便会升级为危机。他认为，学会捕捉早期的反馈，能让人在彻底崩溃前及时调整方向。本期还分享了许多调节神经系统的具体方法，把预防倦怠重新定义为一种可以通过训练获得的、基于身体的能力。

episodeTitle.en: Geoffrey Moore on finding your beachhead, crossing the chasm, and dominating a market
episodeTitle.zh: 杰夫瑞·摩尔谈如何找到突破口、跨越鸿沟、主导市场

bio.en: Geoffrey Moore is the author of Crossing the Chasm, perhaps the most influential book ever written on technology go-to-market strategy, and a longtime advisor to B2B and tech companies on scaling through the adoption lifecycle.
bio.zh: Geoffrey Moore 是《跨越鸿沟》（Crossing the Chasm）的作者，这本书堪称史上最具影响力的技术产品上市策略著作，他长期为 B2B 与科技公司提供跨越采用生命周期、实现规模化的咨询。

guestBioOfficial.en: Geoffrey Moore is an author, speaker, and advisor, widely known for his seminal book Crossing the Chasm: Marketing and Selling Disruptive Products to Mainstream Customers, which many consider the most important book ever written on go-to-market strategy. Moore’s work is focused on the market dynamics surrounding disruptive innovations, and how one overcomes the challenge of transitioning from serving early adopters to the mainstream. In this episode, we discuss: • What “crossing the chasm” means
guestBioOfficial.zh: 杰夫瑞·摩尔是一位作家、演讲家和顾问，因其开创性的著作《跨越鸿沟：向主流客户销售颠覆性产品》而闻名，该书被许多人视为有史以来关于市场进入策略最重要的著作。摩尔的研究聚焦于围绕颠覆性创新的市场动态，以及如何克服从服务早期采用者到主流市场的挑战。在本期节目中，我们将探讨：• “跨越鸿沟”意味着什么

summary.en: Geoffrey uses the 'kindling vs. log' metaphor to explain why, when stuck in the chasm, taking any customer you can find is a mistake—you need to light a fire in one narrow place first. He lays out the bowling-pin strategy for getting past early adopters, the specific go-to-market playbook for each stage of the adoption lifecycle, and the seven deadly sins of crossing the chasm incorrectly. The conversation also covers how to sell to different personas (and why early adopters don't need you to focus on problem and pain) plus some unexpected life advice.
summary.zh: Geoffrey 用“引火物 vs. 原木”的比喻说明：当卡在鸿沟（chasm）中时，来者不拒地抓客户是错的——你需要先在一个狭窄的点上把火点着。他讲解了用“保龄球瓶”策略越过早期采用者、针对不同采用生命周期阶段的特定上市打法，以及跨越鸿沟时最常见的七宗罪。对话还涵盖了如何向不同人物角色销售（以及为何对早期采用者无需执着于“问题”和“痛点”），并附带一些出乎意料的人生建议。

episodeTitle.en: Good Strategy, Bad Strategy | Richard Rumelt
episodeTitle.zh: 《优秀战略与糟糕战略》|理查德·鲁梅尔特

bio.en: Richard Rumelt is a legend in the field of strategy and the author of Good Strategy/Bad Strategy and The Crux, and was a longtime professor at UCLA Anderson and on the faculty of Harvard Business School.
bio.zh: Richard Rumelt 是战略领域的传奇人物，著有《好战略，坏战略》（Good Strategy/Bad Strategy）与《关键难题》（The Crux），曾任 UCLA 安德森管理学院长期教授，亦曾执教于哈佛商学院。

guestBioOfficial.en: Richard Rumelt is a legend in the world of strategy. He’s the author of Good Strategy/Bad Strategy and The Crux: How Leaders Become Strategists, both of which are often recommended by guests on this podcast. From his early days teaching in Iran at a Harvard-sponsored business school to teaching at Harvard Business School itself to over four decades teaching at UCLA’s Anderson School of Management, Richard’s impact resonates globally. His strategic insights are sought after by major corporations including Microsoft, Shell, Apple, AT&T, Intel, and Commonwealth Bank and by governmental organizations such as the U.S. Army Special Operations Command. In this episode, we discuss: • The essential components of a good strategy
guestBioOfficial.zh: 理查德·鲁梅尔特是战略领域的传奇人物。他著有《优秀战略/糟糕战略》和《关键所在：领导者如何成为战略家》两本著作，这两本书常被本播客的嘉宾推荐。从他早年在伊朗哈佛商学院赞助的商学院任教，到哈佛商学院任教，再到加州大学洛杉矶分校安德森管理学院任教四十余年，理查德的影响力享誉全球。他的战略见解深受微软、壳牌、苹果、AT&T、英特尔、联邦银行等大公司以及美国陆军特种作战司令部等政府机构的追捧。在本期节目中，我们将探讨：• 优秀战略的核心要素

summary.en: Rumelt defines strategy as a coherent design for overcoming a high-stakes challenge, built from a diagnosis, a guiding policy, and focused actions. He explains why bad strategy is so common - fluffy goals without diagnosis or action - and how power (asymmetry and advantage) is the hidden engine of real strategy. The conversation is a clear, story-driven tour of what separates great strategy from noise.
summary.zh: Rumelt 将战略定义为“克服高难度挑战的一贯设计”，由诊断、指导方针与聚焦的行动三部分构成。他解释了糟糕战略为何如此普遍——只有模糊目标而缺诊断与行动——以及“权力（power）”（不对称与优势）为何是真正战略的隐藏引擎。本期以清晰、富含故事的方式，剖析了卓越战略与空洞噪声之间的区别。

episodeTitle.en: The art and wisdom of changing teams | Heidi Helfand (Author of Dynamic Reteaming)
episodeTitle.zh: 团队变动的艺术与智慧 | 海蒂·赫尔方德（《动态团队重组》作者）

bio.en: Heidi Helfand is an organizational-design consultant, workshop leader, and author of Dynamic Reteaming, who after two decades in tech became an expert on how to reorganize teams effectively and why change is good for them.
bio.zh: Heidi Helfand 是一位组织设计顾问、工作坊引导者，也是《Dynamic Reteaming》的作者；在科技行业深耕二十年后，她成为“如何有效重组团队”以及“为何变化对团队有益”的专家。

guestBioOfficial.en: Heidi Helfand is the author of Dynamic Reteaming, which outlines practical strategies for orchestrating successful team and company org changes. Her work is informed by more than 20 years in the tech industry at notable companies like AppFolio, Procore, and Expertcity/GoToMeeting. Today, she dedicates her efforts to sharing her knowledge through workshops, comprehensive courses, and consultative services, helping organizations navigate and optimize their team structures. In this episode, we discuss: • The importance of reteaming and reorging
guestBioOfficial.zh: 海蒂·赫尔方德是《动态团队重组》一书的作者，该书概述了成功进行团队和公司组织变革的实用策略。她在科技行业拥有超过20年的经验，曾就职于AppFolio、Procore和Expertcity/GoToMeeting等知名公司。如今，她致力于通过工作坊、综合课程和咨询服务分享知识，帮助组织优化团队结构。在本期节目中，我们讨论了：• 团队和组织变动的重要性

summary.en: Heidi argues that constantly stable teams aren't actually best—dynamic reteaming reduces attrition, stagnation, and knowledge silos—and lays out the five types of reteaming plus the anti-patterns to avoid when reorganizing. She covers what team structure is most conducive to creating brand-new products, why being transparent about reorg plans is worth it, and how she herself became such a remarkably good listener. It's a practical guide to the 'people layer' of building software that most leaders neglect.
summary.zh: Heidi 主张“永远稳定的团队”并非最好——动态重组（dynamic reteaming）能降低流失、停滞与知识孤岛，并梳理了五种重组类型，以及在重组时应避免的反模式。她谈到了哪种团队结构最有利于从零打造新产品、为何把重组计划透明化是值得的，以及她自己是如何成为如此出色的倾听者的。这期节目是关于“做软件时的人”这一被多数领导者忽视的层面的实用指南。

episodeTitle.en: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)
episodeTitle.zh: 掌控你的职业生涯 | 伊桑·埃文斯（亚马逊）

bio.en: Ethan Evans is a former Amazon vice president and executive coach who spent 15 years at Amazon helping build Prime Video, the Amazon Appstore, Prime Gaming, and Twitch Commerce (a billion-dollar business), co-drafted one of Amazon's 14 leadership principles, and holds over 70 patents.
bio.zh: Ethan Evans 是前亚马逊副总裁、高管教练，在亚马逊任职 15 年，参与打造 Prime Video、Amazon Appstore、Prime Gaming 和 Twitch Commerce（价值十亿美元的业务），参与起草亚马逊 14 条领导力原则之一，并拥有 70 多项专利。

guestBioOfficial.en: Ethan Evans is a writer, career coach, course instructor, and retired VP at Amazon. During his 15 years at Amazon, he helped invent Prime Video, Amazon Video, the Amazon Appstore, Prime Gaming (formerly Twitch Prime), and Twitch Commerce. Prior to Amazon, Ethan spent 12 years in technical leadership roles at several East Coast startups. He writes a newsletter, Level Up, which publishes candid career advice and has a growing community of ambitious professionals to connect with. Ethan also offers a range of Leadership Development Courses via live online classes and on-demand courses. In this episode, we discuss: • The Magic Loop framework: a five-step process to grow your career
guestBioOfficial.zh:
伊桑·埃文斯是一位作家、职业教练、课程讲师，也是亚马逊的退休副总裁。在亚马逊的15年间，他参与开发了Prime Video、亚马逊视频、亚马逊应用商店、Prime Gaming（前身为Twitch Prime）和Twitch Commerce等产品。在加入亚马逊之前，伊桑曾在东海岸多家初创公司担任技术领导职位12年。他撰写的时事通讯《Level Up》为有抱负的专业人士提供真诚的职业建议，并拥有不断壮大的社群。伊桑还通过在线直播课程和按需课程提供一系列领导力发展课程。在本期节目中，我们将探讨：
• 魔术循环框架：一个助力职业发展的五步流程

summary.en: Ethan shares a simple but powerful reframe: you don't need many ideas to be seen as inventive—just one good idea every month or two, even if expressing it takes years (what he calls the long arc of Prime and Kindle). He tells a candid story of failing on a major project for Jeff Bezos and what it taught him, and walks through 'The Magic Loop,' a deceptively simple practice he guarantees will help you get promoted. The episode is full of concrete career advice for senior individual contributors and managers, including how to stand out in interviews and how Amazon's core leadership principles actually work.
summary.zh: Ethan 分享了一个简单却有力的重新框架：你不需要很多点子就能被视为极具创造力——每个月想出一个好点子就够，哪怕把它做出来要花好几年（他用 Prime 和 Kindle 的长期打磨来说明）。他坦诚讲述了在一个重要项目上让 Jeff Bezos 失望的经历与教训，并拆解了“魔力循环”（The Magic Loop）——一个看似简单、却保证能帮你升职的方法。这期节目充满面向高级个人贡献者和管理者的具体职业建议，包括如何在面试中脱颖而出，以及亚马逊核心领导力原则的真正运作方式。

episodeTitle.en: How to be more innovative | Sam Schillace (Microsoft deputy CTO, creator of Google Docs)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何更具创新力 | 山姆·施利亚克（Sam Schillace，微软副首席技术官，Google Docs创始人）

bio.en: Sam Schillace is Corporate Vice President and Deputy CTO at Microsoft, leading consumer product, infrastructure, and AI efforts, and is best known for essentially inventing Google Docs with his company Writely.
bio.zh: Sam Schillace 是微软公司副总裁兼副首席技术官（Deputy CTO），领导消费级产品、基础设施与 AI 方面的工作；他最为人知的成就是凭借自己的公司 Writely 几乎凭一己之力发明了 Google Docs。

guestBioOfficial.en: Sam Schillace is deputy CTO and corporate vice president at Microsoft. Prior to working at Microsoft, Sam started a company called Writely, which was acquired by Google and became the foundation of what today is Google Docs. While at Google, Sam helped lead many of Google’s consumer products, including Gmail, Blogger, PageCreator, Picasa, Reader, Groups, and more recently Maps and Google Automotive Services. Sam was also a principal investor at Google Ventures, has founded six startups, and was the SVP of engineering at Box through their IPO. In this episode, we discuss: • The journey of building Google Docs
guestBioOfficial.zh: 山姆·施利亚克是微软副首席技术官兼企业副总裁。在加入微软之前，山姆创办了名为Writely的公司，该公司被谷歌收购，并成为如今Google Docs的基础。在谷歌期间，山姆参与开发了许多消费级产品，包括Gmail、Blogger、PageCreator、Picasa、Reader、Groups，以及最近的Maps和Google Automotive Services。山姆还是Google Ventures的主要投资者，创立过六家初创公司，并在Box上市期间担任SVP工程副总裁。在本期播客中，我们将讨论：• Google Docs的开发历程

summary.en: Sam shares a framework for spotting disruptive innovation: if some people love it and many hate it, it's probably disruptive, whereas broadly 'meh' reactions signal it isn't. He tells the Google Docs origin story and argues that everything around us was once a threatening disruptive idea, so we should expect new ideas to look 'dumb' at first. The conversation also covers first-principles thinking and why undervaluing what comes easily is a career trap.
summary.zh: Sam 分享了一个识别颠覆性创新的框架：如果一部分人狂热喜爱、而许多人强烈厌恶，那它很可能具有颠覆性；相反，若普遍反应平淡，则往往不是。他讲述了 Google Docs 的起源故事，并主张我们周遭的一切都曾是“令人不安的颠覆性想法”，因此应当预期新点子一开始看起来“很蠢”。对话还涉及第一性原理思维，以及为何低估“得来容易之事”是职业陷阱。

episodeTitle.en: The engineering mindset | Will Larson (Carta, Stripe, Uber, Calm, Digg)
episodeTitle.zh: 工程师思维模式 | 威尔·拉森（Will Larson，曾就职于Carta、Stripe、Uber、Calm、Digg）

bio.en: Will Larson is CTO at Carta, an engineering leader at Stripe, Uber, and Calm, and author of An Elegant Puzzle, Staff Engineer, and The Engineering Executive's Primer.
bio.zh: Will Larson 是 Carta 的 CTO，一位曾在 Stripe、Uber 和 Calm 任职的工程领导者，也是《An Elegant Puzzle》《Staff Engineer》与《The Engineering Executive's Primer》等书的作者。

guestBioOfficial.en: Will Larson is the chief technology officer at Carta. Prior to joining Carta, he was the CTO at Calm and held engineering leadership roles at Stripe, Uber, and Digg. He is the author of two foundational engineering career books, An Elegant Puzzle and Staff Engineer, and The Engineering Executive’s Primer, which will be released in February of next year. In our conversation, we discuss: • Systems thinking: what it is and how to apply it
guestBioOfficial.zh: 威尔·拉森（Will Larson）是Carta的首席技术官。在加入Carta之前，他曾担任Calm的CTO，并在Stripe、Uber和Digg担任过工程领导职务。他是两本基础工程职业书籍《An Elegant Puzzle》和《Staff Engineer》的作者，《The Engineering Executive’s Primer》将于明年二月出版。在我们的对话中，我们将讨论： • 系统思维：其定义及应用方式

summary.en: Will shares advice on developing your engineering strategy and strategy in general, the staff/principal engineer path, and what it takes to operate as an engineering executive. He discusses how to think about org design, where technical leaders should focus, and lessons from scaling engineering at Stripe, Uber, and Carta. The episode is a must-read-listener's guide to the engineering leadership ladder.
summary.zh: Will 分享了关于制定工程战略（以及广义战略）的建议、Staff/首席工程师（principal）的成长路径，以及作为工程高管运作需要什么。他讨论了如何思考组织设计、技术领导者应当聚焦何处，以及从在 Stripe、Uber 和 Carta 规模化工程中得到的经验。本期是面向必读听众的、关于工程领导力阶梯的指南。

episodeTitle.en: The UX Research reckoning is here | Judd Antin (Airbnb, Meta)
episodeTitle.zh: 用户体验研究的反思——贾德·安丁（Airbnb、Meta）

bio.en: Judd Antin is a user research leader who built the research practice at Facebook and spent years as head of research at Airbnb, and whose mentees now lead research at Figma, Notion, Slack, and more.
bio.zh: 贾德·安廷（Judd Antin）是一位用户研究领军人物，他曾在 Facebook 建立用户研究体系，并长期担任 Airbnb 的研究负责人，他的许多下属如今在 Figma、Notion、Slack 等公司领导研究团队。

guestBioOfficial.en: Judd Antin has spent 15 years leading research and design teams at companies like Yahoo, Meta, and Airbnb. His direct reports have gone on to lead user research at Figma, Notion, Slack, Robinhood, Duolingo, AllTrails, and more. In our conversation, we unpack the transformation that the user-research field is experiencing. Specifically: • Where user research went wrong over the past decade
guestBioOfficial.zh: 贾德·安丁在雅虎、Meta和Airbnb等公司领导研究与设计团队长达15年，其直接下属后来在Figma、Notion、Slack、Robinhood、Duolingo、AllTrails等公司领导用户研究工作。我们的对话深入解析了用户研究领域正在经历的变革，具体包括：• 过去十年间用户研究领域出现的误区

summary.en: Judd coins "user-centered performance" to describe research done to signal customer obsession rather than to actually learn and change decisions. He argues the goal of research should be to falsify assumptions, not merely validate them. The episode warns against box-checking studies run too late to matter and offers a healthier philosophy for using research.
summary.zh: 贾德创造了"以用户为中心的表演"（user-centered performance）一词，用来描述那些只是为了彰显"以用户为中心"、而非真正为了学习并改变决策的研究行为。他认为，研究的目标应该是去证伪假设，而不只是验证它们。本期提醒人们警惕那些为走流程而在为时已晚时才进行的研究，并提出了更健康的用研理念。

episodeTitle.en: Strategies for becoming less distractible and improving focus | Nir Eyal
episodeTitle.zh: 提升专注力、减少分心干扰的策略 | 尼尔·埃亚尔

bio.en: Nir Eyal is the author of the bestselling books Hooked: How to Build Habit-Forming Products and Indistractable: How to Control Your Attention, and a teacher and consultant at the intersection of psychology, technology, and business.
bio.zh: Nir Eyal 是畅销书《钩住：如何打造让人上瘾的产品》（Hooked）与《不可分心：如何掌控你的注意力》（Indistractable）的作者，也是一位游走于心理学、科技与商业交叉领域的导师与顾问。

guestBioOfficial.en: Nir Eyal is the author of two best-selling books, Hooked: How to Build Habit-Forming Products and Indistractable: How to Control Your Attention and Choose Your Life. He writes, consults, and teaches at the intersection of psychology, technology, and business. His books have sold over 1 million copies in more than 30 languages; he has taught at Stanford’s Graduate School of Business and its Design School; and he has started and sold two startups since 2003. In our conversation, we discuss: • Strategies for becoming less distractible and improving focus
guestBioOfficial.zh: 尼尔·埃亚尔（Nir Eyal）是两本畅销书《上瘾：如何打造让人上瘾的产品》和《心无旁骛：如何掌控注意力，选择人生方向》的作者。他在心理学、科技和商业的交叉领域进行写作、咨询和教学。其著作已在30多种语言中售出超过100万册；他曾在斯坦福大学商学院和设计学院任教；自2003年以来，他已创立并出售了两家初创公司。在我们的对话中，我们探讨了：• 提升专注力、减少分心的策略

summary.en: Nir explains that distraction is not a character flaw but a failure to plan, and introduces a four-step model - master internal triggers, make time for traction, hack back external triggers, and prevent distractions with pacts - to become indistractable. He stresses that the root cause of distraction is often our attempt to escape discomfort, and that scheduling values-based time weekly is more effective than reactive to-do lists. The conversation is packed with practical tactics for regaining focus and doing the work that matters.
summary.zh: Nir 指出，分心不是性格缺陷，而是缺乏规划的结果，并提出了四步模型来变得“不可分心”：掌控内在诱因、为“专注”预留时间、回击外部干扰、用约定（pact）防止分心。他强调，分心的根源往往是我们逃避不适感，而每周基于价值观安排时间，比被动的待办清单更有效。本期充满了重新夺回注意力、去做真正重要之事的实用技巧。

episodeTitle.en: The hierarchy of engagement | Sarah Tavel (Benchmark, Greylock, Pinterest)
episodeTitle.zh: 参与度的层级 | 莎拉·塔维尔（Sarah Tavel，Benchmark、Greylock、Pinterest）

bio.en: Sarah Tavel is a partner at Benchmark, one of the world's preeminent venture capital firms, focusing on consumer and marketplace startups, and was the first product manager at Pinterest.
bio.zh: Sarah Tavel 是 Benchmark 的合伙人，该基金是全球最负盛名的风投机构之一，她专注投资消费级与 marketplace 类初创公司，此前曾是 Pinterest 的首位产品经理。

guestBioOfficial.en: Sarah Tavel is a General Partner at Benchmark and sits on the boards of Chainalysis, Hipcamp, Rekki, Cambly, and Medely. She is a founding member of All Raise, the nonprofit organization working to accelerate the success of women in the venture-capital and VC-backed startup ecosystem. Before Benchmark, Sarah was a partner at Greylock Partners. She joined Pinterest in 2012 as their first PM and launched their first search and recommendations features. She also led three acquisitions as she helped the company scale through a period of hypergrowth. In this episode, we discuss: • Sarah’s Hierarchy of Engagement framework for growing a consumer startup
guestBioOfficial.zh: 莎拉·塔维尔是Benchmark的普通合伙人，同时也是Chainalysis、Hipcamp、Rekki、Cambly和Medely董事会成员。她是All Raise的创始成员之一，这是一个致力于推动女性在风险投资和风投支持的初创企业生态系统中取得成功的非营利组织。在加入Benchmark之前，莎拉是Greylock Partners的合伙人。2012年，她加入Pinterest，担任首位产品经理，推出了该平台的首批搜索和推荐功能。她还领导了三次收购，助力公司在高速增长期内实现规模扩张。在本期播客中，我们将讨论：• 莎拉用于发展消费级初创企业的参与度层级框架

summary.en: Sarah brings a product-and-growth leader's lens to venture investing, sharing how she evaluates consumer and marketplace startups from first principles. She discusses what makes a compelling founder and product, the metrics and motions that signal durable growth, and lessons from her own operating background at Pinterest. The episode is a rare blend of investor and product-leader thinking applied to building and backing companies.
summary.zh: Sarah 以产品与增长领导者的视角看待风险投资，分享了她如何从源头（first principles）评估消费级与 marketplace 初创公司。她讨论了什么造就一个有吸引力的创始人与产品、哪些指标与打法预示着可持续的增长，以及她在 Pinterest 的运营背景中获得的经验。本期罕见地将投资者与产品领导者的思维融合，应用于打造与押注公司。

episodeTitle.en: The essence of product management | Christian Idiodi (SVPG)
episodeTitle.zh: 产品管理的精髓 | 克里斯蒂安·伊多迪（SVPG）

bio.en: Christian Idiodi is a partner at Silicon Valley Product Group alongside Marty Cagan, known as “the most interesting man in the world,” helping companies implement and improve the discipline of product management.
bio.zh: Christian Idiodi 是硅谷产品集团（Silicon Valley Product Group）的合伙人，与 Marty Cagan 共事，被称为“世界上最有趣的人”，帮助各公司落地并改进产品管理的纪律。

guestBioOfficial.en: Christian Idiodi is a partner at Silicon Valley Product Group. After a long product career and founding multiple companies, Christian now spends his time working closely with product leaders at companies big and small to implement and improve their discipline of product management. In today’s episode, we discuss: • Why there’s often a negative perception of product managers, and how we can fix this
guestBioOfficial.zh: 克里斯蒂安·伊多迪（Christian Idiodi）是硅谷产品集团（Silicon Valley Product Group）的合伙人。经过漫长的产品职业生涯并创立多家公司后，克里斯蒂安现在致力于与大大小小的公司产品负责人密切合作，实施并改进他们的产品管理体系。在本期节目中，我们将探讨：• 为何产品经理常被负面看待，以及如何改变这一现状

summary.en: Christian reframes the essence of product management as waking up on behalf of someone else to solve a problem well enough that they give something back, and tackles why the field is so often disliked. He spends significant time on coaching—how to coach your reports and get better coaching from your manager—plus tactics for building trust with leaders. The conversation also shares his single favorite discovery method for figuring out what to build.
summary.zh: Christian 把产品管理的本质重新定义为“替别人醒来、把问题解决好到对方愿意回馈”，并探讨了该领域为何常被人嫌弃。他花大量时间讲教练——如何辅导下属、以及如何从经理那里得到更好的辅导——以及赢得领导者信任的战术。对话还分享了他最偏爱、用来判断“该造什么”的发现方法。

episodeTitle.en: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more
episodeTitle.zh: 杰森·弗里德挑战您对融资、目标、增长等的认知

bio.en: Jason Fried is co-founder and CEO of 37signals, the profitable, bootstrapped company behind Basecamp and HEY that has made money for 24 straight years with no investors, no board, and no plans to sell or go public.
bio.zh: Jason Fried 是 37signals 的联合创始人兼 CEO；37signals 是一家盈利、自筹资金的公司，旗下有 Basecamp 和 HEY，连续 24 年盈利，没有投资人、没有董事会，也无意出售或上市。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jason Fried is the co-founder and CEO of 37signals, the maker of Basecamp and HEY. 37signals is a very different kind of company. With fewer than 80 employees, they have over 100,000 customers, generate tens of millions of dollars in profit each year, and have no investors, board, or any plans to ever raise money or sell the company. In our conversation, we explore a path many tech founders never consider—bootstrapping. We discuss: • Why he and his team prioritize profit above all else
guestBioOfficial.zh: 杰森·弗里德是37signals（Basecamp和HEY的开发商）的联合创始人兼CEO。37signals是一家非常与众不同的公司。员工不足80人，却拥有超过10万名客户，每年创造数千万美元利润，没有投资者、董事会，也无意融资或出售公司。在对话中，我们探讨了一条许多科技创始人从未考虑过的道路——自力更生。我们讨论：•为何他和团队将利润置于首位

summary.en: Jason makes the case that bootstrapping gives founders far more practice at the fundamental skill of making money, and that there's far more room to build a successful, fulfilling, even more lucrative business outside the 'go big or go home' VC path that almost nobody actually wins. He argues constraints like small teams and less cash often produce better outcomes, that gut and instinct are underrated decision tools, that long-term planning is often a mistake, and that work shouldn't feel like war. The episode is a compelling alternative philosophy for building a company on your own terms.
summary.zh: Jason 提出，自筹资金让创始人更多地练习“赚钱”这一根本技能，而且相比几乎无人胜出的“不成功便成仁”的 VC 路线，在它之外有更大的空间去打造成功、充实、甚至更赚钱的事业。他主张小团队、少现金之类的约束往往带来更好的结果，直觉是被低估的决策工具，长期规划常常是错误，工作不应像战争。这期节目是关于“按自己的方式”打造公司的、令人信服的另一种哲学。

episodeTitle.en: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何讲好故事 | 马修·迪克斯（Storyworthy）

bio.en: Matthew Dicks is the author of Storyworthy, a 59-time Moth Story Slam winner, and a teacher of storytelling for business and life.
bio.zh: 马修·迪克斯（Matthew Dicks）是《Storyworthy》一书的作者、59 次 Moth 故事大赛的冠军，也是一位教授商业与生活叙事的老师。

guestBioOfficial.en: Matthew Dicks is a best-selling author, columnist, blogger, podcaster, playwright, and teacher. He wrote my all-time favorite book on storytelling, Storyworthy. He is an elementary school teacher by day and by night teaches storytelling and public speaking to individuals, corporations, universities, religious institutions, and school districts around the world. He’s taught storytelling at Yale, MIT, Harvard, and Purdue, along with Amazon, Salesforce, Slack, Lego, and others. In this conversation, Matthew shares insights and techniques for effective storytelling, including: • The benefits of good storytelling in business
guestBioOfficial.zh: 马修·迪克斯（Matthew Dicks）是一位畅销书作家、专栏作家、博主、播客主、剧作家和教师。他写了一本我最喜欢的讲故事书籍《值得讲述的故事》（Storyworthy）。白天他是小学教师，晚上则为世界各地的个人、企业、大学、宗教机构和学区教授讲故事和公开演讲技巧。他曾在耶鲁大学、麻省理工学院、哈佛大学和普渡大学授课，同时与亚马逊、Salesforce、Slack、乐高等公司合作。在本次对话中，马修分享了有效讲故事的见解和技巧，包括：• 商业中良好讲故事的益处

summary.en: Matthew argues businesspeople love calling themselves storytellers but rarely separate from the herd, which makes them forgettable. He shows that stories - not charts or platitudes - are what human minds actually remember. The episode is a practical, energetic guide to using storytelling to be remembered and influential.
summary.zh: 马修指出，商界人士喜欢自称"讲故事的人"，却很少从人群中脱颖而出，结果变得容易被遗忘。他说明，人脑真正记住的是故事，而非图表或套话。本期是一份实用而充满能量的指南，教你用故事让人记住、产生影响。

episodeTitle.en: Failure
episodeTitle.zh: 失败

bio.en: A special compilation episode in which Lenny revisits the most insightful stories of failure pulled from past conversations, arguing that you can often learn more from failure than from studying successful companies.
bio.zh: 这是一期特别的合集节目：Lenny 从过往对话中挑出最具启发性的“失败”故事重新编排，主张研究失败往往比研究成功公司更能学到东西。

guestBioOfficial.en: In this special compilation episode, we delve into failure—an overlooked source of wisdom. From freezing onstage in front of thousands of people, to coworkers staging an intervention, to huge product investments that went to zero, we’ve pulled our favorite stories of failure from 100+ podcast episodes. I hope these stories serve as a gentle nudge to view failure not as a setback but as a crucial detour toward growth.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 在这期特别合集节目中，我们深入探讨失败——这一常被忽视的智慧之源。从在数千人面前舞台上僵住，到同事们展开劝退行动，再到巨额产品投资化为乌有，我们从100多期播客中精选了最喜欢的失败故事。希望这些故事能给人以启发，让人们不再将失败视为挫折，而是看作通向成长的关键转折。

summary.en: Instead of a standard interview, this episode curates the best failure stories from across the podcast's back catalog into one focused listen. Lenny makes the case that studying how things break—rather than only how the best companies operate—yields some of the most valuable lessons for builders. It's an experiment in thematic compilation, and Lenny invites listener feedback to decide whether to keep doing more like it.
summary.zh: 这期并非标准访谈，而是把播客过往节目中最精彩的失败故事精选编排成一期聚焦的节目。Lenny 提出一个观点：研究事物如何失败（而不只是研究最优秀的公司如何运作）能为建设者带来一些最有价值的经验。这是一次主题合集的尝试，Lenny 也邀请听众反馈，以决定是否继续做更多类似节目。

episodeTitle.en: Radical Candor: From theory to practice with author Kim Scott
episodeTitle.zh: 《激进坦诚》：从理论到实践 作者Kim Scott

bio.en: Kim Scott is the author of Radical Candor, the most-referenced management book on Lenny's podcast, and has coached leaders at Apple, Google, Twitter, and Dropbox.
bio.zh: 金·斯科特（Kim Scott）是《彻底坦率》（Radical Candor）一书的作者，该书是 Lenny 播客中被引用最多的管理类著作，她曾为 Apple、Google、Twitter 和 Dropbox 的领导者担任教练。

guestBioOfficial.en: Kim Scott is the author of Radical Candor, currently the #1 most recommended book on this podcast. The book has sold over 1 million copies and has been translated into 23 languages. Before writing, Kim was a CEO coach at Dropbox, Qualtrics, Twitter, and other tech companies. She was also a member of the faculty at Apple University and before that led AdSense, YouTube, and DoubleClick teams at Google. This spring she’ll be launching Radical Respect, which she considers to be a prequel to Radical Candor. In today’s conversation, we go deep on Kim’s popular framework, including: • What separates radical candor and obnoxious aggression
guestBioOfficial.zh: Kim Scott是《激进坦诚》的作者，该书目前是本播客中推荐度最高的书籍。本书已售出超过100万册，并被翻译成23种语言。在写作之前，Kim曾在Dropbox、Qualtrics、推特等科技公司担任CEO教练。她还曾是苹果大学的教员，在此之前，她曾在谷歌领导AdSense、YouTube和DoubleClick团队。今年春天，她将推出《激进尊重》，她认为这是《激进坦诚》的前传。在今天的对话中，我们深入探讨了Kim广受欢迎的框架，包括：• 激进坦诚与令人不快的攻击行为的区别

summary.en: Kim teaches that the best way to get feedback is to ask "What could I do or stop doing to make it easier to work with me?" rather than a generic request. She explains the two dimensions of Radical Candor - care personally and challenge directly. The episode is a practical guide to building a culture of honest, kind, and effective feedback.
summary.zh: 金指出，获取反馈最好的方式是问"我可以做些什么、或停止做什么，能让我们合作更顺畅？"，而不是泛泛地请求反馈。她阐释了《彻底坦率》的两个维度——真诚关怀与直接挑战。本期是一份关于建立诚实、善意且高效反馈文化的实用指南。

episodeTitle.en: The full-stack PM | Anuj Rathi (Swiggy, Jupiter Money, Flipkart)
episodeTitle.zh: 全栈产品经理 | 阿努吉·拉蒂（曾就职于Swiggy、Jupiter Money、Flipkart）

bio.en: Anuj Rathi is Chief Product and Marketing Officer at Jupiter Money, previously SVP of Revenue and Growth at Swiggy, VP of Product at Snapdeal, and the first PM at Flipkart's buyer experience team.
bio.zh: Anuj Rathi 是 Jupiter Money 首席产品与营销官，此前曾任 Swiggy 营收与增长高级副总裁、Snapdeal 产品副总裁，以及 Flipkart 买家体验团队的第一位产品经理。

guestBioOfficial.en: Anuj Rathi is the Chief Product and Marketing Officer at Jupiter Money, where he leads product management, marketing, design, growth, and analytics. Before Jupiter Money, Anuj served as the Senior Vice President of Revenue and Growth at Swiggy, VP of Product at SnapDeal, a senior PM at Walmart Labs, and the first-ever PM at Flipkart. He’s also one of the most beloved and respected product leaders in India. In this episode, we discuss: • How product management is different in India
guestBioOfficial.zh: 阿努吉·拉蒂（Anuj Rathi）现任Jupiter Money首席产品与营销官，负责产品管理、市场营销、设计、增长和分析等领域。在加入Jupiter Money之前，阿努吉曾担任Swiggy收入与增长高级副总裁、SnapDeal产品副总裁、沃尔玛实验室高级产品经理，以及Flipkart首位产品经理。他也是印度最受尊敬和喜爱的产品领导者之一。在本期节目中，我们将探讨： • 印度产品管理的独特之处

summary.en: Anuj explains how product management differs in India and shares lessons on building product experiences for new-to-internet users at massive scale. He describes operationalizing Amazon's “working backwards” process and why he pushes teams to explore three divergent directions before settling on a plan. The conversation also covers why PMs and companies should be far more full-stack than they typically are.
summary.zh: Anuj 解释了印度市场的产品管理有何不同，并分享了为海量“新上网用户”打造产品体验的心得。他讲述了如何将亚马逊的“逆向工作法”落地，以及为何他推动团队在定案前先探索三个截然不同的方向。对话还涵盖为何产品经理和公司应当比现在更“全栈”。

episodeTitle.en: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)
episodeTitle.zh: 《打造引人注目的产品愿景 | 埃比·阿塔沃迪（YouTube、Netflix、Uber）》

bio.en: Ebi Atawodi is the director of product management at YouTube, where she oversees the creator experience, and previously led payments and fintech product at Uber and Netflix.
bio.zh: Ebi Atawodi 是 YouTube 的产品管理总监，负责创作者体验，此前曾在 Uber 和 Netflix 主导支付与金融科技产品。

guestBioOfficial.en: Ebi Atawodi is Director of Product Management for the Creator Experience at YouTube, former Head of Product at Uber, and a former Director of Product (Payments and EMEA) at Netflix. Known for crafting a strong, unified vision, Ebi empowers her teams to achieve outsized outcomes. In today’s episode, we go deep into vision and strategy, including: • The four key elements of a good vision statement
guestBioOfficial.zh: 埃比·阿塔沃迪是YouTube创作者体验产品管理总监，曾任Uber产品主管，也是Netflix产品（支付与欧洲、中东和非洲地区）总监。以打造强有力的统一愿景而闻名，埃比助力团队取得超出预期的成果。在本期节目中，我们深入探讨愿景与战略，包括：• 优秀愿景声明的四个关键要素

summary.en: Ebi shares some of the most tactical advice Lenny has heard on developing a clear product vision and communicating it effectively to both teammates and executives. She breaks down the craft of product management and how to deliberately get better at it, plus what she's learned about building a strong product culture within a team and across a company. Her philosophy centers on leading with care—'being loved, not liked'—so that hard feedback lands in service of people's growth.
summary.zh: Ebi 分享了 Lenny 听过最具实操性的一些建议，内容是如何打造清晰的产品愿景，并有效地向同事和高管沟通。她拆解了产品管理的“手艺”以及如何有意识地精进，还谈到了在团队和公司层面建立强产品文化的心得。她的理念核心是以关怀来领导——追求“被爱，而非被喜欢”，让尖锐的反馈真正服务于人的成长。

episodeTitle.en: The future of AI in software development | Inbal Shani (CPO of GitHub)
episodeTitle.zh: 人工智能在软件开发中的未来 | 因巴尔·沙尼（GitHub首席产品官）

bio.en: Inbal Shani is a product executive who served as Chief Product Officer of Ironclad and is now Chief Product Officer at LinkedIn, where she leads development of the world's largest professional network.
bio.zh: Inbal Shani 是一位产品高管，曾担任 Ironclad 的首席产品官，现任 LinkedIn 首席产品官，领导全球最大职业社交网络的开发。

guestBioOfficial.en: Inbal Shani is the chief product officer at GitHub, where she leads core product management, along with product strategy, marketing, open source, and communities, including the development of GitHub Copilot. Prior to joining GitHub, she led engineering and product teams at Amazon and Microsoft. In today’s conversation, we discuss: • What Inbal believes is overhyped and underhyped in the rapidly changing field of AI
guestBioOfficial.zh: 因巴尔·沙尼是GitHub的首席产品官，负责核心产品管理、产品战略、市场营销、开源和社区事务，包括GitHub Copilot的开发。在加入GitHub之前，她曾在亚马逊和微软领导工程和产品团队。在今天的对话中，我们将讨论：•因巴尔认为在快速变化的人工智能领域，哪些东西被过度炒作，哪些被低估了

summary.en: In this conversation, Inbal draws on her experience leading product at high-scale companies to share hard-won lessons on what it takes to build and lead great product organizations. She discusses how product leaders can earn trust, scale decision-making, and grow both their teams and their own careers. The episode is full of practical wisdom for product managers and leaders who want to operate at the highest level.
summary.zh: 在这期对话中，Inbal 结合在大型公司领导产品的经验，分享了打造并领导卓越产品组织的来之不易的教训。她谈到产品领导者如何赢得信任、放大决策规模，以及如何让团队与自己一同成长。这期节目充满面向想在高层面运作的 PM 与领导者的实用智慧。

episodeTitle.en: My favorite interview questions from 100+ guests
episodeTitle.zh: 我从100+位嘉宾那里收集的最爱采访问题

bio.en: A special compilation episode in which Lenny gathers the best advice from past guests on how to prepare for, approach, and ace product and tech job interviews.
bio.zh: 这是一期特别的合集节目：Lenny 汇集了过往嘉宾关于如何准备、应对并在产品与技术岗位面试中脱颖而出的精华建议。

guestBioOfficial.en: This is a special episode of the podcast where I've curated my favorite interview questions from over a hundred podcast guests. Whether you're a hiring manager, a job seeker, or simply intrigued by the brilliant minds behind groundbreaking products, these questions offer unique insights into the strategies and philosophies that shape successful interviews.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 本期播客特别环节，我精心挑选了百余位播客嘉宾中最受欢迎的采访问题。无论你是招聘经理、求职者，还是对突破性产品背后的杰出人才感兴趣，这些问题都能为成功面试的策略与理念提供独特见解。

summary.en: Rather than a single interview, this episode curates the most useful interview guidance from across the podcast's guest roster into one focused listen. It distills practical tips on answering behavioral and product-design questions, showcasing your thinking, and standing out to hiring managers. It's a handy resource for anyone preparing for their next product, design, or engineering interview.
summary.zh: 这期并非单次访谈，而是把播客嘉宾阵容中最实用的面试指导精选编排成一期聚焦的节目。它提炼了回答行为与产品设计问题、展示思维方式、以及向招聘经理脱颖而出的实用技巧。对任何准备下一场产品、设计或工程面试的人来说，都是一份便利的参考资料。

episodeTitle.en: Billion dollar failures, and billion dollar success | Tom Conrad (Quibi, Pandora, Pets.com, Zero)
episodeTitle.zh: 百亿美元的失败与百亿美元的成功 | 汤姆·康拉德（Quibi、Pandora、Pets.com、Zero）

bio.en: Tom Conrad is the CEO of Zero and a veteran product and technology leader who helped build foundational iOS features at Apple, served as CTO of Pandora and VP of Product at Snap, and was an executive at the famed failures Pets.com and Quibi.
bio.zh: Tom Conrad 是 Zero 的 CEO，也是一位资深的产品与技术领导者：他曾在 Apple 帮助打造 iOS 的基础性功能，担任过 Pandora 的 CTO 与 Snap 的产品副总裁，还曾任职于那些著名的失败案例 Pets.com 与 Quibi。

guestBioOfficial.en: Tom Conrad is the CEO of Zero and on the board of Sonos. He began his career in engineering at Apple, where he helped build key features that remain in iOS today. Tom was previously the VP of Product at Snap and the chief technology officer of Pandora. He also held leadership positions at notable tech flops Pets.com and Quibi, giving him a unique perspective not only on what it takes to build a successful company but also on lessons from failure. In today’s conversation, we discuss: • Lessons learned from the infamous failures of Pets.com and Quibi
guestBioOfficial.zh:
汤姆·康拉德（Tom Conrad）是Zero公司的首席执行官，同时也是Sonos董事会成员。他的职业生涯始于苹果公司，曾参与开发至今仍保留在iOS系统中的关键功能。此前，他曾担任Snap的副总裁以及Pandora的首席技术官，还在科技界的失败案例Pets.com和Quibi中担任过领导职务。这段经历不仅让他深刻领悟了成功企业的构建之道，也让他从失败中汲取了宝贵经验。在今天的对话中，我们将探讨：
• 从Pets.com和Quibi这些臭名昭著的失败案例中吸取的教训

summary.en: Tom reflects on lessons from both billion-dollar failures (Pets.com, Quibi) and billion-dollar successes (Apple, Pandora, Snap), including why not everyone needs to be a founder. He shares how to choose where to work, the math of a business, and how to avoid burnout while building. The episode is a rare, story-rich blend of failure and success from a true operator.
summary.zh: Tom 反思了十亿美元级失败（Pets.com、Quibi）与十亿美元级成功（Apple、Pandora、Snap）中的经验，包括为什么并非人人都需要成为创始人。他分享了如何选择供职的公司、生意背后的数学逻辑，以及如何在打造产品的同时避免职业倦怠。本期是一位真正从业者对失败与成功的、富含故事的罕见融合。

episodeTitle.en: Redefining success, money, and belonging | Paul Millerd (The Pathless Path)
episodeTitle.zh: 重新定义成功、金钱和归属感 | 保罗·米勒德（《无路之路》）

bio.en: Paul Millerd is the author of The Pathless Path: Imagining a New Story for Work and Life, a book that has resonated widely in the tech community for challenging the default career trajectory.
bio.zh: Paul Millerd 是《无路之路》（The Pathless Path）一书的作者，该书因挑战传统默认职业轨迹而在科技圈引发广泛共鸣。

guestBioOfficial.en: Paul Millerd spent several years working in strategy consulting and on the “default path” before deciding to walk away to work on his own in 2017. His book, The Pathless Path, chronicles his own journey and deep dive into the history of work and has been read by more than 40,000 people. His podcast, The Pathless Path Podcast, highlights conversations with others following unconventional paths. He also runs the online training business StrategyU, helping people learn the skills of consulting without having to work in the industry. In our conversation, Paul shares: • An explanation of the “default path” and the “pathless path”
guestBioOfficial.zh: 保罗·米勒德曾在战略咨询领域工作数年，并遵循“默认路径”，直到2017年决定离开，开始自主创业。他的著作《无路之路》记录了他自己的旅程，并深入探讨了工作的历史，已有超过40,000人阅读。他的播客《无路之路》聚焦于那些走非传统道路的人的对话。他还经营在线培训业务StrategyU，帮助人们学习咨询技能，而无需在该行业工作。在我们的对话中，保罗分享了：• “默认路径”和“无路之路”的解释

summary.en: Paul reframes the 'default path' of work and life as a script we unconsciously follow, and argues that consciously choosing uncertainty can open a more fulfilling route. He shares how a three-month sabbatical - or even a three-hour weekday reset - can create the space to discover what you actually want, and why founders should embrace offering sabbaticals. The conversation is a practical invitation to question the script and design a life on your own terms.
summary.zh: Paul 将工作与生活的“默认路径”重新定义为一种我们在无意识中遵循的剧本，并主张有意识地选择不确定性，反而能通向更充实的人生。他分享了三个月的休假——甚至只是工作日里三小时的抽离——如何创造出发现真正所求的空间，以及为什么创始人应当乐于提供休假。本期是一份务实的邀请：质疑那套剧本，按自己的方式设计人生。

episodeTitle.en: The ultimate guide to product operations | Melissa Perri and Denise Tilles
episodeTitle.zh: 产品运营终极指南 | 梅丽莎·佩里（Melissa Perri）与丹妮丝·蒂勒斯（Denise Tilles）

bio.en: Melissa Perri and Denise Tilles are the authors of Product Operations, with Melissa known for Escaping the Build Trap and both helping companies scale product management through product ops.
bio.zh: 梅丽莎·佩里（Melissa Perri）与丹尼斯·蒂勒斯（Denise Tilles）是《产品运营》（Product Operations）一书的作者；梅丽莎以《逃离构建陷阱》（Escaping the Build Trap）闻名，二人都通过产品运营帮助公司扩展产品管理能力。

guestBioOfficial.en: Melissa Perri is the CEO of Produx Labs, a product management training organization; author of the seminal PM book The Build Trap; and a former Harvard Business School professor of product management. Denise Tilles is the CPO at Grocket, Melissa’s colleague at Produx Labs, and a seasoned product leader with over a decade of experience. Together they authored the new book Product Operations: How successful companies build better products at scale. In today’s episode, they share insights, strategies, and real-world experiences to master all things product ops. We discuss: • What exactly product operations is
guestBioOfficial.zh: 梅丽莎·佩里（Melissa Perri）是产品管理培训机构Produx Labs的首席执行官，权威PM著作《The Build Trap》的作者，同时曾任哈佛商学院产品管理教授。丹妮丝·蒂勒斯（Denise Tilles）是Grocket公司的首席产品官，也是梅丽莎在Produx Labs的同事，她拥有十余年丰富的产品管理经验。两人合著新书《Product Operations：成功公司如何大规模打造优质产品》。在本期节目中，她们将分享见解、策略及真实案例，助你精通产品运营全领域。我们将探讨：• 产品运营究竟是什么？

summary.en: Melissa and Denise make the case for a dedicated product operations function that handles shared systems so PMs can focus the majority of their time on strategic work. They explain the emerging role of product ops and how to build it at scale. The episode is a deep dive into a critical but often missing piece of modern product organizations.
summary.zh: 梅丽莎和丹尼斯论证了：应设立专门的产品运营职能来处理共享系统，让 PM 能把大部分时间聚焦在战略工作上。她们解释了产品运营这一新兴角色，以及如何在规模上构建它。本期深入探讨了现代产品组织中关键却常被缺失的一环。

episodeTitle.en: Brian Chesky’s new playbook
episodeTitle.zh: 布莱恩·切斯基的新策略手册

bio.en: Brian Chesky is co-founder and CEO of Airbnb, which he grew from an apartment startup into an ~$80 billion global business operating in 220 countries.
bio.zh: Brian Chesky 是 Airbnb 联合创始人兼 CEO，他将公司从公寓里的创业项目发展成业务遍及 220 个国家、估值约 800 亿美元的全球化企业。

guestBioOfficial.en: Brian Chesky is the co-founder and CEO of Airbnb. Under Brian’s leadership, Airbnb has grown into a community of over 4 million hosts who have welcomed more than 1.5 billion guests across over 220 countries and regions. I had the privilege of working under his leadership, so it is a great honor to have him on the show. We discuss: • How Airbnb has shifted their thinking on product management
guestBioOfficial.zh: 布莱恩·切斯基是Airbnb的联合创始人兼首席执行官。在布莱恩的领导下，Airbnb已发展成为一个由400多万房东组成的社区，他们在220多个国家和地区接待了超过15亿名客人。我有幸在他的领导下工作，所以很荣幸能邀请他参加节目。我们讨论： • Airbnb如何转变了他们对产品管理的思维方式

summary.en: Brian explains his controversial shift in how Airbnb runs product management—staying close to every design and feature with a single company-wide roadmap—and distinguishes “being in the details” from micromanagement. He describes moving away from paid growth channels toward building the best product and letting word of mouth drive growth. The conversation also covers how he finds balance and avoids burnout while continuing to learn as a leader.
summary.zh: Brian 解释了他引发争议的产品管理改革——贴近每一个设计与功能，并采用全公司单一路线图——并区分了“深入细节”与微观管理。他描述了如何摆脱付费增长渠道，转而打造最好的产品、让口碑驱动增长。对话还涵盖他作为领导者如何寻找平衡、避免倦怠并持续学习。

episodeTitle.en: Marketplace lessons from Uber, Airbnb, Bumble, and more | Ramesh Johari (Stanford professor)
episodeTitle.zh: 优步、Airbnb、Bumble等平台的市场经验 | 拉梅什·乔哈里（斯坦福大学教授）

bio.en: Ramesh Johari is a professor at Stanford University focused on the design and operation of online marketplaces, and has advised and worked with many of the world's largest marketplaces including Airbnb, Uber, Stripe, Bumble, and Stitch Fix.
bio.zh: Ramesh Johari 是斯坦福大学教授，研究方向为在线市场的设计与运营，曾为包括 Airbnb、Uber、Stripe、Bumble 和 Stitch Fix 在内的全球最大的一批市场平台提供咨询与合作。

guestBioOfficial.en: Ramesh Johari is a professor at Stanford University focusing on data science methods and practice, as well as the design and operation of online markets and platforms. Beyond academia, Ramesh has advised some incredible startups, including Airbnb, Uber, Bumble, and Stitch Fix. Today we discuss: • What exactly a marketplace is, if you boil it down
guestBioOfficial.zh: 拉梅什·乔哈里是斯坦福大学教授，专注于数据科学方法与实践，以及在线市场和平台的设计与运营。除学术领域外，拉梅什还为Airbnb、Uber、Bumble和Stitch Fix等知名初创公司提供咨询服务。今天我们讨论：• 若将市场简化至本质，它究竟是什么？

summary.en: Ramesh reframes marketplace businesses around the goal of achieving 'scaled liquidity' on both sides of the platform, and warns that most perceived problems are not marketplace-specific at all. He explains how data science should shift from machine learning to causal inference to truly improve matching and ranking, and why a culture of fast, learning-oriented experiments beats waiting for statistical significance. The conversation is a deep, nerdy dive into building thriving marketplaces.
summary.zh: Ramesh 将市场业务重新定义为追求平台双边“规模化流动性（scaled liquidity）”的目标，并提醒说，大多数看似的问题根本不是市场特有的。他解释了数据科学应当从机器学习转向因果推断，才能真正改善匹配与排序，以及为什么“快速、以学习为导向的实验文化”优于苦等统计显著性。本期是对打造繁荣市场平台的深度、硬核剖析。

episodeTitle.en: Mastering product strategy and growing as a PM | Maggie Crowley (Toast, Drift, TripAdvisor)
episodeTitle.zh: 《精通产品战略，成长为产品经理》| 玛吉·克劳利（Toast、Drift、TripAdvisor）

bio.en: Maggie Crowley is VP of Product at Toast and has held product leadership roles at Charlie Health, Drift, BevSpot, and TripAdvisor.
bio.zh: 玛吉·克劳利（Maggie Crowley）是 Toast 的产品副总裁，曾在 Charlie Health、Drift、BevSpot 和 TripAdvisor 担任产品领导职务。

guestBioOfficial.en: Maggie Crowley is VP of product at Toast and previously vice president and head of product at Charlie Health, senior director of product management at Drift, and a PM at TripAdvisor. She’s also the host of Build, a podcast dedicated to product and product management. In today’s conversation, Maggie shares: • The value of building a broad-based PM skill set
guestBioOfficial.zh: 玛吉·克劳利是Toast的副总裁，此前曾在Charlie Health担任副总裁兼产品主管，在Drift担任产品管理高级总监，并在TripAdvisor担任产品经理。她还是致力于产品和产品管理的播客《Build》的主持人。在今天的对话中，玛吉分享了：• 建立广泛的PM技能的重要性

summary.en: Maggie argues that when you catch yourself saying "that's not my job," it's usually exactly what you should do to move faster. She describes the PM as the emotional center of the team, responsible for keeping everyone motivated and optimistic. The episode is full of grounded advice on ownership, scrappiness, and doing whatever it takes to ship.
summary.zh: 玛吉认为，当你忍不住说"那不是我的活儿"时，那往往恰恰是你应该去做、从而更快推进的事。她把 PM 描述成团队的"情绪中心"，负责让大家保持动力与乐观。本期充满了关于主人翁意识、灵活务实以及"为交付不遗余力"的扎实建议。

episodeTitle.en: Unpacking Amazon’s unique ways of working | Bill Carr (author of Working Backwards)
episodeTitle.zh: 解读亚马逊独特的运营方式 | 比尔·卡尔（Bill Carr，《倒退工作法》作者）

bio.en: Bill Carr is co-author of 'Working Backwards' and a 15-year Amazon veteran who, as VP of Digital Media, launched and ran Amazon Music, Prime Video, and Amazon Studios before later serving as COO of OfferUp and founding the Working Backwards consulting firm.
bio.zh: Bill Carr 是《Working Backwards》的合著者，也是在亚马逊待了 15 年的老将。作为数字媒体副总裁，他发起并运营了 Amazon Music、Prime Video 和 Amazon Studios，之后担任 OfferUp 的 COO，并创立了 Working Backwards 咨询公司。

guestBioOfficial.en: Bill Carr is the co-author of Working Backwards: Insights, Stories, and Secrets from Inside Amazon. With a background at Amazon of over 15 years, Bill played a pivotal role in shaping the company’s global digital music and video ventures, including Amazon Music, Prime Video, and Amazon Studios. After Amazon, Bill was an Executive in Residence with Maveron, an early-stage, consumer-only venture capital firm. He later served as the chief operating officer of OfferUp, the largest mobile marketplace for local buyers and sellers in the U.S. Today he’s the co-founder of Working Backwards LLC, where he helps companies implement Amazon’s time-tested management strategies. In this episode, we discuss: • What exactly “working backwards” is, and how you do it
guestBioOfficial.zh: 比尔·卡尔（Bill Carr）是《倒退工作法》（Working Backwards）的合著者。他在亚马逊任职超过15年，曾深度参与亚马逊全球数字音乐和视频业务的布局，包括亚马逊音乐、Prime视频和亚马逊影业。离开亚马逊后，比尔在早期消费级风险投资公司Maveron担任驻场高管，随后担任美国最大的本地买卖双方移动市场OfferUp的首席运营官。如今，他是Working Backwards LLC的联合创始人，致力于帮助企业实施亚马逊久经考验的管理策略。本期节目讨论议题：• 何为“倒退工作法”及其具体实践

summary.en: Bill Carr distills the operating system behind Amazon's success: working backwards from customer needs (via the PR/FAQ process), single-threaded leaders who own outcomes with dedicated cross-functional resources, and input metrics that drive long-term outputs. He explains why 'disagree and commit' hinges on being heard and then committing with understanding, how a product 'funnel' of PR/FAQs selects the best ideas, and how Amazon's stock-based comp and CEO-backed structures let it tolerate failure and innovate. He also details the Bar Raiser hiring practice and the 'slow is smooth, smooth is fast' mindset.
summary.zh: Bill Carr 提炼了亚马逊成功背后的操作系统：从客户需求倒推（通过 PR/FAQ 流程）、拥有结果并配备专门跨职能资源的单一负责人、以及驱动长期输出的输入指标。他解释了为什么“提出异议并承诺执行”关键在于“被听到、然后带着理解去承诺”，PR/FAQ 的“产品漏斗”如何筛出最好的想法，以及亚马逊基于股票的薪酬和 CEO 背书的结构如何让它容忍失败并创新。他还详述了 Bar Raiser 招聘实践和“慢就是顺、顺就是快”的心智模式。

episodeTitle.en: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)
episodeTitle.zh: 制作和营销

bio.en: Eric Ries is the creator of the Lean Startup methodology and author of the influential book The Lean Startup; he is also founder and executive chairman of the Long-Term Stock Exchange, advising founders on building companies aligned with human flourishing.
bio.zh: Eric Ries 是“精益创业”（Lean Startup）方法论的创造者、畅销书《精益创业》的作者，同时是长期股票交易所（Long-Term Stock Exchange）的创始人兼执行董事长，致力于指导创始人打造与人类福祉相统一的企业。

guestBioOfficial.en: Eric Ries is the creator of the Lean Startup methodology, author of the New York Times bestseller The Lean Startup, and founder of the Long-Term Stock Exchange (LTSE). He’s also a multi-time founder and currently advises startups, VC firms, and larger companies on business and product strategy. In today’s episode, we discuss: • The current state of the Lean Startup methodology
guestBioOfficial.zh: 埃里克·里斯（《精益创业》方法论的创始人）

summary.en: Eric reframes the real risk of startups—not failing, but building a 'zombie' company you hate yet can't leave, and argues founders should take that seriously early. He revisits the current state of the Lean Startup movement, the misconceptions that frustrate him, and how to think correctly about MVPs, pivots, and staying the course. He also explores how AI will reshape startup product development and how to build a business whose values are aligned with human flourishing rather than extracted success.
summary.zh: Eric 重新定义了创业的真正风险——不是失败，而是打造一家你厌恶却无法离开的“僵尸”公司，并主张创始人应尽早认真对待这一点。他回顾了精益创业运动的现状、那些让他困扰的误解，以及如何正确看待 MVP、转型与坚持。他还探讨了 AI 将如何重塑创业公司的产品开发，以及如何建立一家价值观与人类福祉相统一的公司，而非靠“套现”换来的成功。

episodeTitle.en: What AI means for your product strategy | Paul Adams (CPO of Intercom)
episodeTitle.zh: 人工智能对您产品战略意味着什么？ | 保罗·亚当斯（Intercom首席产品官）

bio.en: Paul Adams is Chief Product Officer at Intercom, a role he has held for over ten years, after previously serving as global head of brand design at Facebook, a user researcher at Google, and a product designer at Dyson.
bio.zh: Paul Adams 是 Intercom 的首席产品官（CPO），担任该职务已超过十年，此前曾任 Facebook 全球品牌设计负责人、Google 用户研究员，以及 Dyson 产品设计师。

guestBioOfficial.en: Paul Adams is the longtime chief product officer at Intercom, where he leads the product management, product design, data science, and research teams. Before Intercom, Paul was the global head of brand design at Facebook, a senior user researcher at Google, and a product designer at Dyson. He’s also a best-selling author, a podcast host, and a public speaker. In today’s episode, we discuss: • Practical advice on integrating AI into your organization
guestBioOfficial.zh: 保罗·亚当斯长期担任Intercom的首席产品官，负责领导产品管理、产品设计、数据科学和研究团队。在加入Intercom之前，保罗曾担任Facebook全球品牌设计主管、谷歌高级用户研究员，以及Dyson的产品设计师。他还是畅销书作家、播客主持人和公众演说家。在本期节目中，我们将探讨：• 将人工智能融入组织的实用建议

summary.en: Paul shares candid stories of professional failure - including freezing on stage at Cannes - and argues that failure is essential experience for product leaders. He goes deep on Intercom's all-in embrace of AI, explaining why leaders must move from fear and noise to actively trying the technology, and draws parallels to the mobile shift a decade ago. The episode blends personal vulnerability with sharp advice on building craft-focused, AI-native products.
summary.zh: Paul 坦诚分享了自己职业中的失败经历——包括在戛纳演讲时当众卡壳——并主张失败是产品领导者必不可少的历练。他深入讲解了 Intercom 全面拥抱 AI 的历程，解释领导者为何必须从恐惧与喧嚣转向真正动手尝试这项技术，并与十年前的移动化浪潮作了类比。本期将个人的脆弱坦诚与关于打造注重工艺、AI 原生产品的犀利建议结合在一起。

episodeTitle.en: A step-by-step guide to crafting a sales pitch that wins | April Dunford (author of Sales Pitch)
episodeTitle.zh: 《打造致胜销售话术的分步指南 | 阿普里尔·邓福德（《销售话术》作者）》

bio.en: April Dunford is the world's foremost authority on product positioning and the bestselling author of "Obviously Awesome" and "Sales Pitch," with 25 years as a VP of marketing and advisor to companies like Google and Epic Games; she helps B2B companies translate positioning into sales stories that engage buyers, overcome indecision, and make it easier for customers to choose — and for the company to close more deals.
bio.zh: April Dunford 是全球最权威的产品定位专家、《Obviously Awesome》和《Sales Pitch》两本畅销书的作者，拥有 25 年营销 VP 和顾问经验，曾与 Google、Epic Games 等公司合作；她帮助 B2B 企业把「定位」翻译成能打动买家、克服犹豫不决的销售故事，让客户更容易做决定、也让公司显著提升销售转化。

guestBioOfficial.en: April Dunford is a speaker, mentor, podcaster, best-selling author, and beloved returning guest to the show. Last year, she joined me on the pod to discuss product positioning and differentiated value. Today, April offers invaluable insights from her latest book, Sales Pitch: How to Craft a Story to Stand Out and Win. We go deep on the art of effective pitching and selling, and April shares the specific framework she’s used to successfully pitch products at companies like Google, IBM, Postman, and Epic Games. Together we discuss: • Tactical advice on pitch creation and testing
guestBioOfficial.zh: 阿普里尔·邓福德（April Dunford）是演讲家、导师、播客主、畅销书作家，也是本节目深受欢迎的回归嘉宾。去年她做客我的播客，探讨产品定位与差异化价值。今天，阿普里尔将从她的新书《销售提案：如何打造脱颖而出的成功故事》（Sales Pitch: How to Craft a Story to Stand Out and Win）中分享宝贵见解。我们将深入探讨高效提案与销售的艺术，阿普里尔将分享她曾在谷歌、IBM、Postman和Epic Games等公司成功推销产品所运用的具体框架。我们将共同探讨：• 提案创建与测试的实用建议

summary.en: April Dunford argues that 40–60% of B2B purchases end in "no decision," not because the status quo is good enough but because stressed buyers get paralyzed by indecision and fear of screwing up. Her sales framework has two parts: a "setup" that opens with a market insight, compares the pros and cons of alternative approaches, and lands on a "perfect world" conclusion that aligns the customer with your worldview; and a "follow-through" that introduces your product, focuses on differentiated value, provides proof, handles (including silent) objections, and makes the ask. She stresses that "teaching the customer how to buy" beats piling on FOMO, because buyers need decision-making tools and reassurance they won't get fired. She also notes category creation isn't the only path to a legendary business — most companies start as a niche in an existing category (the bowling-pin strategy) — and, unlike Andy Raskin's "world shift" framework, hers keeps differentiated value at the center. Even just tightening a bad pitch has doubled deals-from-first-call for many companies within two to four weeks.
summary.zh: April Dunford 认为 40%–60% 的 B2B 采购最终「不做决定」，主因不是现状够好，而是买家在压力下「犹豫不决、怕搞砸」。她的销售框架分两块：先「铺垫」——抛出对市场的洞察、对比替代方案的优缺点、得出「完美世界」的结论让客户跟你的世界观对齐；再「跟进」——介绍自己、聚焦差异化价值、给出证据、处理（包括沉默的）异议、提出下一步。她强调「教客户怎么买」比用 FOMO 施压有效得多，因为买家真正需要的是做决定的工具和「不被炒」的安全感。她还指出，创造品类不是建传奇企业的唯一路径，多数公司从现有品类里的细分起步（保龄球瓶策略）；与 Andy Raskin 的「世界转变」框架相比，她的框架始终把「差异化价值」放在核心。哪怕只是收紧一个烂 pitch，很多公司也在两周到一个月内让从首通电话到机会的单子数翻倍。

episodeTitle.en: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)
episodeTitle.zh: 扩展Duolingo、拥抱失败及对拉丁美洲科技领域的洞察 | 吉娜·戈特利夫（Latitud，Duolingo）

bio.en: Gina Gotthilf led growth and marketing at Duolingo, helping grow it from 3 million to over 200 million users mostly through organic channels, and is now co-founder and COO of Latitude, backing the next generation of startups in Latin America.
bio.zh: Gina Gotthilf 曾在 Duolingo 负责增长与市场营销，主要通过自然增长渠道将其用户从 300 万做到超 2 亿，如今是 Latitude 的联合创始人兼 COO，致力于扶持拉丁美洲下一代科技创业公司。

summary.en: Gina shares how Duolingo grew from 3M to 200M+ users through organic and non-paid channels, and what made it one of the rare successful consumer subscription businesses—including a distinctive, quirky brand voice that makes users feel something. She stresses that communication and PR/brand are badly underrated by most startups, walks through failed experiments and biggest wins, and reflects on her time on the Mike Bloomberg presidential campaign. The conversation also covers why Latin America is an exciting startup hub right now and the idea that every life and career has an A-side and a B-side.
summary.zh: Gina 分享了 Duolingo 如何通过自然、非付费渠道从 300 万用户增长到 2 亿多，以及是什么让它成为极少数成功的消费订阅业务之一——包括独特、古怪、能让用户产生情绪的“品牌声音”。她强调沟通和 PR/品牌被大多数初创公司严重低估，逐一复盘了失败的实验与最大的胜利，并回顾了在 Mike Bloomberg 总统竞选团队的日子。对话还涵盖了为何拉美如今是令人兴奋的创业热土，以及“每个人的人生与职业都有 A 面与 B 面”的观点。

episodeTitle.en: Building beautiful products with Stripe’s Head of Design | Katie Dill (Stripe, Airbnb, Lyft)
episodeTitle.zh: 用Stripe设计总监打造精美产品 | 凯蒂·迪尔（Stripe、Airbnb、Lyft）

bio.en: Katie Dill is the Head of Design at Stripe, overseeing product design, brand, research, and design operations, and previously led design at Lyft and Airbnb.
bio.zh: 凯蒂·迪尔（Katie Dill）是 Stripe 的设计负责人，统管产品设计、品牌、用户研究与设计运营，此前曾在 Lyft 和 Airbnb 领导设计团队。

guestBioOfficial.en: Katie Dill is the Head of Design at Stripe. Previously, she was Head of Experience Design at Airbnb and Head of Design at Lyft. Katie has been named one of Business Insider’s 10 People Changing the Tech Industry as well as one of Fast Company’s 100 Most Creative People in Business and received the Girls in Tech “Creator of the Year” award. In today’s episode, she shares: • What makes a design great
guestBioOfficial.zh: 凯蒂·迪尔是Stripe的设计总监。此前，她曾担任Airbnb的体验设计主管和Lyft的设计主管。凯蒂被《商业内幕》评选为"改变科技行业的10位人物"之一，入选《快公司》"商业界最具创造力100人"榜单，并获得Girls in Tech"年度创始人"奖项。在本期节目中，她将分享：• 何为伟大的设计

summary.en: Katie makes the case that beauty and functionality are not opposites - beautiful design actually improves usability, trust, and approachability. She traces how the word "beauty" faded from digitized books as functionality became king, and why that mindset is mistaken. The episode shows how investing in craft pays off in user trust and business results.
summary.zh: 凯蒂指出，美与功能并非对立——美观的设计实际上能提升可用性、信任感与亲和力。她追溯了随着"功能为王"观念的盛行，"美"一词如何从数字化书籍中消退，并说明这种想法是错误的。本期展示了在设计工艺上的投入如何转化为用户信任与商业成果。

episodeTitle.en: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何为你的产品获取媒体关注 | 杰森·费弗（Jason Feifer，《创业家》杂志主编）

bio.en: Jason Feifer is editor-in-chief of Entrepreneur Magazine, a startup advisor, author, and podcast host who gets deeply tactical about how founders can earn press.
bio.zh: Jason Feifer 是《Entrepreneur》杂志的主编、创业顾问、作家兼播客主持人，他非常具体地讲解创始人如何获得媒体曝光。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jason Feifer is the editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine and a former editor at Fast Company. He’s also a podcast host, book author, keynote speaker, and startup advisor. Every week, he shares tips in his newsletter, One Thing Better, to help people become happier and more effective at work. In today’s episode, Jason draws upon his wealth of experience in media to share tactical insights on how to get press coverage. We discuss: • High-level steps to securing press coverage for your product
guestBioOfficial.zh: 杰森·费弗是《创业家》杂志的主编，也是《快公司》的前编辑。他还是播客主持人、书籍作者、主题演讲者和创业顾问。每周，他都会在自己的时事通讯《One Thing Better》中分享小贴士，帮助人们在工作中变得更快乐、更高效。在今天的节目中，杰森凭借其丰富的媒体经验，分享了如何获得媒体报道的实用见解。我们讨论了： • 确保产品获得媒体报道的高级步骤

summary.en: Jason reframes the journalist's mindset: editors and writers don't care about you, they care about their audience—so pitch how you can help them serve readers, not as a service provider. He covers how to find and pitch the right journalist (freelancers are often more responsive), why a publication's mission must shape your pitch, which channels to use to reach out, and how to define what success from press actually looks like. It's a pragmatic, no-nonsense guide to getting coverage for your product.
summary.zh: Jason 重新框定了记者的心态：编辑和记者不在乎你，他们在乎的是读者——所以你的 pitch 要说明你能如何帮他们服务读者，而不是把他们当服务商。他讲了如何找到并对正确的记者出手（自由撰稿人往往更积极）、为何媒体的使命必须塑造你的 pitch、用哪些渠道去联系，以及如何定义“拿到曝光”真正的成功标准。这期节目是关于为产品争取报道的务实、去水分的指南。

episodeTitle.en: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)
episodeTitle.zh: 《Linear内参：用品味、工艺与专注打造设计》|卡里·萨里宁（联合创始人、设计总监、CEO）

bio.en: Karri Saarinen is the co-founder and CEO of Linear, one of the most beloved issue-tracking tools for software teams, and was previously founding designer at Coinbase and principal designer at Airbnb.
bio.zh: 卡里·萨里宁（Karri Saarinen）是 Linear 的联合创始人兼 CEO，该产品是软件团队中最受青睐的任务追踪工具之一；他此前是 Coinbase 的创始设计师、Airbnb 的首席设计师。

guestBioOfficial.en: Karri Saarinen is the co-founder and CEO of Linear, an issue-tracking tool that has quickly become the fastest-growing and most beloved in the world. Before Linear, Karri was the principal designer and co-creator of design systems at Airbnb and the founding designer at Coinbase. In today’s episode, he shares: • How to prioritize craft in product development
guestBioOfficial.zh: 卡里·萨里宁是Linear的联合创始人兼CEO。Linear是一款issue-tracking工具，已迅速成为全球增长最快、最受欢迎的同类产品。在创立Linear之前，卡里曾担任Airbnb的首席设计师和设计系统共同开发者，以及Coinbase的创始设计师。在本期节目中，他将分享：• 如何在产品开发中优先考虑工艺

summary.en: Karri argues that as a product category matures, design quality becomes a basic price of entry rather than a differentiator. He describes how Linear builds with extreme focus on craft, speed, and a small, high-agency team. The episode is a master class in building a fast, opinionated, design-led company.
summary.zh: 卡里认为，随着某个产品品类走向成熟，设计质量会从"差异化优势"变成"入场的基本门槛"。他讲述了 Linear 如何通过极度聚焦工艺、速度和一支小型高自驱团队来打造产品。本期堪称构建一家快速、有主张、以设计驱动的公司的大师课。

episodeTitle.en: Brian Balfour: 10 lessons on career, growth, and life
episodeTitle.zh: 布莱恩·巴尔弗：关于职业、成长和生活的10个经验

bio.en: Brian Balfour is the founder and CEO of Reforge, formerly Head of Growth at HubSpot, who has lived through the rise and fall of every major distribution channel and now predicts a new AI-era distribution platform (likely ChatGPT) will open up within months.
bio.zh: Brian Balfour 是 Reforge 的创始人兼 CEO，曾任 HubSpot 增长负责人。他亲历了每个主要分发渠道的兴衰，现在预言一个 AI 时代的新分发平台（很可能是 ChatGPT）会在几个月内打开。

guestBioOfficial.en: Brian Balfour is the founder and CEO of Reforge. Prior to Reforge, he was the VP of Growth at HubSpot and co-founded three other startups. In today’s episode, Brian shares 10 lessons from his career, growth, and life: • Lesson 1: Inspect the work, not the person.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 布莱恩·巴尔弗是Reforge的创始人兼首席执行官。在Reforge之前，他曾担任HubSpot的增长副总裁，并联合创办了其他三家初创公司。在今天的节目中，布莱恩分享了他职业生涯、成长和生活的10个经验： • 经验1：检查工作，而不是人。

summary.en: Brian Balfour argues a new distribution platform is emerging from the AI shift and will follow a predictable four-step cycle: market consensus (Step 0), a player identifies a moat (Step 1), the platform opens to third parties with a value exchange (Step 2), then closes to monetize and control (Step 3). He predicts ChatGPT is best positioned because of its lead in retention, engagement, and context/memory, and warns the cycle is shortening—so startups must play early and place a focused bet rather than opting out. He also shares what separates companies winning at AI adoption: hard constraints, exiting 'anchors,' and attacking the slowest part of the system.
summary.zh: Brian Balfour 主张一个新分发平台正从 AI 转变中出现，并会遵循可预测的四步周期：市场共识（第0步）、某个玩家识别出护城河（第1步）、平台以价值交换向第三方开放（第2步）、然后为变现和控制而关闭（第3步）。他预测 ChatGPT 位置最好，因其在留存、互动和上下文/记忆上的领先，并警告周期在缩短——所以初创必须早早参与、下聚焦的注，而非退出。他还分享了在 AI 采用上赢的公司之别：硬约束、退出“锚”、以及攻击系统最慢的部分。

episodeTitle.en: What sets great teams apart | Lane Shackleton (CPO of Coda)
episodeTitle.zh: 《卓越团队的秘诀》 | 莱恩·沙克尔顿（Coda首席产品官）

bio.en: Lane Shackleton is the Chief Product Officer at Coda, where he has led product for over eight years, and previously was a Group Product Manager at YouTube.
bio.zh: 莱恩·沙克尔顿（Lane Shackleton）是 Coda 的首席产品官，已在产品岗位深耕八年多，此前是 YouTube 的产品组经理。

guestBioOfficial.en: Lane Shackleton is CPO of Coda, where he’s been leading the product and design team for over eight years. Lane started his career as an Alaskan climbing guide and then as a manual reviewer of AdWords ads before becoming a product specialist at Google and later a Group PM at YouTube. He also writes a weekly newsletter with insights and rituals for PMs, product teams, and startups. In today’s conversation, we discuss: • Principles that set great PMs apart
guestBioOfficial.zh: 莱恩·沙克尔顿是Coda的首席产品官，已在该公司领导产品与设计团队逾八年。他职业生涯始于阿拉斯加登山向导，随后担任AdWords广告手动审核员，之后在谷歌担任产品专员，之后又在YouTube担任集团产品经理。他还每周撰写一篇通讯，为产品经理、产品团队和初创公司提供见解与实践。在今日对话中，我们将探讨：• 卓越产品经理的核心原则

summary.en: Lane argues you should actively seek "oh shit" moments - situations where you feel unqualified - because that's where real growth happens. He reframes the common "are you growing?" question into "how many stretch moments have you had lately?" The episode offers career advice on leaning into discomfort and building a foundation for the next level.
summary.zh: 莱恩认为，你应当主动去寻找"糟了"时刻——那些让你觉得自己不够格的处境——因为真正的成长就在那里发生。他把常见的"你在成长吗？"这个问题，重构为"最近你经历了多少次被拉伸的时刻？"。本期提供了关于拥抱不适感、为下一阶段打下基础的职业建议。

episodeTitle.en: Building Anchor, selling to Spotify, and lessons learned | Maya Prohovnik (Head of Podcast Product)
episodeTitle.zh: 构建锚点、向Spotify出售产品及经验教训 | 玛雅·普罗霍夫尼克（Maya Prohovnik，Podcast产品负责人）

bio.en: Maya Prohovnik was Spotify's Head of Product for podcasting, where she oversaw the product that powered Anchor's rapid hosting growth.
bio.zh: 玛雅·普罗霍夫尼克（Maya Prohovnik）曾任 Spotify 的播客产品负责人，主管驱动 Anchor 快速获取托管市场份额的产品。

guestBioOfficial.en: Maya Prohovnik is currently Spotify’s Head of Podcast Product. She was employee #1 at Anchor, which was acquired by Spotify in 2019 and now powers more than 80% of all new podcasts created in the world. In 2023, Maya was named one of the Most Important People in Podcasting by The Hollywood Reporter. In today’s episode, we discuss:• How Maya operationalizes “dogfooding”• How to balance data-driven decision-making and intuition• Strategies for preserving startup culture in a large organization• Tactical tips to improve at public speaking• How Radical Candor and the Eisenhower matrix transformed her approach to managing people• What’s next at Spotify for Podcasters
guestBioOfficial.zh: 玛雅·普罗霍夫尼克目前是Spotify的Podcast产品负责人。她曾是Anchor的首位员工，Anchor于2019年被Spotify收购，如今为全球80%以上新创播客提供支持。2023年，玛雅被《好莱坞报道》评为播客界最重要人物之一。在本期节目中，我们探讨了：• 玛雅如何实践“自我反馈”模式   • 如何平衡数据驱动决策与直觉   • 在大组织中保留创业文化的策略   • 提升公开演讲技巧的实用技巧   • 激进坦诚和艾森豪威尔矩阵如何改变她的管理方式   • Spotify面向播客创作者的未来规划

summary.en: Maya recounts how the team obsessively reduced friction by quietly having interns manually submit podcasts to Apple behind the scenes, creating a magical one-click experience. She explains this scrappy approach is what drove Anchor's explosive market-share growth. The episode is a lesson in hiding complexity to deliver seeming simplicity at scale.
summary.zh: 玛雅讲述团队如何痴迷于降低摩擦——悄悄让实习生在后台手动把播客提交到 Apple，从而造出"一键发布"的魔法体验。她说明，正是这种灵活务实的做法推动了 Anchor 托管市场份额的爆发式增长。本期是关于"隐藏复杂性、在规模上交付看似简单"的一课。

episodeTitle.en: How to drive word of mouth | Nilan Peiris (CPO of Wise)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何驱动口碑传播 | 尼兰·皮里斯（Nilan Peiris，Wise首席产品官）

bio.en: Welcome to Lenny's Podcast, where I interview world-class product leaders and growth experts to learn from their hard won experiences building and growing today's most successful products. Today my guest is Nilan Peiris. Nilan is chief product Officer at Wise, where he has been for over 11 years, ba
bio.zh: 欢迎来到Lenny的播客，我在节目中采访世界级的产品领袖和增长专家，从他们宝贵的经验中学习如何打造和发展当今最成功的产品。今天的嘉宾是Nilan Peiris。Nilan是Wise公司的首席产品官，他在Wise任职已有11年之久，

guestBioOfficial.en: Nilan Peiris is Chief Product Officer at Wise, one of the fastest-growing (and profitable) tech companies in the world.
