Wise allows anyone to send money in more than 60 currencies to over 160 countries at low cost, and throughout its history has grown primarily through word of mouth. In today’s episode, we discuss: • Tactical advice on driving word of mouth (WOM)
guestBioOfficial.zh: 尼兰·皮里斯（Nilan Peiris）是Wise的首席产品官，Wise是全球增长最快（且盈利）的科技公司之一。Wise允许用户以低成本向全球160多个国家汇款，并主要通过口碑传播实现用户增长。在本期节目中，我们将探讨：• 推动口碑传播的实用建议（WOM）

summary.en: Some people focus on conversion rate, like, "I'm going to make this really, really slick." And that's cool. You get a bit more growth. But to get to recommendation, you're going to blow your user socks off. You have to give them an experience they didn't know was previously possible. And when you are in that place of d
summary.zh: 有些人专注于转化率，比如“我要把产品做得超级流畅”。这很棒，你能获得一些增长。但要实现推荐，你需要让用户惊叹不已。你必须为他们提供前所未有的体验。当你达到这种境界时，

episodeTitle.en: Becoming evidence-guided | Itamar Gilad (Gmail, YouTube, Microsoft)
episodeTitle.zh: 以证据为导向 | 伊塔马尔·吉拉德（曾任谷歌、微软等公司产品高管）

bio.en: Itamar Gilad is a product coach, author, and former longtime Google product manager (Gmail, identity, YouTube) who just published Evidence-Guided: Creating High-Impact Products in the Face of Uncertainty.
bio.zh: Itamar Gilad 是一位产品教练、作家，也是谷歌的长期产品经理（Gmail、账号体系、YouTube），他刚出版了《Evidence-Guided: Creating High-Impact Products in the Face of Uncertainty》。

guestBioOfficial.en: Itamar Gilad is a product coach, author, and speaker with over two decades of experience in senior product roles at Google, Microsoft, and various startups. He is also the author of Evidence-Guided: Creating High-Impact Products in the Face of Uncertainty and publishes a popular product management newsletter. In today’s episode, we discuss: • What it means to be “evidence-guided”
guestBioOfficial.zh: 伊塔马尔·吉拉德是一位拥有二十多年产品管理经验的产品教练、作家和演讲者。他曾在谷歌、微软等公司担任高级产品职位，并著有《以证据为导向：在不确定性中创造高影响力产品》一书，还运营着广受欢迎的产品管理通讯。在本期节目中，我们将探讨：• “以证据为导向”的含义

summary.en: Itamar makes the case for moving teams from opinion-based to evidence-guided decision-making, and shares practical frameworks to do it: the confidence meter, metrics trees, GIST and the GIST board, and a critique of how people mis-use ICE for prioritization. He also covers how to run effective fake-door and Wizard-of-Oz tests (including how the tabbed Gmail inbox started as a facade), and how to make OKRs actually useful. The episode is a toolkit for building high-impact products under uncertainty.
summary.zh: Itamar 主张把团队从“基于观点”的决策转向“基于证据”的决策，并分享了实现它的实用框架：信心计量表（confidence meter）、指标树（metrics trees）、GIST 与 GIST 看板，以及对人们如何误用 ICE 做优先级排序的批评。他还讲了如何运行有效的“假门测试”和“绿野仙踪测试”（包括 Gmail 的分页收件箱最初只是一个 facade），以及如何让 OKR 真正有用。这期节目是在不确定性下打造高影响力产品的工具箱。

episodeTitle.en: How to become a category pirate | Christopher Lochhead (Author of Play Bigger, Niche Down, more)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何成为品类海盗 | 克里斯托弗·洛克黑德（《放大格局、深耕细分》等书作者）

bio.en: Christopher Lochhead is a three-time public company CMO, advisor to 50+ venture-backed startups, and the "Godfather of Category Design" — a 13-time number-one bestselling co-author (Play Bigger, Niche Down, The 22 Laws of Category Design) and co-creator of the Substack Category Pirates.
bio.zh: Christopher Lochhead 是一位三度任职上市公司 CMO、50 多家风投初创的顾问，以及"品类设计教父"——13 次登上榜首的畅销书合著者（《Play Bigger》《Niche Down》《品类设计 22 律》）和 Substack《Category Pirates》的联合创作者。

guestBioOfficial.en: Christopher Lochhead is a 14-time #1 bestselling author, top podcaster, and former 3x public tech company CMO and has been an advisor to over 50 VC-backed tech startups. He is best known as a “godfather” of category design, and Adobe named his book Play Bigger one of “the five greatest marketing books of all time.” In this episode, we discuss:• What exactly category design is • The “Frame It, Name It, Claim It” framework
guestBioOfficial.zh: 克里斯托弗·洛克黑德是14次头号畅销书作家、顶级播客主，并曾担任三家上市科技公司的首席营销官，还为50多家风投支持的科技初创公司提供过咨询服务。他被誉为"品类设计教父"，Adobe将他的《放大格局》一书列为"史上五大营销书籍之一"。在本期节目中，我们将探讨：• 品类设计究竟是什么？ • "框定、命名、主张"框架

summary.en: Christopher makes the case that legendary companies design new categories rather than compete in existing ones: in tech categories, one company captures ~two-thirds of the total value, so competing means fighting for the remaining 24%. He explains category design as framing, naming, and claiming a problem (not just shipping a "better" product), and warns the "better trap" (Threads, Amazon Fire Phone, Red Bull Cola) fails because problems create categories, not vice versa. Practical tools include backcasting (envision the future, then work backward), "reject the premise," strategic languaging (e.g., Otis's "vertical railway," Starbucks's new vocabulary, OpenAI's "LLM"), targeting super-consumers, and the lightning-strike model of marketing powered by word of mouth. He also argues positioning and "product market fit" are dangerously incremental mind-sets.
summary.zh: Christopher 提出论点：传奇公司设计新品类、而不是在已有品类里竞争——在科技品类里，一家公司拿走总价值约三分之二，所以竞争意味着为剩下 24% 打架。他把品类设计解释为框定、命名并主张一个问题（不只是发布一个"更好"的产品），并警告"更好"陷阱（Threads、Amazon Fire Phone、Red Bull Cola）会失败，因为问题造就品类，而非反过来。实用工具包括 backcasting（构想未来再倒推）、"reject the premise"、战略性语言化（如 Otis 的"垂直铁路"、星巴克的新词汇、OpenAI 的"LLM"）、瞄准超级消费者，以及由口碑驱动的闪电袭击营销模型。他还主张定位和"产品市场契合"是危险的渐进式思维。

episodeTitle.en: Picking sharp problems, increasing virality, and unique product frameworks | Oji Udezue (Typeform)
episodeTitle.zh: 精准定位痛点、提升病毒式传播和独特的产品框架 | 奥吉·乌德祖（Typeform）

bio.en: Oji Udezue is Chief Product Officer at Typeform and a veteran product and growth leader who has built and scaled products at Microsoft, Atlassian, Calendly, and Twitter.
bio.zh: Oji Udezue 是 Typeform 的首席产品官（CPO），也是一位资深的产品与增长领袖，曾在 Microsoft、Atlassian、Calendly 和 Twitter 打造并扩展产品。

guestBioOfficial.en: Oji Udezue is Chief Product Officer at Typeform and has held leadership roles at Twitter (Head of Product for Creation and Conversation), Calendly (CPO), and Atlassian (Head of Product for communication tools). He is well-known for bringing a product-led-growth (PLG) mindset to the companies he joins. Additionally, Oji mentors startups, is a Managing Partner at the Kernel Fund, and writes online about product management. In this episode, we discuss: • Oji’s “Where to Fish to Land a Unicorn” and “Zone of Benefit” frameworks
guestBioOfficial.zh: 奥吉·乌德祖是Typeform的首席产品官，曾在Twitter（产品创造与对话部门主管）、Calendly（首席产品官）和Atlassian（通信工具部门主管）担任领导职务。他以将产品主导增长（PLG）思维引入所加入的公司而闻名。此外，奥吉还为初创公司提供指导，是Kernel Fund的管理合伙人，并在网上撰写产品管理相关的文章。在本期节目中，我们探讨了：• 奥吉的“在何处垂钓以捕获独角兽”和“效益区”框架

summary.en: Oji presents frameworks for finding big B2B SaaS ideas by targeting high-frequency, broad workflows, and introduces the 'zone of benefit' concept that a solution must be roughly 3x better than the status quo to win. He discusses how to identify your ideal customer profile and how companies can navigate from low-frequency niches toward category-leading positions. The conversation draws on his rare cross-company perspective on what actually drives product and growth.
summary.zh: Oji 提出了一套寻找大型 B2B SaaS 创意的框架——瞄准高频、广覆盖的工作流，并引入了“收益区间（zone of benefit）”的概念：解决方案必须比现状好大约 3 倍才能取胜。他讨论了如何识别理想客户画像（ICP），以及企业如何从低频小众定位逐步迈向品类领先。对话依托他在多家不同公司的罕见跨视角，剖析了究竟是什么真正驱动产品与增长。

episodeTitle.en: When enough is enough | Andy Johns (ex-FB, Twitter, Quora)
episodeTitle.zh: 当适可而止时 | 安迪·约翰斯（前Facebook、Twitter、Quora员工）

bio.en: Andy Johns is a former legendary growth leader at Facebook, Twitter, Quora, and Wealthfront who left a path to CEO to become a mental-health advocate helping burned-out high achievers and veterans.
bio.zh: Andy Johns 曾是 Facebook、Twitter、Quora 和 Wealthfront 的传奇增长负责人，他放弃了成为 CEO 的职业路径，转而成为心理健康倡导者，帮助精疲力竭的高成就者和退伍军人。

guestBioOfficial.en: Andy Johns is a former tech exec and VC who had a successful run at several startups—including Facebook, Twitter, Wealthfront, and Quora—but left it all behind a few years ago to take a new direction in life. Now a mental health advocate, he aids military veterans with PTSD, guides burnt-out high achievers to new paths, and shares his healing journey from childhood trauma and mental illness through his newsletter, Clues Dot Life. In this episode, we discuss: • Why Andy left his seven-figure VC career behind
guestBioOfficial.zh: 安迪·约翰斯曾是科技高管和风险投资人，曾在Facebook、Twitter、Wealthfront和Quora等多家初创公司成功任职，但几年前他放下一切，转向了新的人生方向。如今，作为心理健康倡导者，他帮助患有创伤后应激障碍的退伍军人，引导精疲力竭的成功人士走上新道路，并通过他的新闻通讯《Clues Dot Life》分享自己从童年创伤和心理疾病中康复的治愈之旅。在本期节目中，我们讨论了：• 安迪为何放弃七位数的风险投资事业

summary.en: Andy shares his personal story of burnout and transformation, explaining the physical and behavioral signals—sleep, relationships, health—that act as flashing red alarms for wellbeing. He lays out a four-step process for making lasting change and how to actually allow that change to happen in your life. The conversation is a candid, real-talk episode on mental health, burnout, and reclaiming your path in and beyond tech.
summary.zh: Andy 分享了自己倦怠与转变的个人故事，讲解了睡眠、人际关系、健康等作为身心健康“红色警报”的生理与行为信号。他给出了实现持久改变的四步法，以及如何真正让改变在自己身上发生。这期对话坦诚直白，聚焦心理健康、倦怠，以及在科技行业内外重新找回人生方向。

episodeTitle.en: An inside look at Figma’s unique GTM motion | Claire Butler (first GTM hire)
episodeTitle.zh: Figma独特的GTM策略解析 | 克莱尔·巴特勒（首位GTM成员）

bio.en: Claire Butler was Figma's 10th employee and first marketing hire, leading its original launch, go-to-market, branding, and positioning, and continues to lead go-to-market and bottom-up growth.
bio.zh: Claire Butler 是 Figma 的第 10 号员工和首位营销员工，领导了其最初发布、进入市场、品牌与定位，并持续负责进入市场与自下而上的增长。

guestBioOfficial.en: Claire Butler was Figma’s first GTM hire and their 10th employee. She led Figma’s early GTM strategy from stealth through monetization. She also helped the team through the journey to find product-market fit and built the team that drove Figma’s unique bottom-up growth motion. Eight years later, as Senior Director of Marketing, she continues to lead Figma’s bottom-up growth motion, along with community, events, social, advocacy, and Figma for education. In this episode, we discuss: • An in-depth look at Figma’s bottom-up GTM motion
guestBioOfficial.zh: 克莱尔·巴特勒是Figma的首位GTM成员，也是公司的第十位员工。她主导了Figma从隐形到变现的早期GTM战略，并帮助团队找到产品与市场的契合点，并组建了推动Figma独特自下而上增长策略的团队。八年后，作为高级营销总监，她继续领导Figma的自下而上增长战略，同时负责社区、活动、社交媒体、客户推广和Figma教育项目。在本期节目中，我们将探讨：• Figma自下而上的GTM策略深度解析

summary.en: Claire gives the first in-depth look at how Figma grew and continues to grow, sharing a two-part go-to-market strategy: winning individual contributors' love, then enabling them to spread the product internally. She offers vivid stories from executing that strategy and how other teams can apply it. The conversation is dense with go-to-market wisdom for bottom-up, IC-led products.
summary.zh: Claire 首次深入展示了 Figma 如何增长并持续增长的：她分享了两步进入市场策略——先赢得个人贡献者（IC）的喜爱，再让他们在组织内自发传播产品。她用生动故事讲述了执行该策略的过程，以及其他团队如何借鉴。对话充满了针对自下而上、由 IC 驱动产品的市场进入智慧。

episodeTitle.en: Inside Etsy’s product, growth, and marketplace evolution | Tim Holley (VP of Product)
episodeTitle.zh: Etsy产品、增长与市场演进之路 | 蒂姆·霍利（VP of Product）

bio.en: Tim Holley is VP of Product at Etsy, where over 10+ years he helped grow GMV from around $500 million to over $13 billion.
bio.zh: Tim Holley 是 Etsy 的产品副总裁，在逾十年的时间里，他帮助该公司将 GMV（成交额）从约 5 亿美元增长到超过 130 亿美元。

guestBioOfficial.en: Tim Holley is VP of Product at Etsy where he leads the Etsy buyer experience. With a tenure spanning more than a decade, Tim has seen the company through many transitions (both in culture, in leadership, and in growth), and his team’s product changes have had a significant impact on buyer retention, conversion, and global expansion. In this episode, we discuss: • Lessons from navigating corporate culture shifts
guestBioOfficial.zh: 蒂姆·霍利（Tim Holley）是Etsy的VP of Product，负责领导Etsy买家体验部门。凭借十余年的从业经验，蒂姆见证了公司在文化、领导层及增长方面的诸多变革，其团队的产品创新对买家留存、转化率及全球扩张产生了重大影响。在本期节目中，我们将探讨：•从企业文化变革中吸取的经验教训

summary.en: Tim shares the big cultural transition Etsy went through as it scaled, and the product and marketplace moves that drove its growth from $500M to $13B+ in GMV. He discusses how to change internal culture, where to find leverage in a two-sided marketplace, and advice for anyone working on marketplaces or seeking growth ideas. The episode is a rare inside look at scaling one of the world's most distinctive marketplaces.
summary.zh: Tim 分享了 Etsy 在规模化过程中经历的重大文化转型，以及推动其 GMV 从 5 亿增长到 130 多亿美元的产品与市场动作。他讨论了如何改变内部文化、在双边市场中何处寻找杠杆，以及给所有做市场平台或寻求增长思路之人的建议。本期是对规模化全球最具特色市场平台之一的罕见内部透视。

episodeTitle.en: An inside look at Deel’s unprecedented growth | Meltem Kuran Berkowitz (Head of Growth)
episodeTitle.zh: Deel前所未有的增长内幕 | 梅尔特姆·库兰·伯科维茨（Meltem Kuran Berkowitz，增长部门负责人）

bio.en: Welcome to Lenny's Podcast where I interview world-class product leaders and growth experts to learn from their hard won experiences building and growing today's most successful products. Today my guest is Meltem Kuran Berkowitz. Meltem is head of growth at Deel, which is arguably the fastest growin
bio.zh: 欢迎来到 Lenny 的播客，在这里我会采访世界一流的产品负责人和增长专家，从他们打造和增长当今最成功产品的亲身经历中学习。今天的嘉宾是 Meltem Kuran Berkowitz。Meltem 是 Deel 的增长负责人，Deel 可以说是有史以来增长最快

guestBioOfficial.en: Meltem Kuran Berkowitz is Head of Growth at Deel, which went from $0 to $300m in ARR in 3 years (fastest company in history to do so). Meltem joined Deel early to lead growth, and currently leads all of the growth and marketing teams including paid ads, content, product marketing, community, brand, and more. In this episode, we discuss: • How Deel found success leveraging low-cost growth channels
guestBioOfficial.zh:
梅尔特姆·库兰·伯科维茨是Deel的增长部门负责人。Deel在三年内将年经常性收入从0提升至3亿美元（创下史上最快达成这一里程碑的公司）。梅尔特姆早期加入Deel，主导增长战略，目前负责所有增长与营销团队，包括付费广告、内容、产品营销、社区、品牌等。在本期节目中，我们探讨了：  
• Deel如何通过低成本增长渠道取得成功

summary.en: ... early days, it's very important to just go back to the basics, build the skeleton before you put on the makeup. So the first question I would ask is, do you have a website? episodeTitle.en: The ultimate guide to JTBD | Bob Moesta (co-creator of the framework)
episodeTitle.zh: JTBD终极指南 | 鲍勃·莫埃斯塔（Bob Moesta，JTBD框架共同创始人）

bio.en: Bob Moesta is co-creator of the Jobs-to-be-Done framework alongside Clay Christensen and founder/CEO of the Rewired Group, helping companies unlock hidden insights to build successful products.
bio.zh: Bob Moesta 是与 Clay Christensen 共同创立“待办任务”（Jobs-to-be-Done）框架的人，也是 Rewired Group 的创始人兼 CEO，帮助企业发掘隐藏洞察以打造成功产品。

guestBioOfficial.en: Bob Moesta is the co-creator of the Jobs To Be Done (JTBD) framework, a close collaborator of Clay Christensen, and CEO and founder of The Re-Wired Group. He has helped launch more than 3,500 new products, services, and businesses and built and sold several startups himself. He is also a fellow at the Clayton Christensen Institute and a guest lecturer at the Harvard Business School, MIT Sloan School of Entrepreneurship, and Northwestern University’s Kellogg School of Management. In this episode, we discuss: • What Snickers and Milky Way can teach us about JTBD
guestBioOfficial.zh: 鲍勃·莫埃斯塔（Bob Moesta）是Jobs To Be Done（JTBD）框架的共同创始人，也是克莱·克里斯滕森（Clay Christensen）的亲密合作伙伴，同时担任The Re-Wired Group的首席执行官兼创始人。他曾助力推出3500余款新产品、新服务和新业务，并亲自创立多家初创公司。除此之外，他还是克莱顿·克里斯滕森研究所的研究员，并在哈佛商学院、麻省理工学院斯隆商学院和西北大学凯洛格商学院担任客座讲师。本期节目讨论议题：• 士力架和Milky Way巧克力能为我们揭示JTBD的哪些奥秘

summary.en: Bob clarifies a core misconception: Jobs-to-be-Done is about context and outcome, not pain versus gain—the context is what makes seemingly irrational behavior rational. He explains how to interview customers to surface the real struggles behind a switch and when the framework is and isn't a good fit. The conversation includes concrete examples of applying JTBD to both zero-to-one and existing products.
summary.zh: Bob 澄清了一个核心误解：待办任务关注的是“情境与结果”，而非“痛苦与收益”——正是情境让看似非理性的行为变得合理。他解释了如何通过访谈客户来挖掘其转换背后的真实挣扎，以及框架何时适用、何时不适用。对话包含了将 JTBD 应用于从 0 到 1 及既有产品的具体例子。

episodeTitle.en: Monetizing passions, scaling marketplaces, and stories from a creator economy vet | Camille Hearst
episodeTitle.zh: 在创作者经济中的先驱：如何将激情变现、扩展市场平台以及分享故事 | 卡米尔·赫斯特

bio.en: Camille Hearst is Head of Fan Monetization at Spotify, previously Head of Product for Creators at Patreon, product marketing manager at YouTube, and the second PM on iTunes, with a background as a founder.
bio.zh: Camille Hearst 是 Spotify 粉丝变现负责人，此前曾任 Patreon 创作者产品负责人、YouTube 产品营销经理，以及 iTunes 第二位产品经理，并有创始人经历。

guestBioOfficial.en: Camille Hearst is Head of Fan Monetization at Spotify, where she finds new ways for fans to connect and for artists to monetize. Previously she was Head of Product for Creators at Patreon, Product Marketing Manager at YouTube, the second Product Manager at iTunes, and VP of Product at Hailo. She also co-founded a company called Kit, which was acquired by Patreon in 2018. In today’s podcast, we discuss: • Advice on building a successful career as a creator
guestBioOfficial.zh: 卡米尔·赫斯特（Camille Hearst）是Spotify粉丝变现部门的负责人，她致力于为粉丝创造新的互动方式，并助力艺术家实现商业化。此前，她曾担任Patreon创作者产品负责人、YouTube产品营销经理、iTunes第二任产品经理，以及Hailo产品副总裁。她还联合创立了名为Kit的公司，该公司于2018年被Patreon收购。在今天的播客中，我们将探讨：• 关于如何打造成功创作者职业生涯的建议

summary.en: Camille shares lessons from building creator and fan-monetization products across Apple, YouTube, Patreon, and Spotify, and the importance of content-market fit alongside product-market fit. She discusses what she learned sitting next to Elon Musk at early Tesla and how to think about audiences' deeper needs. The conversation is geared toward anyone building creator- or community-oriented products.
summary.zh: Camille 分享了在 Apple、YouTube、Patreon 和 Spotify 打造创作者与粉丝变现产品的经验，以及“内容市场匹配”与“产品市场匹配”同等重要。她讲述了在早期 Tesla 紧邻 Elon Musk 工作的所学，以及如何思考受众的深层需求。对话面向所有打造创作者或社区向产品的人。

episodeTitle.en: The ultimate guide to Martech | Austin Hay (Reforge, Ramp, Runway)
episodeTitle.zh: 营销科技终极指南 | 奥斯汀·海（Austin Hay，Reforge、Ramp、Runway）

bio.en: Austin Hay is the Head of Marketing Technology at Ramp and a MarTech advisor to companies like Notion, Airbnb, and Walmart, who was the fourth employee at Branch Metrics and teaches Marketing Technology at Reforge.
bio.zh: Austin Hay是Ramp的营销技术负责人，曾是独角兽公司Branch Metrics的第4号员工，并为Notion、Airbnb、Walmart等公司提供MarTech战略顾问，同时在Reforge开设营销技术课程。

guestBioOfficial.en: Austin Hay is currently Head of Marketing Technology at Ramp and was previously the VP of Business Operations at Runway, the VP of Growth at mParticle, and the fourth employee at the unicorn Branch Metrics. In 2022 he sold his online course, the Marketing Technology Academy, to Reforge, where he now teaches Martech and has a program launching in the fall. He’s consulted on Martech and growth for companies including Notion, Airbnb, Robinhood, Postmates, Walmart, JPMorgan Chase, and many others. In today’s podcast, we discuss: • What exactly marketing technology is
guestBioOfficial.zh:
奥斯汀·海（Austin Hay）目前担任Ramp公司的营销技术部门主管，此前曾在Runway担任业务运营副总裁，在mParticle担任增长副总裁，并是独角兽公司Branch Metrics的第四位员工。2022年，他将自己的在线课程"营销技术学院"出售给Reforge，现在他在Reforge教授营销技术，并将于今年秋季推出新课程。他还为Notion、Airbnb、Robinhood、Postmates、沃尔玛、摩根大通等公司提供营销技术和增长策略咨询。在本期播客中，我们将探讨：  
• 营销技术究竟是什么？

summary.en: Austin Hay breaks down MarTech as the discipline of using technology and tools to drive growth, sitting at the intersection of product, growth, engineering, and marketing. He explains when to hire a dedicated MarTech person (typically around 100-150 employees, when a "village" approach to tools no longer scales) and what to look for: intellectual curiosity, scrappy engineering skills, and cross-functional influence. The conversation covers modern tool stacks for B2C (CDP to warehouse to reverse ETL) and B2B (Salesforce-centric), the shift from deterministic to probabilistic attribution after IDFA and cookie deprecation, and practical frameworks like "tools are meant to solve problems" and "think gray." Austin shares his recommended Golden Stack for both B2C and B2B businesses and his favorite interview questions for hiring MarTech talent.
summary.zh: Austin Hay把MarTech定义为"用技术和工具驱动增长"的学科，它处在产品、增长、工程和营销的交叉地带。他讲清楚了什么时候该招一个专职的MarTech人员——通常是公司到100到150人、靠"群策群力"管工具已经玩不转的时候——以及该看什么特质：求知欲、动手能力强的工程技能，还有跨部门的推动影响力。对话覆盖了B2C（CDP→数据仓库→反向ETL）和B2B（以Salesforce为核心）的现代工具栈、在IDFA和Cookie退场之后归因从"确定性"转向"概率性"的变化，以及"工具是为了解决问题""灰色思考"等实用框架。Austin还分享了他为B2C和B2B分别推荐的"黄金工具栈"，以及招聘MarTech人才时他最爱问的面试题。

episodeTitle.en: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Chris Miller
episodeTitle.zh: 永不止息的好奇心、彻底的责任感，以及HubSpot的制胜增长公式 | 克里斯·米勒

bio.en: Chris Miller is VP of Product for Growth and AI at HubSpot, where he helped create the company's early growth team and turned it into one of the most successful product-led growth businesses in history.
bio.zh: Chris Miller 是 HubSpot 增长与 AI 产品副总裁，他曾帮助创建公司的早期增长团队，并将其打造成史上最成功的产品驱动增长业务之一。

guestBioOfficial.en: Christopher Miller serves as the VP of Product for Growth and AI at HubSpot. Having spent the past seven years at HubSpot, Chris has been at the center of one of the biggest B2B growth stories in history—leading HubSpot’s early growth strategy, their shift to PLG, and now their investment in AI. Beyond his role at HubSpot, he lends his expertise to founders advising them on PLG and their growth strategy broadly. In today’s podcast, we discuss: • The principles of winning teams, careers, and companies
guestBioOfficial.zh: 克里斯·米勒现任HubSpot增长与AI产品副总裁。在HubSpot工作的过去七年里，克里斯始终处于B2B增长史上最传奇篇章的核心人物——他主导了HubSpot的早期增长战略、向PLG模式的转型，以及如今对AI的投资。除HubSpot的角色外，他还为初创企业提供咨询服务，助力他们制定PLG策略和整体增长战略。在本期播客中，我们将探讨：• 成功团队、职业生涯和公司的核心原则

summary.en: Chris covers what it takes to become a successful product leader, the skills the best PMs build, and how to find mentors early in your career. He emphasizes radical ownership and accountability—treating every problem as yours—as the mindset that helped HubSpot's growth team find opportunities others missed. The conversation also stresses why early PMs must “scrape their knees” to learn.
summary.zh: Chris 涵盖了成为成功产品领导者需要什么、顶尖 PM 培养的技能，以及职业生涯早期如何找到导师。他强调“彻底的拥有感与责任感”——把每个问题都当成自己的——这一心态帮助 HubSpot 增长团队发现别人错过的机会。对话还强调早期 PM 必须“摔跟头”才能学到东西。

episodeTitle.en: Velocity over everything: How Ramp became the fastest-growing SaaS startup ever | Geoff Charles
episodeTitle.zh: 速度至上：Ramp如何成为增长最快的SaaS初创公司 | 杰夫·查尔斯

bio.en: Geoff Charles is VP of Product at Ramp, the fastest-growing SaaS business in history, which reached over $100 million in annual run rate within two years using a team of roughly 50 people.
bio.zh: Geoff Charles 是 Ramp 的产品副总裁；Ramp 是史上增长最快的 SaaS 公司，用约 50 人的团队在两年内达到超 1 亿美元年化经常性收入。

guestBioOfficial.en: Geoff Charles is VP of Product at Ramp—the fastest-growing SaaS startup of all time, Fast Company’s #1 Most Innovative Company in North America, and a company I believe we should all study for how they operate, execute, and hire. At Ramp, Geoff has led the product team from the early days, including the development and release of 60+ products and features in the past year alone. He has been building financial services for over a decade, and his interview in Lenny’s Newsletter quickly became one of the most widely read newsletter issues of all time. In today’s podcast, we will discuss: • How velocity is at the heart of Ramp’s culture and success
guestBioOfficial.zh: 杰夫·查尔斯是Ramp的副总裁——Ramp是史上增长最快的SaaS初创公司，曾获《快公司》北美最具创新力企业第一名。我认为我们都应该研究他们的运营、执行和招聘方式。在Ramp，杰夫从早期就领导产品团队，仅过去一年就开发并发布了60多款产品和功能。他从事金融服务领域十余年，其在Lenny’s Newsletter上的采访迅速成为有史以来阅读量最高的通讯内容之一。本期播客我们将探讨：• 速度如何成为Ramp文化和成功的核心

summary.en: Geoff offers a unique glimpse into Ramp's velocity-obsessed operating model: tiny teams (sometimes three engineers) that ship competitors to public companies in months and move billions of dollars a year. He explains how they operationalize a culture of speed through first-principles thinking and strong individual empowerment, how they organize planning and define strategy, and how they interview PMs while keeping an extremely high talent bar. He also addresses the real risk of burnout in such a fast culture and how to avoid it.
summary.zh: Geoff 带我们一窥 Ramp 以速度为核心的运营模式：极小的团队（有时仅三名工程师）能在几个月内做出上市竞品的对手产品，并每年流转数十亿美元。他解释了他们如何通过第一性原理思考和充分授权，把速度文化落到日常；如何组织规划、定义战略；以及如何在保持极高人才标准的同时面试 PM。他也谈到了这种高速文化下真实的倦怠风险，以及如何避免它。

episodeTitle.en: How to measure and improve developer productivity | Nicole Forsgren (Microsoft Research, Github)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何衡量和提升开发者生产力 | 妮可·福斯格伦（微软研究院，Github）

bio.en: Nicole Forsgren is the developer productivity expert behind Accelerate and DORA metrics, helping organizations measure and improve how engineering teams deliver software.
bio.zh: 妮可·福斯格伦（Nicole Forsgren）是《Accelerate》与 DORA 指标背后的开发者生产力专家，帮助组织衡量并改进工程团队交付软件的方式。

guestBioOfficial.en: Dr. Nicole Forsgren is a developer productivity and DevOps expert who works with engineering organizations to make work better. Best known as co-author of the Shingo Publication Award-winning book Accelerate and the DevOps Handbook, 2nd edition and author of the State of DevOps Reports, she has helped some of the biggest companies in the world transform their culture, processes, tech, and architecture. Nicole is currently a Partner at Microsoft Research, leading developer productivity research and strategy, and a technical founder/CEO with a successful exit to Google. In a previous life, she was a software engineer, sysadmin, hardware performance engineer, and professor. She has published several peer-reviewed journal papers, has been awarded public and private research grants (funders include NASA and the NSF), and has been featured in the Wall Street Journal, Forbes, Computerworld, and InformationWeek. In today’s podcast, we discuss: • Two frameworks for measuring developer productivity: DORA and SPACE
guestBioOfficial.zh:
妮可·福斯格伦博士是一位开发者生产力与DevOps领域的专家，她致力于帮助工程团队提升工作效率。她最著名的身份是《精益软件与DevOps实战》（获新乡出版奖）及《DevOps手册》第二版的合著者，同时也是《DevOps现状报告》的作者。她曾助力全球多家大型企业变革其文化、流程、技术及架构。目前，妮可是微软研究院的合伙人，负责开发者生产力研究与战略规划，同时也是谷歌旗下成功退出的科技初创公司的技术创始人兼CEO。此前，她曾担任软件工程师、系统管理员、硬件性能工程师及教授，发表过多篇经同行评审的学术论文，获得过NASA和NSF等机构的公共及私人研究资助，并多次登上《华尔街日报》《福布斯》《计算机世界》和《信息周刊》等媒体专栏。

在本期播客中，我们将探讨：
• 衡量开发者生产力的两个框架：DORA与SPACE

summary.en: Nicole stresses starting with a crisp definition of the problem or goal, since ambiguity is the biggest challenge even at executive levels. She explains the DORA metrics and why measuring outcomes beats activity. The episode is a practical guide to diagnosing and improving developer experience and team performance.
summary.zh: 妮可强调，要从清晰定义"问题或目标"开始，因为模糊性即便在高管层也是最大的挑战。她解释了 DORA 指标，以及为何衡量结果优于衡量活动。本期是一份关于诊断并改进开发者体验与团队绩效的实用指南。

episodeTitle.en: The ultimate guide to A/B testing | Ronny Kohavi (Airbnb, Microsoft, Amazon)
episodeTitle.zh: 《A/B测试终极指南》| 罗尼·科哈维（Airbnb、微软、亚马逊）

bio.en: Ronny Kohavi is widely regarded as the world's leading expert on A/B testing and experimentation, formerly VP and Technical Fellow of Relevance at Airbnb, Corporate VP at Microsoft, and Director of Data Mining at Amazon, and author of Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments.
bio.zh: Ronny Kohavi 被公认为全球 A/B 测试与实验领域的顶尖专家，曾任 Airbnb 相关性副总裁兼技术研究员、微软公司副总裁、亚马逊数据挖掘总监，也是《可信在线受控实验》一书的作者。

guestBioOfficial.en: Ronny Kohavi, PhD, is a consultant, teacher, and leading expert on the art and science of A/B testing. Previously, Ronny was Vice President and Technical Fellow at Airbnb, Technical Fellow and corporate VP at Microsoft (where he led the Experimentation Platform team), and Director of Data Mining and Personalization at Amazon. He was also honored with a lifetime achievement award by the Experimentation Culture Awards in September 2020 and teaches a popular course on experimentation on Maven. In today’s podcast, we discuss: • How to foster a culture of experimentation
guestBioOfficial.zh:
罗尼·科哈维（Ronny Kohavi）博士是一位顾问、教师，也是A/B测试艺术与科学领域的顶尖专家。此前，他曾担任爱彼迎（Airbnb）的副总裁兼技术研究员、微软的技术研究员兼企业副总裁（领导实验平台团队），以及亚马逊的数据挖掘与个性化主管。2020年9月，他荣获实验文化奖的终身成就奖，并在Maven平台上开设了热门的实验课程。在今天的播客中，我们将讨论：  
• 如何培育实验文化

summary.en: Ronny makes the case for 'test everything,' sharing the famous Bing story where moving one search line increased revenue by ~12% ($100M) and the Airbnb new-tab experiment. He explains why most predictions about experiments are humblingly wrong, how to build a culture of trustworthy experimentation, and why trust is the most important element of a successful program. The episode is a tactical masterclass on running experiments that actually move metrics.
summary.zh: Ronny 力主“凡事皆测试”，分享了著名的 Bing 案例——仅仅移动一行搜索结果就带来约 12%（1 亿美元）的营收增长——以及 Airbnb 新标签页实验。他解释了为什么我们对实验结果的预测常常错得离谱，如何建立可信实验的文化，以及为什么“信任”是成功实验体系中最关键的要素。本期是关于运行真正能撬动指标的实验的实战大师课。

episodeTitle.en: The 10 traits of great PMs, AI, and Slack’s approach to product | Noah Weiss (Slack, Google)
episodeTitle.zh: 伟大产品经理、人工智能和Slack的产品方法的10个特质 | 诺亚·韦斯（Slack、谷歌）

bio.en: Noah Weiss is Chief Product Officer at Slack, where he has spent the last seven years, after previously serving as Head of Product at Foursquare and as a product manager at Google and Fog Creek.
bio.zh: Noah Weiss 是 Slack 的首席产品官（CPO），已在那里工作七年，此前曾任 Foursquare 的产品负责人，以及 Google 与 Fog Creek 的产品经理。

guestBioOfficial.en: Noah Weiss is Chief Product Officer at Slack, where he leads all aspects of the product organization, including the self-service SMB business, the team that launched huddles and clips, and the search and machine-learning teams. Prior to Slack, Noah served as SVP of Product at Foursquare. He started his career at Google, leading the structured data search team and working on display ads. In today’s episode, we discuss: • The top 10 traits of great PMs
guestBioOfficial.zh: 诺亚·韦斯（Noah Weiss）是Slack的首席产品官，负责产品组织的各个方面，包括面向中小企业的自助服务业务、推出Huddles和Clips功能的团队，以及搜索和机器学习团队。在加入Slack之前，诺亚曾担任Foursquare的产品副总裁。他的职业生涯始于谷歌，负责结构化数据搜索团队和展示广告。在本期节目中，我们将探讨：• 伟大产品经理的10个特质

summary.en: Noah shares the ten traits of great product managers and how to collaborate effectively with strong, product-minded founders. He explains the 'Complaint Storm' process Slack uses to surface and act on user frustration, and reflects on turning around Slack's self-serve business after it plateaued in 2019. The conversation also covers how he thinks about AI in product after 15 years across Google, Foursquare, and Slack, plus lessons on competing with Microsoft Teams and Discord.
summary.zh: Noah 分享了优秀产品经理的十大特质，以及如何与强势且具备产品思维的创始人高效协作。他介绍了 Slack 用来收集并响应用户情绪的“吐槽风暴（Complaint Storm）”流程，并反思了 2019 年自助业务陷入瓶颈后如何实现逆转。对话还涵盖他基于在 Google、Foursquare 和 Slack 共 15 年经验对产品中 AI 的思考，以及应对 Microsoft Teams 和 Discord 竞争的经验。

episodeTitle.en: LinkedIn’s product evolution and the art of building complex systems | Hari Srinivasan (LinkedIn)
episodeTitle.zh: 领英的产品演进与复杂系统构建之道 | 哈里·斯里尼瓦桑（领英）

bio.en: Hari Srinivasan is VP of Product for LinkedIn's Talent Solutions—the company's largest business, spanning hiring and learning products—and has spent eight-plus years at LinkedIn shaping how the world's professionals find jobs.
bio.zh: Hari Srinivasan 是 LinkedIn 人才解决方案（Talent Solutions）业务的产品副总裁——这是 LinkedIn 最大的业务，涵盖招聘与学习类产品——他在 LinkedIn 任职八年多，深度参与了全球职场人求职方式的塑造。

guestBioOfficial.en: Hari Srinivasan is VP of Product at LinkedIn Talent Solutions, where he oversees LinkedIn Recruiter, LinkedIn Jobs, and LinkedIn Learning. He’s also a frequent guest lecturer at Stanford University. Previously, he served as the CEO and founder of We Created It, which was acquired by LinkedIn in 2014. Hari has a passion for building products, with experience ranging from creating the first U.S. hybrid SUV to developing a No. 1 app and writing a beloved children’s book. In today’s episode, we discuss: • LinkedIn’s unique business model and org structure
guestBioOfficial.zh: 哈里·斯里尼瓦桑是领英人才解决方案部门的产品副总裁，负责领英招聘、领英招聘和领英学习业务。他还是斯坦福大学的常客讲师。此前，他曾担任We Created It的首席执行官兼创始人，该公司于2014年被领英收购。哈里对产品开发充满热情，其经验涵盖从打造美国首款混合动力SUV到开发头号应用程序，再到撰写深受喜爱的儿童书籍。在今天的节目中，我们讨论了：• 领英独特的商业模式和组织结构

summary.en: Hari shares what he's seeing shift in the hiring market—including the rise of skills-first hiring, which translates experience into portable skills to rebalance a frozen labor marketplace—and gives concrete tips to improve your odds of landing a job through LinkedIn. He reflects on lessons from building and maintaining enormously complex systems like LinkedIn, advice for breaking into product management, and how LinkedIn became a source of genuinely valuable (and far less cringe) content over the past couple of years. The episode originated from a spontaneous Twitter request for a LinkedIn insider, and it shows.
summary.zh: Hari 分享了他对招聘市场变化的观察——包括“技能优先招聘”（skills-first hiring）的兴起，即把经历转化为可迁移的技能，以重新平衡冻结的劳动力市场，并给出了通过 LinkedIn 提高求职成功率的实用建议。他回顾了打造与维护 LinkedIn 这类极度复杂系统的经验、进入产品管理的建议，以及 LinkedIn 过去几年如何变成真正有价值（且不再尴尬）的内容来源。这期节目源自一条在 Twitter 上“想请 LinkedIn 内部人来做客”的临时请求，非常有意思。

episodeTitle.en: M&A, competition, pricing, and investing | Julia Schottenstein (dbt Labs)
episodeTitle.zh: 并购、竞争、定价与投资 | 朱莉娅·肖滕斯坦（dbt Labs）

bio.en: Julia Schottenstein is a product leader at dbt Labs, where she leads the dbt Cloud product, and previously held product roles at Facebook and Neural Magic.
bio.zh: 茱莉亚·舍滕施泰因（Julia Schottenstein）是 dbt Labs 的产品负责人，领导 dbt Cloud 产品，此前曾在 Facebook 和 Neural Magic 担任产品职务。

guestBioOfficial.en: Julia Schottenstein is a product lead at dbt Labs, a data transformation company, and an active angel investor in data and infrastructure startups. She first got excited about dbt in 2019 when she was a VC at NEA and decided to make the leap from investor to operator by joining dbt Labs. She also co-hosts the dbt Labs Analytics Engineering Podcast, a show about data trends that impact analytics engineers’ work. In today’s episode, we discuss: • Advice for founders hoping to improve their M&A outcome
guestBioOfficial.zh: 朱莉娅·肖滕斯坦是数据转型公司 dbt Labs 的产品负责人，也是数据和基础设施初创企业的活跃天使投资人。2019 年，她在 NEA 担任风投时，首次对 dbt 产生了浓厚兴趣，随后决定从投资者转变为运营者，加入 dbt Labs。她还联合主持 dbt Labs 分析工程播客，探讨影响分析工程师工作的数据趋势。在本期节目中，我们讨论了：• 希望提升并购成果的创始人建议

summary.en: Julia reframes M&A as the disciplined practice of creating "plan Bs" so you always have optionality with potential buyers. She advises founders to become strategically unavoidable to a small set of buyers by leaning into a genuine competitive advantage without burning bridges. The episode offers a pragmatic playbook for early M&A thinking.
summary.zh: 茱莉亚把并购重新定义为一种有纪律的"准备 B 计划"的实践，让你始终对潜在收购方保有选择权。她建议创始人，通过发挥真正的竞争优势、又不伤和气地切入，使自己在少数几个买家眼中变得"难以忽视"。本期提供了一份务实的早期并购思路与打法。

episodeTitle.en: How to ask the right questions, project confidence, and win over skeptics | Paige Costello (Asana)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何提出正确的问题、展现自信并赢得怀疑者 | 佩奇·科斯特洛（Asana）

bio.en: Paige Costello is a product lead at Asana overseeing the teams responsible for Asana's core product experience across desktop, web, and mobile, after previously serving as Director of Product at Intercom and Group Product Manager at Intuit.
bio.zh: Paige Costello 是 Asana 的产品负责人，领导负责 Asana 桌面端、网页端与移动端核心产品体验的团队，此前曾任 Intercom 产品总监以及 Intuit 的集团产品经理。

guestBioOfficial.en: Paige Costello is a beloved product leader with a reputation as a remarkable coach and mentor. She is currently the Head of Core Product at Asana, where she leads the group responsible for Asana’s web, desktop, and mobile apps. Prior to that role, she served as the Director of Product at Intercom and, before that, as a Group PM at Intuit, where she kickstarted her product career through their renowned APM program. In today’s episode, we discuss: • The unique product development process at Asana and how it’s evolved
guestBioOfficial.zh: 佩奇·科斯特洛是一位备受尊敬的产品领导者，素有杰出教练和导师之称。她目前是Asana的核心产品主管，负责领导团队开发Asana的网页、桌面和移动应用。在此之前，她曾在Intercom担任产品总监，并在Intuit担任集团产品经理，通过其著名的APM项目开启了她的产品生涯。在今天的节目中，我们探讨了：• Asana独特的产品开发流程及其演变

summary.en: Paige discusses how Asana evolved its product development process, shifting from yearly planning toward a six-month horizon with frequent revisiting and outcome-aligned teams. She explains how the organization is structured into pillars and areas, each with a specific target customer and problem space, and why over-specifying roadmaps leads teams to make strange scope trade-offs. The episode is full of practical lessons on scaling product planning without losing agility.
summary.zh: Paige 探讨了 Asana 产品开发的演进过程：从年度规划转向以六个月为周期、频繁复盘、并与成果对齐的团队模式。她解释了组织如何划分为“支柱（pillar）”与“领域（area）”，每一块都有特定的目标客户与问题空间，并说明过度细化路线图反而会让团队做出奇怪的范围取舍。本期充满了在不丧失敏捷性的前提下扩展产品规划的实战经验。

episodeTitle.en: Building minimum lovable products, stories from WeWork & Airbnb, and thriving as a PM | Jiaona Zhang
episodeTitle.zh: 《打造最小可爱产品——来自WeWork和Airbnb的故事，以及如何在产品经理岗位上蓬勃发展 | 庄佳诺》

bio.en: Jiaona Zhang (JZ) is Senior Vice President of Product at Webflow, a lecturer at Stanford teaching product management, and a longtime product leader at Airbnb, Dropbox, and WeWork.
bio.zh: Jiaona Zhang（JZ）是 Webflow 的产品高级副总裁、斯坦福产品管理课程讲师，也是在 Airbnb、Dropbox、WeWork 任职多年的产品负责人。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jiaona Zhang (JZ) is a product leader with a strong background in consumer products and extensive hiring and management experience. She is currently SVP of Product at Webflow as well as a lecturer at Stanford, where she teaches a graduate-level course on product management. Before Webflow, JZ was Head of Product for the Homes Platform at Airbnb and has also led product teams at Airbnb, WeWork, and Dropbox. In today’s episode, we discuss: • Building a “minimum lovable product” rather than a minimum viable product
guestBioOfficial.zh: 庄佳诺（JZ）是一位拥有深厚消费品行业背景、丰富招聘与管理经验的产品领袖。她目前担任Webflow的产品高级副总裁，同时在斯坦福大学担任讲师，教授产品管理的研究生课程。在加入Webflow之前，JZ曾担任Airbnb房屋平台的产品负责人，还曾在Airbnb、WeWork和Dropbox领导过产品团队。在本期节目中，我们将探讨：• 打造“最小可爱产品”而非最小可行产品

summary.en: JZ digs into the most common mistakes early PMs make, the concept of 'minimal lovable products' versus MVPs, and her unique frameworks for roadmapping, prioritization, and OKRs. She shares how to structure your first 90 days as a product leader, lessons from her wild year at WeWork, the best product and leadership advice she's received, and the story of Airbnb Plus and where it went wrong. A recurring theme: become known for being excellent at something specific, because reputation attracts responsibility.
summary.zh: JZ 深入剖析了初级 PM 最常见的错误、“最小化可爱产品”（minimal lovable products）与 MVP 的区别，以及她独特的路线图、优先级排序与 OKR 框架。她分享了作为产品领导者如何规划新公司的前 90 天、在 WeWork 疯狂一年的教训、她收到过最好的产品与领导力建议，以及 Airbnb Plus 的故事与失败原因。一个反复出现的主题是：让自己以“在某件具体的事上极其出色”而闻名，因为声誉会吸引责任。

episodeTitle.en: Lessons from scaling Ramp | Sri Batchu (Ramp, Instacart, Opendoor)
episodeTitle.zh: 《Ramp扩展规模的经验教训 | 斯里·巴楚（Sri Batchu，Ramp、Instacart、Opendoor）》

bio.en: Sri Batchu is the Head of Growth at Ramp, the fastest-growing SaaS and FinTech company in history (which reached $100M in annualized revenue within two years), and previously served as Head of Growth at Instacart and VP of Operations at Opendoor.
bio.zh: Sri Batchu 是 Ramp 的增长负责人。Ramp 是史上增长最快的 SaaS 与金融科技公司——仅用两年就达到了 1 亿美元年化收入。在此之前，他曾任 Instacart 的增长负责人、Opendoor 的运营副总裁。

guestBioOfficial.en: Sri Batchu currently leads growth at Ramp, the fastest-growing SaaS business (and fintech business) in history. Previously, he led growth strategy and operations at Instacart and was one of the first 50 employees at Opendoor, where he built, scaled, and managed a variety of business teams, including analytics, sales, and pricing. During his time there, the company grew from $100M to $5B+ in revenue and to 1,500+ people. In this episode, we discuss:• The surprising tactics behind Ramp’s unprecedented early growth• A breakdown of Ramp’s current growth org and growth channels• Why you need to be “failing conclusively”• Ramp’s unique approach to metrics and measurement• Examples of Ramp’s “secret sauce”: a data- and technology-driven approach to everything• Why Sri prioritizes employee autonomy and flexibility over hours worked• Why team structure is a red herring for growth teams, and what Sri focuses on instead• How to set good North Star metrics, and why you should have more than one• Why Sri prefers payback periods over CAC for measuring investment ROI
guestBioOfficial.zh: 斯里·巴楚目前负责Ramp的增长业务，Ramp是史上增长最快的SaaS公司（及金融科技公司）。此前，他在Instacart负责增长战略和运营，并是Opendoor首批50名员工之一，在那里他组建、扩展并管理了包括分析、销售和定价在内的多个业务团队。在他任职期间，公司营收从1亿美元增长至50亿美元以上，员工规模超过1,500人。本期节目中，我们将探讨：• Ramp早期增长背后令人惊讶的策略   • Ramp当前增长组织和增长渠道的解析   • 何为“彻底失败”   • Ramp独特的指标和衡量方法   • Ramp“秘籍”示例：一切事务均以数据和技术为导向   • 斯里为何优先考虑员工自主性和灵活性而非工作时长   • 团队结构为何是增长团队的误区，以及斯里关注的重点   • 如何设定优秀的北极星指标，以及为何需要多个指标   • 斯里为何更青睐投资回报率而非客户获取成本来衡量投资回报率

summary.en: Ramp seeded its explosive growth with a 'cap table as a growth strategy' — recruiting influential founders and operators as early investors who became its first customers. Its real edge comes from technologizing every channel: a dedicated growth-engineering team automates sales and a shared 'translation layer' maps every team's metric back to a single north-star metric (dollars of SQL pipeline). Culturally, Ramp runs on velocity — working in days not quarters, two-week sprints, calendar audits, and autonomy over hours rather than hours worked. For B2B growth sequencing Sri recommends founder-led sales, then first sales hires, then low-cost targeted marketing (content, community, events, PR), and only later paid, brand, and SEO. He also argues companies should optimize for payback period over CAC or LTV, and design experiments to 'fail conclusively' by maximizing the treatment effect rather than iterating timidly.
summary.zh: Ramp 之所以能爆发式增长，起点是它把「股权结构表当成增长策略」——拉拢有影响力的创始人和运营者成为早期投资人，而这些人又成了它的第一批客户。它真正的壁垒在于把每个渠道都技术化：一支专门的「增长工程」团队自动化销售流程，并用一套共享的「翻译层」把每个团队的指标都映射回同一个北极星指标（销售合格线索带来的美元金额）。在文化上，Ramp 靠的是「速度」——以天而不是季度为单位工作、两周一个冲刺、做日历审计，看重的是自主权和产出而非工作时长。关于 B2B 增长的顺序，Sri 建议先做创始人主导的销售，再招第一批销售，接着做低成本的精准营销（内容、社群、活动、PR），最后才做付费、品牌和 SEO。他还主张企业应该优化「回收周期」而不是 CAC 或 LTV，并且要做「彻底失败」的实验——把能用的手段都押上，而不是小心翼翼地小步迭代。

episodeTitle.en: Building high-performing teams | Melissa Tan (Webflow, Dropbox, Canva)
episodeTitle.zh: 打造高效团队 | 梅利莎·谭（Webflow、Dropbox、Canva）

bio.en: Melissa Tan was the longtime head of growth for Dropbox's B2B business and its first growth PM, later advising companies like Canva, Grammarly, and Miro on growth.
bio.zh: 梅丽莎·谭（Melissa Tan）曾是 Dropbox B2B 业务长期的增长负责人及第一位增长 PM，后来为 Canva、Grammarly、Miro 等公司提供增长咨询。

guestBioOfficial.en: Melissa Tan is an advisor, investor, and growth expert. She’s worked with fast-growing startups like Dropbox, Canva, Grammarly, and Miro, and for the past 2.5 years has been the Head of Growth at Webflow. There, she led the company's self-service business across Product, Marketing, and Growth, in addition to leading the charge on pricing and packaging. Prior to Webflow, she was Head of Growth for Dropbox’s B2B product, where she played a pivotal role in propelling their growth. In today’s episode, we discuss: • Attributes of high-performing teams
guestBioOfficial.zh: 梅利莎·谭是一位顾问、投资者和增长专家。她曾与Dropbox、Canva、Grammarly和Miro等快速成长的初创公司合作，过去两年半一直担任Webflow的增长部门负责人，负责产品、营销和增长部门的自助服务业务，同时主导定价和套餐策略。在加入Webflow之前，她曾担任Dropbox B2B产品部门的增长负责人，为推动该部门增长发挥了关键作用。在本期节目中，我们将探讨：• 高效团队的特质

summary.en: Melissa shares how hiring smart people with no sales background at Dropbox led to unexpectedly innovative go-to-market motions. She champions first-principles thinking over copying playbooks. The episode offers grounded growth advice drawn from scaling one of the most iconic B2B products.
summary.zh: 梅丽莎分享了在 Dropbox 雇佣毫无销售背景的聪明人，反而催生出意料之外的创新获客打法。她推崇"第一性原理思考"，而非照搬套路。本期提供了来自打造最具标志性 B2B 产品之一的扎实增长建议。

episodeTitle.en: Leveraging growth advisors, mastering SEO, and honing your craft | Luc Levesque (Shopify, Meta)
episodeTitle.zh: 借助增长顾问、精通SEO并磨练技艺 | 卢克·莱维斯克（Shopify、Meta）

bio.en: Luc Levesque is the Chief Growth Officer at Shopify and was personally recruited by Mark Zuckerberg to help grow Facebook Messenger, Instagram, and WhatsApp; he previously served as VP of Growth and GM at Tripadvisor and has advised companies like Twitter, Pinterest, Patreon, Thumbtack, and Canva on growth.
bio.zh: Luc Levesque 是 Shopify 的首席增长官（Chief Growth Officer），曾被 Mark Zuckerberg 亲自招揽去推动 Facebook Messenger、Instagram 和 WhatsApp 的增长；他此前担任 Tripadvisor 的增长副总裁兼总经理，并曾为 Twitter、Pinterest、Patreon、Thumbtack 和 Canva 等公司提供增长顾问。

guestBioOfficial.en: Luc Levesque is Chief Growth Officer at Shopify and has advised companies like Canva, Twitter, Pinterest, and Patreon on growth and product strategy. Previously he served as an executive at TripAdvisor, where he built and led the growth team that helped it become the world’s largest travel site. Luc was then recruited by Mark Zuckerberg to Facebook, where he was an executive and held senior product and engineering leadership roles. In today’s episode, we discuss: • Why you need to become world-class at hiring
guestBioOfficial.zh: 卢克·莱维斯克（Luc Levesque）是Shopify的首席增长官，曾为Canva、Twitter、Pinterest和Patreon等公司提供增长和产品策略咨询。此前，他在TripAdvisor担任高管，组建并领导了推动该平台成为全球最大旅游网站的增长团队。随后，马克·扎克伯格将卢克招入Facebook，担任高管并担任高级产品和工程领导职务。在本期节目中，我们探讨了：•为何你需要在招聘方面达到世界级水准

summary.en: Luc makes the case for hiring a great growth advisor, arguing that the right person at the right time can change a company's trajectory with a single sentence and deliver 100% to 1000%+ lifts. He shares how to decide when you need an advisor, how to structure the relationship, and what to look for in one. A large part of the conversation is devoted to SEO as a growth channel—who it suits, how to think about it, and how everything is about to change with AI tools like Bard and ChatGPT. He also offers unexpected advice on self-reflection, building routines, and cold plunges, plus memorable stories from working alongside Zuckerberg and the relentless 'impact' culture at Facebook.
summary.zh: Luc 力陈聘请一位优秀增长顾问的价值，他认为在对的时机遇到对的人，一句话就能改变公司的走向，带来 100% 乃至 1000% 以上的提升。他分享了如何判断自己是否需要顾问、如何设计合作关系，以及该看重顾问的哪些特质。对话的很大篇幅都集中在 SEO 这一增长渠道上——它适合谁、该怎么思考，以及随着 Bard、ChatGPT 这类 AI 工具出现，一切将如何改变。他还给出了关于自我反思、建立日常节奏和冷水浴的意外建议，并讲述了一些与 Zuckerberg 共事、以及 Facebook 那种对“影响力（impact）”近乎偏执的文化里的难忘故事。

episodeTitle.en: Building a long and meaningful career | Nikhyl Singhal (Meta, Google)
episodeTitle.zh: 打造长远且有意义的职业生涯 | 尼克尔·辛格尔（Meta、Google）

bio.en: Nikhyl Singhal has led large consumer and product teams at Google, Facebook, and Credit Karma, and is a former VP of Product at multiple influential companies.
bio.zh: 尼基尔·辛哈尔（Nikhyl Singhal）曾在 Google、Facebook 和 Credit Karma 领导大型消费级与产品团队，并担任过多个具影响力公司的产品副总裁。

guestBioOfficial.en: Nikhyl Singhal is VP of Product at Meta, overseeing teams building messaging, groups, stories, and the main Facebook feed. Before that, he served as the Chief Product Officer at Credit Karma and held various leadership roles at Google, leading teams on Google Photos and Google Hangouts. Nikhyl was also co-founder of three startups, including SayNow and Cast Iron Systems, which were acquired by Google and IBM, respectively. Alongside his successful career, he is passionate about coaching and mentoring, sharing his knowledge through the Skip podcast, newsletter and CPO community. In this episode, we discuss: • Finding your North Star and building a long and meaningful career
guestBioOfficial.zh: 尼克尔·辛格尔（Nikhyl Singhal）：Meta产品副总裁

summary.en: Nikhyl uses the "fake rabbit" dog-track analogy to warn against defining success only as a future title or milestone, after which motivation dies. He urges planning for what comes next - a second act - so your career stays purposeful. The episode is a thoughtful take on long-term career motivation and avoiding the post-achievement void.
summary.zh: 尼基尔用赛狗场上"假兔子"的比喻警告：若把成功仅仅定义为未来的某个头衔或里程碑，一旦达成，动力便会枯竭。他敦促人们规划"下一步"——即第二幕——让职业生涯始终保持意义。本期是对"长期职业动力、避免成就后的空虚"的深思。

episodeTitle.en: Moving fast and navigating uncertainty | Jeremy Henrickson (Rippling, Coinbase)
episodeTitle.zh: 快速行动并应对不确定性 | 杰里米·亨里克森（Rippling、Coinbase）

bio.en: Jeremy Henrickson is Senior Vice President of Product at Rippling, where he leads product and design, and was previously Chief Product Officer at Coinbase, where he oversaw 10x growth of the product and engineering orgs during a turbulent crypto period.
bio.zh: Jeremy Henrickson 是 Rippling 的产品高级副总裁，领导产品与设计团队，此前曾任 Coinbase 首席产品官，在加密市场剧烈波动的时期带领产品与工程组织实现了 10 倍增长。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jeremy Henrickson is Rippling’s SVP of Product, responsible for scaling their product and design team across three continents. Previously, as Chief Product Officer at Coinbase, he oversaw 10x growth of the product and engineering organization and transformed a scrappy startup into a global cryptocurrency platform with tens of millions of users. He began his career at Apple in the 1990s and holds a BS and MS in computer science from Stanford. In today’s episode, we discuss: • Strategies for sustaining focus and momentum at scale
guestBioOfficial.zh: 杰里米·亨里克森是Rippling的SVP产品负责人，负责在三大洲扩展其产品和设计团队。此前，他在Coinbase担任首席产品官期间，领导产品和工程组织实现了10倍的增长，将一家初创公司转变为拥有数千万用户的全球加密货币平台。他于20世纪90年代在苹果公司开始职业生涯，拥有斯坦福大学的计算机科学学士和硕士学位。在今天的节目中，我们讨论了：• 在大规模环境中保持专注和动力的策略

summary.en: Jeremy shares lessons on maintaining velocity at scale and creating a culture of fast decision-making, emphasizing that product leaders should go deep on the hardest problems alongside their teams rather than directing from above. He explains why relying on frameworks can hurt, why he often favors designing for the most complex use cases first over MVPs, what to look for when interviewing PMs, and how to become a true domain expert. The episode is a grounded playbook for product leaders operating at large, complex organizations.
summary.zh: Jeremy 分享了在规模化下保持速度、建立快速决策文化的经验，强调产品领导者应当深入最棘手的问题、与团队并肩作战，而非高高在上发号施令。他解释了为何依赖框架反而有害、为何他常主张先为最复杂的用例做设计而非先做 MVP、面试 PM 时看什么，以及如何成为真正的领域专家。这期节目是在大型复杂组织中运作的产品领导者的踏实手册。

episodeTitle.en: Storytelling with Nancy Duarte: How to craft compelling presentations and tell a story that sticks
episodeTitle.zh: 南希·杜阿尔特（Nancy Duarte）讲述故事：如何打造引人入胜的演示文稿，讲述令人难忘的故事

bio.en: Nancy Duarte is the CEO of Duarte Inc., which has created over 250,000 presentations for leaders including Apple, Google, and Al Gore, and author of books on the art of communication.
bio.zh: 南希·杜阿尔特（Nancy Duarte）是 Duarte 公司的 CEO，该公司为 Apple、Google、阿尔·戈尔等领导者创作了超过 25 万份演示文稿，她也著有关于沟通艺术的书籍。

guestBioOfficial.en: Nancy Duarte is the CEO of Duarte Inc. and has helped create over 250,000 presentations for influential business leaders across the globe, including Apple, TED, the World Bank, and Al Gore’s An Inconvenient Truth. She’s also written six best-selling books, and her TED talk has garnered over 3 million views. She regularly contributes to HBR, MIT-Sloan, and Forbes, and her books are essential reading in leading business schools worldwide. In today’s episode, we discuss: • Why empathy is at the heart of everything Nancy does
guestBioOfficial.zh: 南希·杜阿尔特（Nancy Duarte）是Duarte Inc.的首席执行官，为全球数十位有影响力的商业领袖（包括苹果、TED、世界银行和阿尔·戈尔的《难以忽视的真相》）创作了超过25万份演示文稿。她还撰写了六本畅销书，其TED演讲获得了超过300万次观看。她定期为《哈佛商业评论》、麻省理工斯隆商学院和《福布斯》撰稿，她的书籍是全球顶尖商学院的重要读物。在本期节目中，我们讨论了：• 同理心为何是南希所做一切的核心

summary.en: Nancy teaches the "contrast" framework - using the gap between what is and what could be - as a tool for influence in any format, from big stages to quick asks. She shares how even getting chores done at home can use persuasive structure. The episode is a tactical guide to presenting and communicating with impact.
summary.zh: 南希传授"对比"框架——利用"现状"与"可能"之间的落差——把它作为任何场合（从大型演讲到随口请求）施加影响的工具。她分享了即便在家让丈夫做家务，也能用说服结构。本期是一份关于"有影响力地演示与沟通"的战术指南。

episodeTitle.en: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin
episodeTitle.zh: 战略叙事的力量 | 安迪·拉斯金

bio.en: Andy Raskin is a strategic-narrative expert who helps CEOs and company leaders align their teams around a simple story — a "strategic narrative" — that clarifies why customers need their product and unifies sales, marketing, product, and hiring; he has worked closely with founders and companies including Gong, Salesforce, Uber, Dropbox, Square, and IBM, and his post "The Greatest Sales Deck I've Ever Seen" is widely cited in business circles.
bio.zh: Andy Raskin 是一位战略叙事专家，帮助 CEO 和企业领导者用「战略叙事」这一简单故事让团队对齐——明确为什么客户需要他们的产品，并统一销售、市场、产品和招聘的方向；他曾与 Gong、Salesforce、Uber、Dropbox、Square、IBM 等公司密切合作，其文章《我见过最牛的销售 Deck》在商业圈广受引用。

guestBioOfficial.en: Andy Raskin helps CEOs align their leadership teams around a strategic narrative—a single story that powers success in sales, marketing, product, fundraising, and recruiting. His clients include Gong, Dropbox, Uber, Salesforce, Square, IBM, and many others. In today’s episode, we discuss: • What a strategic narrative is, and how to craft one
guestBioOfficial.zh: 安迪·拉斯金（Andy Raskin）帮助首席执行官们围绕一个战略叙事（strategy narrative）凝聚领导团队——这个单一的故事能驱动销售、市场营销、产品开发、融资和招聘等各领域的成功。他的客户包括Gong、Dropbox、Uber、Salesforce、Square、IBM等众多公司。在本期节目中，我们将探讨：   • 什么是战略叙事，以及如何构建一个成功的叙事

summary.en: Andy Raskin argues that most people still pitch with what he calls the "arrogant doctor" approach — name a problem, then explain why your solution beats the alternatives — but that framing no longer works. He lays out a "strategic narrative" framework: name the shift from an old game to a new game and define the stakes, name the object of the new game (e.g., "turn customers into subscribers"), show the obstacles in the way, and then explain how you help overcome them. Using clients like 360Learning, Zuora, and Gong, plus companies like Drift, he shows how this narrative turns the product into a prop for the story, generates endless marketing content, and becomes the north star for product decisions. Andy also clarifies his skepticism of "category creation" — a category name is just shorthand for a movement, and the story itself is what matters — and notes the framework delivers the most value for B2B enterprise tech companies, especially around Series B or when an old story needs to expand.
summary.zh: Andy Raskin 认为，大多数人在商业里用的还是「傲慢医生」式 pitch——先讲问题，再讲自己的方案为什么更好——但这种套路已经失效了。他提出「战略叙事」框架：先讲世界正在从旧游戏转向新游戏的转变并定义赌注，再给新游戏命名一个目标物（如「把客户变成订阅者」），接着展示通往目标的障碍，最后讲如何克服这些障碍。他用自己的客户（如 360Learning、Zuora、Gong）和 Drift 等公司举例，说明这套叙事能让产品成为故事的道具、让营销内容源源不断，并成为产品决策的北极星。Andy 还澄清了他不太待见「创造品类」的执念——品类名只是运动的简写，真正重要的是故事本身；这套框架对 B2B 企业科技公司价值最大，通常在 B 轮之后或公司需要扩张老故事时最该投入。

episodeTitle.en: The science of product, big bets, and how AI is impacting the future of music | Gustav Söderström
episodeTitle.zh: 产品科学、大赌注以及人工智能如何影响音乐的未来 | 古斯塔夫·索德斯特伦（Gustav Söderström）

bio.en: Gustav Söderström is co-president, chief product officer, and chief technology officer at Spotify, where he oversees the company's global product and technology strategy across product, design, data, and engineering.
bio.zh: Gustav Söderström 是 Spotify 的联合总裁、首席产品官兼首席技术官，负责公司在产品、设计、数据与工程领域的全球产品与技术战略。

guestBioOfficial.en: Gustav Söderström is the Co-President and Chief Product and Technology Officer at Spotify. He is responsible for Spotify’s global product and technology strategy, overseeing the product, design, data, and engineering teams. Prior to Spotify, he founded 13th Lab, a startup that was later acquired by Facebook’s Oculus. He also served as the Director of Product and Business Development for Yahoo Mobile and founded Kenet Works, a company focused on community software for mobile phones, which was acquired by Yahoo in 2006. In today’s episode, we discuss: • How Spotify structures product teams to promote freedom of thought
guestBioOfficial.zh: 古斯塔夫·索德斯特伦（Gustav Söderström）是Spotify的联席总裁兼首席产品与技术官。他负责Spotify的全球产品和技术战略，监管产品、设计、数据和工程团队。在加入Spotify之前，他创立了13th Lab，这家初创公司后来被Facebook的Oculus收购。他还曾担任雅虎移动部门的产品和业务发展总监，并创立了专注于手机社区软件的Kenet Works，该公司于2006年被雅虎收购。在本期节目中，我们将探讨：• Spotify如何构建产品团队以促进思想自由

summary.en: Gustav frames the internet's evolution as curation → recommendation → generation, arguing generative AI will force a rethink of products as profound as the shift to recommendation did. He shares what he's learned about placing big bets and what to do when they fail, how Spotify moved away from squads to its current team structure, and how AI is already reshaping Spotify's product and the future of AI-generated music. He also explains why every great product must pull a 'magic trick,' and offers a memorable (and hilarious) analogy about Swedish business culture.
summary.zh: Gustav 把互联网的演进概括为“策展 → 推荐 → 生成”，主张生成式 AI 将迫使产品被重新设想，其深远程度不亚于当年转向推荐。他分享了关于下大赌注、以及赌注失败该如何应对的经验；Spotify 如何放弃 squad 模式、转向如今的团队结构；AI 已如何重塑 Spotify 的产品与 AI 生成音乐的未来。他还解释了为何每一款伟大的产品都必须耍一个“魔术”，并用一个令人难忘（且好笑）的类比谈了瑞典商业文化。

episodeTitle.en: Lessons on product sense, AI, the first mile experience, and the messy middle | Scott Belsky (Adobe)
episodeTitle.zh: 关于产品意识、人工智能、首英里体验和混沌中期的经验教训 | 斯科特·贝尔斯基（Scott Belsky，Adobe）

bio.en: Scott Belsky is a product legend - founder of Behance (sold to Adobe, where he rose to Chief Product Officer and later Chief Strategy Officer), author of The Messy Middle, and an active angel investor.
bio.zh: Scott Belsky 是一位产品传奇人物——Behance 的创始人（后被 Adobe 收购，他在那里升至首席产品官，后任首席战略官），《混乱的中段》（The Messy Middle）一书的作者，同时也是一位活跃的天使投资人。

guestBioOfficial.en: Scott Belsky is an entrepreneur, author, investor, and currently Adobe’s Chief Strategy Officer and EVP of Design and Emerging Products. He founded Behance, an online platform for creative professionals to showcase and discover work, and served as CEO until its acquisition by Adobe. Scott is an early advisor and investor in several businesses at the intersection of technology and design, including Pinterest, Uber, Warby Parker, Airtable, and Flexport. He is also the author of two nationally bestselling books and founded 99U, a publication and conference focused on productivity in the creative world. In today’s episode, we discuss: • How to strengthen your product sense
guestBioOfficial.zh: 斯科特·贝尔斯基（Scott Belsky）是一位企业家、作家、投资者，目前担任Adobe首席战略官兼设计与新兴产品执行副总裁。他创立了面向创意专业人士展示与发现作品的在线平台Behance，并在Behance被Adobe收购前一直担任CEO一职。斯科特还是科技与设计交叉领域多家企业的早期顾问与投资者，包括Pinterest、Uber、Warby Parker、Airtable和Flexport。他还著有两本全国畅销书，并创立了专注于创意领域生产力的刊物与会议平台99U。在本期节目中，我们将探讨：• 如何强化你的产品敏锐度

summary.en: Scott shares lessons from a career of building and investing, focusing on the 'messy middle' between idea and scale where most of the real work happens. He discusses how to maintain craft and quality amid growth, the role of taste and persistence, and what he looks for in the products and teams he backs. The episode is an inspiring, practitioner's view of what it takes to make enduring products.
summary.zh: Scott 分享了他打造与投资的职业心得，聚焦于介于“想法”与“规模化”之间、绝大多数真正工作发生的“混乱中段（messy middle）”。他讨论了如何在增长中保持工艺与品质、品味与坚持的作用，以及他在押注的产品与团队身上寻找什么。本期是一位实践者对“打造持久产品需要什么”的鼓舞人心的解读。

episodeTitle.en: Frameworks for product differentiation, team building, and first principles thinking | Ayo Omojola
episodeTitle.zh: 《三体》

bio.en: Ayo Omojola is Chief Product Officer at Carbon Health and previously the founding product lead on Cash App's banking team at Square, where he co-created the Cash Card and scaled it into a nine-figure revenue line.
bio.zh: Ayo Omojola 是 Carbon Health 首席产品官，此前是 Square 旗下 Cash App 银行团队的创始产品负责人，共同打造了 Cash Card 并将其发展为上亿美元收入线。

guestBioOfficial.en: Ayo Omojola is Chief Product Officer at Carbon Health, one of the fastest-growing and most innovative health tech companies in the world. Previously, he was a PM leader at Cash App, where he co-created the Cash Card and scaled it to a nine-figure revenue line for Square. He’s also an angel investor in companies like Mercury, Modern Treasury, Faire, and many others. In this episode, we discuss: • How Cash App broke through the noise and became a consumer app success story
guestBioOfficial.zh: 《时间之子》

summary.en: Ayo shares hard-won lessons from building and scaling the Cash Card and Cash App, emphasizing the importance of differentiation when building any consumer product. He argues for going “unreasonably deep” to understand constraints—especially in regulated industries—and that problem selection matters as much as problem solving. The conversation covers why small teams beat big ones, the benefits of hiring founders, and first-principles thinking for product and team building.
summary.zh: Ayo 分享了构建和扩展 Cash Card 与 Cash App 的宝贵经验，强调打造任何消费产品时“差异化”的重要性。他主张“极其深入”地理解约束（尤其在受监管行业），并认为“选对问题”与“解决问题”同样重要。对话涵盖为何小团队优于大团队、雇佣创始人的好处，以及产品与团队建设中的第一性原理思维。

episodeTitle.en: Mastering paid growth | Jonathan Becker (Thrive Digital)
episodeTitle.zh: 《付费增长攻略》|乔纳森·贝克尔（Jonathan Becker，Thrive Digital）

bio.en: Jonathan Becker is a legend of performance marketing whose agency Thrive Digital has planned and executed over $3.5 billion in paid acquisition for companies like Uber, Asana, Square, and MasterClass—this is Lenny's first deep dive into paid growth.
bio.zh: Jonathan Becker 是效果营销（performance marketing）领域的传奇人物，他的代理机构 Thrive Digital 已为 Uber、Asana、Square、Masterclass 等公司规划并执行了超 35 亿美元的付费获取预算——这是 Lenny 首次深入“付费增长”这一主题。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jonathan Becker is the founder and president of Thrive Digital, where he and his team have deployed more than $3.5 billion in paid acquisition budgets for companies like Uber, Asana, Square, Tempur-Pedic, and MasterClass. He spent the first part of his career mastering SEO and is a world expert in DTC, lead generation, demand generation, and user acquisition. In today’s episode, we discuss: • Signs that your company is a good fit for paid growth
guestBioOfficial.zh: 《值得讲述的故事》

summary.en: Jonathan goes deep on paid growth: how privacy shifts changed the game, why creative is now the biggest lever within paid acquisition, and how to think about attribution in a post-cookie world. He shares what to look for when hiring people to run paid growth, and how AI is already reshaping the work—displacing trench-level bid tweaking with more strategic, creative, and validation-focused roles (rough creative drafts now take 1% of the time). It's a comprehensive, practitioner's tour of modern paid growth.
summary.zh: Jonathan 深入“付费增长”：隐私政策的变化如何改变了游戏规则、为何“创意”已成为付费获取中最大的杠杆，以及后 cookie 时代该如何看待归因。他分享了招聘付费增长负责人时看重的点，以及 AI 如何已经在重塑这项工作——把底层的手动调价替换为更偏战略、创意与验证的角色（粗糙创意草稿如今只需 1% 的时间）。这是一场现代付费增长的、由实战者带队的全面巡礼。

episodeTitle.en: Building a culture of excellence | David Singleton (CTO of Stripe)
episodeTitle.zh: 打造卓越文化 | 戴维·辛格尔顿（Stripe首席技术官）

bio.en: David Singleton is Chief Technology Officer at Stripe, guiding its engineering and design teams for over five years, previously VP of Engineering at Google.
bio.zh: David Singleton 是 Stripe 首席技术官，领导其工程与设计团队逾五年，此前曾任 Google 工程副总裁。

guestBioOfficial.en: David Singleton is Chief Technology Officer at Stripe, where he oversees engineering and design teams. Since joining Stripe, David has helped grow the technology org across the U.S. and developed new engineering hubs in Singapore and Dublin as well as Stripe’s fifth hub, remote engineering, across the globe. Before Stripe, he spent 11 years at Google, where he was VP of Engineering, leading product development and coordinating more than 15 different hardware partnerships. In today’s episode, we cover: • Hiring secrets that set Stripe employees apart
guestBioOfficial.zh:
戴维·辛格尔顿（David Singleton）是Stripe的首席技术官，负责监督工程和设计团队。自加入Stripe以来，戴维帮助该公司在美国各地扩展技术团队，并在新加坡和都柏林建立了新的工程中心，还在全球范围内推出了Stripe的第五个远程工程中心。在加入Stripe之前，他在谷歌工作了11年，担任工程副总裁，领导产品开发并协调了超过15个不同的硬件合作项目。在本期节目中，我们将探讨：
• 让Stripe员工与众不同的招聘秘诀

summary.en: David explains Stripe's product-development approach of co-creating with a small set of early users—as with Stripe Billing, built alongside Figma and Slack before broader launch. He argues this means every engineer at Stripe exercises many PM-like attributes, blurring the line between engineering and product. The conversation covers how Stripe builds durable, loved products through deep early-user partnership.
summary.zh: David 解释了 Stripe“与少量早期用户共创”的产品开发方式——如 Stripe Billing 在广泛发布前与 Figma、Slack 一同打造。他认为这让 Stripe 每位工程师都具备许多类 PM 的特质，模糊了工程与产品的边界。对话涵盖 Stripe 如何通过深度的早期用户合作，打造持久且被人喜爱的产品。

episodeTitle.en: How to achieve hypergrowth in your business and career | Carilu Dietrich (Atlassian)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何在业务与职业中实现超增长 | 卡里鲁·迪特里希（Atlassian）

bio.en: Carilu Dietrich is a former CMO who served as head of marketing at Atlassian through its IPO and has advised the CEOs and CMOs of hypergrowth B2B companies including Segment, Miro, 1Password, Bill.com, and Productboard.
bio.zh: Carilu Dietrich 是一位前首席营销官（CMO），在 Atlassian 上市期间担任其营销负责人，并曾为 Segment、Miro、1Password、Bill.com、Productboard 等超高速增长 B2B 公司的 CEO 与 CMO 提供顾问服务。

guestBioOfficial.en: Carilu Dietrich is a former CMO, most notably the Head of Marketing who took Atlassian public. These days she’s an advisor to CEOs and CMOs of hypergrowth B2B companies and has worked with companies like Miro, Segment, Bill.com, 1Password, Productboard, Sprout Social, Weights & Biases, and more. In today’s episode, we discuss: • Patterns across the most successful hypergrowth companies
guestBioOfficial.zh: 卡里鲁·迪特里希曾担任首席营销官，尤其是在带领Atlassian成功上市方面表现突出。如今，她为高增长B2B公司的CEO和CMO提供咨询服务，曾与Miro、Segment、Bill.com、1Password、Productboard、Sprout Social、Weights & Biases等公司合作。在本期节目中，我们探讨了：• 成功的超增长公司有哪些共通模式

summary.en: Hypergrowth cannot be bought with ads alone: it requires an amazing product people love, organic and viral word-of-mouth, and leaders who can "ride the lightning" by hiring ahead of the next stage of scale. Carilu shares her Rule-of-40-style scorecard for picking winning companies (momentum, NPS, net dollar retention, market position) and her famous Post-it life philosophies ("More Yoda, less Wonder Woman," "Hell yes or no," "Worrying is wasted energy"). On go-to-market, she argues product-led growth works best when you land with a single product and only engage sales after real usage signals appear, and that big growth levers are company strategy problems, not departmental ones. The episode closes with candid advice on why most CMOs and CPOs get fired, how to build trust with a CEO, and the career value of chasing the right industry, company, and wave.
summary.zh: 超高速增长不是靠砸广告买来的：它需要一款人们真爱的出色产品、有机且病毒式的口碑，以及能"迎着闪电奔跑"——在下一个规模阶段到来前提前招人的领导者。Carilu 分享了她挑"赢家"公司的 40 法则式打分表（势头、NPS、净收入留存率、市场地位），以及她那些著名的便利贴人生哲学（"多当尤达，少当神奇女侠""要么超兴奋，要么就别""担忧是浪费能量"）。在走向市场上，她主张产品驱动增长最好用单一产品切入，并且只在出现真实使用信号后才让销售介入；大增长杠杆是公司战略问题，不是部门问题。节目最后给出了坦诚的建议：为什么大多数 CMO 和 CPO 会被炒、怎么跟 CEO 建立信任，以及追逐正确行业、正确公司和正确"浪"在职业上的价值。

episodeTitle.en: The ultimate guide to product-led sales | Elena Verna
episodeTitle.zh: 产品主导销售的终极指南 | 埃琳娜·维尔纳

bio.en: Elena Verna is a renowned growth advisor and former head of growth at companies like SurveyMonkey and Dropbox, best known for popularizing the "growth loops" framework and teaching growth strategy at Reforge.
bio.zh: Elena Verna 是知名的增长顾问，曾担任 SurveyMonkey、Dropbox 等公司的增长负责人，以推广"增长循环"（growth loops）框架和在 Reforge 讲授增长战略而闻名。

guestBioOfficial.en: Elena Verna is a leading growth expert with over 15 years of experience in tech. She was SVP of Growth at SurveyMonkey and interim CMO at Miro, where she built high-performing teams that drove significant growth. She recently served as interim Head of Growth at Amplitude and currently advises and is a board member for early-stage startups. In today’s podcast, we discuss: • What product-led sales is
guestBioOfficial.zh: 埃琳娜·维尔纳是一位在科技领域拥有超过15年经验的领先增长专家。她曾在SurveyMonkey担任增长副总裁，并在Miro担任临时首席营销官，在那里她组建了高绩效团队，推动了显著的增长。她最近在Amplitude担任临时增长主管，目前为早期初创公司提供咨询并担任董事会成员。在今天的播客中，我们讨论：• 什么是产品主导销售

summary.en: Elena Verna shares a 10-part playbook of counterintuitive growth tactics, starting with hiring a growth lead much later than most expect (only after product-market fit and roughly $1M ARR) and warning that a declining growth curve cannot be rescued by a growth hire. She argues growth teams should stop over-investing in homepage redesigns, blindly copying competitors, and relying on rented channels like SEO, SEM, and social — instead they must build owned, earned channels (virality, referrals, user-generated content) and continuously overlay new growth models (PLG, sales-led, marketing-led) every 18 months to escape the "Law of Shitty Clickthroughs." She also cautions against testing everything (trust intuition and use pre/post analysis), debunks low-value optimizations (color tweaks, third-party auth, one-off emails, blanket friction removal), and urges treating advisors as career amplifiers and full-time jobs as just one of many monetization options.
summary.zh: Elena Verna 分享了一套由十条反直觉增长打法组成的实战手册：首先，比大多数人预期的更晚才招增长负责人（要等产品市场匹配、约 100 万 ARR 之后），并提醒增长曲线下滑不是靠招人能解决的。她主张增长团队别再过度投入首页改版、盲目抄竞品、依赖 SEO/SEM/社媒这类"租来的渠道"，而该打造自有、赚来的渠道（病毒传播、推荐、用户生成内容），并每 18 个月持续叠加新的增长模型（产品驱动、销售驱动、市场驱动），以避开"烂点击率定律"。她还提醒别什么都测（相信直觉、用前后对比）、戳破了几种低价值优化（改颜色、第三方登录、单封邮件、一刀切去摩擦），并呼吁把顾问当事业放大器、把全职工作只看作众多变现选项之一。

episodeTitle.en: An inside look at how Miro builds product | Varun Parmar (CPO of Miro)
episodeTitle.zh: 制作与营销

bio.en: Varun Parmar is Chief Product Officer at Miro and previously SVP and Chief Product Officer at Box, known for Miro's distinctive product culture.
bio.zh: Varun Parmar 是 Miro 的首席产品官（CPO），此前曾任 Box 的高级副总裁兼首席产品官，以 Miro 独具特色的产品文化而闻名。

guestBioOfficial.en: Varun Parmar is the Chief Product Officer of Miro and has over two decades of experience in the tech industry. Prior to joining Miro, Varun held executive positions as Chief Product Officer at Box and Syncplicity (acquired by Dell EMC) and spent six years in product management at Adobe. He also co-founded Doculus, which was later acquired by Box. In today’s episode, we discuss: • The importance of empathy and how to foster it
guestBioOfficial.zh: Miro产品构建内幕 | 瓦伦·帕马尔（Miro首席产品官）

summary.en: Varun discusses what makes Miro's product culture distinctive, how a visual-collaboration company scales while staying close to users, and lessons from leading product at both Box and Miro. He covers product-led growth, the role of craft and design, and how to keep quality high as a collaboration tool expands across enterprises. The episode is a practitioner's view of building beloved B2B products.
summary.zh: Varun 讨论了是什么让 Miro 的产品文化独具特色、一家视觉协作公司如何在贴近用户的同时规模化，以及从在 Box 与 Miro 领导产品中学到的经验。他涵盖了产品驱动增长、工艺与设计的作用，以及当协作工具向企业扩张时如何保持高品质。本期是关于打造受人喜爱的 B2B 产品的实践者视角。

episodeTitle.en: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何做出更明智的决策，打造愉悦的职业生涯 | 陈仁希（Notejoy、LinkedIn）

bio.en: Ada Chen Rekhi is an executive coach and co-founder of the note-taking product Notejoy, formerly SVP of Marketing at SurveyMonkey and an early LinkedIn marketing leader, who helps founders scale themselves.
bio.zh: Ada Chen Rekhi 是一位高管教练，也是笔记产品 Notejoy 的联合创始人，曾任 SurveyMonkey 营销高级副总裁及 LinkedIn 早期营销负责人，专注于帮助创始人实现自我成长。

guestBioOfficial.en: Ada Chen Rekhi is an executive coach and co-founder of Notejoy. She helps founders scale themselves alongside their teams. She has over a decade of experience leading teams through periods of rapid transition, from the chaos of founding early-stage startups to leadership roles in growing SurveyMonkey and LinkedIn. In today’s podcast, we discuss: • How utilizing a “curiosity loop” can aid you in decision-making
guestBioOfficial.zh: 陈仁希是执行教练及Notejoy联合创始人。她帮助创始人与团队共同成长，拥有十多年带领团队度过快速转型期的经验，经历从早期初创公司的混乱到在SurveyMonkey和LinkedIn担任领导角色的全过程。在本期播客中，我们将探讨：• 如何利用“好奇心循环”辅助决策

summary.en: Ada shares a framework called Curiosity Loops for making better decisions by systematically gathering structured input from your network. She walks through a live exercise mapping Lenny's personal values and offers practical advice for intentionally building an early-career path. The conversation also covers how to thrive as a woman in Silicon Valley, when to get a coach versus doing it yourself, and why aligning work with your values prevents a mid-to-late-career trap.
summary.zh: Ada 介绍了她称为“好奇心循环”（Curiosity Loops）的框架，通过向人脉系统性地收集结构化反馈来做出更好的决策。她现场带领 Lenny 梳理个人价值观，并给出如何有意识地规划早期职业路径的实用建议。对话还涵盖女性如何在硅谷茁壮成长、何时该请教练还是自己来，以及为什么让工作与价值观保持一致能避免中年职业困境。

episodeTitle.en: How to build a cult-like brand | Laura Modi (Bobbie)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何打造具有邪教般吸引力的品牌 | 劳拉·莫迪（Bobbie）

bio.en: Laura Modi is the co-founder and CEO of Bobbie, an organic infant-formula brand, and previously spent years at Airbnb leading hospitality and host community efforts.
bio.zh: 劳拉·莫迪（Laura Modi）是有机婴儿配方奶粉品牌 Bobbie 的联合创始人兼 CEO，此前在 Airbnb 工作多年，负责款待体验与房东社群。

summary.en: Laura shares how Bobbie's head of growth flagged that they were depleting inventory faster than they could replenish, and made the tough call to pause growth to protect existing customers. She explains the discipline of defending your core promise even when demand is skyrocketing. The episode is a lesson in values-driven scaling and saying no at the right moment.
summary.zh: 劳拉讲述了 Bobbie 的增长负责人如何发现库存消耗快于补货速度，并做出暂停增长以保护现有用户的艰难决定。她阐释了即便需求暴涨，也要守住核心承诺的纪律。本期是一堂关于"以价值观驱动扩张、在正确的时刻说不"的课。

episodeTitle.en: Product lessons from Waymo | Shweta Shrivastava (Waymo, Amazon, Cisco)
episodeTitle.zh: Waymo的产品经验启示 | 施维塔·什里瓦斯塔瓦（Waymo、亚马逊、思科）

bio.en: Shweta Shrivastava is Senior Director of Product Management at Waymo, the self-driving car company, and previously held product leadership roles at Amazon and Cisco.
bio.zh: Shweta Shrivastava 是自动驾驶公司 Waymo 的产品管理高级总监，此前曾在 Amazon 和 Cisco 担任产品领导职务。

guestBioOfficial.en: Shweta Shrivastava is a Senior Product Leader at Waymo, an autonomous driving technology company backed by Alphabet. Prior to joining Waymo, she was the CPO of Nauto, where she also worked on AI-assisted driver tools. Shweta has worked in product for over 15 years in senior roles at several companies, including Amazon and Cisco. In today’s episode, we discuss: • How Waymo builds trust with riders
guestBioOfficial.zh: 施维塔·施里瓦斯塔瓦（Shweta Shrivastava）是Alphabet旗下自动驾驶技术公司Waymo的资深产品负责人。加入Waymo之前，她曾担任Nauto的首席产品官，期间也致力于开发AI辅助驾驶工具。施维塔在产品领域拥有超过15年的经验，曾在亚马逊、思科等多家公司担任高级职位。本期节目中，我们将探讨：• Waymo如何建立与乘客的信任

summary.en: Shweta shares product lessons from building autonomous vehicles, including how Waymo creates human-like driving behaviors and treats safety as the foundational product principle. She covers key lessons from her career at Amazon, Cisco, and startups about customer-centric product management, and why listening and empathy are core PM skills in complex technical environments. The episode is a fascinating look at product management inside one of the most advanced AI deployments on the roads today.
summary.zh: Shweta 分享了打造自动驾驶汽车的产品经验，包括 Waymo 如何创造类人的驾驶行为、并将安全视为基础性的产品原则。她讲到了在 Amazon、Cisco 以及初创公司生涯中关于“以客户为中心的产品管理”的关键心得，以及为什么在复杂技术环境中，倾听与同理心是产品经理的核心技能。本期是对当今道路上最先进 AI 部署之一内部产品管理的精彩透视。

episodeTitle.en: Driving alignment within teams, work-life balance, and the changing PM landscape | Nikita Miller
episodeTitle.zh: 推动团队内部协作、工作生活平衡及项目管理格局变革 | 尼基塔·米勒

bio.en: Nikita Miller is SVP of Product at The Knot Worldwide who previously led growth and retention at Trello for over five years and served as VP of Product at Dooly, and is also an angel investor and advisor.
bio.zh: Nikita Miller 是 The Knot Worldwide 的产品高级副总裁，此前曾在 Trello 担任增长与留存负责人逾五年，并在 Dooly 担任产品副总裁，同时也是一位天使投资人与顾问。

guestBioOfficial.en: Nikita Miller is a product leader, angel investor, and advisor. She has built and led product teams at companies ranging from early-stage startups to multinationals, and she is currently SVP of Product Management at The Knot Worldwide. Nikita is passionate about scaling product teams to support high-growth businesses and was a product leader at Trello and Atlassian for five years. In today’s podcast, we cover: • Lessons from building and growing Trello
guestBioOfficial.zh: 尼基塔·米勒是一位产品领袖、天使投资人及顾问。她曾在从初创企业到跨国公司的多个产品团队中任职，目前担任The Knot Worldwide的产品管理高级副总裁。尼基塔热衷于通过扩展产品团队来支持高增长业务，并曾在Trello和Atlassian担任五年产品负责人。本期播客我们将涵盖：• 在Trello的建设与发展中汲取的经验教训

summary.en: Nikita discusses how to drive alignment and urgency within product teams, arguing against the myth of perfect work-life balance in favor of intentionally optimizing for what matters most at each stage. She covers the shifting structure of product teams - the rise of shared-accountability models like the Triad and the declining role of Scrum Masters - and why explicitly defining roles and responsibilities is a catalyst for velocity. The episode also explores empathy, distributed and remote teamwork, and building celebration into products.
summary.zh: Nikita 探讨了如何在产品团队内部推动对齐与紧迫感，主张放弃“完美工作生活平衡”的迷思，转而针对每个阶段最重要的事进行有意识的最优配置。她讲到了产品团队结构的演变——如“三人组（Triad）”式共同担责模式的兴起，以及 Scrum Master 角色的弱化——并解释了为什么明确定义角色与职责是提升团队速度的催化剂。本期还涉及同理心、分布式与远程协作，以及在产品中刻意营造“庆祝感”。

episodeTitle.en: The ultimate guide to adding a PLG motion | Hila Qu (Reforge, GitLab)
episodeTitle.zh: PLG模式终极指南 | 胡佳琦（Reforge、GitLab）

bio.en: Hila Qu is a product-led growth expert best known for her two-part newsletter series on building a product-led growth motion—two of the most-read posts in Lenny's newsletter history—and for advising startups on activation, retention, and funnel optimization.
bio.zh: Hila Qu 是一位产品驱动增长（PLG）专家，她关于如何搭建 PLG 增长体系的两篇系列文章，是 Lenny newsletter 历史上阅读量最高的文章之二；她还就用户激活、留存与漏斗优化为众多初创公司提供顾问指导。

guestBioOfficial.en: Hila Qu is an Executive in Residence at Reforge as well as a renowned growth advisor, angel investor, and published author (her book about growth was named one of the top 10 business books of 2018 in China). Previously, she served as the Director of Growth at GitLab, where she implemented and scaled their PLG motion, and VP of Growth at Acorns, scaling them from 1 million to 5 million users. In today’s episode, we discuss: • The importance of having both a product-led and a sales-led motion for companies of all sizes
guestBioOfficial.zh: 胡佳琦是Reforge的驻场高管，也是知名的增长顾问、天使投资人及出版作家（她的增长类书籍曾入选2018年中国十大商业书籍）。此前，她曾担任GitLab的增长总监，负责实施并扩展其PLG模式，并在Acorns担任增长副总裁，将用户规模从100万扩展至500万。在今天的节目中，我们讨论了：• 无论公司规模大小，产品主导型和销售主导型增长模式的重要性

summary.en: Hila breaks down how to start and optimize a product-led growth motion, beginning with the foundational idea of data-led growth: give away a free product, but in return capture broader reach and, crucially, usage data that reveals which features predict conversion and retention. She walks through the common pitfalls teams hit when getting started, her recommended tools for an initial PLG-oriented team, and how to audit an existing funnel for leaks. The conversation also goes deep on improving activation and retention, plus a clear overview of core PLG concepts like balancing free reach with analytical rigor. Listeners come away with a concrete, high-value playbook for standing up PLG the right way.
summary.zh: Hila 拆解了如何启动并优化产品驱动增长体系，起点是“数据驱动增长”这一基础理念：把免费产品送出去，但作为交换，要获得更广泛的触达，更重要的是拿到使用数据，从而看清哪些功能预示着转化和留存。她梳理了团队刚起步时最常踩的坑、为初始 PLG 团队推荐的工具，以及如何审计现有漏斗找出漏点。对话还深入探讨了如何提升激活和留存，并清晰讲解了 PLG 的核心概念，比如在免费触达和分析严谨之间取得平衡。听众最终会收获一份具体、高价值、能真正落地搭建 PLG 的实战手册。

episodeTitle.en: Thinking beyond frameworks | Casey Winters (Pinterest, Eventbrite, Airbnb, Tinder, Reddit, Grubhub)
episodeTitle.zh: 超越框架的思考 | 凯西·温特斯（Pinterest、Eventbrite、Airbnb、Tinder、Reddit、Grubhub）

bio.en: Casey Winters is a growth and product strategist who has led growth or advised companies including Grubhub, Pinterest, Reddit, Eventbrite (as CPO), Canva, Airbnb, Tinder, and Thumbtack, and was the first repeat guest on Lenny's Podcast.
bio.zh: Casey Winters 是一位增长与产品战略专家，曾领导或与 Grubhub、Pinterest、Reddit、Eventbrite（任 CPO）、Canva、Airbnb、Tinder、Thumbtack 等公司合作或提供顾问，并且是 Lenny 播客第一个返场嘉宾。

guestBioOfficial.en: Casey Winters is a longtime and legendary advisor and operator. He’s worked with companies like Airbnb, Faire, Canva, Whatnot, Thumbtack, Tinder, and Reddit and until recently was the Chief Product Officer at Eventbrite, where he managed the PM, design, research, and growth marketing teams. Before Eventbrite, he led growth and product teams at Pinterest and Grubhub. In today’s episode, we discuss what Casey calls the “zero interest rate phenomenon” product manager and how to avoid becoming one. He provides valuable insights on thinking outside popular frameworks, shipping products efficiently, and avoiding overreliance on user research. We explore the three types of network effects, how to leverage them, and how to break someone else’s network effect. Finally, Casey shares his contrarian approach to interviewing product managers and his thoughts on the future of PM roles with AI.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 凯西·温特斯是一位资深且传奇的顾问与运营者。他曾与Airbnb、Faire、Canva、Whatnot、Thumbtack、Tinder和Reddit等公司合作，近期担任Eventbrite首席产品官，管理产品管理、设计、研究和增长营销团队。在此之前，他曾在Pinterest和Grubhub领导增长与产品团队。在本期节目中，我们将探讨凯西所说的"零利率现象"产品经理，以及如何避免成为这样的产品经理。他将分享如何跳出流行的框架高效交付产品、避免过度依赖用户研究的宝贵见解。我们将探讨三种网络效应、如何利用它们，以及如何打破他人的网络效应。最后，凯西将分享他对产品经理面试的逆向思维，以及他对PM角色在AI时代未来的看法。

summary.en: Casey warns of the "zero interest rate phenomenon product manager" — PMs trained in an era of abundant funding who over-rely on frameworks and research instead of shipping and using judgment. He argues the real PM job (making high-leverage decisions under uncertainty) is AI-resistant, while AI is best used for tedious non-core work. On founder intuition vs team expertise, founders should direct until employees prove they surpass them, then delegate. The episode also breaks down network effects (direct, cross-side, data) and why Grubhub lost to DoorDash despite strong network effects: it underestimated a structurally unprofitable but market-rewarded disruptor. Finally, he explains why consumer subscription businesses are brutally hard (no net dollar retention) and why marketplaces adding SaaS tools beat SaaS tools adding marketplaces.
