summary.zh: Casey 警告了"零利率现象产品经理"——那些在资金充沛年代被训练出来、过度依赖框架和研究、而不是发布和使用判断的 PM。他主张真正的 PM 工作（在不确定性下做高杠杆决定）是抗 AI 的，而 AI 最好用于琐碎的非核心活。在创始人直觉 vs 团队专业上，创始人应该指挥，直到员工证明他们超越自己，然后授权。节目还拆解了网络效应（直接、跨边、数据），以及为什么 Grubhub 尽管有强网络效应还是输给 DoorDash：它低估了一个结构亏损但被市场奖励的颠覆者。最后，他解释了为什么消费订阅生意极其难（没有净收入留存率），以及为什么市场加 SaaS 工具胜过 SaaS 工具加市场。

episodeTitle.en: Taxi mafias, cash vaults & 100% MoM growth: The story of SEA’s biggest startup | Kevin Aluwi (Gojek)
episodeTitle.zh: 出租车黑手党、现金库与月增长率100%：东南亚最大初创企业的故事 | 凯文·阿鲁维（Gojek）

bio.en: Kevin Aluwi is the co-founder and former CEO of Gojek, the Indonesian super-app spanning ride-hailing, payments, and deliveries, which grew into one of Southeast Asia's most valuable startups.
bio.zh: 凯文·阿卢维（Kevin Aluwi）是 Gojek 的联合创始人兼前 CEO，Gojek 是印尼的一款超级应用，涵盖出行、支付与配送，已成长为东南亚最具价值的初创公司之一。

guestBioOfficial.en: Kevin Aluwi is the co-founder and former CEO of Gojek. With over 2.7 million drivers and over 3 billion orders completed, Gojek is the biggest startup in Indonesia and all of Southeast Asia. In today’s podcast, Kevin shares the story of how Gojek overcame endless obstacles—including being underfunded, being unable to send drivers payment, and the local motorcycle mafia coming after their drivers. We cover the importance of brand, the value of doing the hard things, how to be super-scrappy, and helpful tips on building a tech company outside of Silicon Valley.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 凯文·阿鲁维是Gojek的联合创始人兼前首席执行官。凭借超过270万名司机和30亿笔完成的订单，Gojek是印度尼西亚乃至整个东南亚最大的初创企业。在本期播客中，凯文分享了Gojek如何克服重重障碍的历程——包括资金不足、无法向司机支付报酬，以及当地摩托车黑手党对司机的威胁。我们将探讨品牌的重要性、做难事的价值、如何极其高效地开展工作，以及在硅谷以外地区建立科技公司的实用建议。

summary.en: Kevin recounts Gojek's early resistance from motorcycle-taxi syndicates who physically attacked drivers, and how the company responded by hiring private security rather than abandoning its contractors. He shares the operating philosophy behind building a multi-service super-app in a chaotic market. The episode is a raw look at the physical and strategic risks of scaling in emerging markets.
summary.zh: 凯文讲述了 Gojek 早期遭遇摩托车出租车团伙的抵制——他们曾对司机大打出手，以及公司如何通过雇佣私人安保、而非抛弃外包司机来应对。他分享了在混乱市场中构建多业务超级应用的运营理念。本期真实呈现了在新兴市场扩张时所面临的体力与战略风险。

episodeTitle.en: Navigating comms and PR | Lulu Cheng Meservey (Substack, Activision Blizzard)
episodeTitle.zh: 《公关与传播力导航》| 程露思（Substack、动视暴雪）

bio.en: Lulu Cheng Meservey is a communications and PR strategist formerly heading comms at Substack and now advising companies on narrative and messaging.
bio.zh: 露露·程·梅瑟维（Lulu Cheng Meservey）是一位传播与公关策略专家，曾任 Substack 的传播负责人，如今为企业提供叙事与信息传达方面的咨询。

guestBioOfficial.en: Lulu Cheng Meservey was formerly head of comms at Substack (where I host my newsletter and podcast) and is currently the Executive Vice President of Corporate Affairs and Chief Communications Officer at Activision Blizzard. She also writes one of my favorite newsletters, “Flack,” where she shares tactical advice for company comms, PR, and messaging. In today’s episode, we dive deep into the world of PR and comms. We discuss why taking risks is crucial, how to gain attention as an underdog, and why it’s important to have a super-specific audience. Lulu outlines several frameworks I’d never heard of before, including a concentric circles framework for identifying your audience, the cultural erogenous zones, and even a physics-based framework for comms.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 程露思曾担任Substack（我发布新闻通讯和播客的平台）的公关主管，目前是动视暴雪企业事务执行副总裁兼首席传播官。她还撰写了我最喜欢的时事通讯之一《Flack》，在其中为企业公关、传播和信息传达提供策略建议。在今天的节目中，我们深入探讨了公关和传播领域。我们讨论了为何冒险至关重要、如何以弱胜强吸引关注，以及为何必须明确目标受众的重要性。露思介绍了几个我从未听说过的框架，包括用于识别目标受众的同心圆框架、文化敏感区，甚至基于物理学的传播框架。

summary.en: Lulu advises finding your audience's "cultural erogenous zones" - the passions they already care about - and bridging your message to fit that worldview. She argues you can't change someone's core beliefs, but you can connect your offering to what they already love. The episode is a sharp guide to messaging, PR, and earning attention without shouting.
summary.zh: 露露建议找到受众的"文化敏感区"——他们本来就关心的事物——并把你的信息桥接到他们的世界观上。她认为你无法改变一个人的核心信念，却可以把你的产品连接到他们已经热爱的事物上。本期是一份关于信息传达、公关与"不靠喊叫也能赢得注意力"的犀利指南。

episodeTitle.en: Competing with giants: An inside look at how The Browser Company builds product | Josh Miller (CEO)
episodeTitle.zh: 与巨头竞争：浏览器公司打造产品的内部视角 | 乔希·米勒（CEO）

bio.en: Josh Miller is the co-founder and CEO of The Browser Company, the maker of the Arc web browser, and previously led product at TikTok's U.S. operations.
bio.zh: 乔什·米勒（Josh Miller）是 Arc 网页浏览器的开发商 The Browser Company 的联合创始人兼 CEO，此前曾负责 TikTok 美国区的产品业务。

guestBioOfficial.en: Josh Miller is the CEO and co-founder of The Browser Company, where he helped build Arc, my go-to web browser. In today’s episode, we get an inside look at the unique structure and values of The Browser Company and how their company culture has helped them land some of the best talent in tech. Josh shares ways that his company embraces experimentation, including their “optimizing for feelings” approach to building, and explains why extreme transparency is at the forefront of everything they do.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 乔希·米勒（Josh Miller）是The Browser Company的CEO兼联合创始人，他曾助力打造Arc——我日常使用的网页浏览器。在本期节目中，我们深入了解了The Browser Company独特的组织架构与价值观，以及公司文化如何帮助他们吸引了科技领域最优秀的人才。乔希分享了公司如何拥抱实验精神，包括“以用户感受为优化准则”的产品开发方法，并解释了为何极致透明是其一切行动的核心。

summary.en: Josh explains that the most important hiring criterion is "heartfelt intensity" - people who show up with a fire in their belly and a purpose to prove. He describes how The Browser Company approaches product craft by giving small teams ambitious problems and getting out of their way. The episode explores why a cohort of new, opinionated software companies are rebuilding foundational consumer products from scratch.
summary.zh: 乔什认为，最重要的招聘标准是"发自内心的炽热"——即带着一股冲劲和想要证明自己的目标而来的人。他讲述了 The Browser Company 如何通过把宏大的问题交给小团队、然后不加以干涉的方式来打磨产品工艺。本期还探讨了为何一批富有主张的新兴软件公司正在从零开始重建基础性的消费级产品。

episodeTitle.en: The ultimate guide to OKRs | Christina Wodtke (Stanford)
episodeTitle.zh: OKR终极指南 | 克里斯蒂娜·沃特克（斯坦福大学）

bio.en: Christina Wodtke is a multi-time author, Stanford lecturer (product management, game design), and consultant who specializes in OKRs and product development processes, with product leadership experience at LinkedIn, MySpace, Zynga, and Yahoo.
bio.zh: Christina Wodtke 是多次著书者、斯坦福讲师（产品管理、游戏设计）和顾问，专长于 OKR 与产品开发流程，曾在 LinkedIn、MySpace、Zynga 和 Yahoo 担任产品领导。

guestBioOfficial.en: Christina Wodtke is an author, Stanford University professor, and speaker who teaches strategies for building high-performing teams. She’s also the author of Radical Focus, which some consider the de facto guide to OKRs. In today’s episode, we dive into OKRs and how they can be used to help your team achieve better results. Christina shares her expertise on crafting OKRs, how she uses them in her personal life, and common mistakes you should avoid when you sit down to write your own. She discusses effective goal setting and outlines a systematic approach to achieving key results. Finally, Christina gives some specific tips on how to improve your storytelling and drawing skills and explains why it’s smart to set ambitious goals.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·沃特克（Christina Wodtke）是一位作家、斯坦福大学教授和演讲者，专注于团队高效建设的策略。她还著有《激进专注》（Radical Focus）一书，该书被视为OKR的权威指南。在本期节目中，我们将深入探讨OKR及其如何帮助团队取得更佳成果。克里斯蒂娜分享了制定OKR的专业技巧、她个人如何应用OKR的经验，以及制定OKR时应避免的常见误区。她还讨论了有效目标设定的方法，并概述了实现关键成果的系统性方法。最后，克里斯蒂娜为提升讲故事和绘图能力提供具体建议，并解释为何设定雄心勃勃的目标至关重要。

summary.en: Christina goes deep into OKRs—the atomic unit of an objective, what's commonly broken about OKR processes, and how the best companies leverage them. She covers the elements of a healthy OKR cadence, how OKRs fit with mission, vision, strategy, and roadmaps, and the often-overlooked power of celebration. The conversation also touches on storytelling and her most contrarian advice for new PMs.
summary.zh: Christina 深入讲解 OKR——目标的原子单位、OKR 流程常见的毛病，以及顶尖公司如何利用它。她涵盖了健康 OKR 节奏的要素、OKR 如何与使命/愿景/战略/路线图配合，以及常被忽视的“庆祝”力量。对话还涉及讲故事，以及她对新 PM 最反共识的建议。

episodeTitle.en: Hot takes and techno-optimism from tech’s top power couple | Sriram and Aarthi
episodeTitle.zh: 科技界顶级情侣的灼见与技术乐观主义 | 斯里拉姆（Sriram）与阿尔西（Aarthi）

bio.en: Sriram Krishnan and Aarthi Ramamurthy are the hosts of The Aarthi and Sriram Show; Sriram is a former Microsoft/Twitter exec and a16z partner (later a senior White House AI advisor), and Aarthi is a former Netflix, Spotify, and Microsoft product leader and founder of Latent.
bio.zh: Sriram Krishnan 与 Aarthi Ramamurthy 是《The Aarthi and Sriram Show》的主持人：Sriram 曾任 Microsoft/Twitter 高管与 a16z 合伙人（后任白宫高级 AI 顾问），Aarthi 则是前 Netflix、Spotify、Microsoft 产品领导者，也是 Latent 的创始人。

guestBioOfficial.en: Aarthi Ramamurthy and Sriram Krishnan are founders, angel investors, and product leaders who host the podcast Aarthi and Sriram’s Good Time Show. They have both held leadership roles at major technology companies including Meta, Twitter, Snap, Microsoft, and Netflix. In today’s episode, we dive into how and why to build your personal brand, how to deal with imposter syndrome, and stories from Aarthi’s time at Clubhouse and Sriram’s time working with Zuck. Both Aarthi and Sriram share their lessons from past failures and their experience building communities, on techno optimism, and Sriram offers his hot take on the Jobs to Be Done framework.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 阿尔西·拉马穆尔西（Aarthi Ramamurthy）和斯里拉姆·克里希南（Sriram Krishnan）是创始人、天使投资人和产品领袖，他们主持播客《阿尔西和斯里拉姆的欢乐时光》。他们曾在元、推特、Snap、微软和网飞等科技巨头担任领导职务。在本期节目中，我们深入探讨了如何以及为何打造个人品牌，如何应对冒名顶替综合症，以及阿尔西在Clubhouse的经历和斯里拉姆与扎克伯格合作的故事。阿尔西和斯里拉姆分享了他们从过去失败中吸取的教训，以及他们在社区建设、技术乐观主义方面的经验，斯里拉姆还对“工作完成框架”提出了自己的看法。

summary.en: Sriram and Aarthi share lessons from building, operating, and investing across tech, including a pointed critique of the Jobs-to-be-Done framework and what they'd use instead. They discuss how to pick roles, the value of learning in public, and the behind-the-scenes of getting famously hard-to-book guests on their show. The conversation is wide-ranging, funny, and full of practitioner wisdom on careers and product.
summary.zh: Sriram 与 Aarthi 分享了横跨科技圈打造、运营与投资的经验，包括对“待办任务（Jobs-to-be-Done）”框架的尖锐批评，以及他们会用什么来取代它。他们讨论了如何选择职位、公开学习的价值，以及把那些出了名难约的嘉宾请上节目的幕后故事。对话涉猎广泛、妙趣横生，充满了关于职业与产品的实践者智慧。

episodeTitle.en: Career frameworks, A/B testing, onboarding tips, selling to engineers |  Laura Schaffer (Amplitude)
episodeTitle.zh: 职业框架、A/B测试、上手指南、向工程师推销 | 劳拉·沙弗（Amplitude）

bio.en: Laura Schaffer is the Head of Growth at Amplitude, where she took over from Elena Verna, and a seasoned growth leader from prior roles at high-growth consumer products.
bio.zh: 劳拉·谢弗（Laura Schaffer）是 Amplitude 的增长负责人，接替了传奇人物 Elena Verna 的职位，也是一位在高速增长消费产品领域历练丰富的增长领导者。

guestBioOfficial.en: Laura Schaffer is the brand-new VP of Growth at Amplitude. Prior to this role, she spent over 10 years leading product management and growth teams at Twilio, Bandwidth, and Rapid. In today’s episode, we talk about the role of experimentation and data in growth, and Laura shares stories of big wins from her time leading growth teams. She explains how customer insights helped her uplevel her career and how she (surprisingly) thinks about qualitative versus quantitative data. We wrap up our conversation by discussing where the best ideas come from and what you need to know if you’re selling to developers.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 劳拉·沙弗是Amplitude新任命的增长副总裁。在此职位之前，她在Twilio、Bandwidth和Rapid担任了10多年产品管理和增长团队的领导。在今日节目中，我们将讨论实验与数据在增长中的作用，劳拉还将分享她领导增长团队期间取得的重大成功案例。她将解释客户洞察如何帮助她提升职业生涯，以及她对定性数据与定量数据的看法。我们在对话尾声讨论了最佳创意的来源，以及向开发者推销产品时需要注意的事项。

summary.en: Laura describes quietly shipping a high-impact onboarding change late at night and discovering it lifted conversion by about 5% with no personalization. She emphasizes the value of asking forgiveness rather than permission for small, reversible experiments. The episode is full of pragmatic growth-testing wisdom from a seasoned operator.
summary.zh: 劳拉讲述了她如何在深夜悄悄上线一个影响重大的 onboarding 改动，结果发现无需任何个性化就提升了约 5% 的转化率。她强调了对于小而可逆的实验，"先斩后奏"的价值。本期充满了来自资深增长操盘手的务实实验智慧。

episodeTitle.en: Lessons from scaling Stripe | Claire Hughes Johnson (ex-COO of Stripe)
episodeTitle.zh: 从扩展Stripe中吸取的经验教训 | 克莱尔·休斯·约翰逊（Stripe前COO）

bio.en: Claire Hughes Johnson was COO of Stripe for seven years, helping scale it from a startup to a legendary company, and previously spent a decade at Google; she's the author of Scaling People.
bio.zh: Claire Hughes Johnson 曾任 Stripe 首席运营官七年，帮助其从初创公司成长为传奇企业，此前在 Google 工作了十年；她是《Scaling People》一书的作者。

guestBioOfficial.en: Claire Hughes Johnson is the former COO at Stripe where she helped scale the company from a small startup to the legendary company it is today. She also spent close to 10 years at Google, where she filled several executive roles including VP of Global Online Sales and Director of Sales and Ops for Gmail, YouTube, Google Apps, and AdWords. Claire shares invaluable insights from her upcoming book, Scaling People, on how to successfully build and scale organizations. We talk about the importance of building self-awareness and Claire gives tons of tactical advice on how to say things that are hard to say, as well as how to improve your internal communications and so much more.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 克莱尔·休斯·约翰逊（Claire Hughes Johnson）曾担任Stripe公司的首席运营官，助力该公司从一家小型初创企业成长为如今享誉全球的传奇公司。她还在谷歌任职近10年，先后担任过全球在线销售副总裁，以及Gmail、YouTube、Google Apps和AdWords等产品的销售与运营总监。克莱尔在即将出版的新书《Scaling People》中分享了如何成功打造和扩展组织的宝贵见解。我们探讨了提升自我意识的重要性，并获取了她关于如何说出那些难以启齿的话语、如何优化内部沟通等诸多实用建议。

summary.en: Claire digs into the meaty topics from her book Scaling People: building your operational cadence, defining company and personal operating principles, and designing your company's operating system. She argues for being a force for positive momentum and making decisions rather than getting stuck waiting to be told. The conversation is a practical guide to scaling organizations and the people within them.
summary.zh: Claire 深入探讨了其著作《Scaling People》的核心议题：建立运营节奏、定义公司与个人的运营原则，以及设计公司的“操作系统”。她主张成为“正向 momentum”的推动者，主动做决策而非卡在“等被指示”上。对话是扩展组织及其中人才的实用指南。

episodeTitle.en: Lessons from working with 600+ YC startups | Gustaf Alströmer (Y Combinator, Airbnb)
episodeTitle.zh: 从600多家YC初创公司中汲取经验 | 古斯塔夫·阿尔斯特罗默（Y Combinator、Airbnb）

bio.en: Gustaf Alstromer is a group partner at Y Combinator, where he has worked with 600+ startups, and previously started Airbnb's original growth team; he is also a driving force behind YC's focus on climate tech.
bio.zh: Gustaf Alstromer 是 Y Combinator 的集团合伙人，已辅导 600 多家初创公司，此前创办了 Airbnb 最初的增长团队；他也是 YC 聚焦气候科技的重要推动者。

guestBioOfficial.en: Gustaf Alströmer is a Group Partner at Y Combinator, where he has worked with over 600 startups. He’s also a fellow Airbnb alumnus and even started the original Airbnb growth team. In today’s podcast, Gustaf discusses common reasons startups fail and how he helps coach founders on avoiding these mistakes. He explains the attributes that the best founders tend to have, and signs that a company has potential. We also cover the growing space of climate tech, for which Gustaf has a huge passion and where he’s already had an incredible impact. He shares some key areas of innovation and investment in climate tech, some notable companies he’s helped fund, and where he sees potential going forward.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 古斯塔夫·阿尔斯特罗默（Gustaf Alströmer）是Y Combinator的集团合伙人，曾与600多家初创公司合作。他还是Airbnb的前员工，甚至曾创立了Airbnb最初的增长团队。在今天的播客中，古斯塔夫探讨了初创公司失败的常见原因，以及他如何帮助创业者避免这些错误。他解释了优秀创业者通常具备的特质，并指出判断一家公司是否具有潜力的关键信号。我们还讨论了气候科技这一快速发展的领域——古斯塔夫对此充满热情，并已在该领域产生了重大影响。他分享了气候科技领域的关键创新与投资方向，介绍了自己助力融资的知名公司，并展望了未来潜力所在。

summary.en: Gustaf boils startup failure down to one root cause—not talking to users, and therefore never finding product-market fit—and shares the most common mistakes YC founders make and the advice partners give most often. He covers the attributes of successful founders, why having a technical co-founder matters, and how YC's 'make things people want' still holds. The conversation also dives into climate tech: why momentum has shifted, what's new and exciting, and how to think about entering the space.
summary.zh: Gustaf 把创业失败归结为一个根本原因——不与用户交谈，因而永远找不到产品市场契合，并分享了 YC 创始人最常见的错误以及合伙人最常说起的建议。他谈到了成功创始人的共性、为何技术联合创始人至关重要，以及 YC 的“做人们想要的东西”为何至今成立。对话还深入气候科技：势头为何转变、有什么新鲜而令人兴奋的事，以及想进入这个领域该如何思考。

episodeTitle.en: Behind the scenes of Calendly’s rapid growth | Annie Pearl (CPO)
episodeTitle.zh: Calendly快速增长的幕后故事 | 安妮·珀尔（首席产品官）

bio.en: Annie Pearl is Chief Product Officer at Calendly, previously CPO at Glassdoor and a product director at Fox, with experience across consumer and B2B product.
bio.zh: Annie Pearl 是 Calendly 首席产品官，此前曾任 Glassdoor 首席产品官及 Fox 产品总监，在消费级与 B2B 产品方面均有丰富经验。

guestBioOfficial.en: Annie Pearl is the Chief Product Officer at Calendly. Previously, she was Chief Product Officer at Glassdoor, as well as Director of Product Management at Box. She was named one of the most influential women in Bay Area business by the San Francisco Business Times. In today’s episode, Annie shares three paths into product management and advice on how to get your foot in the door. She also gives us an inside look at how Calendly’s product teams are structured, how they transitioned from solely PLG to adding a sales team and unlocking new growth levers, how they do planning, and much more.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 安妮·珀尔是Calendly的首席产品官。此前，她曾在Glassdoor担任首席产品官，并在Box担任产品管理总监。她被《旧金山商业时报》评为湾区商业最具影响力的女性之一。在本期节目中，安妮分享了三条进入产品管理的路径，并为如何踏入这一领域提供了建议。她还带我们深入了解了Calendly的产品团队架构、从纯粹的PLG到加入销售团队并开启新增长杠杆的转型过程、规划方式等等。

summary.en: Annie defines strategy as an integrated set of choices about where you'll play and how you'll win, anchored in a clear winning aspiration. She walks through how Calendly builds product and grew—including the wild story of its first 1,000 users—and how it built a sales team atop a product-led growth motion. The conversation also shares advice on getting into product management and a few killer tips for using Calendly itself.
summary.zh: Annie 将战略定义为一组关于“在哪里竞争、如何取胜”的连贯选择，锚定在清晰的取胜愿望上。她讲述了 Calendly 如何做产品、如何增长（包括获得前 1000 名用户的传奇故事），以及如何在产品驱动增长的基础上建立起销售团队。对话还分享了进入产品管理行业的建议，以及几个使用 Calendly 的绝妙技巧。

episodeTitle.en: An inside look at how CNN builds product | Upasna Gautam
episodeTitle.zh: 《CNN产品打造之道》 | 乌帕斯纳·高塔姆

bio.en: Upasna Gautam is a product and technology leader at CNN, an investor, and an advisor who builds products inside a fast-moving newsroom.
bio.zh: Upasna Gautam 是 CNN 的产品与技术领导者、一位投资人与顾问，她在节奏飞快的新闻编辑室内部打造产品。

guestBioOfficial.en: Upasna Gautam is a product manager at CNN Digital, where she works closely with editorial staff and journalists to build their internal content management system. She is also a longtime meditation coach and a board member of the News Product Alliance. In today’s episode, we delve into how product teams are structured and operate at CNN, how CNN uses OKRs and roadmaps, and the unique challenges and opportunities in designing a digital product for journalists. Upasna also shares a story about her team's product saving the day during the 2020 elections and gives listeners a free mini lesson on meditation.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 乌帕斯纳·高塔姆是CNN Digital的产品经理，她与编辑团队及记者紧密合作，共同开发内部内容管理系统。她还是资深冥想教练及新闻产品联盟董事会成员。在本期节目中，我们将深入探讨CNN产品团队的架构与运作方式、如何运用OKR与路线图，以及为记者打造数字产品的独特挑战与机遇。乌帕斯纳还分享了团队在2020年大选期间力挽狂澜的案例，并为听众奉上免费冥想小课堂。

summary.en: Upasna shares what it's like to build product inside CNN's newsroom, where breaking news constantly interrupts plans and demands thriving in chaos. She discusses bridging the gap between product and editorial through mutual trust, the power of direct customer conversations, and how mindfulness and 'equanimity' became leadership tools for staying calm under fire. The episode is a distinctive look at product management in an unconventional, high-pressure environment.
summary.zh: Upasna 分享了在 CNN 新闻编辑室内部打造产品的体验——突发新闻不断打断计划，要求人在混乱中茁壮成长。她讨论了如何通过相互信任弥合产品与采编之间的鸿沟、直接客户对话的力量，以及正念与“情绪平稳（equanimity）”如何成为在压力下保持冷静的领导力工具。本期是对非常规、高压环境下产品管理的独特透视。

episodeTitle.en: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)
episodeTitle.zh: 《如何白手起家打造价值2亿美元的企业 | 帕特里克·坎贝尔（ProfitWell）》

bio.en: I highly doubt it. I hope that doesn't happen. I've wanted to get you on this podcast ever since I started this podcast. It's always been on my list. You're just generally one of the smartest humans and most amazing humans I know, and so thank you for joining me on this podcast.
bio.zh: 我非常怀疑这一点。我希望这种情况不会发生。自从我开始做这个播客以来，我就一直想邀请你上节目。它一直在我的待办清单上。你无疑是我认识的最聪明、最了不起的人之一，所以感谢你能来参加我的播客。

guestBioOfficial.en: Patrick Campbell is the founder and CEO of ProfitWell, which he bootstrapped and sold for over $200 million. In this special episode, we explore 10 big ideas from Patrick, including tips for hiring employees who align with your company values, creating winning pricing and retention strategies, determining the right time to raise money, and more. Whether you’re just starting out or looking to scale your SaaS business, this must-listen episode offers practical and actionable advice that will help you avoid missteps and think differently.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 帕特里克·坎贝尔是ProfitWell的创始人兼CEO，他白手起家将公司卖出超过2亿美元。在这期特别节目中，我们将探讨帕特里克的10大理念，包括如何招聘与公司价值观一致的员工、制定成功的定价和留存策略、确定合适的融资时机等。无论您是初创企业还是希望扩大SaaS业务规模，这期必听节目都将为您提供实用可行的建议，帮助您避免误区，突破思维。

summary.en: The bratty thing here is that real professional ship. At the end of the day, real... I don't care if you're a marketer or a product person, engineer, ops person, people ops, real professional ship, and they ship at a pretty high frequency for whatever they're doing. In my opinion, your tempo framework is more important
summary.zh: 这里关键的是真正的专业精神。归根结底，真正的……无论你是营销人员、产品经理、工程师、运维人员还是人力资源人员，真正的专业精神，他们会以相当高的频率交付成果。对我来说，你的节奏框架更为重要。

episodeTitle.en: Understanding the role of product ops | Christine Itwaru (Pendo)
episodeTitle.zh: 产品运营角色的理解 | 克里斯汀·伊特瓦鲁（Pendo）

bio.en: Christine Itwaru is a long-time product ops leader at Pendo who transitioned into the role from product management and helps explain what product ops actually does.
bio.zh: Christine Itwaru 是 Pendo 长期的产品运营（product ops）负责人，从产品管理转岗而来，致力于解释产品运营到底做什么。

guestBioOfficial.en: Christine Itwaru is a longtime product operations leader at Pendo and more recently has taken on the larger role of Principal Strategist there. Before leading product ops, Christine spent 12 years in product management. In this episode, we delve into the rapidly growing field of product ops and discover how Christine is part of shaping the role industry-wide. She helps us define the role of product operations, what kind of person would be a good fit for the product ops role, when your company would benefit from product ops, and what red flags to look for if you decide to go down this path.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 克里斯汀·伊特瓦鲁（Christine Itwaru）是Pendo的长期产品运营负责人，并于近期晋升为首席策略师。在领导产品运营之前，克里斯汀曾在产品管理领域深耕12年。在本期节目中，我们将深入探讨快速发展的产品运营领域，了解克里斯汀如何在行业内塑造这一角色。她帮助我们定义产品运营的角色、适合该角色的特质、何时公司会从产品运营中获益，以及若决定走上这条路应注意哪些危险信号。

summary.en: Christine explains what product ops people do day to day, where the line sits between their role and product management, and whether your company would benefit from the function. She discusses whether ops roles in general signal inefficiency and shares why staying close to customer pain is non-negotiable. The conversation is an accessible primer on a rapidly rising function many teams still misunderstand.
summary.zh: Christine 解释了产品运营人员每天的职责、他们的角色与产品管理的边界，以及你的公司是否会从这一职能中受益。她探讨了运营类角色是否意味着组织低效，并分享了为何贴近客户痛苦不可替代。对话是对这个快速崛起、却仍被许多团队误解的职能的清晰入门。

episodeTitle.en: Mastering onboarding | Lauryn Isford (Head of Growth at Airtable)
episodeTitle.zh: 《掌控入职流程 | 劳瑞恩·伊斯福德（Airtable增长负责人）》

bio.en: Lauryn Isford is a growth leader who was most recently Head of Growth at Airtable, and previously led product growth at Facebook and growth for Blue Bottle's e-commerce.
bio.zh: 劳琳·伊斯福德（Lauryn Isford）是一位增长负责人，最近担任 Airtable 的增长负责人，此前曾在 Facebook 领导产品增长，并负责 Blue Bottle 电商业务的增长。

guestBioOfficial.en: Lauryn Isford is a product growth leader and practitioner, who most recently led Growth at Airtable, and is about to start something new 🤫.  In today’s episode, we get into the many tactics Lauryn has learned about optimizing onboarding flows. Lauryn describes how overhauling Airtable’s onboarding led to a 20% increase in activation rate, the company’s unique segmentation process, and why North Star metrics are so vital. Lauryn also shares her framework for a PLG growth funnel, and how to use a reverse trial to leverage the benefits of both freemium products and trials. If you’re looking to find growth opportunities within your funnel, this episode is for you.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 劳瑞恩·伊斯福德（Lauryn Isford）是一位产品增长领袖和实践者，近期在Airtable担任增长部门负责人，即将开启新征程🤫。在本期节目中，我们将深入探讨劳瑞恩在优化入职流程方面的诸多成功策略。她将分享如何通过全面改革Airtable的入职流程，使激活率提升20%，以及公司独特的细分用户流程。同时，她将阐释北极星指标为何至关重要。此外，劳瑞恩还将分享其PLG增长漏斗框架，以及如何利用反向试用模式，充分发挥免费增值产品和试用期的双重优势。如果你正寻求在增长漏斗中挖掘潜力，这期节目不容错过。

summary.en: Lauryn makes the counterintuitive point that a lower activation rate (e.g., 5-15%) is often healthier than a high one, because it correlates with long-term retention. She dives deep into onboarding as one of the most undervalued growth levers and how to find your true activation metric. The episode is a tactical master class on activation and onboarding optimization.
summary.zh: 劳琳提出了一个反直觉的观点：较低的激活率（例如 5%-15%）往往比高激活率更健康，因为它与长期留存更相关。她深入探讨了 onboarding（新用户引导）这一被严重低估的增长杠杆，以及如何找到真正的激活指标。本期是关于激活与新用户引导优化的战术大师课。

episodeTitle.en: Leading with empathy | Keith Yandell (DoorDash, Uber)
episodeTitle.zh: 以同理心为先 | 基思·扬德尔（DoorDash、Uber）

bio.en: Keith Yandell is a longtime DoorDash leader who has run the company's legal, HR, customer support, marketing, and corporate development teams, and previously led litigation at Uber.
bio.zh: 基思·扬德尔（Keith Yandell）是 DoorDash 的资深领导者，曾执掌公司的法务、人力资源、客户支持、市场营销以及企业发展团队，此前在 Uber 负责诉讼业务。

guestBioOfficial.en: Keith Yandell started at DoorDash as Chief Legal Officer and during his tenure has also led the HR, Customer Support, Marketing, and now Corporate Development teams. In today’s episode, we talk about leadership, and how to lead with empathy. We dig into DoorDash’s unique culture and touch on the WeDash program, which requires every employee to complete four deliveries a year in order to better understand the customer experience. Keith shares his “How to Work with Keith” document and discusses the importance of openness in the workplace. He also gives some tips for founders on hiring, engaging with legal, and how to make big decisions when teams are competing for resources.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 基思·扬德尔最初以首席法务官的身份加入DoorDash，在任职期间，他还先后领导过人力资源、客户支持、市场营销以及现任的企业发展团队。在本期节目中，我们将探讨领导力，以及如何以同理心进行领导。我们将深入解析DoorDash独特的企业文化，并提及“WeDash”计划——该计划要求每位员工每年完成四次配送任务，以更好地理解客户体验。基思分享了他的“如何与基思共事”文件，并讨论了职场开放的重要性。他还为创业者提供了招聘建议、与法律团队合作的技巧，以及在团队争夺资源时如何做出重大决策。

summary.en: Keith describes how a founder's drive is the single most decisive factor in a startup's survival through repeated rejection. He explains DoorDash's "no politics, no asshole" culture and the WeDash program that builds empathy by having employees deliver food. The episode offers a master class in leading diverse functions with empathy and giving people honest, growth-oriented feedback.
summary.zh: 基思指出，创始人的那股冲劲，是初创公司在一次次被拒绝后依然存活的最决定性因素。他阐释了 DoorDash"无政治、无混蛋"的文化，以及通过让员工亲自送餐来建立同理心的 WeDash 项目。本期是关于如何以同理心领导多元职能、并给予人们诚实且利于成长的反馈的大师课。

episodeTitle.en: AI and product management | Marily Nika (Meta, Google)
episodeTitle.zh: AI与产品管理 | 玛丽莉·尼卡（Meta、谷歌）

bio.en: Marily Nika is an AI Product Lead at Meta (Reality Labs) and was an AI product manager at Google for eight years; she holds a PhD in Machine Learning and teaches AI Product Management.
bio.zh: 玛丽丽·尼卡（Marily Nika）是 Meta（Reality Labs）的 AI 产品负责人，此前在 Google 做了八年 AI 产品经理；她拥有机器学习博士学位，并教授 AI 产品管理课程。

guestBioOfficial.en: Marily is a computer scientist and an AI Product Leader currently working for Meta’s reality labs, and previously at Google for 8 years. In 2014 she completed a PhD in Machine Learning. She is also an Executive Fellow at Harvard Business School and she has taught numerous courses, actively teaching AI Product Management on Maven and at Harvard. Marily joins us in today's episode to shed light on the role of AI in product management. She shares her insights on how AI is empowering her work, and why she believes that every Product Manager will be an AI Product Manager in the future. We also discuss why PM’s should learn a bit of coding, where they can learn it, and best practices for working with data scientists. Marily shares some insight into building her AI Product Management course and also why she full-heartedly believes you should also create your own course.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 玛丽莉是一位计算机科学家和AI产品负责人，目前就职于Meta的Reality Labs，此前在谷歌工作了8年。她于2014年完成了机器学习博士学位，同时是哈佛商学院的执行研究员，曾在Maven和哈佛大学教授多门课程。在本期节目中，玛丽莉将为我们解读AI在产品管理中的角色。她将分享AI如何助力她的工作，及为何她相信未来每位产品经理都将成为AI产品经理。我们还将探讨产品经理为何应学习编程、在哪里学习编程，以及与数据科学家合作的最佳实践。玛丽莉还将分享她开发AI产品管理课程的经验，以及为何她坚信你也应该创建自己的课程。

summary.en: Marily argues every PM will become an AI PM because nearly every product needs personalization and recommender systems. She shares how ChatGPT helps her write mission statements and user personas, and why PMs should learn basic coding. The episode is a practical guide to working with data scientists and shipping AI features responsibly.
summary.zh: 玛丽丽认为，每个 PM 终将变成 AI PM，因为几乎每个产品都需要个性化与推荐系统。她分享了如何用 ChatGPT 撰写使命宣言与用户画像，以及 PM 为何该学一点编程。本期是一份关于如何与数据科学家协作、负责任地上线 AI 功能的实用指南。

episodeTitle.en: How to foster innovation and big thinking | Eeke de Milliano (Retool, Stripe)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何培育创新与大胆思维 | 伊克·德·米利亚诺（Retool、Stripe）

bio.en: Eeke de Milliano is the head of product at Retool and was one of Stripe's earliest product managers, where she helped build foundational products like Stripe Checkout, Connect, Radar, and Chargeback Protection.
bio.zh: Eeke de Milliano 是 Retool 的产品负责人，也是 Stripe 最早的产品经理之一，曾参与打造 Stripe Checkout、Connect、Radar 和 Chargeback Protection 等基础产品。

guestBioOfficial.en: Eeke de Milliano is the Head of Product at Retool and a former product lead at Stripe. In this episode, we discuss how any team can become an innovation machine. We talk about how a culture of writing led to a team of rigorous thinkers at Stripe. We cover tactics to breed innovative teams that you can replicate at your own company: From embracing retrospectives to creating systems that give individuals the "permission to think big". Eeke shares her framework for prioritizing resources between core products, strategic initiatives, and big bets, and how it helped Retool launch three new products in a year. She also gives a comprehensive overview of the right level of process for companies of different sizes, and how to build a talent portfolio.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 伊克·德·米利亚诺是Retool的产品负责人，曾任Stripe的产品主管。在本期节目中，我们讨论如何让任何团队成为创新机器。我们谈到写作文化如何在Stripe培养出一批严谨思考者。我们分享了培养创新团队的策略，您可以在自己的公司复制：从接受回顾到建立让个人“敢于大胆思考”的制度。伊克分享了在核心产品、战略举措和重大赌注之间分配资源的框架，以及如何助力Retool一年内推出三款新产品。她还全面概述了不同规模公司应采用的合理流程，以及如何构建人才组合。

summary.en: Eeke frames process as inherently variance-reducing—useful for lifting the average but often dragging down the highest performers—and explains how the right amount of process changes by company stage. She digs into what made Stripe's internal culture so uniquely innovative and how to foster and protect innovation as an organization grows. She also shares her approach to building a 'talent portfolio'—intentionally composing a team with complementary strengths rather than hiring clones.
summary.zh: Eeke 将流程本质视为“降低方差”——它能拉高平均水平，却常常拖累最优秀的人才，并解释了流程的恰当程度如何随公司阶段而变化。她深入剖析了 Stripe 内部文化为何如此独特且具创新性，以及组织壮大时如何培养和保护创新。她还分享了打造“人才组合”的方法——有意识地把优势互补的人组合成团队，而非招一批同质化的人。

episodeTitle.en: Lessons from Airtable’s unconventional growth strategy | Zoelle Egner
episodeTitle.zh: Airtable非传统增长策略的启示 | 佐尔·埃格纳

bio.en: Zoelle Egner was one of the earliest employees at Airtable (leading early marketing and customer success), later advised dozens of startups, and is now head of marketing and growth at Block Party.
bio.zh: Zoelle Egner 是 Airtable 最早的员工之一（领导早期营销与客户成功团队），后来为数十家初创公司提供顾问服务，如今是 Block Party 的营销与增长负责人。

guestBioOfficial.en: Zoelle Egner is best known for her time at Airtable (currently valued at $11 billion), where she was the 11th employee and built and led the initial marketing and customer success teams. Currently she’s the Head of Marketing and Growth at Block Party, a company that designs consumer tools for online safety and anti-harassment. In today’s episode, we explore the marketing strategies that helped Airtable punch above its weight and build an established brand. We also dig into how Airtable was able to find its first super-users, how customer success played a key role in getting early traction, and the do’s and don’ts for marketing investments. Zoelle also shares her experience working for VaccinateCA (which ended up playing a massive role in helping get people vaccinated during the pandemic) and several tips for obtaining valuable customer feedback.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 佐尔·埃格纳最为人熟知的身份是Airtable（当前估值110亿美元）的第11位员工，她在那里组建并领导了首批营销和客户成功团队。目前，她是Block Party（致力于设计在线安全与反骚扰消费者工具的公司）的营销与增长负责人。本期节目中，我们将剖析助力Airtable脱颖而出的营销策略，深入解析如何挖掘首批超级用户、客户成功如何助力早期吸引力，及营销投资的取舍。佐尔还分享了她在VaccinateCA（在疫情期间为疫苗接种提供重要助力）的经验，以及获取宝贵客户反馈的几大技巧。

summary.en: Zoelle shares lessons from Airtable's earliest days, including how the team broke into tech, built a marketing machine, and used templates and billboards to drive bottom-up growth. She discusses the power of storytelling, why customer success and marketing should be one team, and tactics for punching above your weight as a small startup. The episode is a rich, operator's guide to early-stage marketing and growth.
summary.zh: Zoelle 分享了 Airtable 最早时期的经验，包括团队如何打入科技圈、打造营销机器，以及用模板和广告牌驱动自下而上的增长。她讨论了讲故事的力量、为何客户成功与营销应当合为同一支团队，以及小初创公司“以小博大”的战术。本期是一份丰富的、关于早期营销与增长的运营者指南。

episodeTitle.en: An inside look at Mixpanel’s product journey | Vijay Iyengar
episodeTitle.zh: Mixpanel产品历程解析 | 维贾伊·伊扬加尔

bio.en: Vijay Iyengar is Head of Product at Mixpanel, and like Lenny came from an engineering background before moving into product.
bio.zh: Vijay Iyengar 是 Mixpanel 的产品负责人，和 Lenny 一样，他也是从工程背景转向产品的。

guestBioOfficial.en: Vijay Iyengar is Head of Product at Mixpanel, and similar to myself, came from an engineering background before transitioning to product. In today’s episode, he explains how Mixpanel has evolved its growth strategy from a fast-paced, feature-focused approach to a more deliberate approach that prioritizes design and user experience. He also shares how Mixpanel irons out customer problems, including implementing internal tools that allow engineering and product teams to respond to customer feedback directly. Additionally, Vijay shares his top SaaS products, books, frameworks, and more. Tune in to gain valuable insights from a seasoned product leader.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 维杰·伊扬格（Vijay Iyengar）是Mixpanel的产品主管，与我一样，他在转行产品经理之前也有工程师背景。在本期节目中，他解释了Mixpanel如何从快节奏、以功能为核心的增长策略，转向更加注重设计和用户体验的谨慎方法。他还分享了Mixpanel如何解决客户问题的方法，包括开发内部工具，让工程和产品团队能够直接响应客户反馈。此外，维杰还分享了他最推崇的SaaS产品、书籍、框架等内容。快来收听，聆听这位资深产品领袖的宝贵见解吧。

summary.en: Vijay shares Mixpanel's product journey, explaining how its growth strategy evolved from a fast-paced, feature-focused approach to a more deliberate one that prioritizes design and user experience. He covers how Mixpanel closes the loop on customer problems with internal tools that let engineering and product respond directly to feedback, plus his favorite SaaS products and frameworks. The episode is a grounded look at scaling product at a data-analytics company.
summary.zh: Vijay 分享了 Mixpanel 的产品历程，解释了它的增长战略如何从“快节奏、以功能为中心”演进为更审慎、优先考量设计与用户体验的方式。他涵盖了 Mixpanel 如何用内部工具打通客户问题的闭环、让工程与产品直接回应反馈，以及他最爱的 SaaS 产品与框架。本期是对一家数据分析公司规模化产品的扎实透视。

episodeTitle.en: How to nail your product positioning | April Dunford (Obviously Awesome)
episodeTitle.zh: 《如何精准定位你的产品 | 阿普里尔·邓福德（Obviously Awesome）》

bio.en: April Dunford is the author of "Obviously Awesome" and one of the world's leading product-positioning experts, with 25 years as a B2B VP of marketing and 200+ tech companies advised (including Epic Games and Google); she turned her five-step positioning method — competitive alternatives, differentiated capabilities, value themes, best-fit customers, market category — into a book that helps founders, PMs, and GTM teams turn positioning from a fuzzy concept into an executable sales story.
bio.zh: April Dunford 是《Obviously Awesome》的作者、全球最权威的产品定位专家之一，拥有 25 年 B2B 营销 VP 经验，合作过 200 多家科技公司（含 Epic Games、Google 等）；她把自己的「五步定位法」（竞争替代方案→差异化能力→价值主题→最佳契合客户→市场品类）写成书，帮助创始人、PM 和 GTM 团队把「定位」从模糊的概念变成可执行的销售故事。

guestBioOfficial.en: April Dunford is the author of the must-read best-selling book Obviously Awesome, a definitive guide to product positioning. She spent 25 years leading marketing, product, and sales teams and now runs her own consulting firm, helping companies of all shapes and sizes nail their positioning. April has worked hands-on with over 200 companies on positioning, including Google, IBM, Postman, and Epic Games. In this episode, April delves into the intricacies of positioning, including its distinction from messaging and branding, and shares real-world examples of products with strong and weak positioning. Additionally, April shares her insights on when to bring in a professional and the key differences between segmentation and personas. Don't miss this opportunity to gain valuable knowledge from a true industry leader.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 阿普里尔·邓福德（April Dunford）是畅销书《Obviously Awesome》（《显而易见的出色》）的作者，这本指南堪称产品定位的权威。她拥有25年领导营销、产品和销售团队的经验，目前经营自己的咨询公司，帮助各种规模的公司精准定位产品。阿普里尔曾与谷歌、IBM、Postman和Epic Games等200多家公司合作进行定位优化。在本期节目中，阿普里尔深入探讨了定位的奥秘，包括其与营销信息和品牌塑造的区别，并分享了产品定位成功与失败的真实案例。此外，她还分享了何时引入专业团队的见解，以及细分市场与用户画像的关键差异。不要错过向行业领袖学习宝贵知识的机会。

summary.en: April Dunford defines positioning as "how your product is best in the world at delivering value a well-defined set of customers cares about" and lays out an actionable five-step method: figure out what you must beat (status quo plus shortlist), list differentiated capabilities, translate them into value themes, define your best-fit customers, then pick the market category that makes that value obvious. She stresses positioning is a team sport — marketing, product, sales, and the CEO must align or everyone tells a different story — and the output is not just a doc but a testable sales narrative. Weak-positioning signals include customers saying "say that again" or "I can do that in a spreadsheet" on sales calls. She also clears up common confusions: positioning is the upstream input to messaging and branding; early products should keep a loose "positioning thesis" and let the market pull them toward the real fit (like a net cast wide, then tightened); and in a B2B purchase with 5–7 people involved, the only persona that matters is the "champion" in the account, whom all marketing should first arm.
summary.zh: April Dunford 把定位定义为「你的产品如何最好地交付某组客户非常在乎的价值」，并给出一个可执行的五步法：先想清楚你要打败什么（现状+短名单），再列差异化能力、翻译成价值主题、定义最佳契合客户、最后选让价值 obvious 的市场品类。她强调定位是团队运动——市场、产品、销售、CEO 必须一起达成一致，否则各说各话；输出不只是一份文档，而是一个能测试的销售叙事。弱定位的信号包括客户在销售电话里说「再说一遍」或「我用表格就能做」。她还厘清了几个常见混淆：定位是 messaging 和品牌的上游输入；早期产品应保持「定位假设」松一点、让市场把你拉向真正契合的细分（像渔网先撒宽、再收紧）；在 B2B 购买里 5–7 人参与，但唯一关键的人物画像是「账户里的 champion（推手）」，所有营销都应先武装他。

episodeTitle.en: How to build your product strategy stack | Ravi Mehta (Tinder, Facebook, Tripadvisor, Outpace)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何构建你的产品战略体系 | 拉维·梅塔（Tinder、Facebook、Tripadvisor、Outpace）

bio.en: Ravi Mehta is co-founder and CEO of Outpace and a veteran product leader who was Chief Product Officer at Tinder, Product Director at Facebook, and VP of Product at Tripadvisor.
bio.zh: Ravi Mehta 是 Outpace 的联合创始人兼 CEO，也是一位资深产品领导者，曾任 Tinder 首席产品官、Facebook 产品总监，以及 Tripadvisor 产品副总裁。

guestBioOfficial.en: Ravi was previously CPO at Tinder, Product Director at Facebook, and VP of Product at Tripadvisor. Currently, he’s co-founder and CEO of Outpace, a coaching platform designed to help people reach their professional goals. In today’s podcast, we dive deep into Ravi’s product strategy stack framework and how it was used to develop a powerful strategy at Tinder. We also cover his other popular frameworks—the frontier of understanding and exponential feedback—and how both of them can help you grow in your career. We discuss the differences between building product at a startup versus a large tech company, and how Ravi has had to shift his mindset as he’s moved away from a product leadership role into a founder role. Finally, he shares a bit about how Outpace is using AI to amplify coaches and help make them more efficient and effective.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 拉维此前曾担任Tinder的首席产品官、Facebook的产品总监，以及TripAdvisor的产品副总裁。目前，他是教练平台Outpace的联合创始人兼首席执行官，该平台致力于帮助人们实现职业目标。在今天的播客中，我们深入探讨了拉维的产品战略堆栈框架，以及该框架如何助力Tinder制定强有力的战略。我们还将探讨他的其他热门框架——理解的前沿与指数级反馈——以及这两个框架如何助力您在职业生涯中成长。我们将讨论在初创公司与大型科技公司中构建产品的差异，以及拉维如何在从产品领导角色转向创始人角色的过程中转变思维模式。最后，他将分享Outpace如何利用人工智能提升教练效率、提高工作成效。

summary.en: Ravi shares the mindshifts required when moving from a big-company product leader to a founder, especially the difference between speed (volume of work) and latency (time to learn from an idea). He explains why plugging into an early-stage founder network early matters more than relying on a big-company network, and introduces his 'product strategy stack' for separating goals, roadmaps, and strategy. The episode is rich with advice for PMs aspiring to start companies.
summary.zh: Ravi 分享了从大公司产品领导者转型为创始人所需的心智转变，尤其是“速度（工作量）”与“延迟（从想法中学习的耗时）”的区别。他解释了为何尽早接入早期创业网络，比依赖大公司人脉更重要，并介绍了用于区分目标、路线图与战略的“产品战略栈（product strategy stack）”。本期为有志创业的 PM 提供了丰富建议。

episodeTitle.en: What differentiates the highest-performing product teams | John Cutler (The Beautiful Mess)
episodeTitle.zh: 高绩效产品团队的秘诀 | 约翰·卡特勒（John Cutler，The Beautiful Mess）

bio.en: John Cutler is one of the most prolific and beloved writers on product management online and a product evangelist at Amplitude, where his unique role has put him in front of a huge share of the world's product teams; he explores what separates high-performing teams from the rest.
bio.zh: John Cutler 是网络上最高产、最受喜爱的产品管理写作者之一，也是 Amplitude 的产品布道师；他独特的工作角色让他接触到了全球很大比例的产品团队，他致力于探究高效团队与普通团队的区别。

guestBioOfficial.en: John Cutler writes the popular and beloved product newsletter The Beautiful Mess. For many years, he was a Product Evangelist at Amplitude, where he ended up meeting and working with a large number of product teams around the world. Through this role, he gained unique insight into how the best product teams operate. In today’s episode, John reflects on leaving his role at Amplitude and explains the attributes that the top 1% of product teams share and the varying ways that companies achieve these core elements. We go deep into some of his favorite frameworks and discuss the best way to apply these frameworks to your work. We also unpack skills like product sense and product mindset, and what he’s planning in his new role at Toast.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 约翰·卡特勒（John Cutler）撰写广受欢迎且深受喜爱的产品通讯《The Beautiful Mess》。多年来，他在Amplitude担任产品布道师，最终结识并与全球众多产品团队合作。通过这一角色，他对顶级产品团队的运作方式有了独特见解。在本期节目中，约翰回顾了他离开Amplitude的经历，解释了顶级1%产品团队共有的特质，以及各公司实现这些核心要素的不同方式。我们深入探讨了他最喜欢的框架，并讨论了如何将这些框架应用于工作。我们还解析了产品感和产品思维等技能，以及他在Toast新职位上的规划。

summary.en: John tackles what differentiates the highest-performing product teams from underperformers—noting that weak teams fail in similar ways while strong teams succeed in many different ones—and why you should be skeptical of the frameworks and tools you read about online. He argues real change starts with self-awareness and an authentic leadership 'vibe' you can flex from, and that the process-versus-people investment question begins with what you actually believe. True to form, it became Lenny's longest episode yet, packed with nuance on making product teams better.
summary.zh: John 探讨了高效产品团队与一般团队的区别——指出弱势团队以相似的方式失败，而强势团队则以多种不同方式成功——以及为何你应对网上读到的框架与工具保持怀疑。他主张真正的改变始于自我觉察，以及一种你可以从中灵活调整的、真实的领导“气质”，而“流程 vs. 人”该投资哪边，起点是你真正相信什么。一如常态，这成了 Lenny 史上最长的一期，充满让产品团队变得更好的细腻洞见。

episodeTitle.en: How to price your product | Naomi Ionita (Menlo Ventures)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何为你的产品定价 | 娜奥米·伊奥尼塔（Naomi Ionita，Menlo Ventures）

bio.en: Naomi Ionita is a Partner at Menlo Ventures, was one of the first B2B product-led growth leaders at Evernote and Invoice2go, and an early mentor at Reforge.
bio.zh: 娜奥米·约尼塔（Naomi Ionita）是 Menlo Ventures 的合伙人，曾是 Evernote 与 Invoice2go 最早的一批 B2B 产品驱动增长（PLG）领导者，也是 Reforge 的早期导师。

guestBioOfficial.en: Naomi Ionita is a Partner at the venture capital firm, Menlo Ventures. She started her career in engineering in 2002, shifted to product in 2006, and built product growth and monetization teams starting over a decade ago as one of the first PLG leaders in B2B. She was an early mentor at Reforge and her expertise is in building full-stack growth teams and cultures, launching new products, and helping existing products monetize and retain their users. Consider today’s episode a master class on monetization and pricing. We talk about common mistakes made by founders, specific experiments for how to determine pricing, and why initial growth sometimes comes at the expense of revenue. Naomi also introduces the concept of the Modern Growth Stack, how AI will play a role in growth, and what she’s most excited about for the future.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 娜奥米·伊奥尼塔（Naomi Ionita）是门洛风投（Menlo Ventures）公司的合伙人。她的职业生涯始于2002年的工程领域，2006年转向产品开发，十多年前就开始组建产品增长和变现团队，是B2B领域首批PLG（产品生命周期管理）领导者之一。她曾是Reforge的早期导师，专长于打造全栈式增长团队与企业文化、推出新产品，以及帮助现有产品实现变现和用户留存。本期节目将为您带来一场关于变现与定价的深度研讨。我们将探讨创始人常犯的错误、如何通过具体实验确定定价策略，以及为何初期增长有时会以牺牲营收为代价。娜奥米还将介绍现代增长堆栈（Modern Growth Stack）的概念、人工智能在增长中的作用，以及她对未来最为期待的创新。

summary.en: Naomi delivers a master class on monetization and pricing, covering common founder mistakes and concrete experiments to set price. She introduces the "Modern Growth Stack" of tools that automate growth work and discusses where AI fits. The episode also warns that early growth is sometimes achieved at the expense of revenue.
summary.zh: 娜奥米带来了一堂关于变现与定价的课，涵盖创始人常犯的错误，以及设定价格的具体实验方法。她提出了能自动化增长工作的"现代增长栈"（Modern Growth Stack）工具概念，并讨论 AI 的位置。本期还提醒：早期增长有时会以牺牲收入为代价。

episodeTitle.en: An inside look at how Figma builds product | Yuhki Yamashita (CPO of Figma)
episodeTitle.zh: 内部视角：Figma如何打造产品 | 山下勇希（Yuhki Yamashita，Figma首席产品官）

bio.en: Yuhki Yamashita is Chief Product Officer at Figma, previously led the redesign of Uber's rider/driver apps and the YouTube iOS app at Google/Microsoft.
bio.zh: Yuhki Yamashita 是 Figma 的首席产品官（CPO），此前曾领导 Uber 乘客/司机端应用的改版，以及 Google/Microsoft 时期的 YouTube iOS 应用。

guestBioOfficial.en: Yuhki Yamashita is Chief Product Officer at Figma. Prior to Figma, he was Head of Design of Uber’s New Mobility efforts, and before that a product manager at Google and Microsoft. Adding to his impressive resume, Yuhki also taught introductory computer science at Harvard. In today's episode, we talk about operationalizing quality, the case against OKRs, and how Figma isn't just known for product-led growth, but also for building a community of empowered users. Yuhki also shares why he thinks storytelling is key to being a great product manager, owning the "why," and the potential impact of Adobe's acquisition of Figma.
guestBioOfficial.zh:
山下勇基（Yuhki Yamashita）是Figma的首席产品官。在加入Figma之前，他曾担任Uber新出行业务的设计主管，此前还曾在谷歌和微软担任产品经理。除此之外，他还曾在哈佛大学教授计算机科学入门课程。  
在本期节目中，我们探讨了如何将质量体系化运作、反对OKR的理由，以及Figma为何不仅以产品驱动型增长闻名，还在构建一个赋权用户的社区。山下勇基还分享了为何他认为讲故事是成为优秀产品经理的关键，如何掌控"为什么"，以及Adobe收购Figma可能带来的影响。

summary.en: Yuhki walks through how Figma builds product, including operationalizing quality, the case against OKRs (which he deprecated in favor of 'commitments' and headlines), and why Figma is known for both product-led growth and a community of empowered users. He shares why storytelling is key to being a great PM, owning the 'why,' and the potential impact of Adobe's acquisition of Figma. The episode is a detailed inside look at one of the most admired product teams.
summary.zh: Yuhki 逐步讲解了 Figma 如何打造产品，包括“将品质操作化”、反对 OKR 的理由（他以“承诺（commitments）”与“标题（headlines）”取而代之），以及为什么 Figma 既以产品驱动增长、又以支持用户的社区著称。他分享了为何讲故事是成为优秀 PM 的关键、拥有“为什么（why）”的重要性，以及 Adobe 收购 Figma 的潜在影响。本期是对最受钦佩的产品团队之一的、详尽的內部透视。

episodeTitle.en: Leveraging mentors to uplevel your career | Jules Walter (YouTube, Slack)
episodeTitle.zh: 借助导师助力提升职业生涯 | 朱尔斯·沃尔特（YouTube、Slack）

bio.en: Jules Walter is a product leader at YouTube who was Slack's first growth PM and later led its monetization and mobile teams, and co-founded nonprofits expanding diversity in tech.
bio.zh: 朱尔斯·沃尔特（Jules Walter）是 YouTube 的产品负责人，曾是 Slack 的第一位增长产品经理，后来领导其变现与移动团队，并联合创办了推动科技行业多样性的非营利组织。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jules Walter is a product leader at YouTube and co-founder of both the Black Product Managers Network and Codepath.org. Previously, he led monetization and mobile growth teams at Slack. He’s also a very well-known leader in the broader product community. In today’s episode, we discuss the skills that matter most to PMs, and how to build those skills. We also spend quite a bit of time talking about the importance of finding mentors to help you learn new skills, how to nail your next job interview, barriers to entry for underrepresented people, and some of the most common paths into product management.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 朱尔斯·沃尔特是YouTube的产品负责人，同时也是Black Product Managers Network和Codepath.org的联合创始人。此前，他曾在Slack领导货币化和移动增长团队。他也是产品社区中广受认可的领袖。在今天的节目中，我们探讨了对产品经理最重要的技能，以及如何培养这些技能。我们还花了大量时间讨论了寻找导师帮助学习新技能的重要性、如何成功应对下一次求职面试、弱势群体进入产品管理领域的障碍，以及一些最常见的进入产品管理领域的路径。

summary.en: Jules emphasizes treating feedback as a gift by genuinely thanking people and internalizing it, even when it stings. He shares lessons on building product sense, running growth at Slack, and creating pathways for underrepresented product managers. The conversation is full of practical advice for early-career PMs on learning faster and seeking honest feedback.
summary.zh: 朱尔斯强调要把反馈当作礼物——真诚道谢并内化吸收，哪怕它让人难受。他分享了在 Slack 做增长的经验、培养产品感的体会，以及为代表性不足的产品经理创造机会的故事。本期充满对早期产品经理如何更快学习、主动寻求真实反馈的实用建议。

episodeTitle.en: Countdown of the top 10 episodes of the year
episodeTitle.zh: 年度十大播客集锦

bio.en: A special year-end episode in which Lenny Rachitsky counts down the 10 most popular conversations from the podcast's first 50 episodes, replaying the most insightful clips from each.
bio.zh: 这是一期特别的年终回顾节目：Lenny Rachitsky 盘点了播客前 50 期中最受欢迎的 10 期对话，并重温了其中最具启发性的片段。

guestBioOfficial.en: If you ever wanted to distill 3,310 hours of knowledge into 60 minutes, then this episode is for you. For the last 6 months, Lenny’s Podcast has been downloaded more than 2 million times and is now a top 10 technology podcast across both Apple and Spotify. And in this special episode, I’m breaking down the top 10 most downloaded episodes, plus sharing my favorite lessons from each. It's unlike anything I've done before, and I hope you love it. Happy holidays, happy new year, and from the bottom of my heart, thank you so much for listening, sharing, and for supporting the podcast. I’ll see you in 2023!
guestBioOfficial.zh: 如果你想把 3,310 小时的知识浓缩成 60 分钟，那么这一期节目就是为你量身打造的。在过去的 6 个月里，Lenny’s Podcast 的下载量已超过 200 万次，目前在苹果和 Spotify 平台上均跻身科技类播客前十。在这期特别节目中，我将盘点下载量最高的十期节目，并分享每期节目中最令我深受启发的经验。这是我前所未有的尝试，希望你们会喜欢。节日快乐，新年快乐！衷心感谢你们的收听、分享和对播客的支持。2023 年见！

summary.en: Rather than a standard interview, this episode is a retrospective on the podcast's first 50 shows and over two million downloads in its first six months. Lenny counts down from the 10th to the number-one most popular episode, sharing a clip or two from each that he found most interesting or that resonated most with listeners. It's a curated highlight reel designed to help listeners revisit the best lessons from the year.
summary.zh: 这期并非标准访谈，而是对播客前 50 期节目、以及上线半年内超 200 万次下载的一次回顾。Lenny 从第 10 名倒数至第 1 名最受欢迎的节目，每期挑出一两段他觉得最有趣或最引发听众共鸣的片段。这是一期精心编排的亮点合集，帮助听众重温这一年里最宝贵的经验。

episodeTitle.en: Launching and growing a podcast | Chris Hutchins (All the Hacks, Wealthfront, Google)
episodeTitle.zh: 推出并发展播客 | 克里斯·哈钦斯（Chris Hutchins，All the Hacks、Wealthfront、谷歌）

bio.en: Chris Hutchins is a former product manager, founder, and investor who went full-time on his podcast All the Hacks, and is head of new product strategy at Wealthfront.
bio.zh: Chris Hutchins 是一位前产品经理、创始人和投资人，现已全职投入他的播客《All the Hacks》，并任 Wealthfront 新产品战略负责人。

guestBioOfficial.en: Chris Hutchins recently left his position as Head of New Product Strategy at Wealthfront to focus full-time on his podcast, All the Hacks. If you’re thinking about starting your own podcast or are simply interested in the process, be sure to check out today’s episode. We dive deep on all things podcasting: the pros and cons, how to climb the charts, and how much time you should expect to spend on each episode from start to finish. We talk in-depth about the process, from pre-production to publication, and share all of the products we use for recording, editing, and publishing. Chris also offers some important tips and tricks on how to get your first subscribers and how to market and grow your podcast, as well as some incredible money-saving hacks that you can start implementing today.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 克里斯·哈钦斯最近离开了Wealthfront新产品战略主管的职位，转而全职专注于他的播客《All the Hacks》。如果你正考虑创办自己的播客，或者只是对这个过程感兴趣，一定要收听今天的节目。我们将深入探讨播客的方方面面：其利弊、如何登上排行榜，以及每集从开始到结束预计需要投入多少时间。我们将详细讨论从前期制作到发布的整个过程，并分享我们用于录音、编辑和发布的所有产品。克里斯还将提供一些重要技巧，帮助你获得首批订阅者，以及如何推广和发展你的播客，还有一些你今天就可以开始实施的超值省钱妙招。

summary.en: Chris shares everything he's learned about launching and growing a podcast—from why simply sticking to a weekly schedule puts you in the top few percent, to the business of independent creation. He also covers bold bets he made at Wealthfront and practical ways to financially optimize your life. The conversation is a playbook for anyone considering the creator path or wanting to build an audience from scratch.
summary.zh: Chris 分享了他关于启动和增长播客的全部心得——从“坚持每周更新就能进入前百分之几”，到独立创作这门生意。他还讲述了在 Wealthfront 下的大胆赌注，以及优化个人财务的实用方法。对话是任何考虑走创作者路线、或想从零建立受众者的实战手册。

episodeTitle.en: Founder-led sales | Pete Kazanjy (Founding Sales, Atrium)
episodeTitle.zh: 创始人主导销售 | 皮特·卡赞吉（Atrium公司创始人销售总监）

bio.en: Pete Kazanjy is the author of Founding Sales - the book Lenny recommends to every B2B founder - and runs the Modern Sales Pros community; he is also CEO and founder of Atrium, a sales-analytics SaaS.
bio.zh: Pete Kazanjy 是《创始销售》（Founding Sales）一书的作者——这本书是 Lenny 推荐给每一位 B2B 创始人的必读——他运营着 Modern Sales Pros 销售社区，同时也是销售分析 SaaS 公司 Atrium 的创始人兼 CEO。

guestBioOfficial.en: Pete Kazanjy is the author of Founding Sales: The Early Stage Go-to-Market Handbook and the founder of Modern Sales Pros, an invite-only peer learning community focused on sales operations and sales leadership. He’s also the co-founder of Atrium, a B2B SaaS company that provides data-driven sales solutions. Pete got his start in product at VMware and then dove deep into the art and science of sales. In today’s episode, we talk about the importance of founder-led sales and how to methodically scale a sales department. He explains the difference between old-school sales and modern sales, which focuses on human connection and solving problems for customers. He also shares actionable tips to improve your sales technique and explains how to use data to monitor your success at different milestones in the sales process.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 皮特·卡赞吉（Pete Kazanjy）是《创始人主导销售：早期阶段市场拓展手册》一书的作者，也是仅限邀请制的同行学习社区Modern Sales Pros的创始人，该社区专注于销售运营和销售领导力。他还是B2B SaaS公司Atrium的联合创始人，Atrium提供数据驱动的销售解决方案。皮特在VMware开启产品生涯，随后深入研究销售的艺术与科学。在本期节目中，我们探讨了创始人主导销售的重要性，以及如何系统性地扩展销售团队。他解释了传统销售与现代销售的区别，后者更注重人际联系和为客户解决问题。此外，他还分享了提升销售技巧的实用建议，并讲解如何利用数据监控销售过程中的不同阶段成果。

summary.en: Pete dismantles the myth that sales is only for natural-born sellers, reframing it as a learnable craft centered on founder-led selling. He explains why founders should sell early - to shape the product, learn positioning, and build a repeatable motion before hiring - and offers a concrete heuristic: hire your first salesperson once you reliably close 15-25% of contacts. The episode is a tactical guide to modern, founder-driven B2B sales.
summary.zh: Pete 打破了“销售只属于天生销售员”的迷思，将销售重新定义为一种可习得的手艺，核心在于创始人亲自销售。他解释了创始人为何应当尽早销售——以便打磨产品、学习定位，并在招人之前建立可复制的动作——并给出了具体启发式：当你能稳定成交 15-25% 的接触对象时，就该招聘第一位销售。本期是关于现代创始人驱动型 B2B 销售的实战指南。

episodeTitle.en: How Notion leveraged community to build a $10B business | Camille Ricketts
episodeTitle.zh: Notion如何借助社区力量打造千亿美元业务 | 卡米尔·里基茨

bio.en: Camille Ricketts was the first marketing hire and longtime head of marketing at Notion, previously head of content and marketing at First Round Capital (launching First Round Review) and did comms/PR at early Tesla.
bio.zh: Camille Ricketts 是 Notion 的第一位营销员工和长期营销负责人，此前曾任 First Round Capital 内容与营销负责人（推出 First Round Review），并在早期 Tesla 负责传播与公关。

guestBioOfficial.en: Camille Ricketts began her career in journalism, at the Wall Street Journal, in 2006. In 2010 she joined Tesla, where she worked in communications alongside Elon Musk. She transitioned into marketing and became the Head of Content and Marketing at First Round Capital and then went on to become the very first marketing hire at Notion. In today’s episode, we dig into community-led growth—what it is, and when and how to pursue it. We get super-specific on how Notion championed their most loyal users and built a passionate community, and the incredible outcome it had for the company’s growth. We also talk about how to create great content, and how content can drive growth for your business and brand.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 卡米尔·里基茨2006年在《华尔街日报》开启记者生涯。2010年，她加入特斯拉，与埃隆·马斯克共事于公关部门。随后，她转战营销领域，先后担任First Round Capital的内容与营销主管，并成为Notion首位营销人才。在本期节目中，我们深入探讨社区驱动型增长——其定义、实施时机及策略。我们将详细解析Notion如何培育核心用户群体，构建充满热情的社区，以及这一策略为公司发展带来的惊人成果。我们还将探讨如何打造优质内容，以及内容如何助力企业与品牌增长。

summary.en: Camille reframes product-market fit through the lens of content-market fit—understanding who your audience is and what they need to avoid failure or gain promotion. She shares lessons from scaling Notion's marketing from near zero and from launching First Round Review, one of the most influential startup publications. The conversation is a practical playbook for content marketing, PR, and building an audience-led growth motion.
summary.zh: Camille 通过“内容市场匹配”的视角重新框定产品市场匹配——理解你的受众是谁、他们有何需求以避免失败或获得晋升。她分享了将 Notion 营销从零做大的经验，以及推出极具影响力的创业出版物 First Round Review 的历程。对话是关于内容营销、公关和打造“受众驱动增长”的实用手册。

episodeTitle.en: The art and science of pricing | Madhavan Ramanujam (Monetizing Innovation, Simon-Kucher)
episodeTitle.zh: 定价的艺术与科学 | 马达万·拉马努贾姆（《创新变现》，西蒙-库彻出版社）

bio.en: Welcome to Lenny's Podcast. I'm Lenny and my goal here is to help you get better at the craft of building and growing products. Today my guest is Madhavan Ramanujam. Madhavan is the author of Monetizing Innovation, the most widely read book on pricing strategy. He's also Senior Partner at Simon-Kuch
bio.zh: 欢迎来到Lenny的播客。我是Lenny，我的目标是帮助你提升打造和发展产品的技能。今天的嘉宾是Madhavan Ramanujam。Madhavan是《创新变现》一书的作者，该书是关于定价策略的最畅销著作。他还是Simon-Kucher & Partners的资深合伙人。

guestBioOfficial.en: Madhavan Ramanujam is a senior partner at Simon-Kucher, where he works with tier-one tech companies like Uber, Asana, and LinkedIn to help them develop their pricing and monetization strategies. He’s also the author of the most widely read book on pricing strategy, Monetizing Innovation. In today’s podcast, we talk about all the elements that go into your pricing strategy. Madhavan gives real-life examples of having conversations about “willingness to pay,” how segmentation should impact your pricing, and when to start thinking about pricing. He also shares tips on how behavioral pricing impacts your thinking, how to restructure your pricing during a downturn, and much more.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 马达万·拉马努贾姆是西蒙-库彻的高级合伙人，与优步、Asana和领英等顶级科技公司合作，帮助他们制定定价和货币化策略。他也是关于定价策略最受欢迎的书籍《创新变现》的作者。在今天的播客中，我们讨论了定价策略的所有要素。马达万给出了关于“支付意愿”对话的真实案例，细说分割策略如何影响定价，以及何时开始考虑定价。他还分享了行为定价如何影响思维、在经济低迷期间如何重组定价等诸多见解。

summary.en: When we talk about pricing, many people quickly gravitate to dollar figures. That's just a price point, that's a dollar figure. But when we think about price, we think about it as a measure. Like liter is a measure of volume, price is a measure of value. And when you think of it this way, it really stands for, do peopl
summary.zh: 当我们谈论定价时，许多人很快就会关注美元数字。这只是一个价格点，是一个具体的数字。但当我们思考价格时，我们把它视为一种衡量标准。就像升是体积的度量单位一样，价格是价值的衡量标准。从这个角度来看，它真正代表的是——用户是否认可你的价值主张。

episodeTitle.en: How to hit revenue targets in a recession | Sahil Mansuri (Bravado)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何在经济衰退中实现收入目标 | 萨希尔·曼苏里（Bravado）

bio.en: Sahil Mansuri is the CEO and founder of Bravado, which built the world's largest online sales community of over 300,000 salespeople and now builds SaaS tools for sellers, drawing on his own background as a longtime salesperson.
bio.zh: Sahil Mansuri 是 Bravado 的创始人兼 CEO，Bravado 打造了拥有超 30 万销售人员的全球最大在线销售社区，并正基于此为销售者打造 SaaS 工具；他本人也有着资深销售员的背景。

guestBioOfficial.en: Sahil Mansuri is the CEO of Bravado, the world’s largest online sales community. Sahil is passionate about sales, and his experience dates all the way back to 2008, working for Obama’s presidential campaign. During his time at Glassdoor, Sahil was able to close some incredible accounts, including Facebook, Google, Microsoft, and Amazon. In today’s podcast, we talk about why sales is a crucial part of any business and how to continue selling successfully through a recession. We get super-specific on building a conservative plan for the near future and cover everything from where to place your best salespeople to restructuring comp plans. The episode is full of great advice about how to shift with this market, improve agility, and perhaps grow an even stronger business with happier customers.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 萨希尔·曼苏里（Sahil Mansuri）是全球最大在线销售社区Bravado的首席执行官。他对销售充满热情，其从业经历可追溯至2008年，当时他曾为奥巴马的总统竞选团队工作。任职Glassdoor期间，萨希尔成功拿下包括Facebook、谷歌、微软和亚马逊在内的多个大客户。在本期播客中，我们将探讨为何销售是任何企业的核心环节，以及如何在经济低迷时期持续实现销售目标。我们将深入解析如何为近期制定保守策略，涵盖从合理配置顶级销售人才到重组薪酬计划等各个方面。这一期播客充满实战建议，助您顺应市场变化、提升敏捷性，并在满足客户需求的同时打造更强劲的业务。

summary.en: Sahil shares how founders and sales leaders should adapt forecasting, quotas, and comp plans to turbulent market conditions, using real-time data from Bravado's 300k-member network. He argues for reforecasting throughout the year rather than annual waterfall planning, and for comp structures that pay on new-business growth to keep incentives aligned. The episode is a data-grounded guide to running sales through uncertainty.
summary.zh: Sahil 分享了创始人及销售领导者应如何依据动荡的市场环境，借助 Bravado 30 万成员网络中的实时数据，来调整预测、配额与薪酬方案。他主张全年持续再预测，而非年度瀑布式规划，并提倡按“新业务增长”计酬的薪酬结构，以保持激励一致。本期是一份以数据为依据、穿越不确定性的销售运营指南。

episodeTitle.en: The ultimate guide to SEO | Ethan Smith (Graphite)
episodeTitle.zh: SEO终极指南 | 伊桑·史密斯（Graphite）

bio.en: Ethan Smith is the CEO of Graphite, a leading SEO and answer-engine-optimization (AEO) agency, and one of the most sought-after experts on how to get products to show up as answers inside LLMs like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity. With 18 years of SEO experience dating back to 2007, he advises many top B2B SaaS and e-commerce companies on capturing the fast-growing answer-engine channel.
bio.zh: Ethan Smith 是 Graphite 的 CEO，一家领先的 SEO 与答案引擎优化（AEO）机构，也是关于"如何让产品作为答案出现在 ChatGPT、Gemini、Perplexity 这类 LLM 里"最抢手的专家之一。他拥有自 2007 年起 18 年的 SEO 经验，为许多顶级 B2B SaaS 和电商公司提供顾问，帮它们抓住这个快速增长中的答案引擎渠道。

guestBioOfficial.en: Ethan Smith is the CEO of Graphite, a boutique growth agency that’s helped companies like MasterClass, Thumbtack, Robinhood, Medium, and Honey develop and execute their SEO strategies. SEO is one of the least-understood levers for growth, while also one with the biggest payoff. This episode is a true master class on all things SEO. Ethan shares a wealth of information, including when you should begin investing in SEO, how to build an SEO team, and the three main buckets of SEO. He explains the difference between topics and keywords, gives the exact heuristics and tools to help you be successful in developing and implementing your own SEO strategy, and also goes deep on how to deal with roadblocks and advocate for resources.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 伊桑·史密斯是精品增长机构Graphite的CEO，该公司曾助力MasterClass、Thumbtack、Robinhood、Medium和Honey等公司制定并执行SEO策略。SEO是增长领域中最不为人理解的杠杆之一，但同时也是回报最丰厚的领域。本期节目是SEO领域的真正大师课。伊桑分享了大量信息，包括何时应开始投资SEO、如何组建SEO团队，以及SEO的三大核心领域。他解释了主题与关键词的区别，提供了帮助您成功开发和实施自己的SEO策略的具体启发和工具，并深入探讨了如何应对障碍和争取资源。

summary.en: AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) is about getting your product cited as an answer inside LLMs; it's closely related to SEO, but the "head" (you must be mentioned as many times as possible across the summarized answer, not just rank #1) and the far larger, longer "tail" of follow-up questions work differently. Most levers overlap with traditional SEO—landing pages, YouTube videos, Reddit, affiliates, and help-center optimization—but you also need offsite citation optimization and must answer every follow-up question on your own pages; unlike Google, early-stage companies can win quickly because a citation can make them show up immediately. Track "share of voice" with an answer tracker across the few high-traffic LLM surfaces, run controlled experiments (test vs. control groups) since most published best practices are unproven, and treat Reddit by being a genuine, helpful user rather than spamming. He also warns that 100% AI-generated content does not work—it drives model collapse and gets filtered—while AI-assisted, human-edited content is the future, and that the core technology is similar enough to SEO that the "everything has changed" hype is mostly misinformation.
summary.zh: AEO（答案引擎优化）是关于让你的产品作为答案被 LLM 引用；它跟 SEO 密切相关，但"头部"（你必须在被总结的答案里被尽可能多地提到，而不只是排第一）以及大得多、长得多的后续问题"尾部"运作方式不同。大多数杠杆跟传统 SEO 重叠——落地页、YouTube 视频、Reddit、affiliates、以及帮助中心优化——但你还需要站外的引用优化，并且必须在你自己的页面上回答每一个后续问题；跟 Google 不同，早期公司能赢得很快，因为一个引用就能让他们马上出现。用答案追踪器在少数高流量的 LLM 界面上追踪"声量份额"，跑有对照组的受控实验（测试组 vs 对照组），因为大多数公开的最佳实践都未被证实；对 Reddit 要做个真实、有用的用户，而不是去灌垃圾。他还警告：100% AI 生成的内容不管用——它会引发模型坍塌、并被过滤掉——而 AI 辅助、有人编辑的内容才是未来；而且核心技术跟 SEO 足够相似，所以"一切都变了"的炒作大多是错误的信号。

episodeTitle.en: How to be the best coach to product people | Petra Wille (Strong Product People)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何成为产品团队最佳教练 | 佩特拉·威尔（Petra Wille，Strong Product People）

bio.en: Petra Wille is an independent product leadership coach and author of Strong Product People, who for a decade has helped product teams and their managers level up, focusing on the crucial first-line manager layer.
bio.zh: Petra Wille 是一位独立的产品领导力教练，也是《强势产品人才》（Strong Product People）一书的作者，十年来一直帮助产品团队及其管理者提升能力，尤其专注于至关重要的“一线经理”层级。

guestBioOfficial.en: Petra Wille is an independent product leadership coach who’s been helping product teams expand their skill sets since 2013. She’s also the author of Strong Product People, which she published in 2021. Alongside her freelance work, Petra curates and co-organizes Mind The Product Engage Hamburg. She started her career as a software developer and in 2008 went to work at Xing, a German social media site, where she learned from two incredible product leaders: Marty Cagan and Jason Goldberg. In today’s podcast, we talk about Petra’s book, and how to help your team grow as a product leader. Petra also shares how to improve your storytelling skills, get better at public speaking, and why community is so important for product managers.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 佩特拉·威尔（Petra Wille）是一位独立产品领导力教练，自2013年起就致力于帮助产品团队提升技能。她还在2021年出版了《强势产品人》一书。除自由职业外，佩特拉还策划并联合组织了Mind The Product Engage Hamburg活动。她职业生涯始于软件开发工程师，2008年加入德国社交媒体网站Xing，在那里她向两位杰出的产品领导者——马蒂·卡根（Marty Cagan）和杰森·戈德伯格（Jason Goldberg）学习。在本期播客中，我们探讨佩特拉的著作，以及如何帮助团队成长为产品领导者。佩特拉还分享如何提升讲故事技巧、提高公开演讲能力，以及为什么社区对产品经理如此重要。

summary.en: Petra explains why coaching - not just managing - is the key skill for new product managers and leaders, and how to do it well. She makes the case that storytelling is essential for getting promoted and rallying teams, and that finding a PM community is one of the highest-leverage moves for growth. Drawing on coaching hundreds of product leaders, she offers concrete ways to develop the 'eight-legged' skill set a modern product person needs.
summary.zh: Petra 解释了为什么“辅导（coaching）”而非仅仅是管理，是新任产品经理与领导者的关键能力，以及该如何做好它。她论证了讲故事对于升职和凝聚团队至关重要，而找到一个产品经理社群则是成长中性价比最高的动作之一。基于辅导数百位产品领导者的经验，她给出了培养现代产品人所需的“八足”技能组合的具体方法。

episodeTitle.en: What it takes to become a top 1% PM | Ian McAllister (Uber, Amazon, Airbnb)
episodeTitle.zh: 成为顶级1%产品经理需要具备哪些条件 | 伊恩·麦卡利斯特（曾任Uber、亚马逊、Airbnb高管）

bio.en: Ian McAllister is the author of the classic product-management essay 'What Separates a Top 1% PM from a Top 10% PM,' a 12-year Amazon veteran who built Amazon Smile and grew Alexa internationally, and now leads global product for Uber's vehicles platform.
bio.zh: Ian McAllister 是经典产品经理文章《是什么让前 1% 的 PM 区别于前 10% 的 PM》的作者，在亚马逊任职 12 年、打造了 Amazon Smile 并推动 Alexa 国际化，如今领导 Uber 车辆平台的全球产品。

guestBioOfficial.en: Ian McAllister is the Senior Director of Product for Vehicles at Uber. Before moving to Uber, Ian spent over a decade directing teams at Amazon, where he created and led Amazon Smile. He was also Director of Product Management at Airbnb, where I was lucky enough to have worked alongside him. In today’s episode, we discuss Ian’s famous document about the essential attributes of the top 1% of product managers. Ian outlines the most important skills to focus on for entry-level PMs and how to broaden your experience and diversify skills as you move up the ladder. He also shares what he learned working with Jeff Wilke, Jeff Bezos, and other leaders at Amazon, and goes in depth on Amazon’s working-backwards framework.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 伊恩·麦卡利斯特是Uber的车辆产品高级总监。在加入Uber之前，伊恩在亚马逊工作了十多年，期间他创建并领导了亚马逊Smile项目。他还曾在Airbnb担任产品管理总监，我有幸与他共事过。今天的节目中，我们将探讨伊恩关于顶级1%产品经理必备特质的著名文档。伊恩概述了入门级PM应关注的最重要技能，以及如何在晋升过程中拓宽经验、多元化技能。他还分享了在亚马逊与杰夫·威尔克、杰夫·贝索斯及其他领导层合作的经验，并深入解读亚马逊的逆向工作法框架。

summary.en: Ian centers his advice on impact—if you wake up trying to maximize impact rather than politics or promotions, that's the guiding light—and breaks down precisely what separates a top 1% PM from everyone else, for both new and senior PMs. He then goes deep on Amazon's 'working backwards' process: how to implement it on your team, and the common ways teams do it wrong. The episode is a must-listen for PMs at any level, with linked templates and guides in the show notes.
summary.zh: Ian 把建议聚焦于“影响力”——如果你每天醒来都想最大化影响力，而非钻营政治或升职，那就是指路明灯，并精准拆解了前 1% 的 PM 究竟有何不同，分别对初级和高级 PM 都适用。接着他深入亚马逊的“逆向工作”（working backwards）流程：如何在团队落地，以及团队常犯的错误。这期节目是任何层级 PM 的必听内容，节目附注中还附上了相关模板与指南链接。

episodeTitle.en: Leaving big tech to build the #1 technology newsletter | Gergely Orosz (The Pragmatic Engineer)
episodeTitle.zh: 离开大型科技公司，创办头号科技新闻通讯 | 格尔盖利·奥罗兹（The Pragmatic Engineer）

bio.en: Gergely Orosz is the author of The Pragmatic Engineer, the top engineering newsletter on Substack, which he writes full-time after leaving a senior engineering role at Uber.
bio.zh: Gergely Orosz 是《The Pragmatic Engineer》的作者，这是 Substack 上排名第一的工程师 newsletter，他在离开 Uber 的高级工程职位后全职写作。

guestBioOfficial.en: Gergely Orosz writes the #1 technology newsletter at Substack, called The Pragmatic Engineer. He started his career as a software developer in the U.K., spent three years at Skype, and followed that role with four years as an engineering manager at Uber before deciding to leave big tech and work for himself. Gergely began pursuing his newsletter full-time in September 2021 and in just one year has amassed 200,000 subscribers. He now makes more money than he did at his salaried tech job, and with freedom and flexibility. In today’s podcast, Gergely shares why he left his well-paying job at Uber, how he got his first 1,000 subscribers, why this kind of work can be stressful and lonely (but ultimately rewarding), and why it takes hard work to build authority and become a great writer. Working solo can be challenging, and in this episode, both Lenny and Gergely offer tips for structuring your unstructured time and finding your focus.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 格尔吉·奥罗兹（Gergely Orosz）在Substack上运营着排名第一的科技资讯通讯《务实工程师》（The Pragmatic Engineer）。他的职业生涯始于英国的软件开发工程师，曾在Skype工作三年，随后在优步担任四年工程经理，之后决定离开大型科技公司，开始自主创业。2021年9月，他开始全职经营自己的资讯通讯，仅用一年时间就吸引了20万订阅者。如今他的收入远超之前在优步的薪资，还能享受自由灵活的工作环境。在本期播客中，格尔吉分享了为何离开高薪职位、如何获得首批1000名订阅者、为何这类工作可能充满压力与孤独（但最终收获满满），以及为何建立个人权威、成为优秀写作者需要付出巨大努力。独立工作固然充满挑战，在本期节目中，莱尼（Lenny）和格尔吉还为听众提供了如何规划碎片化时间、保持专注力的实用建议。

summary.en: Gergely shares what it's actually like to go full-time as a newsletter creator—the day-to-day life, the pros and cons, and why leaving a lucrative Uber job (where he made ~$330K) turned out to pay even better with no theoretical cap. He and Lenny compare notes as two full-time newsletter writers, covering what it takes to succeed and how to get started if you're curious about the creator route. It's a candid, behind-the-scenes look at building a career as an independent writer.
summary.zh: Gergely 分享了全职做 newsletter 创作者的真实体验——日常工作、利弊，以及为何离开 Uber 那份高薪工作（年薪约 33 万美元）后，收入反而没有了理论上限、变得更高。他和 Lenny 作为两位全职 newsletter 写作者交流心得，聊了成功需要什么，以及如果你想走创作者路线该如何起步。这是一期关于独立写作者职业生涯的坦诚幕后分享。

episodeTitle.en: An inside look at how the New York Times builds product | Alex Hardiman (CPO, the New York Times)
episodeTitle.zh: 《纽约时报》产品内幕解析 | 亚历克斯·哈迪曼（纽约时报首席产品官）

bio.en: Alex Hardiman is Chief Product Officer at The New York Times, leading teams building news, cooking, games, audio, and advertising products, previously CPO at The Atlantic and a product leader at Facebook.
bio.zh: Alex Hardiman 是《纽约时报》首席产品官，领导构建新闻、烹饪、游戏、音频及广告产品的团队，此前曾任《大西洋月刊》首席产品官及 Facebook 产品负责人。

guestBioOfficial.en: Alex Hardiman is Chief Product Officer at the New York Times, where she oversees the company’s news, cooking, games, audio and advertising products. Previously, Alex was Chief Product Officer at The Atlantic, and before that she was Head of News Products at Facebook. We discuss how engineers and product people work with writers to create impactful stories, how teams build the incredible visualizations and experiences for NYTimes.com, how product teams are structured within the New York Times, and the good and bad about working at a company like the New York Times versus a FAANG tech company. We also talk about the details behind the New York Times’s acquisition of Wordle and uncover what the Times is dreaming up for its product over the next 10 years.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 亚历克斯·哈迪曼是《纽约时报》的首席产品官，负责监督公司的新闻、烹饪、游戏、音频和广告产品。此前，她曾担任《大西洋月刊》的首席产品官，在此之前，她是Facebook新闻产品部的主管。我们讨论了工程师和产品人员如何与编辑合作创作有影响力的故事，团队如何为NYTimes.com打造令人惊叹的可视化效果和体验，纽约时报的产品团队结构，以及在FAANG科技公司与纽约时报工作的好处与不足。我们还讨论了纽约时报收购Wordle的细节，以及未来10年纽约时报的产品愿景。

summary.en: Alex describes how impact at the Times is in service of its mission to strengthen an informed democracy, not the other way around, with impact measured in subscribers and even policy change triggered by reporting. She reflects on being at the center of major storms—Facebook after the 2016 election and the Times during COVID—and what product teams can learn from working alongside journalists. The conversation covers the unique dynamics of building product at a mission-driven news organization versus a FAANG tech company.
summary.zh: Alex 阐述了《纽约时报》的影响力如何服务于“强化知情民主”这一使命，而非相反——影响力既体现在订阅增长，也体现在报道引发的政策变化上。她回顾了自己身处多次风暴中心的经历（2016 年大选后的 Facebook、新冠疫情初期的《纽约时报》），以及产品团队与记者协作的体会。对话还对比了在使命驱动的新闻机构与 FAANG 科技公司做产品的不同动态。

episodeTitle.en: How to work through fear, give hard feedback, and doing layoffs with grace | Matt Mochary
episodeTitle.zh: 如何克服恐惧、给予坦诚反馈，并优雅地进行裁员 | 马特·莫查里

bio.en: Matt Mochary is a renowned executive coach who has worked with the CEOs of OpenAI, Coinbase, Reddit, Rippling, and Notion, and authored the widely-shared CEO training document.
bio.zh: 马特·莫查里（Matt Mochary）是一位知名的高管教练，曾辅导 OpenAI、Coinbase、Reddit、Rippling、Notion 等公司的 CEO，并撰写了被广泛传播的首席执行官培训文档。

guestBioOfficial.en: Matt Mochary, CEO of Mochary Method, is a full-time executive coach who has worked with some of the biggest names in tech and finance, including investor Naval Ravikant and the CEOs of Notion, OpenAI, Coinbase, Reddit, and many others. In today’s podcast, we talk about the skill of firing people, why it’s so important, and Matt’s framework for approaching layoffs. We go deep on recognizing emotions like anger and fear, and what to pay attention to when you feel angry or fearful. He also shares how to build new products within a larger company, important tips on how to make sure everyone in the organization feels valued and heard, carving out time for your top goal, and how an energy audit can help you eliminate tasks that are draining your energy.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 马特·莫查里是Mochary Method的首席执行官，是一位全职高管教练，曾与科技和金融领域的多位大腕合作，包括投资者纳维尔·拉维坎特，以及Notion、OpenAI、Coinbase、Reddit等公司的首席执行官。在今天的播客中，我们将探讨解雇员工的技巧、其重要性，以及马特处理裁员的框架。我们将深入探讨识别愤怒和恐惧等情绪，以及当你感到愤怒或恐惧时需要注意什么。他还分享了如何在大型公司内开发新产品、确保组织中每个人都感到被重视和倾听的重要技巧、为你的首要目标腾出时间，以及能源审计如何帮助你消除消耗能量的任务。

summary.en: Matt stresses that layoffs must be delivered one-on-one by a manager, never by email or group message, to preserve dignity and avoid backlash. He shares frameworks for running companies transparently and the famous "Mochary method" for CEO effectiveness. The episode is a master class in humane, high-accountability leadership.
summary.zh: 马特强调，裁员必须由直属上级一对一当面告知，绝不能用邮件或群消息，以保留尊严、避免反弹。他分享了透明运营公司的框架，以及著名的"莫查里方法"CEO 效能体系。本期是关于"有人情味、又高度担责"的领导力大师课。

episodeTitle.en: How Snyk built a product-led growth juggernaut | Ben Williams (VP of Product at Snyk)
episodeTitle.zh: Snyk如何打造产品主导的增长引擎 | 本·威廉姆斯（Snyk产品副总裁）

bio.en: Ben Williams is VP of Product at Snyk, where he built the company's developer-growth organization and helped scale the developer-first security platform from an early-stage startup into an $8.6B-valued leader serving millions of developers.
bio.zh: Ben Williams 是 Snyk 的产品副总裁，他在那里搭建了公司的开发者增长组织，并帮助这家“开发者优先”的安全平台从早期初创公司成长为估值 86 亿美元、服务数百万开发者的行业领军者。

guestBioOfficial.en: Ben Williams is VP of Product at Snyk, an industry-leading security platform for developers, last valued at $8.5b. He’s also a product and growth advisor with over 20 years of experience building and scaling high-performing product and growth teams. Through product-led growth, product-led sales, and community, Snyk rapidly scaled and won over the lucrative developer audience. In today’s episode, Ben shares the successful growth levers that helped Snyk get started, all of the details of how Snyk has structured their growth, product, and marketing teams and set them up for success in terms of cross-collaboration—and also how their initial plan for self-serve monetization fell flat. We go into Ben’s many useful tips for product-led growth, including his thoughts on free vs. paid versions, trials, and how to build amazing growth teams.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 本·威廉姆斯是Snyk的产品副总裁，Snyk是一家行业领先的开发者安全平台，最新估值达85亿美元。他还是一位拥有20多年经验的产品与增长顾问，曾成功组建并扩展高绩效的产品与增长团队。通过产品主导的增长、产品主导的销售以及社区建设，Snyk迅速发展并赢得了利润丰厚的开发者群体。在本期节目中，本分享了助力Snyk起步的成功增长杠杆、Snyk如何构建其增长、产品和营销团队并为跨部门协作做好准备的所有细节，以及他们最初的自助式货币化计划为何失败。我们深入探讨了本对产品主导增长的诸多实用建议，包括他对免费版与付费版、试用版的看法，以及如何组建出色的增长团队。

summary.en: Snyk's early growth came from a narrow, developer-first wedge—starting with Node.js open-source security and winning the Node community through conferences, content, and a free CLI—before expanding languages and adding enterprise governance features. A defining lesson is that self-serve monetization stalled until the team built 'table stakes' enterprise features and leaned into product-led sales, while powerful growth loops (GitHub fix PRs, Snyk Advisor, security education) kept fueling acquisition and activation. Ben details how to run an effective growth org: cross-functional, outcome-based teams (acquisition/activation/monetization/platform), a 'decision science' function, and a loop-based growth model documented qualitatively and quantified quarterly. He also shares a crisp framework for vision/mission, practical advice on freemium packaging and activation metrics (a team fixing a vulnerability within 30 days), plus his favorite tools and books.
summary.zh: Snyk 早期的增长来自一个又窄又“开发者优先”的楔子——从 Node.js 开源安全起步，通过会议、内容和免费的命令行工具赢得 Node 社区——之后才扩展语言并加上企业级治理功能。一个关键教训是：在团队构建出“桌面筹码”级的企业功能、并转向产品驱动销售之前，自助变现一直停滞；而强大的增长闭环（GitHub 修复 PR、Snyk Advisor、安全教育）持续为获取和激活供能。Ben 详细讲了怎么运营一个有效的增长组织：跨职能、按结果组织的团队（获取/激活/变现/平台）、一个“决策科学”职能，以及一个定性记录、按季度量化的闭环式增长模型。他还分享了一个清晰的愿景/使命框架、关于免费增值打包和激活指标（一个团队在 30 天内修复一个漏洞）的实用建议，以及他最喜欢的工具和数据/书籍。

episodeTitle.en: Lessons from one of the world’s top executive recruiters | Lauren Ipsen (Daversa Partners, GC)
episodeTitle.zh: 全球顶级高管猎头公司的经验之谈 | 劳伦·伊普森（Daversa Partners，首席法务官）

bio.en: Lauren Ipsen is a veteran people and talent leader who has built and scaled hiring and talent functions at high-growth technology companies.
