bio.zh: 劳伦·伊普森（Lauren Ipsen）是一位资深的人力资源与人才领导者，曾在多家高增长的科技公司搭建并扩展招聘与人才体系。

guestBioOfficial.en: Lauren Ipsen is one of the most well-known and respected executive recruiters in the industry, having placed over 90 senior product leaders at companies including Twitter, Reddit, Opendoor, Postmates, Nextdoor, and many others. She is currently the Director of Executive Talent at General Catalyst, and prior to that was a senior leader at Daversa Partners. In today’s podcast, Lauren shares advice for founders on hiring senior product leaders, tips for product leaders on finding better opportunities, and the most common mistakes recruiters make. She talks about how to play the long game of networking to find the best talent and about recruiting best practices, and we also dive deep on market mapping, LinkedIn, and how to approach reference checks.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 劳伦·伊普森（Lauren Ipsen）是业界最知名且备受尊敬的高管猎头之一，曾为推特（Twitter）、红迪网（Reddit）、Opendoor、Postmates、Nextdoor等多家公司成功引荐了90余位资深产品负责人。她目前担任General Catalyst公司执行人才总监，此前曾在Daversa Partners担任高级领导职务。在本期播客中，劳伦为初创企业创始人分享了招聘资深产品负责人的建议，为产品负责人提供了寻找优质机会的秘诀，并剖析了招聘过程中最常犯的错误。她还深入探讨了市场洞察、领英使用技巧，以及如何有效开展背景调查。

summary.en: Lauren argues you should always keep a pulse on the talent market, whether or not you're hiring, so you know what "good" looks like. She encourages founders to build relationships with exceptional people long before a specific need arises. The episode is a playbook for proactive, high-quality hiring and staying close to great talent.
summary.zh: 劳伦认为，无论是否在招聘，都应持续关注人才市场动态，这样才能知道什么是"好"的标准。她鼓励创始人在具体需求出现之前，就与杰出人才建立关系。本期是一份关于主动、高质量招聘，并贴近优秀人才的手册。

episodeTitle.en: Building Substack | Sachin Monga (Substack, Facebook)
episodeTitle.zh: Substack平台建设 | 萨钦·蒙加（Substack、Facebook）

bio.en: Sachin Monga is Head of Product at Substack, which he joined via the acquisition of his startup Cocoon, and previously spent over seven years at Facebook working on video, the developer platform, and the ads growth team.
bio.zh: Sachin Monga 是 Substack 的产品负责人，他通过自己初创公司 Cocoon 被收购而加入 Substack，此前曾在 Facebook 工作逾七年，负责视频、开发者平台与广告增长团队。

guestBioOfficial.en: Sachin Monga is the Head of Product at Substack, a platform that I personally use every day, and love. Before Substack, Sachin co-founded an app called Cocoon, which he ended up selling to Substack. Before that, he spent over seven years at Facebook as a PM working on video and camera products, building out the developer platform, and leading the ads growth team. In today’s episode, we dive deep on all things Substack. Sachin shares what it’s like transitioning from a large product team at Facebook to a small growth team. He discusses how to work with a hands-on founder and why you must be comfortable with rapid change in a PM role. He also shares unique features of Substack that make it an optimized experience for readers and writers, how he’d like to see it improved, and tips for anyone wanting to get started writing online.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 萨钦·蒙加是Substack的首席产品官，我个人每天都在使用并喜爱这个平台。在加入Substack之前，萨钦联合创立了一款名为Cocoon的应用，最终将其出售给Substack。此前，他在Facebook担任产品经理七余年，负责视频和相机产品、开发者平台建设，并领导广告增长团队。在本期节目中，我们将深入探讨Substack的方方面面。萨钦分享了从Facebook大型产品团队向Substack小型增长团队过渡的经历，讲述了如何与亲力亲为的创始人合作，以及PM岗位为何必须适应快速变化的环境。他还分享了Substack为读者和作者优化体验的独特功能，谈及希望改进的方向，并为有意开启在线写作之路的人们提供建议。

summary.en: Sachin walks through how Substack builds product as it transitions into a product-driven company, structured around writer, reader, and growth teams. He shares lessons from the legendary Substack Recommendations feature, and how he navigates working with a strong product-minded founder (Chris Best) as head of product. The episode is a rare look at the product engine behind a platform that reshaped independent writing and publishing.
summary.zh: Sachin 拆解了 Substack 在向“产品驱动型公司”转型过程中如何打造产品，其组织围绕“作者团队、读者团队与增长团队”展开。他分享了传奇功能“Substack 推荐（Recommendations）”的经验，以及作为产品负责人如何与产品思维极强的创始人（Chris Best）共事。本期罕见地揭示了重塑独立写作与出版平台的背后产品引擎。

episodeTitle.en: Category creation and brand building | Barbra Gago (Pando, Miro, Greenhouse, Culture Amp)
episodeTitle.zh: 类别创造与品牌建设 | 芭芭拉·加戈（Barbra Gago，Pando、Miro、Greenhouse、Culture Amp）

bio.en: Barbra Gago is founder and CEO of Pando, a career-progression platform democratizing promotion and feedback, previously CMO and Global Head of Marketing at Miro and VP of Marketing at Greenhouse.
bio.zh: Barbra Gago 是 Pando 的创始人兼 CEO，Pando 是一个让晋升与反馈更普惠的职业发展平台，此前曾任 Miro 首席营销官兼全球市场负责人，以及 Greenhouse 营销副总裁。

guestBioOfficial.en: Barbra Gago is the founder and CEO of Pando, where she’s democratizing career progression. Previously she worked as the Chief Marketing Officer and Global Head of Marketing at Miro, where she helped create an entirely new software category for the space, and also served as VP of Marketing at Greenhouse, where she led go-to-market strategy. In today’s episode, we cover three main topics: category creation, branding and rebranding, and building opinionated software. Barbra discusses how she was able to rebrand Miro and launch a whole new category—and why her attempt to do that at Greenhouse failed. We cover the benefits of building your own category, and when it makes sense to do so and when it doesn’t. She also shares the importance of getting to know your users, why a great brand is informed by its values, and why Pando is built in an opinionated way.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 芭芭拉·加戈（Barbra Gago）是Pando的创始人兼CEO，她正在推动职业发展民主化。此前，她曾在Miro担任首席营销官和全球营销主管，为该领域创造了一个全新的软件类别，还在Greenhouse担任营销副总裁，负责市场推广策略。在本期节目中，我们将围绕三个主要话题展开讨论：类别创造、品牌与品牌重塑，以及构建有态度的软件。芭芭拉将讲述她如何成功重塑Miro品牌并开创全新类别，以及为何她在Greenhouse的尝试以失败告终。我们还将探讨创建自己的类别的好处，以及何时适合这样做，何时不适合。她还将分享了解用户的重要性，伟大品牌如何由其价值观驱动，以及Pando为何以有态度的方式构建。

summary.en: Barbra explains category creation—how she rebranded Miro and launched the “visual collaboration” category, and why a similar attempt at Greenhouse failed. She shares why a great brand is informed by its values and why Pando is built as opinionated software for career growth. The conversation covers branding, rebranding, and the strategic decision of when (and when not) to create your own category.
summary.zh: Barbra 讲解了品类创造——她如何重塑 Miro 品牌并推出“可视化协作”品类，以及在 Greenhouse 类似尝试为何失败。她分享了为何优秀品牌由其价值观塑造，以及 Pando 为何作为“有主张的”软件来构建职业发展。对话涵盖品牌、品牌重塑，以及何时（不该）自创品类的战略决策。

episodeTitle.en: How to build trust and grow as a product leader | Fareed Mosavat (Reforge, Slack, Instacart, Pixar)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何建立信任并成长为产品领导者 | 法里德·莫萨瓦特（Reforge、Slack、Instacart、Pixar）

bio.en: Fareed Mosavat is the Chief Development Officer at Reforge and a veteran product leader who, before Reforge, led growth at Slack and Instacart, served as VP of Product at Runkeeper and GM at Zynga, and spent six years building 3D animation tools at Pixar.
bio.zh: Fareed Mosavat 是 Reforge 的首席发展官（Chief Development Officer），也是一位资深产品负责人；在加入 Reforge 之前，他曾在 Slack 和 Instacart 主导增长，担任 Runkeeper 的产品副总裁、Zynga 的总经理，并在皮克斯工作了六年，开发 3D 动画工具。

guestBioOfficial.en: Fareed Mosavat is Chief Development Officer at Reforge, where he leads production, content, and new-product experiences. Previously, he led growth and product teams at Slack and Instacart, was a GM at Zynga, and also served as VP of Product at RunKeeper. Before all of that, Fareed’s fascinating career began in engineering for Pixar, where he learned the art of storytelling and collaboration. In today’s episode, we talk about how his time at Pixar influenced the way he thinks about product, why it’s so difficult to become a better PM, and how to avoid the “manager death spiral.” Fareed shares important insights on how to earn the trust of your manager and coworkers, the four types of product work—and why you need to understand all four. He also provides solid examples of how to generalize your learnings and explains why this will expand your options, make you a better PM, and boost your chances of moving into a leadership role.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 法里德·莫萨瓦特（Fareed Mosavat）是Reforge公司的首席开发官，负责产品、内容和新产品体验。此前，他曾在Slack和Instacart领导增长和产品团队，在Zynga担任总经理，并在RunKeeper担任产品副总裁。在此之前，法里德令人惊叹的职业生涯始于皮克斯动画工作室的工程师，在那里他学会了讲故事和协作的艺术。在本期节目中，我们探讨了他在皮克斯的经历如何影响他对产品的思考方式，为什么成为一名更优秀的产品经理如此困难，以及如何避免"管理者职业生涯的恶性循环"。法里德分享了如何赢得经理和同事信任的重要见解，以及四种产品工作类型——并解释为何需要理解这四种类型。他还提供了如何将所学知识推广应用的实例，并解释了这样做将如何拓展你的选择范围，助你成为更出色的产品经理，并增加晋升领导职位的机会。

summary.en: Fareed argues that the only way to get better at product management is to do the real work—shipping real products for real customers with real data—because training, mentorship, and reading are merely layers on top of raw repetition. He walks through the difficult transition from individual contributor to manager, emphasizing that crossing 'the canyon' requires deliberately expanding your scope and owning outcomes rather than tasks. A core theme is creating opportunities to take on more responsibility: great PMs accelerate by seeking out the highest-leverage work and proving they can handle bigger bets. He also shares practical advice on how to build the reps that compound into senior product judgment, making this a field guide for any PM who wants to level up from solid executor to influential leader.
summary.zh: Fareed 认为，提升产品管理能力唯一的途径就是去做真正的工作——为真实的客户、用真实的数据去交付真实的产品——因为培训、导师指导和阅读都只是在大量重复练习之上的一层包装。他拆解了从一线执行者（IC）到管理者那段艰难的跨越，强调跨过这道“峡谷”需要刻意扩大自己的影响范围，并对结果而非任务负责。一个核心主题是创造机会去承担更多责任：优秀的 PM 会主动去寻找杠杆最高的事情，并证明自己能扛得起更大的赌注，从而加速成长。他还分享了如何通过一次次实战积累出高阶产品判断力的实用建议，对每一位想从靠谱执行者进阶为有影响力的领导者 PM 来说，这都是一份实战指南。

episodeTitle.en: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)
episodeTitle.zh: 人性化产品开发 | 阿德里尔·弗雷德里克（Reddit、Lyft、Facebook）

bio.en: Adriel Frederick is VP of Product at Reddit (Reddit X), where he incubates and scales new products, previously serving as Director of Product at Lyft (marketplace and pricing) and an early product manager at Facebook focused on user acquisition.
bio.zh: Adriel Frederick 是 Reddit（Reddit X）的产品副总裁，负责孵化并扩展新产品，此前曾任 Lyft 产品总监（负责市场与定价团队）以及 Facebook 早期专注用户获取的产品经理。

guestBioOfficial.en: Adriel Frederick is VP of Product Management at Reddit X, where he helps incubate and scale new products. He is a former Product Lead at Facebook, as well as a former PM and Director of Product at Lyft. In today’s episode, we focus on what it takes to become a better product leader. Adriel shares anecdotes from his time at Lyft and Facebook, insights about how to lead through tough times, why there isn’t an algorithmic solution to everything, why R&D teams need to be a part of the core mission, the tangible benefits of working on diverse teams, and his thoughts on the future of AI. He also introduces the concept of cannonballs, why you should focus on the marginal user, why organization and empathy are the most important PM skills, and so much more.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 阿德里尔·弗雷德里克（Adriel Frederick）是Reddit X的副总裁（产品管理），负责孵化和扩展新产品。他曾担任Facebook的产品主管，也是Lyft的产品经理和产品总监。在本期节目中，我们将聚焦如何成为更出色的产品负责人。阿德里尔分享了他在Lyft和Facebook的经历，讲述如何在逆境中引领团队，为何没有万能的算法解决方案，研发团队为何应融入核心使命，多元化团队的切实益处，以及他对AI未来的见解。他还引入了“炮弹策略”概念，解释为何应关注边缘用户，组织能力和同理心是产品经理最重要的技能等观点。

summary.en: Adriel shares what it takes to become a better product leader, drawing on anecdotes from Lyft and Facebook about leading through tough times and the limits of algorithmic solutions. He argues there isn't always an algorithmic answer to every problem and that R&D teams must be embedded in the core mission. The conversation also covers the tangible benefits of diverse teams, his experience as Facebook's first Black PM, and his forward-looking thoughts on AI.
summary.zh: Adriel 结合在 Lyft 和 Facebook 的经历，分享了如何成为更优秀的产品领导者，包括如何在困境中领导团队，以及算法解决方案的局限。他认为并非所有问题都能靠算法解决，研发团队必须融入核心使命。对话还涵盖多元化团队的实际价值、他作为 Facebook 首位黑人产品经理的经历，以及对 AI 的前瞻思考。

episodeTitle.en: Building better roadmaps | Janna Bastow (Mind the Product, ProdPad)
episodeTitle.zh: 构建更优路线图 | 詹娜·巴斯托（Janna Bastow，Mind the Product，ProdPad）

bio.en: Janna Bastow is co-founder and CEO of ProdPad, the product management tool, and co-creator of Mind the Product, the global product management community and conference series.
bio.zh: Janna Bastow 是产品管理工具 ProdPad 的联合创始人兼 CEO，也是全球产品管理社区与会议系列 Mind the Product 的共同创办人。

guestBioOfficial.en: Janna Bastow is a former product manager, and currently the CEO and co-founder of ProdPad. She also co-founded Mind the Product, a community for PMs, which has grown to 300,000 members across the world. In today’s podcast, Janna discusses the limitations of timeline-based Gantt charts and her “Now/Next/Later” framework. She also shares stories about hosting conferences and gives some great tips on how to improve your presentation skills and cope with performance anxiety.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 詹娜·巴斯托曾是产品经理，目前是ProdPad的首席执行官兼联合创始人。她还共同创立了面向产品经理的社区Mind the Product，该社区在全球已拥有30万名成员。在今天的播客中，詹娜讨论了基于时间表的甘特图的局限性，以及她的“现在/接下来/以后”框架。她还分享了举办会议的经验，并就如何提升演讲技巧和应对表现焦虑提供了宝贵建议。

summary.en: In this conversation, Janna shares hard-won lessons from building both a product-management software company and the world's largest product community. She covers how to run effective product strategy and roadmapping, how to engage stakeholders and keep a roadmap outcome-driven rather than feature-driven, and what years of watching thousands of PMs have taught her about what good product management looks like. The episode is a practical guide for product leaders who want to sharpen how their teams think and operate.
summary.zh: 在这期对话中，Janna 分享了她同时打造一家产品管理软件公司和全球最大产品社区的来之不易的经验。她讲了如何做有效的产品战略与路线图、如何调动干系人并让路线图以“成果”而非“功能”为导向，以及多年来观察成千上万名 PM 后她对“好产品管理”的理解。这期节目是想提升团队思考与运作方式的产品领导者的实用指南。

episodeTitle.en: How to build a high-performing growth team | Adam Fishman (Patreon, Lyft, Imperfect Foods)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何打造高效增长团队 | 亚当·菲什曼（Patreon、Lyft、Imperfect Foods）

bio.en: Adam Fishman is a veteran growth and product leader who was Lyft's first growth hire, later led product and growth at Patreon where he helped build one of the most successful creator platforms, and today advises companies and teaches growth through his newsletter and Reforge.
bio.zh: Adam Fishman 是一位资深的增长与产品领导者，曾是 Lyft 最早的 growth 招聘员工，后来在 Patreon 主导产品与增长、参与打造业内最成功的创作者平台之一，如今通过他的 Newsletter 和 Reforge 为企业做顾问并教授增长。

guestBioOfficial.en: Adam Fishman has decades of experience building and scaling some incredible businesses, like Lyft, Patreon, and Imperfect Foods. He is currently an Executive in Residence at Reforge and an advisor to numerous companies on growth, product, strategy, and company building. In today’s episode, Adam shares his growth PM competency model to help founders identify specific skills when hiring growth leaders, how to structure feedback, and how to identify gaps in your growth team. He also discusses the role of onboarding in retention and how to evaluate a company as a prospective employee.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 亚当·菲什曼（Adam Fishman）拥有数十年打造和扩展惊人业务的经验，曾操盘Lyft、Patreon和Imperfect Foods等公司。目前，他是Reforge的驻场高管，也是多家公司的增长、产品、战略及公司建设顾问。在本期节目中，亚当分享了他的增长PM能力模型，帮助创业者在招聘增长团队领导时识别特定技能，如何构建反馈机制，以及如何识别增长团队中的空白环节。他还探讨了入职流程在留存率中的作用，以及作为潜在员工如何评估一家公司。

summary.en: Adam lays out his Growth Competency Model with four pillars—growth execution, customer knowledge, growth strategy, and communication & influence—arguing the goal is to build a balanced team, not hire a mythical 11-out-of-10 unicorn. He makes the case that onboarding is the most underrated growth lever because it touches 100% of users and drives retention; at Patreon, connecting creators with the right person at the right time and then productizing that lifted creator revenue by 25%. On hiring, he favors internal transfers or rising talent strong on execution and customer knowledge, bringing in specialists like SEO only once the fundamentals are in place. Finally, his PMF framework (People, Mission, Financials) helps candidates evaluate employers—do backchannel references and observe exec-team dynamics before you commit.
summary.zh: Adam 提出了「增长能力模型」，包含四大支柱——增长执行、客户认知、增长战略、沟通与影响力——目的是组建能力互补的均衡团队，而不是去寻找一个样样 11 分的独角兽。他把引导流程（onboarding）视为最被低估的增长杠杆：它触达 100% 的用户、塑造第一印象，并直接驱动留存；在 Patreon，通过在对的时间把创作者连到真人、再把这些做法产品化，把创作者的前两个月收入提升了 25%。招聘上他建议优先内部转岗或上升期人才（看重执行力和客户认知），只有在基础打牢后才从外部引入 SEO 之类的专家。最后他用「PMF 框架」（人 People、使命 Mission、财务 Financials）帮求职者评估雇主，主张做反向背景调查、观察高管团队的互动动态，再决定要不要加入。

episodeTitle.en: Developing a growth model + marketplace growth strategy | Dan Hockenmaier
episodeTitle.zh: 构建增长模型与市场增长策略 | 丹·霍肯迈尔

bio.en: Dan Hockenmaier is VP of Growth at Faire, a B2B marketplace for independent retailers, where he owns growth modeling and marketplace strategy; before Faire he led growth at Thumbtack and founded Basis One, a consultancy that built growth models for 20-30 startups.
bio.zh: Dan Hockenmaier 是 Faire 的增长副总裁。Faire 是一个面向独立零售商的 B2B 市场，他在那里负责增长建模与市场策略；加入 Faire 之前，他在 Thumbtack 领导增长，并创立了 Basis One——一家为二三十家创业公司搭建增长模型的咨询公司。

guestBioOfficial.en: Dan Hockenmaier is an expert on marketplace strategy and growth. He was previously the Director of Growth at Thumbtack as well as a partner at Reforge, where he co-created the monetization track. Currently, he is the Head of Strategy and Analytics at Faire. In today’s episode, Dan shares the building blocks of a growth model, important considerations when building your growth model, and how to get started. We also chat about retention best practices, the complexity of building a marketplace, the future of marketplaces, and when it makes sense to add a SaaS business to a marketplace, and vice versa.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 丹·霍肯迈尔是市场策略与增长领域的专家。他曾担任Thumbtack增长总监，也是Reforge合伙人，共同开创了变现路径。目前，他担任Faire的战略与分析负责人。本期节目中，丹将分享增长模型的构建要素、构建增长模型时需考虑的关键因素，以及如何破题。我们还将探讨留存最佳实践、构建市场的复杂性、市场未来的发展方向，以及何时将SaaS业务引入市场，反之亦然。

summary.en: A growth model breaks a business down into a few building blocks — acquisition, retention, and monetization for SaaS, plus transaction volume and order value for marketplaces — and the biggest, most under-appreciated lever is almost always retention, especially the very first user experience. Building the model yourself from first principles is the point (templates help little), and the payoff is a common currency to allocate resources across teams during planning. For marketplaces, demand is the only thing that truly matters: liquidity is the first metric to nail, share of wallet measures depth over breadth, and you should acquire supply only insofar as it improves the customer experience. The future of marketplaces trends toward higher commissions for more value-chain work, with businesses that need supplier creativity (Etsy, Faire) staying marketplaces while commoditized ones (ride-sharing) consolidate into owned-supply models.
summary.zh: 增长模型把一个生意拆成几个积木块——SaaS 是获客、留存、变现，市场类再加上交易量和客单价——而最大、最被低估的杠杆几乎永远是留存，尤其是第一次用户体验。从第一性原理自己把模型搭出来才是关键（模板帮助不大），回报是能在规划时给跨团队资源分配提供一把通用货币。对市场来说，需求才是唯一真正要紧的：流动性是第一个要搞定的指标，钱包份额衡量的是深度而非广度，而且你只在『它能改善客户体验』的范围内去获取供给。市场的未来趋势是：为价值链里更多的工作收更高佣金；需要供给方创意的生意（Etsy、Faire）会留在市场模式，而商品化的（打车）会整合进自有供给模型。

episodeTitle.en: Build better products with continuous product discovery | Teresa Torres
episodeTitle.zh: 通过持续产品探索打造更优质产品 | 特蕾莎·托雷斯

bio.en: Teresa Torres is a product discovery coach and the author of Continuous Discovery Habits, who has helped thousands of product teams adopt a continuous discovery practice.
bio.zh: Teresa Torres 是一位产品发现（discovery）教练，也是《持续发现习惯》（Continuous Discovery Habits）一书的作者，她已帮助数千支产品团队建立起持续发现的工作方法。

guestBioOfficial.en: Teresa Torres is an internationally acclaimed author, speaker, and coach. She teaches a structured and sustainable system for continuous discovery that helps product teams infuse their daily product decisions with customer input. She’s coached hundreds of teams at companies of all sizes, from early-stage startups to global enterprises, in a variety of industries. She has taught over 11,000 product people discovery skills through the Product Talk Academy and hundreds through her coaching practice, and is the author of Continuous Discovery Habits.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 特蕾莎·托雷斯（Teresa Torres）是国际知名的作家、演讲者和教练。她教授了一套结构化且可持续的持续探索体系，帮助产品团队将客户反馈融入日常产品决策。她曾为各种规模的公司（从初创企业到全球企业）数百个团队提供指导，涉及多个行业。通过Product Talk Academy，她已为11,000多名产品人员传授探索技能，并通过教练实践帮助数百人提升技能。她是《持续探索习惯》一书的作者。

summary.en: Teresa makes the case for continuous discovery: talking to customers every week and mapping opportunities and solutions with opportunity solution trees. She explains why discovery is a habit, not a one-off research phase, and how it keeps teams connected to real customer problems between releases. The episode is a practical, grounding guide to the product discovery practice every team can adopt.
summary.zh: Teresa 论证了“持续发现”的必要性：每周与客户交谈，并用“机会—解决方案树（opportunity solution trees）”来梳理机会与方案。她解释了为什么发现是一种习惯、而非一次性的研究阶段，以及它如何让团队在版本之间始终与真实的客户问题保持连接。本期是一份务实、扎根的指南，关于每支团队都能采纳的产品发现实践。

episodeTitle.en: Using behavioral science to improve your product | Kristen Berman (Irrational Labs)
episodeTitle.zh: 利用行为科学优化产品 | 克里斯汀·伯曼（Irrational Labs）

bio.en: Kristen Berman is the CEO and co-founder of Irrational Labs, a behavioral-design firm that helps companies like Google, Airbnb, and Microsoft build better products, and co-founded the Common Cents Lab at Duke.
bio.zh: 克里斯滕·伯曼（Kristen Berman）是行为设计公司 Irrational Labs 的 CEO 兼联合创始人，该公司帮助 Google、Airbnb、微软等企业打造更好的产品；她还联合创办了杜克大学的 Common Cents Lab。

guestBioOfficial.en: Kristen Berman is the CEO and co-founder of Irrational Labs, where she helps companies like Google, Airbnb, PayPal, Microsoft, and LinkedIn improve their products and services through behavioral design research. She is also the co-founder of Common Cents Lab, a Duke University initiative dedicated to improving the financial well-being of low- to middle-class Americans. In today’s episode, Kristen shares the 3B Framework of Behavioral Design and uses real-life examples to illustrate what influences behavior change and the common biases that get in the way of building successful products. She also explains how to keep users engaged and how you can implement behavioral design research to drive innovation and growth.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 克里斯汀·伯曼（Kristen Berman）是Irrational Labs的首席执行官兼联合创始人，她通过行为设计研究帮助谷歌、爱彼家、贝宝、微软和领英等公司优化产品与服务。同时，她还是杜克大学"共同分钱实验室"（Common Cents Lab）的联合创始人，该项目致力于提升美国中低收入群体的财务健康水平。在本期节目中，克里斯汀分享了行为设计的"3B框架"，并通过真实案例解析影响行为改变的因素以及阻碍产品成功的常见偏见。她还将讲述如何保持用户参与度，以及如何运用行为设计研究来推动创新与增长。

summary.en: Kristen explains how behavioral science reveals that people act on emotion and social norms, not pure rationality, and how products can be designed to steer better behavior. She introduces the 3B Framework of Behavioral Design with real case studies, including work with TikTok. The episode shows how to apply psychology to drive engagement and growth without manipulation.
summary.zh: 克里斯滕解释了行为科学如何揭示：人是基于情绪与社会规范行事，而非纯粹理性，以及产品如何被设计来引导更好的行为。她以 TikTok 等真实案例介绍了"行为设计 3B 框架"。本期展示了如何运用心理学推动用户参与和增长，且不带操纵色彩。

episodeTitle.en: Customer-led growth | Georgiana Laudi (Forget The Funnel)
episodeTitle.zh: 《客户主导的增长》 | 乔治亚娜·劳迪（Georgiana Laudi，Forget The Funnel）

bio.en: Gia Laudi (Georgiana Laudi) is the founder of the consultancy Forget The Funnel, where she works hands-on with SaaS companies to diagnose their biggest growth bottlenecks and frequently doubles or triples conversion across their product flows.
bio.zh: Gia Laudi（Georgiana Laudi）是咨询公司 Forget The Funnel 的创始人，她亲手帮助 SaaS 公司诊断最大的增长瓶颈，并常常将其产品流程中的转化率提升两到三倍。

guestBioOfficial.en: Georgiana Laudi is the co-founder and CEO of a consulting agency called Forget The Funnel, where she helps SaaS companies scale and improve conversion rates through customer-led growth. She’s also a marketing and growth advisor to companies like MarketerHire, SparkToro, and Sprout Social. Previously, she was the VP of Marketing at Unbounce and has worked in growth marketing for over 20 years. In today’s episode, Gia speaks about how to identify your ideal customer, how to map their user flows in order to find the biggest growth opportunities, and examples of product changes she’s recommended that have led to the largest growth unlocks. She shares the exact process she works through with founders to uncover opportunities, as well as how to increase subscriptions and retention for SaaS businesses.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 乔治亚娜·劳迪（Georgiana Laudi）是咨询机构Forget The Funnel的联合创始人兼首席执行官，她通过客户主导的增长策略，帮助SaaS公司实现规模扩张和转化率提升。她还是MarketerHire、SparkToro和Sprout Social等公司的营销与增长顾问。此前，她曾担任Unbounce的营销副总裁，从事增长营销领域逾20年。在本期节目中，吉娅将探讨如何识别理想客户、如何通过用户流图谱找准最大增长机遇，以及她为客户推荐的成功产品改进案例。她将分享与创始人共同挖掘增长机会的具体流程，并揭示如何提升SaaS企业的订阅量与用户留存率。

summary.en: Gia makes the case that traditional funnels and pirate metrics like MQLs and SQLs are flawed because they put the business—not the customer—at the center and ignore everything that happens after acquisition, from retention to expansion. She shares the exact process she uses to find a company's biggest growth opportunities: identify your most important customers, map their journey through the product, set goals around their behavior, and then execute against those insights. A key point is that recurring-revenue businesses cannot treat growth as ending at acquisition, or they will not survive. The conversation is packed with practical tactics and stories about turning customer-centric diagnosis into measurable conversion wins.
summary.zh: Gia 指出，传统的漏斗模型以及 MQL、SQL 这类“海盗指标”是有问题的，因为它们把企业而非客户放在中心，并且完全忽略了获客之后发生的一切——从留存到扩展收入。她分享了自己在寻找公司最大增长机会时使用的完整流程：先锁定最重要的客户，再描绘他们在产品中的使用旅程，围绕他们的行为设定目标，然后基于这些洞察去执行。一个关键点是：订阅制营收的企业绝不能把增长当成“获客即结束”，否则就无法存活。整期内容充满了实战技巧和真实故事，教你如何把以客户为中心的诊断，转化为可衡量的转化提升。

episodeTitle.en: Growth tactics, retention strategies, and becoming a better writer | Julian Shapiro (Demand Curve, Hyper, Webflow, TechCrunch)
episodeTitle.zh: 朱利安·夏皮罗（Julian Shapiro）：增长策略、留存策略与提升写作能力 | （Demand Curve、Hyper、Webflow、TechCrunch）

bio.en: Julian Shapiro is the founder of Demand Curve, a growth-training company that has helped thousands of startups with their growth strategy, and previously wrote the growth column at TechCrunch and led marketing at Webflow.
bio.zh: 朱利安·夏皮罗（Julian Shapiro）是增长培训公司 Demand Curve 的创始人，已帮助数千家初创公司制定增长战略；他此前曾为 TechCrunch 撰写增长专栏，并担任 Webflow 的市场营销副总裁。

guestBioOfficial.en: Julian Shapiro is widely known as the founder of Demand Curve, where he’s helped thousands of companies figure out their growth strategy. He also wrote the growth marketing column at TechCrunch, was VP of Marketing at Webflow, and even created an animation engine called Velocity that’s now used in apps like Uber and WhatsApp. In today’s episode, Julian dives deep on product-led acquisition (PLA) and why he believes it’s the best way to grow your company. He shares specific marketing strategies for growth and retention and speaks about his framework for creating novel, engaging content, and how to choose topics for that content. He also discusses a framework called the Curiosity Faucet, inspired by prolific creators such as Ed Sheeran, John Mayer, Taylor Swift, and Neil Gaiman, to help you unlock your own creativity.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 朱利安·夏皮罗（Julian Shapiro）是Demand Curve的创始人，他帮助数千家公司制定增长战略。他还为TechCrunch撰写了增长营销专栏，曾担任Webflow的营销副总裁，甚至创建了名为Velocity的动画引擎，该引擎现已应用于Uber和WhatsApp等应用程序。在今天的节目中，朱利安深入探讨了产品主导型收购（PLA），并解释了为什么他认为这是发展公司的最佳方式。他分享了具体的增长和留存营销策略，并谈到了他创建新颖、引人入胜内容的框架，以及如何为这些内容选择主题。他还讨论了一个名为"好奇心水龙头"的框架，该框架灵感来自Ed Sheeran、John Mayer、Taylor Swift和Neil Gaiman等多产创作者，帮助你释放自己的创造力。

summary.en: Julian makes the case for product-led acquisition (PLA) as the most durable and capital-efficient way to grow a company. He shares concrete tactics for improving retention and a framework for producing novel, engaging content, including the "Curiosity Faucet" creativity method. The episode also covers how to pick topics and write in a way that earns attention.
summary.zh: 朱利安主张"产品驱动获取"（PLA）是公司最持久、最具资金效率的增长方式。他分享了提升留存的具体策略，以及创作新颖、有吸引力内容的框架，包括"好奇心水龙头"这一激发创造力的方法。本期还涉及如何选题，以及如何写出真正能赢得注意力的内容。

episodeTitle.en: Why product-led growth is the future | Elena Verna (Amplitude, Miro, Surveymonkey)
episodeTitle.zh: 为何产品主导增长是未来趋势 | 埃琳娜·维尔纳（Amplitude、Miro、Surveymonkey）

bio.en: Elena Verna is a world-leading growth and monetization expert who has scaled product-led growth and product-led sales at companies including Amplitude, Miro, SurveyMonkey, MongoDB, and Netlify, and teaches experimentation and growth at Reforge.
bio.zh: Elena Verna 是世界领先的增长与变现专家，曾在 Amplitude、Miro、SurveyMonkey、MongoDB、Netlify 等公司规模化地打造产品驱动增长与产品驱动销售，并在 Reforge 教授实验与增长课程。

guestBioOfficial.en: Elena Verna has led growth at some of today’s most successful B2B businesses, including Miro as CMO, Surveymonkey as SVP of Growth, and now at Amplitude as interim Head of Growth. She’s also worked closely with over a dozen companies on growth and product strategy, including companies like MongoDB, Clockwise, and Netlify (where she sits on the board of directors). Elena is undoubtedly one of the smartest people on growth strategy in the world.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 埃琳娜·维尔纳曾在当今一些最成功的B2B企业领导增长团队，包括在Miro担任首席营销官，在Surveymonkey担任增长副总裁，现在在Amplitude担任临时增长主管。她还与十几家公司密切合作，参与增长和产品战略，包括MongoDB、Clockwise和Netlify（她在Netlify担任董事会成员）。埃琳娜无疑是全球增长战略领域最聪明的人之一。

summary.en: Elena Verna gives a deep, opinionated masterclass on product-led sales (PLS) — the emerging go-to-market motion that turns self-serve usage into larger sales-led contracts. She distinguishes PLG (individual, self-serve monetization capped around $10K) from PLS, which builds a "bridge" from an individual user's job-to-be-done up to an enterprise-level solution, with sales owning the escalator because products are bad at conveying enterprise value. Key concepts covered: PQA (product-qualified account) vs PQL vs MQL and the three lead-attribution channels; why every sales-led company should add a product-assist element and make product accountable for pipeline; the four roles needed (product, analytics, marketing, sales) and a "Wizard of Oz" start before buying tooling; behavioral signals like admin switches and terms-of-use page views; and common pitfalls (treating PLS like top-down sales, spamming users, excluding marketing). She stresses patience (12+ months of usage before enterprise contracts) and ends by speculating that AI will automate sales conversations next.
summary.zh: Elena Verna 给了一堂有观点、极深入的产品驱动销售（PLS）大师课——这是一种新兴的 go-to-market 打法，把自助用量转化成更大的、销售驱动的合同。她区分了 PLG（个人的、自助变现上限约 1 万美元）和 PLS：PLS 在个人的"待完成任务"和企业级方案之间建一座"桥"，由销售拥有那部扶梯，因为产品不擅长传达企业价值。涵盖的关键概念：PQA（产品合格账户）vs PQL vs MQL，以及三种线索归因渠道；为什么每个销售驱动公司都该加"产品辅助"元素、并让产品对管道可问责；需要的四个角色（产品、分析、营销、销售）以及买工具前"绿野仙踪式"的起步；管理员切换、使用条款页浏览等行为信号；以及常见坑（把 PLS 当自上而下销售、spam 用户、排除营销）。她强调耐心（企业合同前需 12 个月以上用量），最后猜想下一步 AI 会自动化销售对话。

episodeTitle.en: Building a meaningful career | Jason Shah (Airbnb, Amazon, Microsoft, Alchemy)
episodeTitle.zh: 构建有意义的职业生涯 | 杰森·沙阿（Jason Shah，Airbnb、亚马逊、微软、Alchemy）

bio.en: Jason Shah is a product leader whom Lenny worked with at Airbnb and who later led product in Web3; he shares deep, tactical advice on leadership, hiring, pushing back on your CEO, and advancing your career.
bio.zh: Jason Shah 是一位产品负责人，Lenny 曾在 Airbnb 与他共事，他后来也在 Web3 领域领导产品；他分享了关于领导力、招聘、如何对 CEO 说“不”、以及职业晋升的深入而具体的建议。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jason Shah has led product teams at Amazon, Airbnb, Microsoft, and Yammer and currently leads the product team at Alchemy (one of the most important web3 infrastructure companies). In addition, he’s an advisor, investor, and two-time founder. In today’s episode, Jason discusses what it’s like to be a PM in web3, why his role at Amazon made such a big impact on his life and career, what makes a great leader, and how to hire well. He also shares his unique perspective on building a meaningful career and life.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 杰森·沙阿曾在亚马逊、Airbnb、微软和Yammer领导产品团队，目前在Alchemy（最重要的web3基础设施公司之一）领导产品团队。此外，他还是顾问、投资者和两次创业者。今天的节目中，杰森讨论了在web3中担任产品经理的感受、他在亚马逊的角色如何对他的生活和职业生涯产生重大影响、如何成为优秀的领导者，以及如何招聘优秀人才。他还分享了他对构建有意义的职业生涯和生活的独特见解。

summary.en: Jason reframes 'pushback' as a negative word that puts you in a mindset of disagreeing, and instead advocates shifting direction or helping the business succeed when you disagree. He shares what it's like to be a PM in Web3 through crypto winter, how to lead a team through ups and downs while keeping morale and focus, and a wealth of advice on leadership, hiring, pushing back, working backwards, and career advancement. The episode is full of 'juicy' practical wisdom for product leaders at any stage.
summary.zh: Jason 把“pushback（顶撞/反对）”重新定义为一个负面词汇，会让人陷入“必须不同意”的心态，他主张在意见相左时改为“调整方向”或“帮助业务成功”。他分享了在加密寒冬中做 Web3 PM 是怎样的体验、如何在起伏中领导团队并保持士气与专注，以及大量关于领导力、招聘、向上管理、逆向工作与职业晋升的建议。这期节目充满对各阶段产品领导者都实用的“干货”。

episodeTitle.en: When to invest in new acquisition channels | Adam Grenier (Uber, MasterClass)
episodeTitle.zh: 何时投资新获客渠道 | 亚当·格雷尼尔（Adam Grenier，优步、MasterClass）

bio.en: Adam Grenier is a growth and marketing leader who built Uber's growth marketing team and infrastructure from scratch, served as VP of Product and Marketing at Lambda School and VP of Marketing at MasterClass, and now advises companies and invests while shaping the emerging "Growth CMO" model.
bio.zh: Adam Grenier 是一位增长与营销领导者，曾在 Uber 从零搭建增长营销团队与基础设施、担任 Lambda School 产品与营销 VP 及 MasterClass 营销 VP，如今作为顾问和投资人在新兴获客渠道与「增长型 CMO」理念上影响行业。

guestBioOfficial.en: Adam Grenier is the former Head of Growth Marketing and Innovation at Uber, where he helped build Uber’s growth infrastructure from the ground up. He is also the former VP of Product and Marketing at Lambda School, and former VP of Marketing at MasterClass. These days, Adam is a growth and marketing advisor to many companies, as well as a teacher through Reforge. In today’s episode, Adam shares how to determine whether a new channel is worth exploring, the rise of the growth CMO, and how improv classes can improve team bonding and create a more positive, “yes” culture. He also speaks candidly about his own struggles with burnout and depression and shares some incredible tools that have helped him along the way.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 亚当·格雷尼尔曾任优步增长营销与创新部门主管，助力该公司从零到一搭建增长基础设施。他还曾担任Lambda School产品与营销副总裁，以及MasterClass营销副总裁。如今，亚当是多家公司的增长与营销顾问，同时通过Reforge授课。在本期节目中，亚当分享了如何判断新渠道是否值得探索、增长型CMO兴起的趋势，以及即兴表演课程如何促进团队凝聚力并营造更积极的“是”文化。他还坦诚谈及自己曾遭遇的职业倦怠与抑郁症，并分享了帮助他渡过难关的实用工具。

summary.en: Adam lays out a three-ingredient framework for evaluating emerging acquisition channels: overlap between the channel's strengths and your customer and business needs (a green light only if they align), the channel's DNA (its stage and monetization strategy—matching theirs earns you an edge), and your own company DNA (risk appetite and existing channel mix). He advises testing with minimal resources, treating it like "fishing" and not letting it bleed past a quarter, noting only ~5% of new channels truly pan out. On the "Growth CMO," he argues product and marketing must be married at the hip and run with an agile, experimental mindset—traditional CMOs often fail because of that mismatch. He closes with a candid mental-health arc: burnout is often actually depression, distinguishable by whether you still show up for what you love, and therapy, a supportive partner, transparent friends, and meditation are what got him through.
summary.zh: Adam 提出评估新兴获客渠道的「三要素框架」：媒介优势是否与客户需求和公司目标重叠（重叠才亮绿灯）、渠道的 DNA（所处阶段、变现方式，匹配对方变现策略能拿到先发优势）、以及公司自身 DNA（风险偏好与现有渠道组合）。他建议用最小资源先「钓鱼」测试、别拖过一个季度，并提醒真正跑通的渠道只有约 5%。关于「增长型 CMO」，他认为产品与营销必须绑在一起、用敏捷和实验心态运作，传统 CMO 常因不匹配而失败。最后他坦诚分享心理健康历程：倦怠常其实是抑郁，区分在于你是否还愿意投入热爱的事；therapy、伴侣、透明朋友圈和冥想是撑过来的关键。

episodeTitle.en: How to build a powerful marketing machine | Emily Kramer (Asana, Carta, MKT1)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何打造强大的营销机器 | Emily Kramer（Asana、Carta、MKT1）

bio.en: Emily Kramer is a B2B marketing leader who built and led the early marketing teams at Asana, Carta, Ticketfly, and Astro (acquired by Slack), writes the popular MKT1 newsletter, and now advises, invests in, and runs a fund for early-stage B2B startups.
bio.zh: Emily Kramer 是一位 B2B 营销负责人，曾在 Asana、Carta、Ticketfly 和 Astro（被 Slack 收购）从零搭建并带领早期营销团队，运营广受欢迎的 MKT1 通讯，现在为早期 B2B 初创提供顾问、投资，并管理一支相关基金。

guestBioOfficial.en: Emily Kramer led and built the marketing teams at Asana, Carta, Ticketfly, and Astro (acquired by Slack). These days, she’s the co-founder of MKT1, where she helps founders and marketers build and scale their marketing functions. Emily is also a well-respected angel investor and writes my favorite marketing newsletter (MKT1). In today’s episode, she shares her insights on when to hire marketers, how to determine which type of marketing hire is best for your team, how to best work with marketing, and what red flags to look for. Emily shares actionable templates and some incredible frameworks that are sure to expand your marketing knowledge.
guestBioOfficial.zh: Emily Kramer曾在Asana、Carta、Ticketfly和Astro（被Slack收购）领导并建立营销团队。如今，她是MKT1的联合创始人，帮助创始人和营销人员建立并扩展他们的营销职能。Emily还是一位备受尊敬的天使投资人，还撰写了我最喜欢的营销通讯（MKT1）。在今天的节目中，她分享了她对何时聘请营销人员、如何确定哪种类型的营销招聘最适合你的团队、如何最好地与营销部门合作以及应注意哪些危险信号的见解。Emily分享了可行的模板和一些令人惊叹的框架，这些框架必将拓展你的营销知识。

summary.en: Emily introduces a "fuel vs. engine" framework for marketing: fuel is the content and value you create, while the engine is how you distribute it to the right people, and the first step before hiring is diagnosing which side is your biggest constraint. For your first marketing hire she recommends a "pie-shaped" (π) generalist who is an expert in one of product, content, or growth marketing, proficient in a second, and able to set strategy across all three. In product-led growth, marketing—not just product—should own top-of-funnel and web conversion, with clear DRIs and a smooth marketing-to-product handoff so the user experience stays consistent. She stresses judging a marketing team by impact goals and full-funnel conversion rates rather than activity metrics, and using lightweight frameworks like AOR (areas of responsibility) lists and GACCS briefs to align marketing and product. Finally, she shares how functional experts can become sought-after angel investors by articulating one clear, specific value-add—such as helping founders build their marketing function.
summary.zh: Emily 提出了一个营销的"燃料 vs 引擎"框架：燃料是你创造的内容和价­值，引擎是你如何把这些送到对的人手里，而在招人之前的第一步，是诊断哪一侧是你最大的瓶颈。关于第一个营销招聘，她推荐招一个"π 型"通才——在产品、内容、增长三类营销中有一项是专家、第二项是熟手，并且能在三者之上定战略。在产品驱动增长（PLG）里，拥有漏斗顶部和网页转化的应该是营销、而不只是产品，并且要有清晰的 DRI 和顺畅的"营销到产品"衔接，让用户体­验保持一致。她强调要用"影响目标"和全漏斗的转化率、而不是"活动指标"来衡量一个营销团队，并用 AOR（责任领域）清单和 GACCS 简报这类轻量框架来对齐营销和产品。最后，她分享职能专家如何把自己清晰、具体的价值贡献（比如帮创始人搭建营销职能）讲清楚，从而变成人人争抢的天使投资人。

episodeTitle.en: Overcome imposter syndrome and accelerate your career | Julie Zhuo (Sundial, Facebook)
episodeTitle.zh: 克服冒名顶替综合症，加速职业发展 | 朱莉·卓（Sundial，Facebook）

bio.en: Julie Zhuo spent 13 years at Facebook, rising from an individual-contributor designer to VP of Product Design, and is the bestselling author of The Making of a Manager.
bio.zh: 朱莉·卓（Julie Zhuo）在 Facebook 工作了 13 年，从一线设计师成长为产品设计副总裁，并著有畅销书《创作者之路》（The Making of a Manager）。

guestBioOfficial.en: Julie Zhuo is the co-founder of Sundial, a company that helps builders make meaningful use of data to fulfill their mission. With over 400K followers across social media, she is one of the most influential leaders in product design, and product thinking broadly. Julie started her career at Facebook as a product designer and eventually led teams of 100+ designers as the VP of Design. Her experience leading at Facebook motivated her to publish the Wall Street Journal best seller The Making of a Manager in 2019. On the side, Julie shared her thoughts on technology, design, and leadership in The Looking Glass, the blog that inspired Lenny’s Newsletter.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 朱莉·卓是Sundial的联合创始人，该公司致力于帮助开发者有效利用数据实现使命。她在社交媒体上拥有超过40万粉丝，是产品设计和产品思维领域最具影响力的领导者之一。朱莉的职业生涯始于Facebook，担任产品设计师，最终以产品副总裁身份领导超过100名设计师团队。她在Facebook的领导经验促使她于2019年出版《经理人修炼之道》，登上《华尔街日报》畅销书榜单。此外，她还在博客《镜报》上分享对科技、设计和领导力的见解，该博客启发了Lenny’s Newsletter的创立。

summary.en: In Lenny's very first episode, Julie shares hard-won career advice, from overcoming imposter syndrome to running effective product review meetings. She discusses what great design hiring and feedback look like, and how her immigrant background shaped her relentless work ethic. The conversation is a foundational primer on product leadership and personal growth.
summary.zh: 在 Lenny 的第一期节目中，朱莉分享了来之不易的职业建议，从克服冒名顶替综合征到如何开好产品评审会。她探讨了什么是优秀的设计招聘与反馈，以及移民背景如何塑造了她不懈的工作态度。本期堪称产品领导力与个人成长的入门基石。

episodeTitle.en: The role of AI in new product development | Ryan J. Salva (VP of Product at GitHub)
episodeTitle.zh: 人工智能在新产品开发中的作用 | Ryan J. Salva（GitHub产品副总裁）

bio.en: Ryan J. Salva is VP of Product at GitHub, where he incubated and launched GitHub Copilot - one of the most transformative developer tools of the decade - and previously spent a decade at Microsoft and started in philosophy and English.
bio.zh: Ryan J. Salva 是 GitHub 的产品副总裁，在 GitHub 他孵化并推出了 GitHub Copilot——十年来最具变革性的开发者工具之一——此前他在微软工作十年，学术背景始于哲学与英语。

guestBioOfficial.en: Ryan J. Salva is the VP of Product at GitHub, where he led the incubation and launch of Copilot, which uses OpenAI to suggest code and entire functions in real time, right from your editor, and is changing the way we build software. Ryan is an experienced developer and product manager, with over a decade of experience working for Microsoft before moving to lead the GitHub product team. In today’s episode, he shares how Copilot got its start, how it moved from prototype to live product, and how he structures R&D teams within larger companies. He also discusses the ethical questions surrounding AI use and how to build a successful product team, and shares the inside story of the development of Copilot.
guestBioOfficial.zh: Ryan J. Salva是GitHub的产品副总裁，他领导了Copilot的孵化与发布。Copilot利用OpenAI实时在编辑器中建议代码和整个函数，正在改变我们构建软件的方式。Ryan是一位经验丰富的开发者和产品经理，在加入GitHub产品团队之前，曾在微软工作了十多年。在今天的节目中，他将分享Copilot的起源、从原型到上线产品的转变过程，以及他如何在大型公司中构建研发团队。他还将探讨围绕人工智能使用的伦理问题、如何组建成功的产品团队，并分享Copilot开发的幕后故事。

summary.en: Ryan tells the story of how GitHub Copilot went from a small R&D bet to a product used by millions, and what it takes to incubate a big bet inside a large company. He shares how Copilot keeps developers in flow by bringing context into the editor, and surprising use cases - from educators teaching kids to code to small businesses building internal tools with student teams. The episode is a fascinating look at building AI developer tooling at scale.
summary.zh: Ryan 讲述了 GitHub Copilot 如何从一个小小的研发赌注，成长为被数百万人使用的产品，以及在大公司内部孵化大型赌注需要什么。他分享了 Copilot 如何通过把上下文带进编辑器，让开发者保持在“心流”中，以及一些出人意料的使用场景——从教育者教孩童写代码，到小企业与学徒团队共建内部工具。本期是对规模化打造 AI 开发者工具的精彩透视。

episodeTitle.en: How to grow a subscription business | Yuriy Timen (Grammarly, Canva, Airtable)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何发展订阅业务 | 尤里·蒂门（Yuriy Timen，曾就职于Grammarly、Canva、Airtable）

bio.en: Yuriy Timen is a growth advisor who spent eight and a half years at Grammarly building its growth and marketing function into the household-name brand it is today; he now advises 4-5 subscription and consumerized B2B companies at a time (including Canva, Airtable, Otter, Hims, and Flow Health) on finding and scaling their core growth engines.
bio.zh: Yuriy Timen 是一位增长顾问。他在 Grammarly 待了八年半，把公司的增长和营销体系打造成了今天这个人尽皆知的品牌；如今他一次同时辅导 4 到 5 家订阅型和“消费化”的 B2B 公司（包括 Canva、Airtable、Otter、Hims、Flow Health 等），帮它们找到并放大核心增长引擎。

guestBioOfficial.en: Yuriy Timen was Global Head of Marketing and Growth at Grammarly, and is now a full-time growth advisor, having worked with more than a dozen companies, including Canva, Airtable, Whimsical, Otter.ai, Oyster, Flo Health, and Clay. In today’s episode, Yuriy discusses the ever-changing world of growth, emerging growth tactics, and how to find your growth engine. You’ll learn the most effective strategies for driving user acquisition, how to balance and diversify organic and paid channels, when it’s time to change plans, how to vet new growth channel opportunities, and much more.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 尤里·蒂门曾是Grammarly的全球营销与增长负责人，如今是全职增长顾问，已与Canva、Airtable、Whimsical、Otter.ai、Oyster、Flo Health和Clay等十余家公司合作。在本期节目中，尤里将探讨不断变化的增长领域、新兴增长策略，以及如何找到自己的增长引擎。你将学习到吸引用户的最有效策略、如何平衡和多元化自然和付费渠道、何时需要调整计划、如何评估新增长渠道机会等等。

summary.en: Yuriy lays out a practical framework for how subscription and consumer companies should think about their three core growth engines-virality/referrals, SEO, and paid-and how to tell which one fits. He argues most companies are powered by a single 80/20 growth engine and warns against diversifying too early (when small) or too late (when over-reliant at scale). On paid, he explains why the current budget contraction actually creates an edge for disciplined, well-instrumented companies, and why SEO is becoming more attractive as the 'grow-at-all-costs' urgency fades. He also shares concrete benchmarks (e.g., 20-35% visitor-to-free-user and 5%+ free-to-paid conversion) and why onboarding is almost always the highest-leverage investment.
summary.zh: Yuriy 给出了一个非常落地的框架，讲订阅型和消费级公司该怎么思考三大核心增长引擎——病毒/推荐、SEO 和付费——以及如何判断哪个适合自己。他认为大多数公司其实只靠一个 80/20 的增长引擎驱动，并警告说：太小的时候多元化太早、太大的时候又过度依赖单一渠道而多元化太晚，都是坑。关于付费，他解释了为什么当下预算收缩反而给有纪律、埋点完善的公司创造了优势，以及为什么随着“不惜一切代价增长”的紧迫感消退，SEO 正变得更有吸引力。他还分享了关键基准（比如访客到免费用户 20%–35% 的转化、免费到付费 5% 以上），以及为什么上手流程几乎永远是高杠杆的投入。

episodeTitle.en: Persuasive communication and managing up | Wes Kao (Maven, altMBA, Section4)
episodeTitle.zh: 《说服性沟通与向上管理》| 韦斯·考（Maven、altMBA、Section4）

bio.en: Wes Kao co-created the Alt-MBA with Seth Godin and co-founded Maven, and is a writer and educator focused on operations, management, and executive communication.
bio.zh: Wes Kao 与 Seth Godin 共同创造了 Alt-MBA，并联合创立了 Maven，她是一位专注于运营、管理与高管沟通的写作者和教育者。

guestBioOfficial.en: Wes Kao has worked with Seth Godin (where she co-founded the altMBA and served as executive director), David Perell on his Write of Passage course, Professor Scott Galloway on Section4, and Morning Brew. Currently, she’s the co-founder of Maven, a cohort-based learning platform where I taught my own course. Wes is passionate about telling stories that stay true to the creator’s intentions while keeping your audience listening. In today’s episode, you will learn how to use state changes to keep your audience engaged, how to communicate more clearly by focusing on the how more than the why, how to manage up for success, and how to communicate your priorities to set a boundary.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 韦斯·考曾与赛斯·高丁（她曾与其共同创立altMBA并担任执行董事）、大卫·佩雷尔（David Perell）在其Write of Passage课程中合作，跟随斯科特·加洛维教授（Scott Galloway）参与Section4项目，并为Morning Brew工作。目前，她是Maven的联合创始人——这是一个基于课程的学习平台，我曾在那里教授自己的课程。韦斯热衷于讲述既忠实于创作者意图又能让听众保持专注的故事。在本期节目中，您将学习如何利用状态变化来保持听众的参与度、如何通过关注“如何”而非“为什么”来更清晰地沟通、如何向上管理以取得成功，以及如何传达您的优先事项以设定边界。

summary.en: Wes shares how to communicate as an executive and increase your influence, built around the idea that the biggest problem in communication is the illusion that it has taken place. She covers being specific instead of vague, earning trust through clarity, and why strong communication compounds across a career. The episode is a practical guide to a high-leverage skill most people underinvest in.
summary.zh: Wes 分享了如何以高管的方式沟通、提升影响力，其核心是：沟通中最大的问题，就是“以为沟通已经发生”的错觉。她涵盖了用具体取代含糊、通过清晰赢得信任，以及为什么出色的沟通会在整个职业生涯中产生复利。本期是关于一项大多数人投入不足的高杠杆技能的务实指南。

episodeTitle.en: The art of product management | Shreyas Doshi (Stripe, Twitter, Google, Yahoo)
episodeTitle.zh: 产品管理的艺术 | 施雷亚斯·多希（Stripe、Twitter、Google、雅虎）

bio.en: Shreyas Doshi is a product leader and one of today's most consistently insightful voices on the craft of product management, drawing on senior product roles at Google, Twitter, Yahoo, and Stripe.
bio.zh: Shreyas Doshi 是一位产品领导者，也是当下对产品管理手艺最具持续洞察力的声音之一，其经验来自在 Google、Twitter、Yahoo 和 Stripe 的高级产品职务。

guestBioOfficial.en: Shreyas Doshi is a treasure trove of wisdom and tactical insights on product, strategy, psychology, leadership, and life. Over the course of his career, he’s PM’d at Google, Twitter, Yahoo, and Stripe—where he joined as its fourth product manager, later becoming Stripe’s first PM manager and helping define and grow its product management function from ~5 to more than 50 people. Since leaving Stripe, Shreyas has amassed a huge Twitter following in large part thanks to consistent sharing of high-quality insights on the art of product management.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 施雷亚斯·多希在产品、战略、心理学、领导力和生活方面拥有宝贵的智慧和战术见解。在其职业生涯中，他曾在谷歌、Twitter、雅虎和Stripe担任产品经理——他以Stripe第四位产品经理的身份加入，后来成为Stripe首位产品管理经理，助力将其产品管理团队从约5人扩展至50余人。离开Stripe后，施雷亚斯在Twitter积累了大量粉丝，这很大程度上得益于他持续分享关于产品管理艺术的高质量见解。

summary.en: Shreyas shares his philosophy of high-leverage product work, including the art of saying no, focusing on outcomes over output, and protecting cognitive bandwidth for the few things that matter. He discusses how to develop product taste, the discipline of ignoring most requests, and why great PMs think in terms of leverage and systems. The episode is a dense, actionable masterclass in the craft of product management.
summary.zh: Shreyas 分享了他关于高杠杆产品工作的理念，包括说“不”的艺术、聚焦产出之上的成果、以及为少数要事保护认知带宽。他讨论了如何培养产品品味、忽略大多数请求的自律，以及为什么优秀的产品经理以杠杆与系统的方式思考。本期是关于产品管理手艺的、信息密集且可落地的导师课。

episodeTitle.en: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group
episodeTitle.zh: 产品之道 | 硅谷产品集团的马蒂·卡根

bio.en: Marty Cagan is the author of Inspired and Empowered and a partner at SVPG, widely regarded as one of the most influential voices in modern product management.
bio.zh: 马蒂·卡根（Marty Cagan）是《Inspired》与《Empowered》的作者、SVPG 的合伙人，被公认为现代产品管理领域最具影响力的声音之一。

guestBioOfficial.en: How do you maintain your product mojo? What are common diseases of product teams, and how do you avoid them? Why should you focus less on problem discovery and more on solution discovery? After working as a product leader for over 20 years, Marty Cagan started Silicon Valley Product Group to help product teams operate at a higher level. In this conversation, Marty shares what Steve Jobs can teach you about building product, how to structure your teams for innovation, how to improve your product culture, which trends in PM to ignore, and much more. After this, you'll never think about building teams the same way. Join us.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 如何保持产品灵感？产品团队常见的“病症”及应对之道？为何应更注重解决方案的探索而非问题发现？拥有20余年产品领导经验的马蒂·卡根创立了硅谷产品集团，致力于助力产品团队提升运营水平。在本次对谈中，马蒂将分享史蒂夫·乔布斯在产品打造方面的启示、创新型团队的构建方法、产品文化的优化策略、产品管理需忽视的潮流趋势等诸多观点。听完这场对谈，您将重新审视团队组建之道。欢迎加入。

summary.en: Marty discusses the principles of strong product organizations, including empowered, cross-functional teams and the importance of real product strategy. He shares how the best companies separate discovery from delivery and invest in continuous learning. The episode distills decades of coaching the world's top product teams into core lessons.
summary.zh: 马蒂探讨了强大产品组织的原则，包括被赋能的跨职能团队，以及真正的产品战略的重要性。他分享了顶尖公司如何把"探索"与"交付"分开，并持续投入学习。本期将他辅导全球顶级产品团队数十年的经验，提炼为核心要点。

episodeTitle.en: The art of building legendary brands | Arielle Jackson (Google, Square, First Round Capital)
episodeTitle.zh: 《打造传奇品牌的艺术》 | 阿里尔·杰克逊（Arielle Jackson，曾就职于Google、Square、First Round Capital）

bio.en: Arielle Jackson spent nine years at Google helping grow Gmail from a side project, was one of the first marketers at Square, and has advised 100+ early-stage companies on brand and marketing; she now teaches startup brand strategy and is a marketer-in-residence at First Round.
bio.zh: Arielle Jackson 在 Google 工作了九年，助力 Gmail 从一个副项目成长起来；她是 Square 最早的营销人员之一，并为 100 多家早期公司提供品牌与营销建议；她现在讲授创业品牌策略，并是 First Round 的驻场营销人。

guestBioOfficial.en: What makes a great brand? After working at Google and Square, Arielle Jackson has spent the past eight years consulting startups on how to create powerful messaging that works. In this jam-packed episode, she shares how to pick a winning name for your company, create a brand purpose that excites your team and customers, and position your company and its products for success. You don’t want to miss this one!
guestBioOfficial.zh: 什么造就了一个伟大的品牌？在谷歌和Square工作后，阿里尔·杰克逊过去八年一直为初创公司提供如何创建强有力的信息传递策略的咨询服务。在这期内容丰富的节目中，她将分享如何为你的公司选一个获胜的名字，创建一个能激发团队和客户热情的品牌宗旨，以及为你的公司及其产品定位成功的方向。你一定不想错过这一期！

summary.en: Arielle covers three core topics: naming strategies for your startup or product, a framework for developing your brand (purpose, positioning, personality), and how to get PR. She argues a bad name won't kill a great company but a good name helps, and that brand is the overall marketing and strategy, not just the name. The conversation is a practical guide for early founders shaping how the world sees them.
summary.zh: Arielle 涵盖了三个核心主题：为创业公司或产品命名策略、打造品牌的框架（使命、定位、个性），以及如何做公关。她认为坏名字不会毁掉好公司，但好名字有帮助，且品牌是整体的营销与战略，而非仅仅名字。对话为早期创始人塑造自身形象提供了实用指南。

episodeTitle.en: The rituals of great teams | Shishir Mehrotra, Coda, YouTube, Microsoft
episodeTitle.zh: 优秀团队的仪式感 | 希希尔·梅赫罗特拉，Coda，YouTube，微软

bio.en: Shishir Mehrotra is co-founder and CEO of Coda, the all-in-one doc, spreadsheet, and product workspace, and previously spent over a decade at Google/YouTube, where he was a VP leading core product areas including YouTube's homepage and watch experience.
bio.zh: Shishir Mehrotra 是 Coda 的联合创始人兼 CEO，Coda 是一款集文档、表格与产品工作区于一体的工具；此前他在 Google/YouTube 工作逾十年，担任副总裁，领导包括 YouTube 首页与观看体验在内的核心产品领域。

guestBioOfficial.en: Shishir Mehrotra is the co-founder and CEO of Coda, and formerly head of product and engineering at YouTube. In this episode, he shares his insights on growth strategy, how he evaluates talent, a peek at his upcoming book The Rituals of Great Teams, why reference checks are the most important step in the interview process, and so much more. Join us.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 希希尔·梅赫罗特拉（Shishir Mehrotra）是Coda的联合创始人兼CEO，曾任YouTube产品与工程部门负责人。本期节目中，他将分享自己对增长战略的见解、如何评估人才、对其即将出版的《优秀团队的仪式感》一书的展望、为何背景调查是面试过程中最重要的一环等诸多观点。欢迎收听。

summary.en: Shishir shares how Coda builds product and culture, including its famous 'operating principles' and approaches to docs-as-products. He discusses lessons from scaling YouTube, how to create alignment through shared principles rather than process, and why building a new category requires patience and a clear point of view. The episode offers a thoughtful look at founder-led product philosophy.
summary.zh: Shishir 分享了 Coda 如何打造产品与文化，包括其著名的“运营原则（operating principles）”以及“文档即产品”的思路。他讨论了规模化 YouTube 的经验、如何通过共享原则而非流程来达成对齐，以及为何开辟新品类需要耐心与清晰的立场。本期对创始人驱动的产品哲学给出了富有思考的透视。

episodeTitle.en: How to launch and grow your product | Ryan Hoover of Product Hunt and Weekend Fund
episodeTitle.zh: 如何推出并发展你的产品 | Product Hunt和Weekend Fund的瑞安·胡佛

bio.en: Ryan Hoover is the founder of Product Hunt and a full-time investor through his fund Weekend Fund, and previously spent time as a product manager before becoming a well-known figure in tech.
bio.zh: Ryan Hoover 是 Product Hunt 的创始人，也是通过其基金 Weekend Fund 全职从事投资的人，在成为科技圈知名人物之前，他曾担任过产品经理。

guestBioOfficial.en: Thousands of new products launch each year, but very few last. Ryan Hoover has seen thousands of products launched over the course of his time running Product Hunt and through his investing, and in this episode you’ll hear what Ryan has learned about launching products, growing products, and raising capital. Plus, we play a made-up game called “What would you rather upvote?” Join us!
guestBioOfficial.zh: 每年有成千上万的新产品推出，但极少能长久存续。瑞安·胡佛在运营Product Hunt期间及投资经历中见证了数千款产品的诞生。在本期节目中，您将听到瑞安在产品推出、产品发展及融资方面的深刻见解。此外，我们还将玩一个虚构的游戏——“你更愿意点赞什么？”。快来加入我们吧！

summary.en: Ryan reflects on the surreal experience of building Product Hunt into a tech institution and the hidden weight of public recognition, while openly discussing the anxiety and mask of confidence that come with being a founder/CEO. He shares lessons from his writing and investing, and the importance of community and showing up authentically. The conversation blends personal vulnerability with practical founder wisdom.
summary.zh: Ryan 回顾了将 Product Hunt 打造成科技圈标志性产品的超现实经历，以及公众知名度背后隐藏的重量，同时坦诚分享了身为创始人/CEO 伴随而来的焦虑与“自信面具”。他分享了写作与投资中的心得，以及社区与真诚在场的重要性。本期将个人的脆弱坦诚与务实的创始人智慧融为一体。

episodeTitle.en: How to scrappily hire for, measure, and unlock growth | Crystal Widjaja, Gojek and Kumu
episodeTitle.zh: 何以以低成本招聘、精准衡量并释放增长潜力 | 水晶·维迪雅加（Gojek、Kumu产品负责人）

bio.en: Crystal Widjaja is Chief Product Officer at Kumu and was a growth leader at Gojek, where she built and led the growth team through its rise to Southeast Asia's largest super app.
bio.zh: Crystal Widjaja 是 Kumu 首席产品官，曾任 Gojek 增长负责人，在那里建立并领导增长团队，助其成长为东南亚最大的超级应用。

guestBioOfficial.en: You don't need lots of employees to achieve impressive growth, but you do need a unique approach to hiring and measuring what matters most. Crystal Widjaja has used scrappy tactics to unlock massive success for Gojek (a wildly successful ride-share app in South East Asia) and is currently the Chief Product Officer at Kumu. In this episode, she shares the exact strategies she’s used as a product leader to hack growth, hire the best, and perfect data collection. Join us.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 要实现显著增长，您无需大量员工，但需要采用独特的招聘方式并关注最关键的衡量指标。水晶·维迪雅加曾为Gojek（东南亚极为成功的网约车平台）破解增长难题，如今担任Kumu首席产品官。在本期节目中，她将分享作为产品领导者如何破解增长难题、招聘顶尖人才并优化数据收集的具体策略。欢迎加入我们。

summary.en: Crystal shares the biggest growth unlocks she's seen across Gojek and other large consumer businesses, and which growth investments pay off versus which don't. She digs into growth models, tips for accelerating growth, and why most analytics efforts fail—and how to avoid that. The conversation also covers how to hire and structure a growth team, plus her nonprofit Generation Girl for getting young women into STEM.
summary.zh: Crystal 分享了她在 Gojek 及其他大型消费业务中所见的最大增长突破，以及哪些增长投入有回报、哪些没有。她深入增长模型、加速增长的技巧，以及为何多数数据分析努力会失败——又如何避免。对话还涵盖如何招聘和搭建增长团队，以及她帮助年轻女性进入 STEM 的非营利项目 Generation Girl。

episodeTitle.en: How to create a winning product strategy | Melissa Perri
episodeTitle.zh: 如何制定成功的产品策略 | 梅丽莎·佩里

bio.en: Melissa Perri is the author of Escaping the Build Trap and a leading voice on product strategy and product management training.
bio.zh: 梅丽莎·佩里（Melissa Perri）是《逃离构建陷阱》（Escaping the Build Trap）的作者，也是产品战略与产品管理培训领域的领军声音。

guestBioOfficial.en: Every company wants to develop a winning strategy—but what are signs your strategy isn’t working, and how do you change course? Melissa Perri has worked trained PMs and product leaders at nearly all the Fortune 100 companies, and in this conversation shares how to reset a struggling strategy, align your team, and build winning strategy. Join us.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 每个公司都希望制定成功的战略——但当你的战略不起作用时，该如何识别问题所在，又该如何调整方向？梅丽莎·佩里曾为近乎所有《财富》100强公司培训产品经理和产品负责人，本次对话中她将分享如何重置陷入困境的战略、团结团队并构建成功的产品策略。欢迎加入我们。

summary.en: Melissa explains why she does not recommend the Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe), noting that even fans end up ripping it apart and rebuilding it. She traces how the "product owner" role emerged from Scrum rather than true product management. The episode clarifies the difference between output-focused roles and real product management.
summary.zh: 梅丽莎解释了为何她不推荐使用规模化敏捷框架（SAFe），指出即便是它的拥护者最终也会将其拆解、重建。她追溯了"产品负责人"角色如何从 Scrum 而非真正的产品管理中产生。本期厘清了"聚焦产出"的角色与真正产品管理之间的区别。

episodeTitle.en: How to unlock your product leadership skills | Ken Norton, Ex-Google
episodeTitle.zh: 如何解锁产品领导力 | 肯·诺顿（前谷歌高管）

bio.en: Ken Norton spent 14 years at Google leading product teams behind Google Docs, Calendar, and Maps, and now works full-time as an executive coach for product leaders.
bio.zh: 肯·诺顿（Ken Norton）在 Google 工作了 14 年，领导过 Google Docs、Calendar 和 Maps 等产品团队，如今是全职的产品高管教练。

guestBioOfficial.en: Advancing as a product leader requires new skills and a new mindset. Ken Norton is an executive coach who works with some of the top people in product to help them get unstuck and find creativity again in their approach to problems and their careers. After 14 years as a Product Manager at Google, Ken brings deep experience in leadership and shares with us the lessons he most often offers his clients to unlock growth. Join us.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 要想在产品领导岗位上有所突破，需要具备新技能和新思维。肯·诺顿是为顶尖产品团队提供辅导的执行教练，帮助他们突破瓶颈，重新激发解决问题和职业发展的创造力。肯在谷歌担任产品经理14年，积累了深厚的领导经验，并将为客户提供的最常用增长策略与我们分享。欢迎加入我们。

summary.en: Ken emphasizes that product management is leadership from day one, even without formal authority. He discusses the creative versus reactive mindset and why the art of PM-ing matters more than the science. The episode covers overcoming imposter syndrome, common PM blind spots, and how to find and evaluate a good coach.
summary.zh: 肯强调，产品经理从第一天起就是领导者，即便没有正式职权。他探讨了"创造性"与"被动反应"两种心态，以及为何产品管理的"艺术"比"科学"更重要。本期涵盖如何克服冒名顶替综合征、PM 常见的盲点，以及如何找到并评估一位好教练。

episodeTitle.en: How to sell your ideas and rise within your company | Casey Winters, Eventbrite
episodeTitle.zh: 如何在公司推销自己的想法并晋升 | 凯西·温特斯（Casey Winters），Eventbrite

bio.en: Casey Winters is a growth and product strategist who has led growth or advised companies including Grubhub, Pinterest, Reddit, Eventbrite (as CPO), Canva, Airbnb, Tinder, and Thumbtack, and was the first repeat guest on Lenny's Podcast.
bio.zh: Casey Winters 是一位增长与产品战略专家，曾领导或与 Grubhub、Pinterest、Reddit、Eventbrite（任 CPO）、Canva、Airbnb、Tinder、Thumbtack 等公司合作或提供顾问，并且是 Lenny 播客第一个返场嘉宾。

guestBioOfficial.en: The people who rise fastest in product know how to sell their ideas to customers, and also to their coworkers. Casey Winters, the Chief Product Officer at Eventbrite (previously at Grubhub, Pinterest, and advisor to dozens of companies) shares what it takes to be successful as you rise in the ranks within product. In this episode we’ll talk about how to land presentations, how to win over executives with strategic communication, the skill sets that are most in demand in product, and new growth trends. Join us.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 在产品领域晋升最快的人懂得如何向客户推销自己的想法，也知道如何说服同事。凯西·温特斯（曾任职于Grubhub、Pinterest，并为数十家公司提供顾问服务）现任Eventbrite首席产品官，将分享在产品领域晋升成功的秘诀。本次对谈将探讨如何成功完成演示、如何通过战略沟通赢得高管支持、产品领域最受欢迎的技能，以及新兴的增长趋势。欢迎加入我们。

summary.en: Casey warns of the "zero interest rate phenomenon product manager" — PMs trained in an era of abundant funding who over-rely on frameworks and research instead of shipping and using judgment. He argues the real PM job (making high-leverage decisions under uncertainty) is AI-resistant, while AI is best used for tedious non-core work. On founder intuition vs team expertise, founders should direct until employees prove they surpass them, then delegate. The episode also breaks down network effects (direct, cross-side, data) and why Grubhub lost to DoorDash despite strong network effects: it underestimated a structurally unprofitable but market-rewarded disruptor. Finally, he explains why consumer subscription businesses are brutally hard (no net dollar retention) and why marketplaces adding SaaS tools beat SaaS tools adding marketplaces.
summary.zh: Casey 警告了"零利率现象产品经理"——那些在资金充沛年代被训练出来、过度依赖框架和研究、而不是发布和使用判断的 PM。他主张真正的 PM 工作（在不确定性下做高杠杆决定）是抗 AI 的，而 AI 最好用于琐碎的非核心活。在创始人直觉 vs 团队专业上，创始人应该指挥，直到员工证明他们超越自己，然后授权。节目还拆解了网络效应（直接、跨边、数据），以及为什么 Grubhub 尽管有强网络效应还是输给 DoorDash：它低估了一个结构亏损但被市场奖励的颠覆者。最后，他解释了为什么消费订阅生意极其难（没有净收入留存率），以及为什么市场加 SaaS 工具胜过 SaaS 工具加市场。

episodeTitle.en: Nickey Skarstad (Airbnb, Etsy, Shopify, Duolingo) on translating vision into goals, operationalizing product quality, second-order decisions, brainstorming, influence, and much more
episodeTitle.zh: 尼基·斯卡斯塔德（曾任Airbnb、Etsy、Shopify、Duolingo产品总监）将探讨如何将愿景转化为目标、产品质量的运营化、二阶决策、头脑风暴、影响力等诸多议题。

bio.en: Nickey Skarstad is a product leader at Duolingo (and formerly Airbnb and The Wing) known internally as a PM who gets things done, and a repeated community recommendation as an under-the-radar guest.
bio.zh: 尼基·斯卡斯塔德（Nickey Skarstad）是 Duolingo 的产品负责人（此前在 Airbnb 和 The Wing），以"能把事做成"的 PM 闻名于内部，也是社群反复推荐、却低调的嘉宾。

guestBioOfficial.en: Nickey Skarstad is a Director of Product Management at Duolingo, where she is leading a stealth 0 → 1 product. Prior to Duolingo, she was VP of Product at The Wing, Product Lead at Airbnb, where she led much of the Experiences product team,  Product Lead at Shopify, and Director of Product Management at Etsy.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 尼基·斯卡斯塔德现任Duolingo产品管理总监，此前曾在The Wing担任产品副总裁、Airbnb产品负责人（负责大部分体验产品团队）、Shopify产品负责人以及Etsy产品管理总监。

summary.en: Nickey walks through setting vision, translating it into goals, and executing with alignment, plus how to run effective product review sessions. She shares the skills that powered her rise from forum moderator to director of product. The episode is a grounded playbook for turning strategy into shipped, high-quality product.
summary.zh: 尼基逐步讲解了如何设定愿景、转化为目标并对齐执行，以及如何开好产品评审会。她分享了让自己从论坛版主一路成长为产品总监的本领。本期是一份扎实的手册，关于如何把战略变为已交付、高质量的产品。

episodeTitle.en: Manik Gupta (ex-CPO Uber, Google Maps) on how to build consumer apps, why it’s useful to be optimistic about technology, creating inflections in your PM career, the changing CPO role, and more
episodeTitle.zh: Manik Gupta（前优步、谷歌地图首席产品官）谈如何打造消费者应用、为何对科技保持乐观态度、在产品管理生涯中创造转折点、CPO角色的变化等

bio.en: Manik Gupta led two of history's most successful consumer products - Google Maps as director of product and Uber as Chief Product Officer - and later joined Microsoft as a Corporate VP.
bio.zh: 马尼克·古普塔（Manik Gupta）曾领导史上最成功的两款消费级产品——作为产品总监领导 Google Maps，并担任 Uber 的首席产品官——后来以企业副总裁身份加入微软。

guestBioOfficial.en: Manik Gupta has led two of the most successful consumer products in history—Google Maps, where he was Director of product for the Maps team, and Uber, where he was CPO. After leaving Uber, he spent some time working on a product to help people avoid getting COVID called CVKey, and most recently he took on a role at Microsoft as Corporate Vice President leading many of their consumer efforts.
guestBioOfficial.zh: Manik Gupta曾领导过两款史上最成功的消费级产品——谷歌地图（他在该团队担任产品总监）和优步（担任首席产品官）。离开优步后，他致力于开发一款帮助人们避免感染新冠病毒的应用CVKey，最近还加入微软，担任负责多个消费者业务的企业副总裁。

summary.en: Manik shares lessons on building consumer products, structuring product teams, and the difference between company-market fit and product-market fit. He reflects on what it was like to be CPO at Uber versus Google versus Microsoft. The episode also offers career advice for anyone aiming to become a CPO.
summary.zh: 马尼克分享了打造消费级产品、搭建产品团队，以及"公司-市场契合"与"产品-市场契合"之别的心得。他回顾了在 Uber、Google 与微软担任 CPO 的不同体验。本期还为有志成为 CPO 的人提供了职业建议。

episodeTitle.en: Merci Grace (ex-Head of Growth at Slack) on PLG, interviewing, storytelling, building a diverse team, hiring salespeople, building a growth team, and much more
episodeTitle.zh: Merci Grace（前Slack增长部门主管）谈产品生命周期管理、面试技巧、讲故事、组建多元化团队、招聘销售人员、建立增长团队等

bio.en: Merci Grace is the founder and CEO of Panobi, was previously Head of Growth and Head of Product at Slack, and is a co-founder of Women in Product.
bio.zh: 梅西·格雷斯（Merci Grace）是 Panobi 的创始人兼 CEO，此前曾任 Slack 的增长负责人与产品负责人，也是 Women in Product 的联合创始人。

guestBioOfficial.en: Merci Grace has been a founder, an investor (at Lightspeed Ventures), head of product and growth (at Slack), and is now a founder again (Panobi). She’s also one of the co-founders of Women in Product, and Fast Company named her one of the Most Creative People in 2017.
guestBioOfficial.zh: Merci Grace曾是创业者、Lightspeed Ventures投资人、Slack产品与增长部门主管，如今再次创业（Panobi）。她还是Women in Product的联合创始人之一，《快公司》杂志曾将她评为2017年度最具创造力人物之一。

summary.en: Merci explains that product-led growth still often needs sales, depending on whether the buyer needs top-down buy-in. She covers common mistakes going PLG, signs you're ready for it, and when to hire your first head of growth. The episode is a rich guide to PLG, interviewing, storytelling, and building diverse, high-performing teams.
summary.zh: 梅西阐释了：产品驱动增长（PLG）往往仍需要销售，取决于买家是否需自上而下的批准。她涵盖了做 PLG 的常见误区、何时适合 PLG，以及何时招聘第一位增长负责人。本期是关于 PLG、面试、讲故事与打造多元高效团队的丰富指南。

episodeTitle.en: Sanchan Saxena (VP of Product at Coinbase) on the inside story of how Airbnb made it through Covid; what he’s learned from Brian Chesky, Brian Armstrong, and Kevin Systrom; much more
episodeTitle.zh: 桑钱·萨克塞纳（Coinbase产品副总裁）将分享Airbnb如何度过新冠疫情的内部故事；他从布莱恩·切斯基、布莱恩·阿姆斯特朗和凯文·西斯特罗姆身上学到的经验；以及更多内容。

bio.en: Sanchan Saxena is VP of Product at Coinbase and was previously Head of Product and GM at Airbnb, founder and Head of Product of Instagram Shopping, Director of Product at Yahoo, and a PM at Microsoft.
bio.zh: Sanchan Saxena 是 Coinbase 的产品副总裁，此前曾任 Airbnb 产品负责人兼总经理、Instagram Shopping 创始人兼产品负责人、Yahoo 产品总监，以及微软产品经理。

guestBioOfficial.en: Sanchan Saxena is VP of Product at Coinbase. Before Coinbase, Sanchan was Head of Product and GM at Airbnb, founder and Head of Product of Instagram Shopping, Director of Product Management at Yahoo, and Lead PM at Microsoft.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 桑钱·萨克塞纳现任Coinbase产品副总裁。在加入Coinbase之前，他曾在Airbnb担任产品负责人和总经理，创立并领导Instagram Shopping产品团队，还曾在雅虎担任产品管理总监，并在微软担任首席产品经理。

summary.en: Sanchan shares the inside story of how Airbnb navigated COVID when travel stopped, and the lessons he learned from working alongside exceptional CEOs like Brian Chesky, Brian Armstrong, and Kevin Systrom. He covers how to set up a product development process at a startup, when to hire your first PM, and when (and when not) to A/B test. The episode is full of hard-won wisdom from scaling products at the world's top companies.
summary.zh: Sanchan 分享了 Airbnb 在疫情导致旅行停摆时如何渡过难关的内幕，以及他与 Brian Chesky、Brian Armstrong、Kevin Systrom 等杰出 CEO 共事所学到的经验。他涵盖了如何在初创公司建立产品开发流程、何时招聘第一位 PM，以及何时（以及何时不）该做 A/B 测试。本期充满了在世界顶级公司规模化产品过程中锤炼出的硬核智慧。

episodeTitle.en: Brandon Chu on building product at Shopify, how writing changed the trajectory of his career, the habits that make you a great PM, pros and cons of being a platform PM, how Shopify got through Covid
episodeTitle.zh: 布兰登·朱（Brandon Chu）在Shopify的职业生涯：如何在产品管理中突破极限

bio.en: Brandon Chu is a former VP of Product and GM of Platform at Shopify, where he helped define and scale the company's product organization, and the creator of influential writing on product management (The Black Box of Product Management / The Linear Method).
bio.zh: Brandon Chu 曾任 Shopify 产品副总裁兼平台总经理，帮助定义并扩展了公司的产品组织，也是极具影响力的产品管理著作（The Black Box of Product Management / The Linear Method）的作者。

guestBioOfficial.en: Brandon Chu is VP of Product at Shopify, where he leads the app platform ecosystem, new initiatives group, and M&A investments. Brandon helped scale Shopify’s PM team from five to hundreds, and worked his way up from an IC Senior PM. Prior to Shopify, he was a Director of PM at FreshBooks and, before that, a founder. Brandon might be best known for his writing on the art and science of product management as part of a collection on Medium he calls “The Black Box of Product Management.”
guestBioOfficial.zh: 布兰登·朱（Brandon Chu）是Shopify的副总裁产品部，负责应用平台生态系统、新项目组和并购投资。布兰登曾将Shopify的产品管理团队从5人扩展至数百人，并从初级产品经理一路晋升。在加入Shopify之前，他曾担任FreshBooks的产品管理总监，此前还是一名创业者。布兰登最为人熟知的身份是Medium上“产品管理黑盒”专栏的作者，通过该专栏，他分享了产品管理的艺术与科学。

summary.en: Brandon shares mental models for product and platform strategy, including “shipping is a feature” and the discipline of making high-leverage decisions with limited information. He discusses scaling product and engineering at Shopify, aligning teams around crisp context, and why small teams that start small avoid wasted engineering resources. The conversation is a masterclass in product judgment, platform thinking, and developing product managers.
summary.zh: Brandon 分享了产品与平台策略的思维模型，包括“交付即功能”（shipping is a feature），以及用有限信息做出高杠杆决策的纪律。他讨论了在 Shopify 扩展产品与工程、围绕清晰上下文对齐团队，以及为何小团队从小起步能避免工程资源浪费。对话堪称产品判断力、平台思维和培养产品经理的大师课。

socials.platform: Making Good Decisions as a Product Manager

episodeTitle.en: Gibson Biddle on his DHM product strategy framework, GEM roadmap prioritization framework, 5 Netflix strategy mini case studies, building a personal board of directors, and much more
episodeTitle.zh: 吉布森·比德尔将分享他的DHM产品战略框架、GEM路线图优先级框架、5个Netflix战略迷你案例研究、如何组建个人董事会等诸多内容。

bio.en: Gibson Biddle is a veteran product leader who served as VP of Product at Netflix and Chief Product Officer at Chegg, and now advises companies and teaches product strategy through his popular newsletter on product leadership.
bio.zh: Gibson Biddle 是一位资深产品负责人，曾任 Netflix 产品副总裁、Chegg 首席产品官，如今通过自己广受欢迎的“产品领导力”newsletter 为企业提供咨询并讲授产品战略。

guestBioOfficial.en: Before getting into teaching full-time, Gibson Biddle was VP of Product at Netflix and CPO at Chegg (a textbook rental and homework help company). He now spends his days speaking, writing, and hosting workshops on product leadership, strategy, and culture. There are very few people in the world who’ve worked with, and had an impact on, more product managers.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 在全职教学之前，吉布森·比德尔曾担任Netflix产品副总裁和Chegg（一家教材租赁和作业辅导公司）的首席产品官。他如今致力于通过演讲、写作和主持研讨会来传授产品领导力、战略和文化方面的知识。在全球范围内，极少有人曾与更多产品经理共事并对他们产生过深远影响。

summary.en: In this conversation, Gibson draws on his experience shaping strategy at Netflix and Chegg to share durable lessons on product leadership and how to build a compelling product vision. He discusses the difference between a product strategy and a product culture, how to make smart bets on features, and why focusing on customer value and a clear roadmap matters more than chasing every new idea. The episode is a masterclass in pragmatic product management for leaders who want to scale both impact and clarity.
summary.zh: 在这期对话中，Gibson 结合在 Netflix 和 Chegg 制定战略的经验，分享了关于产品领导力、以及如何打造有说服力的产品愿景的持久经验。他区分了“产品战略”与“产品文化”，讲解了如何对功能做出明智的押注，以及为何聚焦客户价值与清晰的路线图，比追逐每一个新点子更重要。这期节目是关于务实产品管理的公开课，献给想要同时放大影响力和清晰度的领导者。

episodeTitle.en: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more
episodeTitle.zh: 杰基·巴瓦罗（Jackie Bavaro）将谈及如何提升产品战略能力、战略的定义、产品经理需避免的陷阱、职业发展、晋升管理层等诸多话题。

bio.en: Jackie Bavaro is a product leader and co-author of the bestselling PM guides Cracking the PM Interview and Cracking the PM Career, drawing on product experience at Amazon, Facebook, and Dropbox.
bio.zh: Jackie Bavaro 是一位产品负责人，也是畅销 PM 指南《Cracking the PM Interview》和《Cracking the PM Career》的合著者，产品经验来自 Amazon、Facebook 和 Dropbox。

guestBioOfficial.en: Jackie Bavaro is the author of the best-selling books Cracking the PM Interview and Cracking the PM Career. She was most recently at Asana, where she joined as its first product manager and later became the head of product. Earlier in her career, Jackie was a PM at Google and Microsoft, where she worked on high-impact products such as Google Search and Microsoft SharePoint.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 杰基·巴瓦罗是《破解产品经理面试》和《破解产品经理职业生涯》两本畅销书的作者。她最近就职于Asana公司，担任其首位产品经理，随后晋升为产品负责人。此前，她曾在谷歌和微软担任产品经理，参与过谷歌搜索和微软SharePoint等高影响力产品的开发。

summary.en: In this conversation, Jackie shares practical, battle-tested advice for product managers at every stage, drawn from her experience shipping products at major tech companies and from coaching thousands of PMs through her books. She covers how to break into product management, what separates strong PMs from the rest, and how to navigate the career ladder from IC to leader. The episode is a grounded, no-fluff guide to building a successful product career.
summary.zh: 在这期对话中，Jackie 分享了面向各阶段产品经理的实战建议，这些经验既来自她在大型科技公司交付产品的经历，也来自通过著作指导过成千上万名 PM 的积累。她讲了如何进入产品管理领域、优秀 PM 与普通 PM 的区别，以及如何从个人贡献者走向领导者。这期节目是打造成功产品生涯的踏实、去水分的指南。

socials.platform: Books: Cracking the PM Interview and Cracking the PM Career

episodeTitle.en: Gokul Rajaram on designing your product development process, when and how to hire your first PM, a playbook for hiring leaders, getting ahead in you career, how to get started angel investing, more
episodeTitle.zh: 戈库尔·拉贾拉姆将探讨如何设计产品开发流程、何时及如何聘请首位产品经理、招聘领导者的指南、职业发展、如何开启天使投资等诸多话题。

bio.en: Gokul Rajaram is a product and business leader at DoorDash, a prolific angel investor, and a board member at companies including Coinbase, Pinterest, and The Trade Desk, who describes himself simply as a 'startup helper.'
bio.zh: Gokul Rajaram 是 DoorDash 的产品与业务负责人、高产的天使投资人，并担任 Coinbase、Pinterest、The Trade Desk 等公司的董事，他却把自己简单称作一名“创业帮手”。

guestBioOfficial.en: Gokul Rajaram serves on the executive team at DoorDash, where he leads the Caviar product line. Previously he worked at Square, where he was also on the executive team and led a number of key product lines, and as a product director at Facebook, where he helped the company transition its advertising business to become mobile-first. Earlier in his career, Gokul was a product director for Google AdSense, where he helped launch the product and grow it into a substantial portion of Google’s business. Gokul also serves on the boards of Coinbase, Pinterest, and The Trade Desk and is a prolific angel investor, having invested in companies like Airtable, Khatabook, and 100+ more.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 戈库尔·拉贾拉姆（Gokul Rajaram）在DoorDash的执行团队中任职，负责领导Caviar产品线。此前，他曾在Square担任高管，负责多个核心产品线；还在Facebook担任产品总监，助力该公司将广告业务转型为移动优先战略。职业生涯早期，戈库尔曾担任Google AdSense产品总监，成功将该产品推向市场，并使其成为谷歌业务的重要组成部分。戈库尔还担任Coinbase、Pinterest和The Trade Desk的董事会成员，同时也是一位活跃的天使投资人，曾投资Airtable、Khatabook等100多家公司。

summary.en: Gokul packs in practical wisdom on choosing where to work, how to do product development at startups, structuring product teams, hiring, and angel investing—all while balancing an intense DoorDash job, multiple public-company boards, and a busy mentoring schedule. He's known as one of the most humble, generous operators in tech, and the episode is a wide-ranging tour of lessons from someone who helps founders constantly. Listeners get concrete guidance on the decisions that most shape a builder's career.
summary.zh: Gokul 浓缩了大量实用智慧：如何选择工作平台、如何在创业公司做产品开发、如何组织产品团队、如何招聘以及如何做天使投资——而这一切都要在 DoorDash 高强度工作、多家上市公司董事身份和繁忙的导师日程之间取得平衡。他以科技圈最低调、最慷慨的操盘手之一而闻名，这期节目是一场地地道道的“过来人”经验巡礼。听众能收获关于那些最能塑造建设者职业生涯的决策的具指导。

episodeTitle.en: The Room Where It Happens — 2021 teaser
episodeTitle.zh: 特别内容：The Room Where It Happens 预告

bio.en: Teaser_2021 is a short promotional teaser episode with no single guest, used to preview the podcast and its upcoming conversations.
bio.zh: Teaser_2021 是一期短小的宣传预告节目，没有单一嘉宾，用于预告本播客及其即将推出的对话。

guestBioOfficial.en: A short archive teaser featuring Greg Isenberg and Sahil Bloom. It is not a regular Lenny's Podcast interview.
guestBioOfficial.zh: 一段由 Greg Isenberg 与 Sahil Bloom 出镜的存档预告，并非 Lenny's Podcast 的常规嘉宾访谈。

summary.en: This is a brief teaser episode that previews the kinds of guests and topics featured on the podcast rather than a full interview. It highlights the show's focus on product, growth, and career lessons from world-class operators. Listeners can treat it as a trailer for the broader series.
summary.zh: 这是一期简短的预告节目，预览了本播客所邀嘉宾与话题的类型，而非完整访谈。它突出了节目对产品、增长，以及来自世界级从业者的职业经验的聚焦。听众可将其视为整个系列的一支预告片。
